new_confirmed.name: SpineSAC — phantom C-arm 2D/3D registration dataset (Image Guided Robotic Surgery lab, HTIC / IIT Madras)
new_confirmed.access: Open now, no login, no request step. Both lenses crawled and downloaded anonymously (HTTP 200/206): raw DICOMs, PNGs, APLP.txt, roi_config.json and CT slices. Drive tree = 6 top-level folders, 1,254 folders, 5,492 files, 4.15 GB. Per-file direct download works via drive.usercontent.google.com; the plain folder HTML caps at 50 entries, so use embeddedfolderview for listing and gdown --remaining-ok or per-file fetches for the CT folders (309–986 files each). Repo public, created 2026-06-29, last push 2026-07-15. No DOI; no paper found on the web or arXiv.
new_confirmed.what: 59 scenarios in datasets.py (split 40/10/9) referencing 118 processed PNG X-rays — 116 distinct images, 58 distinct AP–LP pairs (Train_Set is byte-identical, same MD5, to ganga_accuracy_study_set1). Three lumbar sawbones phantoms with three conventional MDCT series, not CBCT: set1/A (GE Optima CT520, 552–553 slices at 0.625 mm) used by 43 scenarios; ClosedSawBonesCT/A (GE Optima CT520, 308–309 slices at 1.25 mm) by 11; Thancopen (Siemens SOMATOM go.Now, 985–986 slices, 'Inner Ear' protocol) by 5. Each scenario carries APLP.txt (two 3x4 matrices; GE_SCN3 holds 48 numbers instead of 24), P_Imf/P_ImfAP/LP.txt, x0.txt, TARGET.txt and roi_config.json. Raw acquisition DICOMs are also on the Drive (234 outside the Output folders) but datasets.py does not reference them.
new_confirmed.serves: NEED A only (real C-arm acquisitions with a same-object CT and recoverable per-view geometry), and only for phantoms. Not NEED B: no instruments, no per-vertebra labels.
new_confirmed.licence: No data licence anywhere on the Drive (no LICENSE, README or terms file). The repo's LICENSE.md is Apache-2.0 with the copyright line left as the unfilled template, and the GitHub API reports Apache-2.0; the README badge claims MIT and links to a LICENSE file that does not exist. The code licence does not state reuse terms for the images. No DOI.
new_confirmed.caveats: Five device sources, not three, and the attribution does not rest on folder names: native headers give GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS 'FLUOROSTAR' (GE-OEC FluoroStar, 12 scenarios), SKANRAY TECHNOLOGIES at 'JAIN HOSPITAL', 16-bit, 0.22 mm (9), and ziehm imaging/EXP8000 (12); the Ganga set carries a burned-in 'Cios_Select' overlay (Siemens, 10 incl. Train_Set); the Thancopen frames have a native SIEMENS Healthineers XA header (5). The lenses differ on the 11 closed-sawbone scenarios — one read them as Siemens with no model in the header, the other as Cios Select from a burned-in '02-05-2026' overlay. DICOM metadata in the PROCESSED files is untrustworthy: every Ganga file, the cadaver LP and many cropped files carry one reused Philips AlluraXper / 'TNMSC, Chennai' / 2020-02-26 template header, and the 0.74181640625 mm pixel spacing hard-coded in datasets.py, environment.py and utils.py is that template's ImagerPixelSpacing applied to every C-arm (the Skanray native header says 0.22 mm). The referenced PNGs are processed: intensity-inverted, bead grid removed or inpainted, several mirrored (burned-in text reads backwards), 10 are RGB, 80 of 118 are named filtered_xray_*; outputAP.json shows 'warpedImage' and 'UD_InPaint_Image' with a 2D2D bead calibration at 0.66–0.89 px reprojection error. The 'ground-truth 6-DoF pose' is NOT per scenario: gt_pose and TARGET.txt hold three distinct values, one per CT, identical across GE, Skanray, Ziehm and Ganga on set1/A — all per-scenario geometry is in APLP.txt, and how the CT-to-world reference was established is undocumented. roi_config.json holds one unlabelled box per view plus the author's local Windows paths; nothing names L3–L5, which appears only in the README's TRE text. The README's claim that paths 'resolve perfectly with no manual edits' is false for 16 of 59 entries (ClosedSawBonesCT/A sits under closedsawbonedata/, and 'SET1'..'SET4' are 'SET 1'..'SET 4'); all 118 PNGs are present once corrected. 'Ganga Hospital' is not stated in any primary source — only the folder name; the X-ray headers name JAIN HOSPITAL and the folder is BMJH, the CTs name GEM Hospital and MARUTI SCANS AND LABS. Anatomy is a little wider than claimed: the set1 and closed-phantom CTs include a sacrum and the closed-phantom AP shows the lumbosacral junction; no femora or full pelvis. The cadaver material shown in the README is one lateral X-ray (BMJH/CAD/SET 1) with no AP and no CT, so the cadaver result cannot be reproduced. The Drive holds unreferenced extras (Skanray SCN 1/2/6, GEM SET 1–5, ZIEHM/SET 1, a 419 MB NIfTI, a 100 MB 'Accuracy study.zip') and one stray Windows executable (SanDiskSecureAccessV3.1_win.exe, 8.6 MB). Header hygiene: the set1/A CT DICOM PatientName carries a real personal name although the object is a phantom.

new_confirmed.name: TROG 15.01 SPARK trial database (KIM prostate SBRT): kV intrafraction and setup projections on 5 linacs + planning CT
new_confirmed.access: Open, no login, no request. All 12 .7z archives return HTTP 200 with Accept-Ranges: bytes on the public bucket, and both lenses decoded LZMA2 blocks by range request and rendered real frames and CT. The landing page returns Cloudflare 403 to plain curl but serves a Chrome-impersonating client (curl_cffi); the bucket directory listing is AccessDenied, so the file URLs must be taken from the record. Girder-style partial fetching is not needed — plain curl works on the bucket.
new_confirmed.what: 48 living prostate SBRT patients, 5 fractions each, across five Australian centres: Center1 9 patients (Varian TrueBeam, .tiff), Center2 20 (TrueBeam), Center3 5 (TrueBeam), Center4 10 (Varian Trilogy, .hnd), Center5 4 (Elekta XVI, .his + Frames.xml, no MV). About 1.1M frames in total (~620k kV, ~476k MV). Each patient has a planning CT with RTSTRUCT/RTPLAN/RTDOSE, KIM logs with 2D/3D gold-marker positions, couch shifts and trajectory logs. Per-frame gantry angle in the TIFF file name, the .hnd header or Frames.xml.
new_confirmed.serves: NEED A in principle (real kV projections of the pelvis with a same-patient planning CT and per-frame angle), but only the setup-CBCT sweeps are usable; see caveats.
new_confirmed.licence: CC BY 4.0 (DataCite rightsList and the handle record). Cite Keall et al., IJROBP 2020;107(3):530-538. Data article: Sengupta et al., Med Phys 2025;52(3):1941-1949, doi 10.1002/mp.17529 (epub 2024-11-23), CC BY. The analysis-code repo (github.com/Image-X-Institute/SPARK_Data_Analysis_Code) carries no licence file.
new_confirmed.caveats: Sizes were wrong in the candidate: the download is 960.45 GB compressed in 12 archives (Center1 113.73, Center2 intrafraction 126.99/110.35/95.96/60.84/64.89 + AllOtherData 1.32, Center3 85.58/59.89 + 0.53, Center4 222.70, Center5 17.68 GB); 3.6 TB is the UNCOMPRESSED total (~3.52 TB from the 7z headers). Most kV frames are useless for spine work: treatment-arc frames are collimated to roughly a 6 cm (Varian) to 9 cm (Elekta) square on the prostate markers and show only the pubis, seeds and femoral-head edges. Only the setup sweeps are full field — TrueBeam KIM session 0 (100,471 of 404,248 kV TIFFs, ~503 frames per fraction); one lens found no full-field setup frames at all at Center4, so 'setup-CBCT projections on 5 linacs' is not supported for the Trilogy site. L5 was absent from every frame either lens rendered, and the sacrum is only partly visible (AP largely obscured by bowel gas; distal sacrum and coccyx show on lateral). Format corrections: Elekta frames are 512x512 (Frames.xml and the 524,388-byte .his), not 1024x1024; Trilogy is 1024x768; only the Center1–3 TIFFs are 1024x774 uint32. Rate is not uniformly 10 Hz — Elekta ~4.6–5.5 Hz, Varian setup ~16 Hz, Varian arcs ~10.6 Hz. The recorded angle is the MV gantry angle; the kV source sits 90 degrees away, so the kV projection angle must be derived (the KIM logs carry a kV gantry column). The README's 0.388/0.4 mm 'at isocentre' times 1024 gives the physical panel widths, so those values are probably detector-plane pitch — check before using the geometry for pose. Planning CT: one lens found, by grouping 512x512 series, that Center5 Patient02 has only Elekta XVI CBCT reconstructions (DERIVED/SECONDARY, 270x270 and 410x410) and no planning CT; the other lens states every patient has one. Treat that as unresolved. Bonus: reconstructed XVI CBCT volumes ship for at least Center5 Patient01. Frames taken during MV delivery carry visible scatter banding (909 of 1034 kV frames in one Elekta fraction have MVOn=True). The TROG DOI 10.58118/p5ks-zh06 is a by-request HeSANDA catalogue record, not an open mirror, and carries no licence. Elekta 'Synergy' is not stated in any primary source (README says 'Elekta'; Frames.xml StationName is 'M2Agility'). No vertebra or spine labels anywhere.

new_confirmed.name: RTK public patient data on data.kitware.com: Centre Léon Bérard patients 1–2 and POPI (Elekta XVI 4D-CBCT projections + planning CT)
new_confirmed.access: Open, anonymous, verified by streaming whole archives to the end. The Girder API returns 200 with Content-Length for every item, no login, no DUA. The server ignores HTTP Range but honours Girder's offset/endByte parameters, which is how geom.xml and the .mat files were pulled out of the zips without a full download. Girder's counter shows 134 completed downloads of CLBpatient1 CBCT.zip. The full 10-phase POPI 4D CT is NOT on Girder — it is at CREATIS (www.creatis.insa-lyon.fr/~srit/POPI/Images/Dicom, 4DCT-Dicom.tar 774 MB); the old tux.creatis links 301-redirect there.
new_confirmed.what: Three subjects, 1,976 real raw Elekta XVI kV projections in total: CLBpatient1 656 .his (656 matrices in geom.xml), CLBpatient2 676, POPI 644 (644 lines in sphase.txt; file dates 2007-01-17). Frames are 512x512 16-bit, 524,388 bytes each, ~0.8 mm pixels, 360 degrees at ~5.5 fps. geom.xml gives RTK circular geometry with SID 1000, SDD 1536 and a 3x4 matrix per projection. POPI also ships the Elekta XVI database tables FRAME.DBF and IMAGE.DBF for rtkelektasynergygeometry. Folder totals: CLBpatient1 3.84 GB, CLBpatient2 5.32 GB, POPI 1.87 GB.
new_confirmed.serves: NEED A (real clinical Elekta kV projections with a same-subject planning CT and a per-projection matrix), thorax only.
new_confirmed.licence: None. The Girder collection's terms field is empty and every folder and item has empty description and metadata. Apache-2.0 covers the RTK code, not the data. The POPI-model page asks for citation of the Léon Bérard Cancer Center & CREATIS and Vandemeulebroucke et al., ICCR 2007 — an attribution request, not a licence. No ethics or consent statement appears in the MA-ROOSTER paper. Redistribution and derivative terms are unstated.
new_confirmed.caveats: POPI is not a half-fan scan: its ProjectionOffsetX runs −5.2 to +1.3 mm against −114 to −119 mm for CLB1 and CLB2, so the 'offset detector at about −119 mm' applies only to the two CLB patients. Planning 4D CT is on Girder only for CLB1 (10 phases, 512x512x170, 0.879x0.879x2 mm, with 4D.mhd) and CLB2 (10 phases, 512x512x218, 1.365x1.365x2 mm — which contradicts the paper's claim that both are 512x512x170 at 0.88 mm); POPI's Girder folder holds only muCT.mha (float, 360x141x482, permuted) plus uchar masks. Rigid CBCT-to-CT transforms exist only for CLB1 and CLB2: CLB1's CBCT2CT.mat is an exact axis permutation plus translation with zero residual rotation, which looks like an isocentre or setup mapping rather than a fitted registration; CLB2's has sub-degree rotations and ships a flipMatrix.mat. POPI has no .mat. The pre-corrected correctedProjs.mha (666 and 687 MB) are log-transformed with the stereotactic body frame and table forward-projected and subtracted — they are processed, not detector intensities, so any bowtie/scatter/lag calibration must start from the raw .his. CLB1 frames contain an implanted port with metal artefact and the SBF honeycomb mesh plus table; the CLB1 lateral is dominated by the mesh and cut off by the half-fan detector, so vertebrae are not readable on it. Three subjects, thorax only, no lumbar spine or pelvis. 'Lung-cancer patients' is not stated for these specific subjects in the primary sources read; the institution comes from the folder names and author affiliations. The rtkelektasynergygeometry README example data (elekta.tgz, 619 MB) belongs to the Catphan 503 phantom folder, not to these patients.

new_confirmed.name: Giessen/Jena canine biplanar fluoroscopy of the lumbosacral junction with same-dog CT (Front Vet Sci 2021 + Jena Collection of X-ray Movies)
new_confirmed.access: On request only — the raw data CANNOT be downloaded now. Verified 2026-09-22 after passing the site's proof-of-work gate: film pages and the Solr metadata index are public, but every file request through MCRFileNodeServlet returns HTTP 403 without login, including files on records that carry a 'Public Domain from 2017-12-05' date. Films 606 and 612–615 are in state 'new' with worldReadableComplete false. The archive directs enquiries to Prof. Martin S. Fischer ([e-mail withheld]); the papers say only that raw data 'will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation' — a promise, not a release.
new_confirmed.what: Four living German Shepherds filmed on a treadmill with a custom biplanar C-arm fluoroscope (Siemens Neurostar base, 400 mm image intensifiers, Weinberger Visario, planes at 63 degrees, 100 kV, 500 fps, SID 520–750 mm), with per-frame 6-DoF poses for pelvis, sacrum, L6 and L7 from scientific rotoscoping against a same-dog helical CT (Philips Brilliance 16, 1 mm). Undistortion-grid and steel-sphere calibration-cube films are archived with the recordings, so the projection geometry is recoverable. Companion studies with the same rig cover the craniocervical junction (Chihuahuas/Labradors 10.3389/fvets.2021.709967; Cavalier King Charles Spaniels PLOS ONE 2023) with head, spine and pelvis CT.
new_confirmed.serves: NEED A (real biplanar fluoroscopy with same-subject CT, solved pose and archived calibration), animal.
new_confirmed.licence: Articles CC BY; no licence stated for the data, and the archive files are gated.
new_confirmed.caveats: Dogs, not humans — seven lumbar vertebrae, different lumbosacral geometry. What is openly downloadable today is only CC BY supplementary video: the lumbosacral paper's 39.3 MB supplement (Video 3 is a real single-view lumbar/pelvic fluoroscopy clip at 640x426, 25 fps, 76 s, downsampled H.264; Videos 1 and 4 are rotoscoped bone-model overlays; Video 2 is the room camera), eight MP4s from the 709967 companion, a 61 MB zip of 10 MP4s from the PLOS ONE S1 File, and eight transcoded HLS preview streams on subproject 167 (1080x720, 25 fps, ~17.6 s, single view). None of those contains CT, poses or calibration images, and all are transcoded, so they are useless for image-formation work. The archive also holds beagle and dachshund films and one canine cadaver lumbar/thoracic mobility film (szeb_film_00000024) with calibration-body films, but no CT for those.

updates_to_known.name: C-ArmLSpine
updates_to_known.update: Full read of the release (see carmlspine_expectations for the item-by-item picture). Headline new facts: the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.22768651 (concept 22768650, single version, CC BY 4.0, creator Feng Qianjin, published 2026-09-17) holds ONE file, C-ArmLSpine.zip, 15,581,614,253 bytes, md5 6bccd47979a2a1c9b200dc427fefeb54; 60,058 entries, 23.35 GB uncompressed, 149 case folders, and NO README, CSV, JSON, mask, landmark, pose, split or NIfTI file anywhere — DICOM only. The device is a FIRST Imaging (Jiangsu First-Imaging / 一影医疗, Nantong + Shanghai) Surgio-B51; NMPA 国械注准20233060458 lists model Surgio-B51s, Class III, approved 2023-04-06; a 2025 tender names a Surgio-B51-MC. The only published user is PRSCS-Net (Zhang W, Zhao L, Gou H, Gong Y, Zhou Y, Feng Q; Med Image Anal 2024;97:103283; PMID 39094463), which is closed access and could not be retrieved from three routes (ScienceDirect captcha from this machine, a grid compute node and a reader proxy), so its ground-truth pose method, split and results on this data remain unread. The GitHub repo ZWC-SMU/C-ArmLSpine (created 2026-09-15) holds only a README in 10 commits, no code and no licence file; its download link points at the owner's /uploads/ edit URL. 'DAF-Reg', named in the README as a user, has no published record. Third-party numbers exist: LayersReg (arXiv 2606.26647) re-implemented PRSCS-Net as a baseline on DeepFluoro/Ljubljana and reports MAE(R) 1.35 deg and Dist(T) 1.93 mm — not PRSCS-Net's own C-ArmLSpine results.

updates_to_known.name: DeepFluoro
updates_to_known.update: Two new open re-hosts. (1) xvr-data on Hugging Face (eigenvivek/xvr-data, 4.8 GB, 1,703 files, last modified 2026-08-10) ships DeepFluoro, the Balgrist Femur set and Ljubljana as standardized DICOM/NIfTI with ground-truth extrinsics/intrinsics, fiducials and per-frame segmentation .pt files, ready for DiffDRR/xvr; DiffDRR-Datasets is deprecated in its favour; overall licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 with the DeepFluoro portion keeping CC BY-NC 4.0. The xvr Nature 2026 data statement names only DeepFluoro, Femur and Ljubljana as public real X-ray data. (2) 2D3D-RegQuality (HF suemincho/2D3D-RegQuality, MIT, 10.57967/hf/6825, 2025-10-28) pairs DeepFluoro real X-rays with DRRs rendered at sampled perturbed poses plus a CSV of pose, mTRE and a binary registration-quality label (dataset_real.zip 11.7 GB, dataset_simulated.zip 21.7 GB) — a ready-made real-versus-DRR set with pose-error labels. Searcher pass only; no verifier verdict in this run.

updates_to_known.name: Ljubljana spine 2D-3D gold standard (2D-3D-GS, Tomazevic et al.)
updates_to_known.update: Current route and contents: the 2017 path contents/tools/GoldStandard/GSPublic/GSPublic.zip now 404s; the live file is https://lit.fe.uni-lj.si/data/research/resources/2D-3D-GS/2D-3D-GS.zip, 79,049,365 bytes, dated 2021-06-16. Contents are 18 float32 X-ray images, each with a .rad file giving detector pose and source position, plus CT and MR as PER-VERTEBRA L1–L5 crops only — there is no whole-specimen volume, so there is no surrounding soft tissue for DRR or scatter calibration. Licence conflict: the resource page says CC BY-NC-ND while the bundled user guide still requires a signed agreement; either way it is non-commercial, which matters for the product track. The LIT resource list holds no other spine 2D-3D set. (The zip and user guide already sit in the CTSpinoPelvic1K-1 working tree.) Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: Utrecht ISI 2D-3D registration gold standard (van de Kraats et al., IEEE TMI 2005)
updates_to_known.update: This lead is lost, not merely hard to find. The database page was live from 2006 to about 2012-06 and by 2013-08-08 read 'This database is no longer available'. The 51 MB download sat behind a one-day key and a no-redistribution agreement and was never captured in the Wayback Machine under any ISI, UMC Utrecht or Erasmus host. Documented contents: AP and lateral fluoroscopy of two cadaveric lumbar segments (3 and 5 vertebrae) with 3DRX, CT and MR of the same specimens, source/detector/volume poses in one world frame, per-vertebra 2D and 3D masks for 8 vertebrae, and 200 start positions; formats .raw/.sta volumes and .raw/.rad projections. Last documented users were Birkfellner and Spoerk (Vienna, 2009–2012). The only route is a private copy from van Walsum or Niessen (Erasmus MC), Penney (KCL), Tomazevic (Ljubljana) or the Vienna licensees. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: Balgrist ex-vivo lumbar CT + multi-device C-arm (Jecklin et al., Sci Rep 2025)
updates_to_known.update: The promised public test subset does not exist. The Sci Rep data statement says the paired set is withheld 'due to restrictions relating to pending patent applications' and is available from the corresponding author on reasonable request, and points to github.com/MrMonk3y/IXGS for 'a small dataset for testing derived from the ex-vivo data'; as of 2026-09-21 that README says 'Under Construction', the last push was 2025-04-25 and there is no data. The underlying set is 6 ex-vivo human specimens with at least 50 X-rays each on a Siemens Cios Spin, CT on a SOMATOM Edge Plus. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: SheepSpineX
updates_to_known.update: Device and counts recovered from X2P-Net (Bioengineering 2026;13(2):178, PMC12938846): a Siemens Arcadis Varic image-intensifier C-arm, 9 sheep cervical spines (4–7 vertebrae each) from a slaughterhouse, 30 AP/LAT pairs per spine, with annotated 3D vertebral locations. Data statement: 'further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding authors'. The companion BiSpineX set is synthetic DRRs. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: Goswami 2020 IOERT pig lower limb
updates_to_known.update: Correction to the known entry, which lists this as Elekta kV. The DataCite record for 10.21227/gxpd-d998 describes 7 C-arm projections at different poses of a pig lower-limb specimen, geometrically calibrated with fiducials on the applicator, plus its CT, CC BY 4.0 on IEEE DataPort. The C-arm model is not stated in the record. Limb anatomy — useful only for device/geometry calibration. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: TCIA CT Colonography localizers (the known localizer route)
updates_to_known.update: The localizer route is much wider than CT Colonography (530) and COVID-19-NY-SBU (345). A strict NBIA pass (localizer series of 6 images or fewer plus a diagnostic CT of more than 20 images in the same study) found about 1,148 further patients across 29 collections — largest TCGA-KIRC 164, CMB-LCA 102, TCGA-BLCA 99, TCGA-OV 97, CPTAC-UCEC 73, TCGA-LIHC 71, CMB-MML 66, TCGA-UCEC 56, CMB-CRC 53, CPTAC-CCRCC 46, TCGA-STAD 45; a looser description match gives 2,697 patients in 55 collections. Scanners span about 15 models and 5 vendors, and the geometry is recoverable from DICOM. None in Spine-Mets-CT-SEG, Spinal-Multiple-Myeloma-SEG, Pelvic-Reference-Data, Pancreas-CT or KiTS. Caveats: localizer physics (line-scan fan beam, heavy post-processing) is unlike a C-arm, the counts rest on a SeriesDescription heuristic with no body-part check, many scouts are chest or head only, and same-session pairing is unverified. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: TCIA diagnostic radiographs with same-patient CT (small overlaps)
updates_to_known.update: Two independent sweeps narrowed this. An IDC v24 sweep (idc-index 0.12.5) found only 15 collections with patients holding both CT and RF/XA/DX/CR, and no RTIMAGE at all. The only non-chest pairs not already known: TCGA-CW-6088 (2 CT-urogram exams, 4 Fuji CR films) and TCGA-D1-A2G5 (3 CR) have genuine AP pelvis films in the SAME session as a 1 mm abdominopelvic CT covering L3–L5, sacrum and pelvis; CMB-LCA MSB-09794 has an upright lateral thoracic-spine film with a CT 29 days later — 8 films across 3 patients, CC BY 3.0. The NBIA sweep adds VAREPOP-APOLLO (AP-7CQ6: portable abdomen AP on a Carestream DRX-Revolution one day before an abdomen/pelvis CT, plus 11 barium fluoroscopy series), COVID-19-AR, TCGA-BLCA (7–10 patients with abdominal DX/CR + CT), one TCGA-KIRC urogram and one CMB-PCA cystourethrogram; LIDC-IDRI's 290 radiograph patients are chest only. Both sweeps agree there is no hidden large film-plus-CT torso cohort in TCIA beyond CMB-MML and the localizers. Patient counts differed between passes. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: FluoroSAM Loop-X full-torso cadaver (JHU)
updates_to_known.update: Spine-DART (Íñigo, Killeen, Uneri, Khan, Unberath; Front Robot AI 2026;10.3389/frobt.2026.1759366, PMC12980022, arXiv 2512.05803) reports one cadaver on a medPhoton Loop-X with a CT and 35 fluoroscopic images at varied orientations (biplane pairs) carrying 'accurate projection matrices' from the device, 16 vertebrae collected and 12 reconstructed, TotalSegmentator ground truth with manual refinement, and 32 clinician-graded real X-ray paths. Its data statement — 'will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation' — is an explicit request route the known FluoroSAM entry lacked. It may be the same specimen; confirm when requesting. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: UCLA ExacTrac kV setup radiographs + planning CT (Charters 2024, 254 patients)
updates_to_known.update: A larger predecessor exists in the same lineage: Petragallo, Lamb et al., Med Phys 2023 (10.1002/mp.16359) used stereoscopic ExacTrac kV setup X-rays with planning CT for 429 spine radiotherapy patients over 1,592 fractions from six or more institutions (UCLA, UCSF, Beth Israel Lahey, UAMS, UT Health San Antonio, Piedmont, Kaiser) with a Brainlab co-author, including simulated off-by-one-vertebra shifts. The data statement could not be read (Wiley 403) and no deposit was found. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: Osaka/NAIST hip radiographs + CT/QCT cohort (Otake, Sato, Gu)
updates_to_known.update: A new device in the same lineage: MICCAI 2025 paper 5182 (Suehara, Gu, Otake, Uemura, Sato) reports 77 real EOS biplanar pelvis/hip radiographs each 2D-3D registered to the same patient's CT, before and after total hip arthroplasty — the only real slot-scanner-to-CT pairing found. The paper's dataset link reads N/A, so it is a collaboration lead. The parent cohort (Sci Rep 2023 10.1038/s41598-023-35075-x, 475 patients; MedIA 2023 10.1016/j.media.2023.102970, 305 with QCT, standing/supine/abduction/adduction poses) remains available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: Hohai/Changzhou lumbar intraoperative X-ray + CT (LineReg, Shen et al.)
updates_to_known.update: A third paper in the lineage: FlowReg, 'universal spinal CT/X-ray registration' (Shen, Nong, Zhou), accepted at MICCAI 2026 with the Changzhou clinical partner Luming Nong as co-author. The repo github.com/shenao1995/FlowReg was created 2026-06-17 and holds only a README; the sibling lineReg README still lists 'Dual-view registration on Real X-rays' as not done. Neither repo has data or a data link, and that FlowReg uses real X-rays is inferred from the lineage, not seen. LineReg itself (Med Phys 2026, 10.1002/mp.70385, PMID 41833531) reports 10 patients, 90 real registration samples and 710 edge-annotated images; the article is closed and the data statement was not read. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: MrOS (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men)
updates_to_known.update: Access facts that change the plan. Images are NOT on MrOS Online, which serves derived data only; image requests go through a Publications Committee analysis plan plus a DUA, possibly with an ancillary-study proposal (Publication Guidelines v5.9, 2025-07-25). The route works — a UW group received 10,351 annotated lateral spine radiographs covering 67,215 vertebral bodies from the Coordinating Center under a DUA. The NIA AgingResearchBiobank holds no MrOS images. As of 2026-09-21 all MrOS Online accounts are disabled pending NIH identity-verified re-registration with an institutional email. Protocol: films and QCT are from the same baseline visit for about 3,600–3,786 men, film SID fixed at 1016 mm; but the CT is three limited slabs (T12/L1–L2 at 1 mm, mid-L3 to mid-L5 at 5 mm, hip at 3 mm), so the sacrum, SI joints and L5–S1 junction are in NO CT series, and the CT is supine so each vertebra must be registered separately. NIA terms say 'not available for commercial use'. Searcher pass only.

updates_to_known.name: CTSpine1K / SMU registration lineage (context for C-ArmLSpine)
updates_to_known.update: Earlier 3D/2D spine registration work from the same Southern Medical University group evaluated only on CTSpine1K — SGReg (Mi, Yin, Zhao, Chen, Zhou, Feng; Phys Med Biol 2023, 10.1088/1361-6560/acd29d) and an orthogonal-view reconstruction method (Mi, Zhou, Feng; Nan Fang Yi Ke Da Xue Xue Bao 2023;43(9):1636-1643, PMC10563102). No paper other than PRSCS-Net was found that uses C-ArmLSpine; of the 9 works citing PRSCS-Net, none does. First author Wencong Zhang's SMU master's thesis ('基于深度学习的3D/2D配准方法研究', mid-term review 2024-04-29) probably documents the in-house collection, but no online copy was found.

refuted_or_useless.name: HKU MedIP cbct_projection (hku-mip/cbct_projection, 4 records)
refuted_or_useless.why: Synthetic, not acquired. Each npz stores separate primary, primary_mc and scatter channels, and the same TCIA patients recur under all three vendor geometries (XVI, TrueBeam, IBA), so these are Monte Carlo projections rendered from TCIA CTs. The per-geometry scatter could still serve as a scatter-model prior (MIT, 10.57967/hf/9369).

refuted_or_useless.name: CBCT-IQ (Siemens ARTIS pheno thorax/pelvis phantom CBCT)
refuted_or_useless.why: Reconstructed volumes and reader-scored slices only; no 2-D projections released, so nothing to calibrate an image-formation model against.

refuted_or_useless.name: Xia et al. 2018 thorax X-ray + CT interventional set (Zenodo 1400558)
refuted_or_useless.why: Ex-vivo pig LUNG model only — no spine and no torso skeleton.

refuted_or_useless.name: MIQR-CC ERCP fluoroscopy (19,018 Ziehm/Philips frames, figshare 31079236)
refuted_or_useless.why: No CT and no spine labels (biliary diagnoses only). At most an unlabelled source of real torso C-arm fluoroscopy for domain adaptation or detector false-positive checks.

refuted_or_useless.name: Bournemouth/AECC quantitative fluoroscopy frames (OSF z2jby)
refuted_or_useless.why: Diagnostic weight-bearing lumbar fluoroscopy at 224 px with no CT, and no label files in the zip central directory — fails both needs. The passes also disagreed on size (45,968 frames in 139 folders vs ~58 or 89 subjects vs 28,894 frames). Possible unlabelled real-domain source only.

refuted_or_useless.name: Orthopedic screw images (HF austin-carnahan/orthopedic-screw-images)
refuted_or_useless.why: Post-operative diagnostic lumbar radiographs with screw masks — not intraoperative or interventional fluoroscopy, and no CT.

refuted_or_useless.name: MFHI Multi-modal Femoral Head Imaging (IEEE DataPort 10.21227/71rx-wh92)
refuted_or_useless.why: Cropped 512x512 femoral-head patches from diagnostic films, CT reduced to 20 coronal slices, and only 10 of 209 patients uploaded. No usable CT volume, no pelvic field, not fluoroscopy — the extremity exception does not apply.

refuted_or_useless.name: Yaniv C-arm CBCT fiducial phantoms (Zenodo 4445444)
refuted_or_useless.why: Non-anatomical fiducial phantoms; geometry calibration only, no anatomy to render or name.

refuted_or_useless.name: LDCT-and-Projection-data (Mayo, TCIA)
refuted_or_useless.why: Helical diagnostic CT raw projections (narrow-row fan beam), not 2-D radiographs or C-arm frames. At most a spectrum and attenuation reference.

refuted_or_useless.name: TVGH-SpineXR (IEEE DataPort 10.21227/x6bb-7r75)
refuted_or_useless.why: Diagnostic full-spine radiographs with no CT and no fluoroscopy, so neither need applies. Worth reconsidering separately for radiograph level-ID: it carries T1–L5 per-vertebra level labels, masks and endplates, the same kind as the known BUU/VinDr sets.

refuted_or_useless.name: BMTVG / SpineAlign (Imperial College / Humanitas)
refuted_or_useless.why: No X-ray frames released at all — only RGB-D video, CT-derived vertebra meshes and CAD files.

refuted_or_useless.name: XMAPortal UNLV10 / BROWN100 Canine Hip Cadaver
refuted_or_useless.why: Meets neither need: no CT or 3D volume listed, files gated (metadata only), not intraoperative. The existence of a bead or CT model is a guess.

refuted_or_useless.name: Ferret mating biplanar X-ray videos (Zenodo 14176276)
refuted_or_useless.why: No CT, no calibration, no labels, not intraoperative.

refuted_or_useless.name: Vienna porcine cadaver head 2D/3D gold standard (Pawiro et al. 2011)

refuted_or_useless.why: Title-only lead, recorded as not real X-ray (likely DRR-trained), anatomy unstated, no data link. Recheck when the MICCAI 2026 paper pages stop returning 401.

refuted_or_useless.why: Ex-vivo motion study, so not intraoperative (fails B), and no CT (fails A).

refuted_or_useless.why: Title only: real X-ray unverified, target likely thoraco-abdominal soft tissue, and it adds no release, count or access fact to the known CT2X-IRA entry (which itself remains paywalled and unverified).

refuted_or_useless.name: SOF (Study of Osteoporotic Fractures)
refuted_or_useless.why: No CT or QCT at any visit and no intraoperative labels — meets neither need.

refuted_or_useless.name: Health ABC lateral CT scout with single axial slices
refuted_or_useless.why: No volume CT (one 10 mm slice at L4–L5) and no spine or pelvis radiographs, so no 2D/3D pairing is possible.

refuted_or_useless.name: FORMEN (Fujiwara-kyo Osteoporosis Risk in Men)
refuted_or_useless.why: DXA and SXA only — no CT, no radiographs, not public.

refuted_or_useless.name: Utah Hive Cam-FAIS dual-fluoroscopy release (10.7278/S5d-btv7-ztpw) and the companion standing-APT record (10.7278/S5d-6yyb-3qjg)
refuted_or_useless.why: As released these hold ZERO X-ray images. Both packages ship CT (or synthetic CT), meshes, landmarks and per-frame or static 6-DoF pelvis/femur transforms, and both READMEs state the biplane frames and calibration are not included. They remain request leads to Anderson/Atkins (Utah), not usable datasets.

refuted_or_useless.name: UMN biplane radiographic spine osteokinematics validation (hdl 11299/211384)

refuted_or_useless.why: Only GIFs and code are public; the projections and planning CT are not released. A direct request is plausible given the same institute released SPARK and CHIRP openly, but there is no route today.
