refuted_or_useless.why: Only the analysis code is released (BSD-3-Clause, Zenodo 21516903). The 8,717 triggered kV images from 49 patients are 'subject to institutional and regulatory restrictions'; the only path is a collaboration request to P. Retif.

refuted_or_useless.name: AI Hub (Korea) datasets 610 and 611
refuted_or_useless.why: Not obtainable by this project as constituted: applications are restricted to Korean nationals and analysis happens inside an online secure zone with no download. 610 also has no CT and does not state whether vertebral levels are labelled; 611 has no C-arm data and no pose. A Korean collaborator would be required.

refuted_or_useless.name: Pure duplicate merges (SpineSAC x2, RabbitCT x6, Zhao pelvis phantom x4, SPARK x2, MATCH x2, Lungman x2, CMB-MML x3, TCIA localizers x2, TCIA film+CT overlaps x3, NIT Warangal x5, LineReg x3, Spine-DART x4, UC Davis x2, MINTOS x2, Manipal x2, SX-Stitch x2, Southeast Univ x2, SJTU biplanar x3, PLA pelvic x3, Osaka/NAIST x2, C-ArmLSpine x5, xvr-data x2, 2D3D-RegQuality x4, Balgrist Femur x3, ScienceDB head phantom x4, Utah Hive x4)
refuted_or_useless.why: Not refutations — these were the same records surfaced under different titles by different passes and were merged with their evidence URLs unioned. Recorded here only so the candidate count is not double-read. Where merged passes disagreed (SpineSAC vendor split, NIT Warangal 9 patients/51 sets vs 2 patients/13 projections, SJTU 64 vs 50 subjects, Osaka 475 vs 305) both readings were kept rather than one chosen.

carmlspine_expectations.item: One download: C-ArmLSpine.zip, 15,581,614,253 bytes (15.58 GB), md5 6bccd47979a2a1c9b200dc427fefeb54, CC BY 4.0, single version (no v2 yet), sole creator Feng Qianjin. The record's only related identifier is a citation to PRSCS-Net.

Inside: ZIP64, 60,058 entries, 23,347,039,978 bytes uncompressed. One top-level folder C-ArmLSpine/ holding case1 … case149 — no zero padding, no gaps. 58,911 entries end in .dcm, 698 are extensionless DICOM, 449 are directories.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Range-read of the zip central directory (https://zenodo.org/api/records/22768651/files/C-ArmLSpine.zip/content)

carmlspine_expectations.item: Expect NO annotations of any kind. There is no README, CSV, JSON, label, mask, landmark, pose, geometry, split or NIfTI file anywhere in the archive — DICOM only. The Zenodo description is the entire documentation and says nothing about IRB, consent, patients vs cadavers, surgery type, levels, labels, pose, splits or geometry.

Layout for 147 of 149 cases: caseN/C-arm/ with 2 DICOM X-ray frames, and caseN/CBCT/ with exactly 394 axial slices. 109 cases use numeric names (C-arm/0001.dcm, 0002.dcm; CBCT/0000.dcm–0393.dcm); the rest use long DCMTK-style UID filenames.

Two cases break the layout and will break a naive loader. case39: three C-arm frames (AP at 0.0 deg plus TWO laterals at 90.0 deg) and 696 files in CBCT/ (394 slices + 301 raw projections + one 698-byte stub). case134: no C-arm/ folder at all — its AP (0.0 deg) and lateral (90.0 deg) 2048x2048 frames sit INSIDE CBCT/ as extensionless XA.* files beside 394 CT.* slices, with an extra ori/ folder holding 301 raw projections. case134 does have both frames; an earlier project note saying otherwise is wrong.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Zip central directory + per-file header reads

carmlspine_expectations.item: Totals to expect: 299 AP/lateral frames, 58,706 CBCT slices (149 x 394) and 602 raw projection frames (2 x 301).

The 2-D frames are DICOM X-Ray Angiographic Image Storage (1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.12.1), Modality XA, ImageType ORIGINAL/PRIMARY/SINGLE PLANE, SeriesDescription 'DR', one frame each, 2048x2048, 16-bit unsigned, MONOCHROME2, explicit VR little endian, uncompressed, rescale slope 1 / intercept 0. Manufacturer 一影医疗 (FIRST Imaging), model Surgio-B51, station YiYing_3DCarm, software OR01-00.012.001 (November) or .002 (December). ApplicationName is '单帧摄影' (single-shot) on 294 frames and '连续摄影' on 3.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Per-file header survey of all 297 C-arm/ frames

carmlspine_expectations.item: Geometry is identical on every frame: DistanceSourceToDetector 1140 mm, DistanceSourceToPatient 745 mm, so nominal isocentre magnification is 1.530. PixelSpacing reads 1.0 x 1.0 mm — a placeholder that is physically impossible (2048 mm) — and ImagerPixelSpacing is absent. Private (0029,0033) reads '30cm'. Do not use the DICOM pixel spacing for geometry.

The detector is almost certainly an iRay Jupi 1212X, inferred from the reconstruction-config path in private tag (0037,0014) of every raw projection: 'C:/FICBCT/IRayJupi1212X/FICBCT_3DC_110kv_300_FDK_noSC_AutoMAR_fR002.000.xml'. That panel is 12x12 inch IGZO/CsI, 2048x2048 at 150 um, 16-bit. On that basis the true pixel is about 0.150 mm at the detector and 0.098 mm at the 745 mm source distance for the 2048-square frames, and about 0.300 / 0.196 mm for the 2x2-binned 1024-square projections. The 2048 x 0.150 = 307.2 mm panel back-projected to isocentre gives about 201 mm, which matches the 197 mm CBCT cube — a consistency check that supports the inference.

View is identified by PositionerPrimaryAngle, not by filename order. AP frames read 0.0 deg (129), 0.1 (16), 0.2, 0.9 or -0.1; laterals read 90.0 (137) or 89.9 (11); PositionerSecondaryAngle spans -0.6 to 0.9. In case39 and case118 the first file is NOT the AP frame. One case is not an AP/lateral pair at all: case118 pairs its AP with an OBLIQUE frame at -58.1 deg.

Exposure: kVp 73–99, with AP median about 73–75 (73–86) and lateral median about 87–88 (80–99); tube current 23–29 mA; AveragePulseWidth 28–114 ms. ExposureTime is a constant 10 in every frame while ExposureTimeInms reads 1834–1942, so the ExposureTime tag is meaningless. AEC is implied by the spread.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Per-file header survey (218–297 frames parsed across two passes)

carmlspine_expectations.item: The 2-D frames are PROCESSED display images, not raw or log-linear data: visible edge-enhancement halos at cortical margins, air and bowel gas bright (MONOCHROME2), and per-image value ranges that vary wildly (case1 AP 625–4848 vs its lateral 443–62,432). PixelIntensityRelationship is present but empty, and Smallest/LargestImagePixelValue are sometimes inconsistent with the pixels. No unprocessed version of the 2-D frames is in the release.

Every CBCT is exactly 394 x 394 x 394 at 0.5 mm isotropic — a 197 mm cube centred on (0,0,0), ImagePositionPatient running (-98.25,-98.25,-98.25) to (-98.25,-98.25,+98.25), axial orientation [1,0,0,0,1,0], PatientPosition FFS, 16-bit unsigned with RescaleIntercept -1024 and slope 1 (HU-like, air near -1000), default window 300/2000, ImageType DERIVED/PRIMARY/AXIAL/3DSLICE, manufacturer 'yiying Imaging', station YIYING-CBCT. The CBCT KVP tag is 0 or garbage (e.g. 1371883213) and must be ignored.
carmlspine_expectations.source: First and last slice headers of all 149 CBCTs

carmlspine_expectations.item: Standard DICOM grouping will not work. Every file — including each individual slice of one CBCT — carries its own random-UUID StudyInstanceUID and SeriesInstanceUID, and no file has a FrameOfReferenceUID. Only the case folder links a frame pair to its CBCT, and slices must be stacked by ImagePositionPatient or InstanceNumber, never by series.

Raw CBCT sweeps exist for two cases only (case39 and case134): 301 frames each, 1024x1024 uint16 XA, 111 kVp, 12–13 mA, pulse width 15–23 ms, same SDD 1140 / SOD 745. PositionerPrimaryAngle runs +122.0 deg to -51.5 (case134) or -54.3 (case39), a 173.5–176.3 deg short scan in about 29 s (~10 frames/s), and the angle tag updates only about every 5 frames (58 distinct values, mean step 0.59 deg). Each sweep ships a 698/788-byte companion object whose (0037,0101) says 'rebuild Template ZIP FILE' with an EMPTY payload — no reconstruction template is actually included.

Each raw projection secretly carries a second image: private tag (0037,0020), an OW of 2,097,152 bytes, holds another 1024x1024 uint16 frame that looks near-raw and linear — body 300–1300, air 13,000–14,000, visible uncorrected half-row line defects, rotated 180 deg relative to the main image. The stored main pixels follow main ≈ 2373·ln(raw) − 7817 (R² 0.86), i.e. log-compressed and spatially processed. Whether the private frame is offset- or gain-corrected is unknown.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Pixel extraction and regression on case134/ori projections

carmlspine_expectations.item: Anatomy is lumbar and lumbosacral only, with no thoracic coverage above T12. From the project's own automated TotalSegmentator + SPINEPS labelling of the CBCTs (the release ships no labels): 137 of 149 CBCTs include the sacrum; the top level is L1 in 104 cases, L2 in 35, T12 in 3 and L3 in 1, with 4 cases showing sacrum only; the commonest sets are L1–L5+S (93) and L2–L5+S (34). Labellers agreed on 814 of 910 vertebrae, with 22 variant cases (e.g. case136 read as L2–L6). No femoral head in 31 of 31 CBCTs checked.

Expect clothed, apparently living subjects with NO spinal instrumentation. Contact sheets and an AP pose grid over 72 cases show varied bowel gas and distinct anatomy per case, no pedicle screws, rods, retractors or cages, and occasional small external metal consistent with clothing fasteners or skin markers (case17, case77, case78, case93). 18 of 149 CBCTs have voxels above 3000 HU and 24 have more than 1000 voxels above 2000 HU. This is a visual reading, not a stated fact.

The timing does not match the 'routine intraoperative imaging' description. All 149 cases fall on five days — 2023-11-11 (case134), 11-12 (case39), 11-18 (38 cases, 09:38–16:29), 12-11 (66 cases, 09:20–17:54), 12-12 (43 cases, 09:39–16:21) — with consecutive cases starting a median 3.4–4.2 minutes apart (minimum about 2 minutes). Within a case, AP comes first, the lateral about 20–30 s later, and the CBCT 81–415 s (median 99 s) after the first frame. UID timestamps agree with the header times, so the clock was not shifted. Separate surgeries every four minutes are not plausible; this reads as a consecutive imaging session over many subjects, for a reason the release does not give.
carmlspine_expectations.source: Per-file header survey of all 149 cases

carmlspine_expectations.item: Demographics and site tags are placeholders — do not use them. PatientSize is 1.80 and PatientWeight 0 in every frame; PatientBirthDate equals the study date on frames and is 20200101 on CBCT slices; there is no PatientAge; PatientSex reads F 83, M 62, non-standard 'W' 3 and 'O' 1, and all 38 cases of 2023-11-18 are M. PatientName is caseN, PatientIdentityRemoved YES, DeidentificationMethod 'Basic Application Confidentiality Profile'. InstitutionName is 'SMU' everywhere; InstitutionAddress is '江苏南通' on the XA frames and 'Pudong, SH' on the CT slices — both matching the manufacturer's own Nantong and Shanghai sites, so they are probably vendor or de-identifier defaults, not the acquisition site. One residual identifier survives: the raw sweep in case134/ori keeps PatientID '1895112604_20231111.151002.079', and that prefix recurs across days in private (0029,0016), so it is most likely a device key plus timestamp.

The files were rewritten during de-identification, in two different toolchains: most by DCMTK 3.6.1 (explicit VR), 39 cases by another writer in implicit VR (ImplementationClassUID 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.2.135.1066.101, '1.5.0/WIN32'). Study and Series UIDs were replaced with UUID strings that are not valid DICOM UI values, which some parsers will reject. The raw case134 projections keep the device-side writer OFFIS_DCMTK_365 and source AE 'CarmAETitle'.

You will have to derive pose yourself, and the header geometry nearly does it. Rendering a DRR of the CBCT at the header geometry (beam along the CBCT y axis for AP and x for lateral, SOD 745, SID 1140, centred on the origin) matched real AP frames with 3.6/-1.2 mm (case1) and 3.6/-2.4 mm (case50) residual detector shifts; a 6-case refinement moved 1–3 mm in plane, +7–18 mm in depth and 1–5 deg in rotation. The device's image-axis convention (rot180, mirror) had to be found by hypothesis search, not read from a header. Accuracy is limited by patient motion in the roughly 1.5 minutes between the frames and the CBCT.

Dose tags are misused but decodable: DoseValue (3004,0012) and 'DoseUnits' (3004,0002) both hold numbers whose ratio is a constant 245.2 (range 244.8–245.4, n=220) — exactly (30.0 cm x 595/1140)^2 cm^2 for the IEC reference point at 745-150 mm. So DoseValue is probably reference-point air kerma (mGy) and the units field is probably DAP (mGy·cm²) for an open 30 cm field. Radiographs read a median 0.13 (0.029–4); the CBCT sweeps read 8.61 (case134) and 10.86 (case39).

The code side is empty. GitHub ZWC-SMU/C-ArmLSpine (created 2026-09-15, 10 commits to 2026-09-19) holds only README.md — no code, no loaders, no licence file, and one release tag with no assets. The README repeats the Zenodo text, links the owner's edit URL (zenodo.org/uploads/22768651) rather than the public record, asks for a PRSCS-Net citation, names an unpublished 'DAF-Reg' as a second user, and its first draft carried a copy-paste line, 'f you find KGFT useful'. The account's only other repo is KGFT, unrelated. No PRSCS-Net or DAF-Reg code exists publicly, so no author loader, geometry parameter or pose convention can be read from anywhere.

Lineage of the device is solid even though the specs are not: FIRST is Jiangsu First-Imaging Medical Equipment Co. (一影医疗), Haimen/Nantong manufacturing with Shanghai R&D; NMPA 国械注准20233060458 covers 'Surgio-B51s', Class III, approved 2023-04-06 to 2028-04-05, for intraoperative fluoroscopy, radiography and 3-D tomography; hospital tenders in 2024 list it as Surgio-B51 at 2.4–2.8 M CNY. A company-co-authored paper (PDS-MAR, Phys Med Biol 2023, 10.1088/1361-6560/ad00fc) names the 'B51s' explicitly for sheep-back K-wire projections. No FDA 510(k) and no CE/MDR record was found — the device appears to be China-market only.

carmlspine_unknowns: How PRSCS-Net obtained ground-truth pose on C-ArmLSpine — device geometry, manual alignment, intensity registration or fiducials — is unread, because the full text is behind a ScienceDirect captcha that defeated three routes (this machine, a Wayne State grid compute node, a reader proxy) and no repository or Wayback copy exists. The header geometry nearly aligns frames to CBCT (residuals about 1–4 mm in plane and 7–18 mm in depth in a 6-case pilot), which SUGGESTS but does not prove a geometry-derived reference.

PRSCS-Net's own C-ArmLSpine numbers (mTRE, success rate, rotation and translation error), how many of the 149 cases it used, its train/validation/test split, whether the set was test-only or fine-tuned on, its preprocessing (resampling, cropping, intensity conversion, DRR settings) and the SDD and pixel size it assumed. Its failure definition and its CTSpine1K results are likewise unknown.

Whether the subjects are living patients, volunteers or cadavers; whether any surgery took place at all; and what indication or procedure applies. The release says 'routine intraoperative imaging procedures', but 148 cases arrive roughly four minutes apart on a handful of days and the images show no instrumentation and some apparent clothing metal.

IRB or ethics approval, consent, and the collecting hospital or site are stated nowhere — not on Zenodo, not on GitHub, not in the abstract. 'SMU' and the Nantong / Pudong address tags are most likely de-identifier and vendor defaults. Whether one Surgio-B51 unit or several produced the data is also unknown (the recurring private key suggests one).

How many DISTINCT patients the 149 cases represent. A per-case TotalSegmentator L2–L4 volume/extent fingerprint over the 116 cases whose L2–L4 are not cut by the field edge found no near-identical pair (closest pair 1.1% apart against a 2.1% first percentile), which fits mostly distinct subjects but is weak evidence given segmentation noise.

The exact detector-to-image orientation convention (how stored frames are rotated or mirrored relative to the C-arm), the C-arm axis to CBCT DICOM axis mapping, and the isocentre location beyond 'the CBCT cube is centred on (0,0,0)'. These were recovered by hypothesis search in this project, not documented by the authors, and no projection matrices or geometric calibration are in the release.

Which source-to-isocentre distance is right: the DICOM says 745 mm on every frame, while the company-co-authored PDS-MAR simulation uses DSO 617 mm with the same DSD 1140 mm. Whether the SID is genuinely fixed at 1140 mm is unconfirmed.

Confirmation of the detector identity. iRay Jupi 1212X is inferred from a reconstruction-config file path, never stated by the manufacturer. Whether the 2048-square frames are native 1x1 readout or resampled, and whether the 1024-square projections are 2x2 binned, are both unconfirmed.

The 2-D processing chain — log transform, LUT, dynamic-range compression, edge enhancement — is undocumented, PixelIntensityRelationship is blank, and no unprocessed version of the 2-D radiographs ships. Whether the private (0037,0020) raw CBCT frame is offset- or gain-corrected is also unknown.

The meaning of the private tags: (0029,0016/0020/0028/0029/0033/0050/0051/0052/0053/0063 'LIH'/'LSH'), (0035,0012), (0037,0011)=0.69, (0037,0020), and the CT-slice ExposureTime=130. The dose fields' units are inferred from a constant ratio, not stated.
Whether a physical anti-scatter grid is fitted, and its ratio. The marketing names only a 'virtual grid' (虚拟滤线栅) and the reconstruction config says noSC (no scatter correction).

The recorded sweep is 173.5–176.3 degrees against a nominal 180 with 300 views, the angle tag updates only about every 5 frames, and nothing states whether the 3-D orbit is orbital or propeller, or whether the B51 is isocentric or uses the company's patented 'variable-isocentre' non-isocentric design (patent CN112971814).

No public Surgio-B51 / B51s specification sheet exists: tube power, kV and mA ranges, focal spot, heat capacity, filtration, collimator, AEC behaviour and fluoroscopy frame rates are all unpublished, and the company removed product specifications from its website after a 2025 regulator notice. Do not carry over the older 'Taishan' CMOS 8 kW figures — different product. No MTF, NPS, DQE, CNR, CTDI, low-contrast or geometric-accuracy measurement for this unit was found anywhere.
Which hardware revision produced the 2023 data, given three model strings in circulation: Surgio-B51 (DICOM and tenders), Surgio-B51s (NMPA certificate) and Surgio-B51-MC (a 2025 contract).
The DAF-Reg paper named in the README — venue, status and whether it uses C-ArmLSpine with a different protocol — has no published record in web, Semantic Scholar or arXiv searches.

Wencong Zhang's SMU master's thesis ('基于深度学习的3D/2D配准方法研究', mid-term review 2024-04-29) probably documents the collection and the ground-truth procedure, but no online copy (CNKI or otherwise) was located.
Whether a v2 of the Zenodo record will add labels, poses or splits. The record was four days old when read, and the GitHub repo was still being edited.

Full texts of the other First-Imaging-affiliated papers (HIDE-Net, Lag-Net, FDA-Recon, MAE-Recon) were not accessed, so whether any of them describes this same Surgio-B51 chain — and Lag-Net explicitly concerns an amorphous-silicon panel, not IGZO — is unestablished.

Process note, not a data unknown: an earlier pass sent the user's email address to the Unpaywall API as that service's required parameter. That should not have happened and is recorded here so it is not repeated.
final.coverage_note: Across two rounds and 344 queries the search covered: general data repositories by API (Zenodo, figshare, Dryad, DataCite and OpenAIRE DOI sweeps, IEEE DataPort, Hugging Face datasets, Science Data Bank, heidata Heidelberg, Kitware/Girder, OSF, university repositories at Sydney eScholarship, Utah Hive, UMN Conservancy, Penn and UCSF); the imaging archives (TCIA NBIA API across all public collections with a modality sweep for RF/XA/CR/DX plus a localizer/scout description sweep, and an independent NCI IDC v24 pass with idc-index that found only 15 collections holding both CT and a radiographic modality); code and model hosts (GitHub repo search, Hugging Face model and dataset cards); and the literature by API rather than by web search (Europe PMC, PubMed, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Unpaywall, arXiv), which is how most of the request-only clinical sets surfaced. Angles worked: intraoperative and interventional spine C-arm; radiotherapy kV, triggered-kV, ExacTrac, CyberKnife and CBCT projection archives; CT localizers and scanograms as cheap real projections; diagnostic radiograph-plus-CT overlaps; dynamic and biplane videofluoroscopy (clinical, veterinary and the XMAPortal/XROMM biomechanics portal, which round 1 had missed entirely); legacy lab-hosted 2D/3D gold standards recovered through the Wayback CDX API (Utrecht ISI, Ljubljana LIT); conference programmes (MICCAI 2025 and 2026, SPIE, IPCAI leads); epidemiological cohorts with same-subject films and CT (MrOS US and Hong Kong, Framingham MDCT, AGES-Reykjavik, SOF, Health ABC, FORMEN); phantom and cadaver device studies; and vendor and regulator sources for the C-ArmLSpine device (NMPA registration database, Chinese hospital tenders, iRay detector datasheets, openFDA). Two limits should be read with this. First, several angles were never worked: Gitee and Baidu-Pan-hosted Chinese releases, Google Dataset Search, the OpenAIRE graph beyond one probe, Code Ocean, authenticated GitHub code search, OpenReview venues (MIDL, NeurIPS D&B, ICLR), the IPCAI/SPIE/ISBI abstract books and MICCAI workshop proceedings, forensic post-mortem-CT-versus-antemortem-radiograph identification sets, EUDAMED, and non-spine interventional torso domains (EVAR, TACE, PCNL, ERCP) where a C-arm sees the lumbar spine and a CT exists — one Zenodo and one DataCite probe there returned nothing, so the yield looks low but is not established. Second, and more important for how this synthesis should be read: the verifier transcript that reached me was truncated, so of about 83 deduplicated candidates only four carry a visible verifier verdict (SpineSAC, TROG SPARK, RTK CLB/POPI, Giessen–Jena canine), and only those appear in new_confirmed. The remainder are neither confirmed nor refuted here; they rest on searcher-level evidence and need re-verification before use. The strongest of them, in rough order: FORCAST-EST (heidata 10.11588/data/GIWRQA, open CC BY 4.0, Siemens Artis DynaCT sweeps of a lumbar-spine phantom plus CBCT, with and without metal); NIT Warangal 2D-3D-sci-registration (public level-named L1–L5 centroids in both CT and X-ray, images on request); VerSeg-Net (per-level L1–S1 masks on real Philips UNIQ FD20 lumbar fluoroscopy, 50 patients, explicit sharing statement); TCIA CMB-MML/AML interventional spine XA with same-patient CT; the wider TCIA localizer route; SJTU/TAOiMAGE calibrated biplanar lumbar radiographs with registered CT; Spine-DART Loop-X cadaver; BG Klinik MINTOS three-detector cadaver lumbar series; the Osaka/NAIST hip cohort and its new EOS arm; RabbitCT's Zenodo re-release; and FAU Surgical-Device-Detection (38 real spine projections with implant masks and calibrated matrices).

facts.fact: Zenodo record 22768651 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22768651; concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22768650; version index 0, the only version) is titled 'C-ArmLSpine'. It was published 2026-09-17, is open access under CC BY 4.0, and names one creator, Feng Qianjin (ORCID 0000-0002-3830-5120, no affiliation given). Its only related identifier is 'cites' 10.1016/j.media.2024.103283 (PRSCS-Net). It holds one file, C-ArmLSpine.zip: 15,581,614,253 bytes, md5 6bccd47979a2a1c9b200dc427fefeb54.

The record's description is the only dataset documentation: 149 cases 'collected during routine intraoperative imaging procedures', each with an AP and a lateral C-arm X-ray and a CBCT from the same FIRST Surgio-B51 mobile C-arm, suggested for X-ray-to-CT reconstruction, representation learning, 3D/2D registration and navigation. It says nothing about IRB or ethics, consent, patients versus cadavers, surgery type, spinal levels, labels, pose, splits or geometry.

I read the zip's central directory over HTTP range requests without downloading the archive. It is ZIP64 with 60,058 entries, all files deflated, 23,347,039,978 bytes uncompressed. The only top-level item is C-ArmLSpine/, holding 149 folders named case1 to case149 (no zero padding, no gaps). There is no README, CSV, JSON, label, mask, landmark, pose/geometry, split or NIfTI file anywhere: 58,911 entries end in .dcm, 698 are extensionless DICOM, and the other 449 are directories.

147 of 149 cases have the layout caseN/C-arm/ (2 DICOM X-ray frames) plus caseN/CBCT/ (394 axial DICOM slices). 109 cases use numeric names (C-arm/0001.dcm and 0002.dcm; CBCT/0000.dcm to 0393.dcm). The others name files by DCMTK-style UID (1.2.276.0.7230010.3.1.4.3422429371....dcm). File order does not fix which frame is AP: in case39 and case118 the first file is not the AP frame.

Two cases break the layout. case39: C-arm/ holds 3 frames (AP 0.0 deg plus two 90.0 deg laterals), and CBCT/ holds 696 files: 394 slices, 301 raw 1024x1024 CBCT projection frames (XA) and one 698-byte DICOM. case134 has no C-arm/ folder. Its AP (0.0 deg) and lateral (90.0 deg) 2048x2048 frames sit inside CBCT/ as extensionless XA.* files next to 394 CT.* slices, and an extra folder ori/ holds 301 raw projections plus one 788-byte DICOM. So case134 does have both frames; the project handoff's 'case134 has no frames' is wrong. Totals: 299 AP/lateral frames, 58,706 CBCT slices (149 x 394), 602 raw projections.

The 297 frames in C-arm/ folders, read header by header, are all DICOM X-Ray Angiographic Image Storage (1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.12.1), Modality XA, ImageType ORIGINAL/PRIMARY/SINGLE PLANE, SeriesDescription 'DR', one frame each. All are 2048x2048, BitsAllocated/BitsStored 16, unsigned, MONOCHROME2, Explicit VR Little Endian, uncompressed, Rescale slope 1 and intercept 0, PixelIntensityRelationship empty. ApplicationName is '单帧摄影' (single-shot radiography) for 294 frames and '连续摄影' (continuous) for 3 (case13 x2, case64). Manufacturer '一影医疗' (First Imaging), model Surgio-B51, station 'YiYing_3DCarm', software OR01-00.012.001 (November studies) or OR01-00.012.002 (December).

Frame geometry tags are the same for all 297 frames: DistanceSourceToDetector 1140 mm and DistanceSourceToPatient 745 mm, so nominal isocentre magnification is 1.530 (computed). PixelSpacing is 1.0 x 1.0, with no ImagerPixelSpacing, which is a placeholder. Private (0029,0033) = '30cm', and (0029,0052) appears to be the angle x 10. No frame has FrameOfReferenceUID, a projection matrix, landmarks or overlays. Shutter edges span the full 0-2048 in the frame examined (case1). ExposureTime tag is 10 in every frame, while case1 also stores Exposure Time in ms = 1839.

PositionerPrimaryAngle gives the view. AP frames read 0.0 (129), 0.1 (16), 0.2, 0.9 or -0.1 deg. Lateral frames read 90.0 (137) or 89.9 (11). One case, case118, pairs its AP (0.0 deg) with an OBLIQUE frame at -58.1 deg instead of a lateral. PositionerSecondaryAngle ranges from -0.6 to 0.9 deg. kVp runs 73-99: AP median 75 (73-86), lateral median 88 (80-99); tube current 23-29 mA.

The detector is probably an iRay Jupi1212X: the raw-projection headers carry the reconstruction-configuration path (0037,0014) 'C:/FICBCT/IRayJupi1212X/FICBCT_3DC_110kv_300_FDK_noSC_AutoMAR_fR002.000.xml' (inferred: 300-projection FDK reconstruction at 110 kV, no scatter correction, automatic metal-artefact reduction). iRay lists the Jupi1212X as a 12x12-inch IGZO/CsI dynamic flat panel, 2048x2048 at 150 um pitch (307.2 mm), 16-bit A/D, 50 fps at 1x1 and 100 fps at 2x2 binning. That fits 150 um pixels for the 2048-square frames, not the DICOM 1.0 mm, and 2x2-binned 300 um pixels for the 1024-square raw projections (inference).

CBCT volumes, checked on the first and last slice of all 149: CT Image Storage, Modality CT, ImageType DERIVED/PRIMARY/AXIAL/3DSLICE, manufacturer 'yiying Imaging', station 'YIYING-CBCT'. Each is exactly 394 slices of 394x394, PixelSpacing 0.5 x 0.5 mm, SliceThickness 0.5 mm, 16-bit unsigned, RescaleIntercept -1024 and slope 1 (HU-like), window 300/2000. ImageOrientationPatient is [1,0,0,0,1,0] and PatientPosition 'FFS'. ImagePositionPatient runs from (-98.25,-98.25,-98.25) at instance 1 to (-98.25,-98.25,+98.25) at instance 394, so each CBCT is a 197 mm isotropic cube centred on (0,0,0). The CBCT KVP tag is 0 or garbage (e.g. 1371883213, -314268332) and should not be used.

Standard DICOM grouping cannot link images. Every file, including each slice of one CBCT, has its own random-UUID StudyInstanceUID and SeriesInstanceUID, and no file has FrameOfReferenceUID. Only the case folder ties a frame pair to its CBCT, and slices must be stacked by ImagePositionPatient or InstanceNumber, not by series.

Raw CBCT sweeps exist only for case39 and case134, 301 frames each: 1024x1024 uint16 XA, 111 kV, 12-13 mA, same SID 1140 and SOD 745. PositionerPrimaryAngle runs from +122.0 deg (first frame) to -51.5 deg (last), a ~173.5 deg short scan. case134's sweep took 15:12:31-15:13:00 (about 29 s, about 10 frames/s) and began 29 s after its lateral frame. Each sweep comes with a 698- or 788-byte DICOM holding (0037,0101) 'rebuild Template ZIP FILE' and an empty (0037,0102) OW, so no reconstruction template is actually included. Projection frames also carry an undocumented private (0037,0020) binary array of about 3,800 bytes.

Acquisition timing is not what 'routine intraoperative imaging' would suggest. All 149 cases were acquired on five days: 2023-11-11 (case134), 2023-11-12 (case39), 2023-11-18 (38 cases, 09:38-16:29), 2023-12-11 (66 cases, 09:20-17:54) and 2023-12-12 (43 cases, 09:39-16:21). Within a day, consecutive cases start a median 205-255 s apart (minimum 122 s). Within a case, AP comes first, the lateral follows about 20-30 s later, and the CBCT StudyTime is 81-415 s (median 99 s) after the first frame. UID timestamps agree with the header times (e.g. case1 UID 1702351783 = 2023-12-12 11:29:43 +08:00 against AcquisitionTime 11:29:41), so the times were not visibly shifted. Separate surgeries every 4 minutes are not plausible. The set looks like a consecutive imaging session of many subjects (inference; the reason is unknown).

Demographic tags are mostly placeholders. Frames give PatientSex F (83 cases), M (62), the non-standard 'W' (3) and 'O' (case134); all 38 cases of 2023-11-18 are M. PatientSize is 1.80 in every frame that has it, PatientWeight 0, and PatientBirthDate equals the study date. CBCT headers have PatientSex empty and BirthDate 20200101. No PatientAge is present. PatientName = caseN, PatientIdentityRemoved YES, DeidentificationMethod 'Basic Application Confidentiality Profile'. The C-arm/ frames' PatientID is empty, but the raw sweep in case134/ori keeps PatientID '1895112604_20231111.151002.079' (a prefix that recurs across days in private tag (0029,0016), so probably a device key plus timestamp, not a patient identifier).

Site tags are unreliable. InstitutionName is 'SMU' in all files (set by the de-identifier). InstitutionAddress is '江苏南通' (Nantong, Jiangsu) in the frames and 'Pudong, SH' in the CBCT slices. First Imaging (江苏一影医疗设备有限公司) is itself registered in Haimen District, Nantong, with R&D centres in Shanghai and Beijing. So these address tags may be vendor defaults and do not establish where the data were acquired.

The images look like LIVING, clothed subjects with no spinal instrumentation. The project's contact sheets and AP pose QC grid (72 cases) show varied bowel gas and distinct anatomy per case. No pedicle screws, rods, retractors or cages are visible. Several frames show small external metal objects consistent with clothing fasteners or skin markers (e.g. case17 square object, case77 coil, case78 rings, case93 small clip). In the CBCTs, 18 of 149 cases have voxels above 3000 HU and 24 have more than 1000 voxels above 2000 HU. This is a visual inference, not a stated fact.

A crude test found no evidence that cases repeat the same subject. On a grid job (40411083), I compared per-case TotalSegmentator L2-L4 volumes and bounding extents, for the 116 cases whose L2-L4 are not cut by the field edge. No pair was near-identical: the closest pair differed by a median 1.1% against a 2.1% first percentile over all pairs, and the closest pairs cross days and recorded sex. The median L3 volume was 48.3 ml (5th-95th percentile 38.2-66.5). This fits mostly distinct subjects, but segmentation noise makes it weak evidence.

Levels in the field come from the project's automated TotalSegmentator + SPINEPS labelling of the CBCTs; the release provides no labels. 137 of 149 CBCTs include the sacrum. Top level is L1 in 104, L2 in 35, T12 in 3 and L3 in 1. Most common sets: L1-L5+S (93), L2-L5+S (34), L1-L5 without sacrum (8). Four cases contain only sacrum. Labellers agreed on 814 of 910 vertebrae, with 22 variant cases (e.g. case136 read L2-L6). The handoff reports no femoral head in 31 CBCTs checked. The data are lumbar and lumbosacral, reaching T12 at most; there is no thoracic coverage.

The header geometry nearly registers each frame to its CBCT. In the project's check, a DRR of the CBCT at the header geometry (beam along the CBCT y axis for AP, x for lateral, SOD 745, SID 1140, centred on the origin) best matched real AP frames with 3.6/-1.2 mm (case1) and 3.6/-2.4 mm (case50) residual shifts at the detector. In the 6-case pilot, refinement moved in-plane 1-3 mm, depth +7-18 mm, and rotation 1-5 deg. The device's image-axis convention (rot180, mirror) had to be found by hypothesis search, not read from the headers. A nominal 'ground-truth' pose is therefore derivable from the device geometry, but its accuracy is limited by patient motion in the ~1.5 min between frames and CBCT (inference).

The GitHub repository ZWC-SMU/C-ArmLSpine was created 2026-09-15. It holds only a README.md in 10 commits (2026-09-15 to 2026-09-19), no code, no licence file and no data loaders. It has one release, tag 'C-ArmLSpine' (created 2026-09-17), with no binary assets. The README repeats the Zenodo description, links to https://zenodo.org/uploads/22768651 (the owner's edit URL, not the public /records/ page), asks users to cite PRSCS-Net, and lists two 'Related Works': [1] PRSCS-Net and [2] 'DAF-Reg: Delta-pose Regression with Adaptive Fusion for patient-specific single-view 2D/3D rigid registration'. The first README draft had a copy-pasted line, 'f you find KGFT useful'.

GitHub user ZWC-SMU (created 2026-08-12, bio 'SMU-ZWC') has only two public repositories: C-ArmLSpine and KGFT (Kernel-Guided Feature Transform, an unrelated ResNet/ViT/LLaMA module with an arXiv citation to Feng Qianjin et al.). GitHub repository search returns nothing for 'PRSCS-Net', 'PRSCS registration' or 'Surgio-B51'. No PRSCS-Net or DAF-Reg code is public, so no author loader, config, geometry parameter or pose convention could be read.

PRSCS-Net: Zhang W, Zhao L, Gou H, Gong Y, Zhou Y (corresponding, [e-mail withheld]), Feng Q (corresponding, [e-mail withheld]). School of Biomedical Engineering, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, with the Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Medical Image Processing. Med Image Anal 2024 Oct; 97:103283, epub 2024-07-20, doi 10.1016/j.media.2024.103283, PMID 39094463, 64 references, no competing interests declared. The abstract describes C-ArmLSpine as an 'in-house dataset' used alongside public CTSpine1k. The method is single-view: a differentiable backward/forward projection operator in a single-view cycle-synthesis network rebuilds 3D geometry features from one real intraoperative view plus one synthesised view. A self-reconstruction path encodes the preoperative CT, and a progressive path of two sub-registration networks estimates pose by two-step warping of volume features.

Crossref funders for PRSCS-Net: Guangzhou Municipal Science and Technology Project 2024A04J9911; NSFC 12126603, 62001207 and 62276122; Natural Science Foundation of Guangdong Province 2023A1515011956 and 2024A1515012291. Crossref also lists Elsevier TDM full-text links (api.elsevier.com, which needs an API key and entitlement).

The PRSCS-Net full text could not be obtained. Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and Unpaywall all report it closed access with no repository copy. ScienceDirect returned a 403 captcha page from this machine, from a Wayne State grid compute node (job 40411065) and through a reader proxy. ResearchGate returned 403, and the Wayback Machine has no snapshot. None of the paper's data description, ground-truth pose method, splits, preprocessing, SDD or results tables could be read.

First author Wencong Zhang (张文聪) was a master's student at SMU's School of Biomedical Engineering. His thesis topic was '基于深度学习的3D/2D配准方法研究' (deep-learning-based 3D/2D registration), presented at the 2024-04-29 mid-term progress review. So a master's thesis probably describes the in-house data, but no online copy (CNKI or other) was found.

No other paper was found that uses C-ArmLSpine. Earlier 3D/2D spine registration papers from the same SMU group evaluated only on CTSpine1k: SGReg (Mi J, Yin W, Zhao L, Chen Y, Zhou Y, Feng Q; Phys Med Biol 2023; doi 10.1088/1361-6560/acd29d) and an orthogonal-view reconstruction method (Mi J, Zhou Y, Feng Q; Nan Fang Yi Ke Da Xue Xue Bao 2023;43(9):1636-1643; PMC10563102). DAF-Reg, listed in the README, turned up in no search of the web, Semantic Scholar or the arXiv API, so it is probably unpublished or under review.

Semantic Scholar lists 9 papers citing PRSCS-Net; none uses C-ArmLSpine. LayersReg (Wang X et al., arXiv 2606.26647, 2026-06-25) re-implemented PRSCS-Net as a baseline on its own X-ray/CT task: DRRs from CTSpine1K and VerSe, real evaluation on DeepFluoro and Ljubljana, 1.0 mm resampling, 224x224x192 crops. There PRSCS-Net scored MAE(R) 1.35 +/- 1.08 deg, Dist(T) 1.93 +/- 1.16 mm, NCC 0.93 and SSIM 0.71, against LayersReg 0.68 deg / 1.41 mm. These are third-party numbers, not PRSCS-Net's own C-ArmLSpine results.

Timeline: PRSCS-Net called the data 'in-house' in July 2024; the data were acquired 2023-11-11 to 2023-12-12; the public release came 2026-09-17 (Zenodo and GitHub). The paper thus used data acquired 7-8 months before its July 2024 epub (computed). Whether the paper used all 149 cases, or the same subset, is unknown.

unknowns: How PRSCS-Net obtained ground-truth pose on C-ArmLSpine (device geometry, manual or intensity registration, fiducials) could not be read because the full text is paywalled behind a captcha. The header geometry nearly aligns frames to CBCT (residual about 1-4 mm in-plane and 7-18 mm in depth in the project's pilot), which suggests but does not prove a geometry-derived reference.

PRSCS-Net's C-ArmLSpine results (mTRE, success rate, rotation and translation errors), how many cases it used, its train/validation/test split, whether C-ArmLSpine was test-only or fine-tuned on, its preprocessing (resampling, cropping, intensity conversion, DRR settings), and the SDD and pixel size it assumed are all unknown. So are its CTSpine1k results and its failure definition.

Whether the subjects are living patients, volunteers or cadavers; whether any surgery took place; and what surgery or indication applies. The release says 'routine intraoperative imaging', but 148 cases arrive about 4 minutes apart on 4 days, and the images show no instrumentation and some apparent clothing metal.

IRB or ethics approval, consent and the collecting hospital or site are stated nowhere (Zenodo, GitHub or abstract). 'SMU' and the Nantong/Shanghai address tags may be de-identifier or vendor defaults. Whether one or several physical Surgio-B51 units were used is also unknown.
How many distinct patients there are: 149 cases do not have to be 149 people. The vertebra-volume fingerprint test was only weakly informative.

The exact detector-to-image orientation convention (rotation or mirroring of stored frames relative to the C-arm), the C-arm axis to CBCT DICOM axis mapping, and the isocentre location beyond 'CBCT centred on (0,0,0)'. These were inferred by the project's registration search, not documented by the authors.

Whether the 2048x2048 frames are raw or vendor-processed (log, gain, LUT, edge enhancement), since PixelIntensityRelationship is empty. The 1024x1024 raw projections are presumably raw detector output.
The meaning of private tags (0029,0016/0020-0054), (0035,0012) and (0037,0020), and of the misused dose tags (3004,0002)/(3004,0012) in the frames.
The content of the DAF-Reg paper named in the README (venue, status, and whether it uses C-ArmLSpine with a different protocol).
Wencong Zhang's master's thesis text (probably on CNKI, not found online), which would likely describe the in-house data collection and ground-truth procedure.
Whether a v2 of the Zenodo record will add labels, poses or splits. The record was 4 days old when read.

Process note, not a data unknown: the Unpaywall API query for this DOI was sent with the user's email address as its required 'email' parameter. That was an error, since the address should not have gone to a third-party service.

Process note: two small grid jobs ran for this work: 40411065 (full-text fetch attempt, ScienceDirect captcha) and 40411083 (per-case vertebra volumes, output /rs/rs_grp_oschome/go2432/tmp/prscs/vertvol.json). The full zip listing and header surveys are in the session scratchpad as listing.tsv, survey_carm.json and survey_cbct.json.

facts.fact: 'FIRST' is Jiangsu First-Imaging Medical Equipment Co., Ltd. (江苏一影医疗设备有限公司; brand 一影医疗, 'Yiying', English 'FIRST IMAGING'). It is not 福斯特 or 菲森. Its registered and manufacturing address is 南通市海门区临江镇临江大道188号B2 (Haimen, Nantong, Jiangsu), and its web and office address is 上海市浦东新区康安路388弄2号 (Zhangjiang, Pudong, Shanghai). Contact: [e-mail withheld], [phone withheld].

Company structure: founded 2018 per company and investor pages (one earlier trade article says 2015). It has an 800 m² R&D centre in Shanghai, a 3,000 m² production line in Nantong, a 2,000 m² key-component line in Xianju, Zhejiang, and a software R&D centre in Beijing. A sister entity, 'Shanghai First-Imaging Information Technology Co., Ltd.', appears as a paper affiliation. The founder and CEO is Dr. 奚岩 (Yan Xi; SJTU BS/PhD, postdoc at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute; e-mail [e-mail withheld]).

The company's product line has four families. Ortho-A series: a small 3D C-arm with a 30 s scan and a patented 'variable-isocentre' (变等中心) non-isocentric geometry. Surgio-B series: a 'large flat panel / large FOV' mobile C-arm CT offering intraoperative tomography, fluoroscopy and peripheral DSA. Surgio-B71: an integrated single-unit variant. Combo-S and Supero-O (a mobile O-arm style CBCT with a 43×43 cm detector) make up the rest. The Surgio-B marketing text names an IGZO flat-panel detector, TwinPulse dual-pulse technology, AutoPOSE auto-positioning, a 'virtual collimator' and a 'virtual grid' (虚拟滤线栅), metal-artefact removal, and RoboLINK/3DLINK navigation and robot interfaces (DICOM 3.0).

NMPA registration: 国械注准20233060458, registrant 江苏一影医疗设备有限公司, product 移动式C形臂X射线机, model 'Surgio-B51s', Class III. Approved 2023-04-06, valid to 2028-04-05. Composition: X-ray generation device, X-ray imaging device and accessories. Intended use: fluoroscopy, radiography and 3-D tomographic imaging during surgery. Hospital tenders filed under this certificate list the model as 'Surgio-B51' (for example Xiangyang TCM Hospital, 2024-12-31, 2.385 M CNY; Baoji Central Hospital, 2024-12-05, 2.783 M CNY; Zhangzhou '大平板移动式C臂CT系统', 2024-07-31, 2.46 M CNY).

A 2025 government procurement contract names the variant 'Surgio-B51-MC' (江苏一影 移动式C臂X射线机). It was bought by Jiangnan University Affiliated Hospital (Wuxi) for 2,048,000 CNY under project JSZC-320200-XWJC-G2025-0061, with a 3-year warranty. The contract contains no technical specifications.

Other First-Imaging registrations found: 国械注准20243062393 (a mobile C-arm adding peripheral vascular subtraction imaging, valid to 2029-11-26; model not confirmed) and 国械注准20243060051 (Combo-S31-M). An older 3D flat-panel mobile C-arm, '泰山' (Taishan), carries the Jiangsu Class II certificate 苏械注准20212060026 and is advertised with a CMOS flat panel, an 8 kW tube, a 4K display and TwinPulse. The Taishan specifications must not be carried over to the Surgio-B51.

FDA: openFDA 510(k) and registration/listing searches returned no matches for applicant 'First-Imaging', 'First Imaging', 'Yiying' or 'Jiangsu … Imaging', nor for device names Surgio, Supero or Ortho-A. No CE/MDR certificate was found either. The device appears to be China-market only.

The C-ArmLSpine release (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.22768651, a single 15.58 GB C-ArmLSpine.zip, CC-BY-4.0, creator Feng Qianjin, published 2026-09-17) contains 60,058 zip entries: 58,911 .dcm files plus about 700 UID-named DICOM files. There are 149 case folders. 148 have a C-arm/ folder (147 with 2 radiographs, case39 with 3). Every case has a CBCT/ folder holding 394 axial slices. Only case134 (ori/ folder) and case39 (inside CBCT/) also carry the raw CBCT projection series. I read the central directory and selected member headers with HTTP range requests, without downloading the full zip.

The C-ArmLSpine 2-D DICOM headers read Manufacturer '一影医疗', ManufacturerModelName 'Surgio-B51', StationName 'YiYing_3DCarm' and SoftwareVersions 'OR01-00.012.001' (Nov 2023) or 'OR01-00.012.002' (Dec 2023). SOP class is X-Ray Angiographic Image Storage (1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.12.1), Modality XA, SeriesDescription 'DR', ApplicationName '单帧摄影' (single-frame radiography), RadiationMode PULSED, RadiationSetting SC, RecommendedDisplayFrameRate 30. Private (0029,0016) begins '1895112604_' on 287 of 297 radiographs, which is consistent with a single unit.

C-ArmLSpine 2-D geometry tags: DistanceSourceToDetector 1140 mm and DistanceSourceToPatient 745 mm on every image (magnification about 1.53). PositionerPrimaryAngle is about 0° for AP and about 90° for lateral. Rows × Columns are 2048 × 2048, 16-bit unsigned, MONOCHROME2. PixelSpacing (0028,0030) is 1.0000\1.0000 mm, which is a placeholder: 2048 mm is physically impossible. ImagerPixelSpacing (0018,1164) is absent. A private tag (0029,0033) reads '30cm'. PixelIntensityRelationship (0028,1040) is present but empty in every 2-D file.

C-ArmLSpine 2-D exposure tags across 218 parsed radiographs: kVp 73–98 (AP median 73, range 73–86; lateral median 87, range 80–98). XRayTubeCurrent 23–27 mA (XRayTubeCurrentInuA 23,700–27,600). AveragePulseWidth 28–114 ms (median 62). ExposureTime is 10 on every image. ExposureTimeInms is 1834–1942. Automatic exposure selection is implied by the variation.

The detector is almost certainly an iRay Jupi 1212X, inferred rather than stated. Private tag (0037,0014) in every raw CBCT projection names the reconstruction configuration file 'C:/FICBCT/IRayJupi1212X/FICBCT_3DC_110kv_300_FDK_noSC_AutoMAR_fR002.000.xml'. That points to an iRay Jupi 1212X detector, a 110 kV / 300-view protocol, FDK reconstruction, no scatter correction and automatic metal-artefact reduction. It is consistent with the 2048×2048 radiographs, the '30cm' private tag and First-Imaging's 'IGZO FD' marketing.

iRay Jupi 1212X datasheet: IGZO TFT sensor with direct-deposition CsI scintillator, 12 × 12 inch active area, 2048 × 2048 matrix, 150 µm pixel pitch, 3.3 lp/mm limiting resolution, 16-bit A/D. Frame rate is 50 fps at 1×1 and 100 fps at 2×2 in the English sheet (45/90 fps in the Chinese sheet). Other specifications: 10GigE/CXP interface, 337 × 332 × 39 mm, 5.5 kg, <2.5% first-frame lag, switchable gain. It is marketed for fixed and mobile C-arm fluoroscopy.

Derived pixel sizes, assuming the Jupi 1212X at 150 µm: 2048² radiographs are about 0.150 mm at the detector and about 0.098 mm at the 745 mm source distance. 1024² CBCT projections (2×2 binned) are about 0.300 mm at the detector and about 0.196 mm there. The DICOM PixelSpacing of 1.0 mm must not be used for geometry.

C-ArmLSpine raw CBCT orbit, case134 (2023-11-11): 301 XA frames (InstanceNumber 0–300), 1024×1024, 111 kVp, 12 mA (12,500 µA), pulse width 15–20 ms, SID 1140 and SOD 745 mm, ProtocolName '3', ExposureTimeInms 30,387. PositionerPrimaryAngle falls from +122.0° to −51.5° (173.5° recorded) with PositionerSecondaryAngle 0.4–0.6°. The acquisition lasted 15:12:31 to 15:13:00, about 29 s or about 10 frames/s. The angle tag updates only about every 5 frames (58 distinct values), and the mean step is 0.59°/frame. Private (0037,0010)=300 is the nominal view count, (0029,0020)=301 and (0037,0011)=0.69 is of unknown meaning. A 788-byte companion object carries (0037,0101) 'rebuild Template ZIP FILE' with an empty payload.

C-ArmLSpine raw CBCT orbit, case39 (2023-11-12): 301 frames, 111 kVp, 13 mA, pulse width 18–23 ms, ExposureTimeInms 30,460. The angle runs from +122.0° to −54.3° (176.3° recorded) over 15:04:10 to 15:04:39. The configuration file is the same IRayJupi1212X/110kv_300_FDK file.

C-ArmLSpine reconstructed CBCT: SOP class CT Image Storage, ImageType DERIVED\PRIMARY\AXIAL\3DSLICE, Manufacturer 'yiying Imaging', StationName 'YIYING-CBCT'. Each volume is 394 × 394 × 394 at 0.5 mm isotropic (PixelSpacing and SliceThickness both 0.5), a cube of about 197 mm centred on ImagePositionPatient (−98.25, −98.25, −98.25). ImageOrientationPatient is axial; PatientPosition is FFS. Pixel data are 16-bit unsigned with RescaleIntercept −1024 and slope 1, i.e. HU-like, with air at about −1000. The default window is C300/W2000, and the KVP and mA tags are zero or garbage. The 197 mm cube matches the 307 mm detector scaled back to a 745 mm source distance (about 200 mm), so that SOD is plausibly the true isocentre distance.

What the files store, from pixel inspection. The 2-D radiographs are processed display images, not raw or log data. They show strong edge enhancement (dark halos at cortical margins), air and bowel gas appear bright (MONOCHROME2), and the value range varies widely per image: case1 AP spans 625–4848 while its lateral spans 443–62,432, and case104 AP spans 559–2528. SmallestImagePixelValue and LargestImagePixelValue are sometimes inconsistent with the pixels.

Each raw CBCT projection carries two images. Private tag (0037,0020), OW of 2,097,152 bytes, holds a second 1024×1024 uint16 frame that looks like a raw linear detector image: body values about 300–1300, air about 13,000–14,000, visible uncorrected half-row line defects, and a 180° rotation relative to the main image. The main Pixel Data follow main ≈ 2373·ln(raw) − 7817 (R² 0.86, or r 0.93 after 31-px smoothing), so they are log-compressed and spatially processed, with air bright. Whether the private frame is offset- or gain-corrected is unknown.

Dose tags are misused. DoseValue (3004,0012) and DoseUnits (3004,0002) both hold numbers, and their ratio is constant at 245.2 (range 244.8–245.4, n=220). That equals (30.0 cm × 595/1140)² cm², where 595 mm = 745 − 150 mm is the IEC reference point. This suggests DoseValue is reference-point air kerma (probably mGy) and the 'DoseUnits' field is DAP (probably mGy·cm²) for an open 30 cm field. Radiographs have a median DoseValue of 0.13 (range 0.029–4). CBCT projection headers carry 8.61 (case134) and 10.86 (case39).

The C-ArmLSpine DICOM was rewritten during de-identification. Most files were written by DCMTK 3.6.1 (explicit VR); 39 cases were rewritten in implicit VR by another toolkit (ImplementationClassUID 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.2.135.1066.101, '1.5.0/WIN32'). The raw case134 projections keep the device-side writer OFFIS_DCMTK_365 with source AE 'CarmAETitle'. StudyInstanceUID and SeriesInstanceUID were replaced by UUID strings, which are invalid UI values. DeidentificationMethod reads 'Basic Application Confidentiality Profile'. InstitutionName is 'SMU' (one raw file says '医院'). InstitutionAddress is '江苏南通' on XA and 'Pudong, SH' on CT; these look like device defaults that match the manufacturer's Nantong and Shanghai sites, not the acquisition site.

C-ArmLSpine acquisition timing: all 149 cases fall on five dates, 2023-11-11 (case134), 2023-11-12 (case39), 2023-11-18 (38 cases, 09:38–16:29), 2023-12-11 (66 cases, 09:20–17:54) and 2023-12-12 (43 cases, 09:39–16:21). The median gap between successive cases is 3.4–4.2 min (p10 about 2.7, p90 about 10–13 min). In case1 the sequence is AP (11:29:41), then lateral (11:30:03), then CBCT slices (11:31:00). PatientSize is 1.80 and PatientWeight 0.0 everywhere, which are defaults. This pace sits poorly with the README's 'routine intraoperative imaging procedures'. The images show lumbar spine with bowel gas and no instruments.

A paper co-authored by First-Imaging names the device. PDS-MAR (Lyu, Wu, …, Yan Xi, Yang Chen, Wentao Zhu; Phys Med Biol 2023, doi 10.1088/1361-6560/ad00fc; arXiv 2306.11958) states that sheep-back K-wire projections 'were acquired using a commercial intraoperative CBCT system (B51s) from First-Imaging Medical Equipment Co., Ltd.', and that human-body phantoms (abdomen, head) were scanned on a First-Imaging system. The data were pre-processed with First-Imaging's commercial correction software (field correction, denoising, water beam-hardening correction). Its simulation (Table 1) used DSD 1140 mm, DSO 617 mm, a 1024×1024 detector at 0.45 mm, 300 views over 180°, and a 512³ volume at 0.55 mm; the 617 mm DSO differs from the DICOM's 745 mm.

Other papers with First-Imaging affiliations that likely use the company's CBCT hardware and data (full texts not accessed): HIDE-Net projection-domain metal segmentation (Med Phys 2025, PMID 40017345, clinical CBCT); Lag-Net (CMPB 2025, PMID 40233441, lag correction for amorphous-silicon flat-panel CBCT); FDA-Recon (Med Image Anal 2026, PMID 41494314) and MAE-Recon (Med Phys 2026, PMID 41589426), both sparse-view CBCT; a helical-like upright robotic-arm CBCT (Med Phys 2025, PMID 40665576); Twin-ViMReg standing-CBCT knee (CMIG 2025, PMID 41037979); and SMART multi-source CT with RPI (TRPMS 2025, PMID 40808799).

Papers using C-ArmLSpine itself: PRSCS-Net (Zhang W, Zhao L, Gou H, Gong Y, Zhou Y, Feng Q; Med Image Anal 97:103283, 2024; closed access; describes C-ArmLSpine as an 'in-house dataset') and DAF-Reg (single-view 2D/3D rigid registration; no published record found). Both come from the Southern Medical University group (GitHub ZWC-SMU).

An earlier First-Imaging 'intraoperative CT' C-arm (CMEF launch article, undated, circa 2020) was offered with either a high-end CMOS or a standard a-Si flat panel and a 27-inch display. It is described as a C-arm rotating uniformly on its C-track, continuously exposing to build CBCT, with a high-power pulsed source and a three-axis motorised gantry. This predates the IGZO Surgio-B and should not be assumed to match it.

A 2025-08-22 statement on First-Imaging's site says the company removed unapproved advertising from its website after a regulator notice, and clarifies that its 'variable isocentre' claim refers to patent CN112971814 (C型臂定位方法及成像方法), which covers positioning of a non-isocentric C-arm. This probably explains why the current product pages carry no technical specifications.

Local working files from this investigation: the zip central-directory index (cd.json), per-file header harvests (headers_all.json, dates.json, angles_C-ArmLSpine_case134_ori.json, angles_C-ArmLSpine_case39_CBCT.json), extracted sample DICOMs in zipout/ and renders in png/. All are in the scratchpad folder cited as this fact's source. The range-request reader remotezip.py can pull any single member of the Zenodo zip.

unknowns: No public Surgio-B51 or B51s spec sheet was found: tube power, kV and mA ranges, focal spot, heat capacity, filtration, collimator, AEC behaviour and fluoroscopy frame rates are unpublished. The company removed product specifications from its site in 2025. The Taishan's 8 kW CMOS figures belong to a different product.

C-arm mechanics are unknown: C depth or free space, C opening, orbital and propeller ranges, whether the B51 is isocentric or uses the non-isocentric 'variable-isocentre' design, and whether the 3-D sweep is orbital or propeller. DICOM records only the patient-relative primary angle (+122° to about −52/−54°).

The true 3-D arc: the recorded sweep is 173.5–176.3° while the nominal is 180° (PDS-MAR simulation). The angle tag updates only about every 5 frames. No projection matrices or geometric calibration are in the DICOM.
Which isocentre distance is correct: the DICOM gives 745 mm, the PDS-MAR simulation 617 mm, and whether the SID is fixed at 1140 mm is unconfirmed.

Confirmation of the detector: iRay Jupi 1212X is inferred from a reconstruction-config file path, not stated by the manufacturer. Whether 2048² radiographs are native 1×1 readout or resampled, and whether the 1024² CBCT frames are 2×2 binned, are both unconfirmed.
Whether a physical anti-scatter grid is fitted, and its ratio. The marketing names only a 'virtual grid', and the reconstruction config says 'noSC'.
The exact 2-D processing chain (edge enhancement, LUT, dynamic-range compression). PixelIntensityRelationship is blank, and no raw or unprocessed version of the 2-D radiographs is in the release.

Whether the private (0037,0020) raw CBCT frame is offset- or gain-corrected, and the meaning of private tags (0037,0011)=0.69, (0029,0020)=301, (0029,0028)=42, (0029,0029)=21, (0029,0050)/(0029,0051), (0029,0053), (0029,0063) 'LIH'/'LSH', (0035,0012) and the CT-slice ExposureTime=130.
The units and definition of the dose fields: DoseValue and DoseUnits look like reference air kerma and DAP, but this is inferred from a constant ratio.

Where and on whom C-ArmLSpine was acquired: the institution fields hold defaults, and the 3–4 min spacing between cases conflicts with 'routine intraoperative' patient imaging. Patient versus specimen or phantom, and the hospital, are not established. PRSCS-Net full text was not accessible.
The meaning of the model suffixes: Surgio-B51 (DICOM and tenders), Surgio-B51s (NMPA certificate) and Surgio-B51-MC (2025 contract), and which hardware revision produced the 2023 data.

No published image-quality measurement for the Surgio-B51 was found: no MTF, NPS, DQE, CNR, CTDI, low-contrast detectability or geometric accuracy on any phantom. The only numbers found are iRay's detector datasheet values.
Full texts of HIDE-Net, Lag-Net, FDA-Recon and MAE-Recon were not accessed, so it is not established whether they used Surgio-B51 data or which detector (a-Si for Lag-Net) they describe.
No FDA 510(k) or CE/MDR record was found. Absence from openFDA was checked; EUDAMED was not queried.
DAF-Reg has no published record, and its venue is unknown.

gaps: Biomechanics motion-capture repositories were never queried directly. XMAPortal (xmaportal.org, Brown XROMM) has about 130 studies of calibrated biplanar X-ray video, usually with CT of the same animal. Its public listing (https://xmaportal.org/webportal/larequest.php?request=alldata, opened) shows trunk and pelvis studies: Iguana Lung Ventilation (BROWN5, public), Pelvic Mobility in Turtles (BROWN40, public), Quail Hip ROM (BROWN68, public), Tinamou Walking and Running (XMA2, public), Snake Fluoromicrometery (XMA5, public), plus Ferret Back Muscle Function, Monitor Lizard, Tegu, Alligator and Boa lung ventilation (non-public but browsable). The portal is read-only and moving to xma.xromm.brown.edu. The earlier XROMM/biplane queries all had spine terms attached and never reached this portal. SimTK (simtk.org) was also never searched: only 48 SimTK items have DataCite DOIs (prefix 10.18735, checked), so most projects are invisible to DataCite.

Legacy 2D/3D gold-standard datasets hosted on lab web pages. The Utrecht ISI database of van de Kraats et al. (IEEE TMI 2005) is in the Wayback Machine at http://web.archive.org/web/20060223001719id_/http://www.isi.uu.nl:80/Research/Databases/GS/data.php (opened). That page describes MR, CT, 3DRX and AP plus lateral fluoroscopic images of 2 cadaveric spinal segments (3 + 5 vertebral bodies), with 2D/3D masks and full world-coordinate source and detector geometry. The data files themselves are not archived because downloads went through an agreement form. Nothing searched so far checked whether it, or the Vienna/Pawiro, Tomaževič/Ljubljana or Markelj-review datasets, has been re-hosted. The Wayback CDX API, archive.org advancedsearch and Academic Torrents were never used.

Conference paper pages were read one at a time, never systematically. The MICCAI 2025 list (https://papers.miccai.org/miccai-2025/, 1.9 MB, fetched) has about 40 X-ray, fluoroscopy, CBCT, DRR, 2D/3D and biplanar titles, and each paper page has a 'Link to the Dataset(s)' field. Only paper 1018 and DAX were opened. MICCAI 2026 pages currently return HTTP 401. OpenReview venues (MIDL 2024-2026, NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks 2024-2026, ICLR 2026), the IPCAI 2025/2026, SPIE Medical Imaging 2026 and ISBI 2026 abstract books, and MICCAI workshop proceedings (AE-CAI) were never swept.

Controlled-access epidemiological cohorts with same-subject spine radiographs and CT: MrOS (baseline abdominal QCT plus supine lateral spine radiographs in the same men, per PMC4029749), SOF, the Framingham Osteoporosis Study with Framingham MDCT, AGES-Reykjavik, Health ABC and Hong Kong/Swedish MrOS. None sit in open repositories, and none were searched through BioLINCC, dbGaP, NIA AgingResearchBiobank or MrOS Online.

Interventional torso domains outside spine surgery, where C-arm frames show the lumbar spine or pelvis and a preoperative CT exists, were barely touched: EVAR/iliac stenting DSA and fluoroscopy with CTA, TACE and uterine artery embolisation with CBCT, PCNL/ureteroscopy fluoroscopy with CT, KUB radiograph with NCCT for urolithiasis, and ERCP. There was only one Zenodo 'angiography AND CT' query. A quick DataCite probe and a GitHub probe returned nothing relevant, so the chance looks low. That is why this is not proposed as a new angle.

Also not searched: Gitee and Baidu-Pan-hosted Chinese releases; Google Dataset Search and the OpenAIRE Graph API, which index non-DataCite institutional repositories; Code Ocean capsules; GitHub code search, which needs auth (repository search was rate-limited during this check); forensic PMCT-versus-antemortem-radiograph identification datasets; the NCI IDC BigQuery modality index beyond the TCIA NBIA pass.

new_angles.prompt:
Goal: find REAL calibrated X-ray fluoroscopy (biplanar or single-plane) of the SPINE, RIBS/TORSO, SACRUM or PELVIS/HIP, paired with a CT of the SAME subject (animal, cadaver or human), where the projection pose is known or recoverable (DLT calibration cube, undistortion grid, camera matrices). Also useful: real spine or pelvis fluoroscopy with bone landmark or marker labels. Search the biomechanics repositories that earlier dataset searches never queried directly.
(1) XMAPortal (Brown XROMM). The public listing https://xmaportal.org/webportal/larequest.php?request=alldata shows about 130 studies. Public ones include Iguana Lung Ventilation BROWN5, Pelvic Mobility in Turtles BROWN40, Quail Hip ROM BROWN68, Tinamou Walking and Running XMA2, Morphology and Function of Wild and Domesticated Turkeys BROWN21 and Snake Fluoromicrometery XMA5. Non-public but browsable: Ferret Back Muscle Function BROWN33, Monitor Lizard Breathing and Locomotion BROWN42, Tegu Lung Ventilation BROWN29, Alligator Lung Ventilation BROWN10, Boa Lung Ventilation BROWN63, Snake rectilinear locomotion BROWN88, Loggerhead turtle, and others. The portal is read-only and migrating to https://xma.xromm.brown.edu, so check both. For every study whose X-ray field contains vertebrae, ribs, pelvis, sacrum or hip, open the study and trial pages and report: whether raw X-ray videos or frames are downloadable without login; whether calibration files (DLT coefficients, calibration-object images, undistortion grids) exist; whether CT of the same individual is in the study or on MorphoSource (search morphosource.org for the specimen); the X-ray hardware (image intensifier or flat panel, kV, mA, frame rate) if stated; and the licence. Also search the portal's metadata and advanced search for mammal trunk studies: pig, rat, dog, primate, human.
(2) XROMM-keyword deposits with NO anatomy filter, then filter by anatomy yourself. Use Dryad (https://datadryad.org/api/v2/search?q=XROMM and q=biplanar fluoroscopy), Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/api/records?q=XROMM&sort=mostrecent&size=50), figshare, DataCite (https://api.datacite.org/dois?query=XROMM&sort=-created&page[size]=50), and MorphoSource media whose descriptions mention XROMM.
(3) SimTK (simtk.org). Its site search renders by JavaScript, so use WebSearch 'site:simtk.org fluoroscopy', 'site:simtk.org biplane', 'site:simtk.org dual fluoroscopy spine OR lumbar OR pelvis OR hip', and read the project Downloads pages.
(4) Human dual-fluoroscopy or dynamic-stereo-X-ray labs that publish CT-paired spine, hip or pelvis data: Utah Orthopaedic Research Lab (Anderson, Atkins; the Utah Hive record cftes-sc590 was already read, so look for other records), MGH Bioengineering (G. Li, lumbar dual fluoroscopy), Pitt Biodynamics (Anderst, cervical and lumbar DSX), Henry Ford Bone and Joint Center, Mayo Clinic. Check their lab pages and any repository they name.
Fetch with Bash via: wsl -e bash -lc "curl -s 'URL'" (Windows sockets flake). Return DATA only, write no files. Every candidate needs at least one evidence URL you actually opened. Say plainly when the anatomy is non-mammalian, when CT is absent or only a mesh, or when the data needs a login or request.

Goal: recover older lab-hosted 2D/3D registration gold-standard datasets that pair REAL C-arm fluoroscopy or rotational X-ray projections of the spine or pelvis with CT of the same specimen and a known projection geometry, plus any re-hosted copies or successors.
Known lead: the Utrecht Image Sciences Institute '2D-3D registration gold standard' database (van de Kraats EB et al., 'Standardized evaluation methodology for 2-D-3-D registration', IEEE TMI 2005;24(9):1177-89). The Wayback copy http://web.archive.org/web/20060223001719id_/http://www.isi.uu.nl:80/Research/Databases/GS/data.php describes Dataset 1: MR, CT, 3DRX and AP plus lateral fluoroscopic images of 2 cadaveric spinal segments (3 + 5 vertebral bodies), 2D and 3D masks, source, detector and volume positions in a world coordinate system, and 200 starting positions. The download went through agreement.php and commence_download.php, and the data files are not in the Wayback CDX index.
Tasks: (1) Use the Wayback CDX API (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=isi.uu.nl/Research/Databases/GS/&matchType=prefix and matchType=domain filters) and the archived index.php, download.php and results.php to learn the file names, sizes, any later host or contact, and whether the files were ever at another URL (umcutrecht.nl, image.sciences.uu.nl, ftp). (2) Pull forward citations of van de Kraats 2005 (OpenAlex cites: filter, Semantic Scholar /citations, Crossref) and check papers from 2015 onward that used 'the Utrecht dataset' or 'ISI gold standard' for a data-availability link, GitHub copy or Kaggle re-upload. Search GitHub, Zenodo, figshare, Kaggle and HF for 'van de Kraats', 'Utrecht 2D-3D', 'ISI gold standard', '3DRX spine'. (3) Do the same for the other classic gold standards: Tomaževič, Likar and Pernuš (Comput Aided Surg 2004, Ljubljana cadaveric lumbar spine; the user may already hold it, so report only NEW mirrors, versions or companion sets from the Ljubljana group such as lit.fe.uni-lj.si); Pawiro, Gendrin and Birkfellner (Vienna, 2011; pig, so say plainly if head-only); the dataset table in Markelj et al., 'A review of 3D/2D registration methods for image-guided interventions', MedIA 2012; Otake and Siewerdsen LevelCheck (JHU); Hurvitz and Joskowicz. For each, run Wayback CDX on the lab URL cited in the paper. (4) Query archive.org advancedsearch (https://archive.org/advancedsearch.php?q=(fluoroscopy OR 2D-3D OR C-arm) AND (spine OR vertebra OR pelvis)&fl[]=identifier,title&rows=100&output=json), Academic Torrents (academictorrents.com browse and search for fluoroscopy, C-arm, CBCT projections, 2D/3D) and the OpenAIRE Graph API (https://api.openaire.eu/graph/v1/researchProducts?search=fluoroscopy%20spine&type=dataset and similar) for anything not already covered by DataCite.
Fetch with Bash via: wsl -e bash -lc "curl -s 'URL'". Return DATA only, write no files. Every candidate needs an evidence URL you actually opened. Say plainly whether the files are actually retrievable today, retrievable only on request, or lost.

Goal: find recently released REAL X-ray datasets from conference papers. NEED A: real C-arm fluoroscopy, O-arm/Loop-X/Airo or CBCT sweep projections, kV images or radiographs of the spine, sacrum, pelvis or torso, paired with CT or CBCT of the same subject, ideally with a known pose. NEED B: real intraoperative spine or pelvis fluoroscopy with vertebra-level, sacrum, landmark, screw or needle labels. Such links often live only on conference paper pages, not in indexed repositories.
(1) MICCAI open-access pages: the list pages https://papers.miccai.org/miccai-2025/ (about 1.9 MB, fetchable), and the same for miccai-2024, 2023, 2022 and 2021. Each paper has a 'Paper Information and Reviews' page (for example /miccai-2025/1018-Paper2022.html) with 'Link to the Code Repository' and 'Link to the Dataset(s)' fields. Grep every list for titles matching X-ray|fluoro|C-arm|2D/3D|2D-3D|3D/2D|DRR|CBCT|cone-beam|biplanar|orthogonal X-ray|intraoperative|radiograph|pedicle|vertebra|spine|pelvi|hip. Open each matching paper page, extract the dataset and code links, and open them. Already seen, so skip: Weakly-Supervised 2D/3D registration (paper 1018), DAX, FluoroSAM, RadGS-Reg. MICCAI 2026 pages currently return HTTP 401; re-check https://papers.miccai.org/miccai-2026/ and the MICCAI 2026 accepted-paper list or conference site.
(2) The OpenReview API (https://api2.openreview.net/notes/search?term=fluoroscopy&source=forum&limit=100, and the venue-filtered invitation queries) for MIDL 2024, 2025 and 2026, NeurIPS 2024-2026 Datasets and Benchmarks track, ICLR 2026, and MICCAI workshop venues. Use the terms fluoroscopy, C-arm, X-ray CT, 2D/3D registration, DRR, CBCT projections, spine X-ray, pelvis X-ray.
(3) The IPCAI 2025 and 2026 accepted papers (IJCARS special issues; use the arXiv versions), the SPIE Medical Imaging 2026 image-guided procedures track, ISBI 2026 and CARS 2026 abstract books, and the AE-CAI and DEMI workshops. Open the GitHub or project pages they cite and look for real-data releases, including Google Drive or Baidu Pan links in READMEs.
Fetch with Bash via: wsl -e bash -lc "curl -s 'URL'". Return DATA only, write no files. Every candidate needs an evidence URL you actually opened. Say plainly when a release is synthetic (DRR-only), CT-only, chest-only, or 'available on request'.

Goal: find controlled-access or application-based research cohorts that hold REAL radiographs, or any other 2-D X-ray, of the lumbar or thoracic spine, sacrum or pelvis AND a CT of the SAME participant. Open repositories (Zenodo, DataCite, figshare, TCIA) have already been searched exhaustively, so these gated cohorts are the remaining gap. Leads:
(a) MrOS (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men). Per PMC4029749 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4029749/), baseline abdominal QCT scans and supine lateral spine radiographs exist for the same men. Determine from https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu and https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov whether the IMAGES themselves (not just derived variables) are distributed, their format, the QCT field of view (which vertebral levels, whether the pelvis is included), how many men have both, and the access route.
(b) SOF (Study of Osteoporotic Fractures); Hong Kong MrOS; Swedish MrOS.
(c) The Framingham Osteoporosis Study lateral spine radiographs with the Framingham Heart Study MDCT abdomen and chest scans. Check the image-data access policy through BioLINCC, dbGaP or the Framingham research application.
(d) AGES-Reykjavik (hip and spine QCT plus radiographs?), Health ABC, the Rotterdam Study, HUNT, FORMEN/Fujiwara-kyo (Japan) and CARDIA. Also check the dbGaP and BioLINCC catalogues for 'lateral spine radiograph' together with 'QCT' or 'CT' imaging substudies.
(e) NCI Imaging Data Commons. Use the public BigQuery-free portal or the idc-index Python package's metadata (pip install idc-index; its index lists Modality per SeriesInstanceUID) to list patients with both CT and any of RF, XA, DX, CR or RTIMAGE, including collections outside the TCIA NBIA pass already done. Report only non-chest pairs or pairs whose X-ray covers spine, pelvis or abdomen.
For each cohort report: the participant count with both modalities, the anatomy in each, the X-ray type (radiograph, DXA or fluoroscopy), whether the images or only derived measurements are shared, the access mechanism and cost, and any pose or geometry metadata. candidate.name: SpineSAC phantom C-arm 2D/3D dataset (IGRS lab, HTIC IIT Madras)
candidate.why_relevant: The strongest new open NEED A item. It has 59 real AP+lateral C-arm scenarios (118 X-rays) of three sawbones lumbar phantoms. Each scenario has the phantom CT (DICOM), 3x4 AP/LP projection matrices (APLP.txt, P_Imf.txt), a ground-truth 6-DoF pose, an initial pose (x0.txt) and L3-L5 ROI boxes (roi_config.json). The Drive folders are named by vendor: GE (12 scenarios), SKANRAY (9) and ZIEHM (12), plus a Ganga Hospital accuracy-study set. That gives several C-arm makes for the device terms. One pass read the README as not naming the models, so the vendor attribution rests on folder names. Caveats: the X-rays are PNGs and some are named 'filtered_xray_*', so they are processed rather than raw. The subjects are phantoms only. The cadaver data shown in the paper is not in datasets.py. There is no DOI and no data licence; the repo text says Apache-2.0 and its badge says MIT.

corrections: Access is confirmed. The Drive folder 1ogGfKXpsRUV-l5eW7azMJTexrZ1Qhiar is readable by anyone with the link. I crawled it anonymously (6 top-level folders, 1,254 folders, 5,492 files, 4.15 GB) and downloaded 12 raw DICOMs, 118 PNGs, 59 APLP.txt files, 59 roi_config.json files and CT slices with no login (HTTP 200/206).

Vendor attribution does not rest on folder names alone, and the candidate's list is incomplete. Headers of the raw acquisition DICOMs, which sit in datasets-.../datasets/BMJH/, give GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS 'FLUOROSTAR' (GE-OEC FluoroStar, 2024-09-11/14), SKANRAY TECHNOLOGIES (InstitutionName 'JAIN HOSPITAL', 2024-11-14, 16-bit, 0.22 mm) and ziehm imaging (ZiehmNetPort, station EXP8000, 2024-09-13/15). The 16 closed-sawbone and Thancopen scenarios were acquired on SIEMENS Healthineers (model not in the header; 2026-02 to 2026-03). The Ganga images carry a burned-in 'Cios_Select 21-09-2025' overlay, so they are Siemens Cios Select. That gives five sources, not three: GE 12, Skanray 9, Ziehm 12, Cios Select 10 (the 9 Ganga plus Train_Set), and Siemens with no model named 16.

Some DICOM headers cannot be trusted. Every Ganga DICOM, the cadaver LP, the closedsawbonedata/GEM set, and many processed or cropped files carry an identical Philips AlluraXper / 'TNMSC, Chennai' / 2020-02-26 / PatientID 722013-570-... header. It is plainly a template the lab's software reuses. The hard-coded pixel spacing 0.74181640625 (datasets.py, environment.py, utils.py) is that template's ImagerPixelSpacing, applied to every C-arm. It is not a per-device value; the Skanray raw header says 0.22 mm.

The X-rays are not only processed PNGs. Raw acquisition DICOMs are also on the Drive: 234 .dcm files outside the Output folders, with AP/LP pairs for GE, Skanray and Ziehm SCN 1-12 under BMJH/, plus Ganga, colsed_sawbonect_data and Thancopen. The 118 PNGs that datasets.py points to are processed. They are intensity-inverted, most calibration beads are removed, several are mirrored (the burned-in text reads backwards), and 10 are RGB.

The count is 118 file references but 116 distinct images. Train_Set (set1/ap.png, set1/lp.png) is byte-identical (same MD5) to ganga_accuracy_study_set1's AP and LP. Both are in the training split, so there are 58 distinct AP-LP pairs.

The ground-truth pose is not an independent measurement per scenario. gt_pose takes only three distinct values across the 59 entries, one per CT, and it is identical across GE, Skanray, Ziehm and Ganga on set1/A. Each scenario's TARGET.txt holds that same T0. All per-scenario geometry therefore lives in APLP.txt, which holds two 3x4 matrices (24 numbers) in 58 files; GE_SCN3's holds 48 numbers.

The ROI boxes are not per-vertebra L3-L5 boxes. roi_config.json has one unlabelled box per view (roi_ap, roi_lp) plus image sizes and the author's local paths (<another author's local path>/CODEZ/HTIC_IITM_Internship/...). Nothing names L3-L5; that level range appears only in the README's TRE text.

The README says the paths 'resolve perfectly with no manual edits'. That is false for 16 of 59 entries. Eleven closed-sawbone entries point to ClosedSawBonesCT/A, which on the Drive sits at closedsawbonedata/ClosedSawBonesCT/A. Five Ganga entries use 'SET1'..'SET4' where the Drive folders are 'SET 1'..'SET 4'. All 118 PNGs are present once those paths are corrected.

Cadaver data: the Drive has datasets-.../BMJH/CAD/SET 1, which is 15 files (8.4 MB) holding one LP X-ray (template header), its outputs and no CT. The cadaver results cannot be reproduced from this release.

The Drive holds more than the 59 scenarios. The folders include BMJH/SKANRAY SCN 1, 2 and 6, which datasets.py does not use; closedsawbonedata/GEM 040620205 SET 1-5; BMJH/ZIEHM/SET 1; a 419 MB Masked_DRR_ImFusion.nii; a 100 MB 'Accuracy study.zip'; two misfiled SIEMENS 'Fluorospot Compact S1' images in BMJH/SKANRAY; and a stray Windows executable (BMJH/ZIEHM/SCN 11/SanDiskSecureAccessV3.1_win.exe, 8.6 MB).

Institutions and sites are broader than HTIC plus Ganga. The X-ray headers name JAIN HOSPITAL, and the folder is BMJH. The CTs name GEM Hospital (GE Optima CT520) for set1/A and the closed sawbones, and MARUTI SCANS AND LABS (Siemens SOMATOM go.Now, 'Inner Ear' protocol) for Thancopen. The Ganga Hospital link rests only on the folder name 'Ganga Data'.

All three CTs are phantoms; I rendered axial slices of each, showing sawbones on stands with no soft tissue. However, the set1/A CT header carries PatientName 'KHALEEL', a personal name. Record it as a header-hygiene issue; the content is not a patient.

Licence: there is no data licence anywhere on the Drive; no LICENSE, README or terms file exists in the tree. Yes. These are real C-arm acquisitions of sawbones phantoms, not DRRs and not MV portal images. I downloaded and viewed examples from every group.
