corrections: Vendor attribution is broader than claimed, and more solid in some places than in others. GE is confirmed as a GE OEC Fluorostar: native DICOM header 'GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS FLUOROSTAR', RF, 2024-09-14, plus burned-in 'GE-OEC Fluorostar'. Skanray is confirmed by a native header ('SKANRAY TECHNOLOGIES', 'JAIN HOSPITAL', StudyDescription 'Lumbar', 2024-11-14). Both native files come from the Drive's BMJH copy, not the '2d_3dRL dataset' folder that datasets.py reads. ZIEHM rests on the folder name only; its wrapped DICOM carries a template header.

The candidate says the Ganga set's device is not stated. It is: the raw Ganga X-rays carry a burned-in 'Cios_Select 21-09-2025' (Siemens). The 11 closed-sawbone scenarios are also Cios Select (burned-in 'Cios_Select 02-05-2026'). The 5 Thancopen X-rays have a native header 'SIEMENS Healthineers' XA 'Raw Data' (2026-03-26). So 25 of the 59 scenarios were acquired on Siemens units, not GE/Skanray/Ziehm.

'Ganga Hospital' is not stated in any primary source. The path is only 'Ganga Data/Accuracy study/ganga'. The images show the set1 sawbones phantom, which shares the set1/A CT and an identical gt_pose; they are not clinical subjects.

The 0.74181640625 mm pixel spacing in datasets.py is not a physical property of these C-arms. Every processed DICOM (IP/APIP.dcm, AP.dcm, LP.dcm, meta/0.dcm), across all vendor folders, carries one stamped template header: Philips AlluraXper, 'TNMSC, Chennai', StudyDate 2020-02-26, 'Head 3D', ImagerPixelSpacing 0.7418. The native Skanray header gives 0.22 mm. Treat DICOM metadata in the processed files as untrustworthy for device terms.

The 'ground-truth 6-DoF pose' is a single constant per CT: 3 distinct values across all 59 scenarios (TARGET.txt 'T0' is identical for every set1 scenario). All per-scenario geometry is in the projection matrices, which come from a 2D bead-grid calibration (outputAP.json: RegistrationType '2D2D', reprojection error 0.66–0.89 px). The README does not document how the CT-to-world ground truth was established.
ROI labels are one [x1,y1,x2,y2] box per view per scenario, not per-vertebra boxes. There are no vertebral level labels in datasets.py; L3–L5 appear only as TRE regions in the README.

'Processed rather than raw' is only half right. The referenced PNGs are processed (80/118 'filtered_xray_*', and the outputs contain dewarped and inpainted images). But raw originals are on the Drive for many scenarios: Thancopen XA_TEST_*.dcm, Ganga spine_image_*.dcm, closed-sawbone *.bmp, and BMJH GE/Skanray native DICOMs.
Anatomy is more than 'lumbar only'. The set1 and closed-phantom CTs include the sacrum, and the closed-phantom AP shows the lumbosacral junction. No femora or full pelvis were seen.

Cadaver data: the Drive has a BMJH/CAD/SET 1 folder with a single lateral X-ray (LP.dcm) that looks like a human specimen, with no AP view. It is not in datasets.py and I found no cadaver CT, so the README's cadaver result cannot be reproduced from the released data.
The CTs are conventional MDCT (GE Optima CT520 twice, Siemens SOMATOM go.Now), not CBCT.

Privacy: the set1 CT DICOM PatientName holds a real personal name (PatientID '3D C-ARM'), even though the scanned object is a phantom. The headers are not de-identified. Burned-in X-ray overlays carry placeholder demographics.

I could not check the Drive folder dates (2026-07-09/10). The repo dates are confirmed: created 2026-06-29, last push 2026-07-15. Institution confirmed as HTIC IIT Madras: the org 'Image Guided Robotic Surgery' lists @htic.iitm.ac.in emails and robotics.hticlab.org.

candidate.name: TROG 15.01 SPARK trial database (KIM prostate SBRT): kV intrafraction and setup-CBCT projections on 5 linacs + planning CT
candidate.why_relevant: The strongest new open NEED A source on the radiotherapy side. It has real kV pelvic projections from three kV imager chains at five sites: Varian TrueBeam (3 centres), Varian Trilogy and Elekta XVI. Each patient has a planning CT, the gantry angle is known per frame, and implanted gold fiducials give independent 2D/3D ground truth for checking a pose. It is a separate trial from the known SPARE set and covers pelvis, not thorax. Caveats: frames taken during MV delivery carry MV scatter. The field is prostate-centred, so the sacrum and coccyx are probably in view and L5 at most at the edge. Every patient has gold markers, and images may be collimated. No image archive was opened. Center5.7z (Elekta, 17.7 GB) is the smallest place to start.

candidate.xray_kind: kV intrafraction projections at 10 Hz through the treatment arcs, plus setup-CBCT projections (MV portal frames also present, out of scope)
candidate.licence: CC BY 4.0 (cite Keall et al., IJROBP 2020;107(3):530-538)

verdicts.access_now: Open and downloadable now, with no login and no request step. DOI 10.25910/qg5d-6058 redirects (302) to the USyd eScholarship handle 2123/31090, which is marked "Access status: Open Access". The handle item itself holds only README.pdf (378.8 KB; metadata flag "workflow.metadata.only Yes"). The data are 12 .7z archives listed as dc.bitstream.url on the public bucket https://ses-data.library.sydney.edu.au/public/31090_Keall/ (AWS S3 behind CloudFront). On 2026-09-21 all 12 returned HTTP 200 with Accept-Ranges: bytes, and plain curl works on the bucket. The handle HTML page returns 403 to plain curl (Cloudflare) but loads with Chrome TLS impersonation (curl_cffi). The bucket directory listing is AccessDenied, so the URLs must come from the record. Download was verified, not assumed. I range-fetched and decoded five LZMA2 blocks (about 130 MB in total) from Center5.7z and Center2_IntrafractionImages_Patient01-04.7z. This yielded valid Elekta .his frames, a Frames.xml, Varian 32-bit TIFF frames, a frame-info CSV and DICOM CT, and the frames render as real pelvic kV images. Archive sizes (Content-Length), with Last-Modified 2023-11-30 for all: Center1 113.73 GB; Center2 intrafraction 126.99 / 110.35 / 95.96 / 60.84 / 64.89 GB (patients 01-04 / 05-08 / 09-12 / 13-16 / 17-20); Center2_AllOtherData 1.32 GB; Center3 intrafraction 85.58 GB (patients 01-03) and 59.89 GB (patients 04-05); Center3_AllOtherData 0.53 GB; Center4 222.70 GB; Center5 17.68 GB. Total 960.45 GB compressed; about 3.52 TB uncompressed, summed from the 7z headers. The second DOI, 10.58118/p5ks-zh06 (TROG), is only a HeSANDA catalogue record, not a data copy. Its landing page says "Access can be requested via the Health Data Australia catalogue ... or email [e-mail withheld]" and links back to the USyd handle.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. DataCite rightsList for 10.25910/qg5d-6058 gives "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International", SPDX cc-by-4.0, and the handle record says dc.rights "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0". The README asks users to cite Keall et al., IJROBP 2020;107(3):530-538. The TROG DataCite record 10.58118/p5ks-zh06 carries no rights statement. The anonymisation and analysis code repository (now github.com/Image-X-Institute/SPARK_Data_Analysis_Code, redirected from ACRF-Image-X-Institute) has no licence file according to the GitHub API. The data paper (Sengupta et al., Med Phys 2025;52(3):1941-1949, 10.1002/mp.17529, PMC11880642) is itself CC BY.
verdicts.counts: 48 patients, 5 fractions each. Per centre, from data paper Table 1 and confirmed by archive folder names: Center1 has 9 patients (TrueBeam, .tiff); Center2 20 (TrueBeam); Center3 5 (TrueBeam); Center4 10 (Trilogy, .hnd); Center5 4 (Elekta XVI, .his). File counts come from the 7z headers of all 12 archives, read by HTTP range, not from a full download. Entries under KV folders total about 620k and under MV folders about 476k, so about 1.10M frames; the "about 1 million" claim is confirmed. TrueBeam kV TIFFs: 404,248, of which 100,471 (24.9%) belong to KIM session 0, typically 503 frames per fraction sweeping about 360 degrees (the setup CBCT sweep). Center4: 279,590 .hnd files. Center5: 55,503 .his kV frames, each 524,388 bytes, which is 512x512 16-bit (confirmed by Frames.xml Width/Height 512), plus 91 _Frames.xml files, and no MV frames. Uncompressed sizes: Center1 452 GB; Center2 intrafraction 581 + 483 + 433 + 269 + 285 GB; Center3 382 + 267 GB; Center4 326 GB; Center5 30.1 GB. The data paper's "3.6 Tb" matches the uncompressed total (about 3.52 TB), not the 0.96 TB download.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real kV projections of living patients, verified by decoding and rendering frames: laptop-scratchpad:spark\tb_frames.png and ...\spark\c5_frames2.png. TrueBeam frames are 1024x774 uint32 TIFFs written by the Matrox Imaging Library. The gantry angle is the last underscore-separated number in each file name, and each fraction has a Ch1_frame_info.csv of (file, angle, timestamp). Elekta frames are HIS (id 0x7000, 68+32-byte header) at 5.5 Hz. Their Frames.xml gives per-frame GantryAngle, DeltaMs, MVOn, and UCentre/VCentre (panel offset); in the frame set I opened, UCentre is 112.6 mm (preset "Pelvis M20", field "POST CB").
verdicts.anatomy: Two very different fields of view, confirmed by rendering. (1) Setup-CBCT sweeps show a wide pelvis: TrueBeam KIM session 0, and the Elekta "POST CB" set. In them, acetabula, femoral heads, pubis, ilium, bowel gas and three gold seeds are visible (Center2 Patient01 Fx01 around gantry 300-308 degrees; Center5 Patient02 Fx05). (2) Frames from the treatment arcs are tightly collimated to a small square around the prostate: TrueBeam sessions 1 and 2 (Center2 Patient01 Fx01), and Elekta intrafraction frames (Center5 Patient03 Fx01). On the TrueBeam frames the square is roughly 250x280 px of 1024x774, about 10 cm at isocentre at 0.388 mm/px; this is estimated from the render, not measured. The square contains the pubic symphysis and the seeds, with no sacrum or lumbar spine. Several Elekta intrafraction frames were nearly featureless for a reason I did not establish. So for spine work only about 25% of the kV frames (the setup-CBCT sweeps) are wide-field. Whether L5 or S1 appear even in those was not established: I rendered only oblique angles in two fractions. I did not measure the SI extent; the TrueBeam panel covers about 300 x 397 mm at isocentre, centred on the prostate.
verdicts.paired_ct: Mostly yes, with one gap and one bonus. Grouping the 7z-header file sizes by 512x512 slice size, 47 of 48 patients have a 512x512 CT series. Center5 Patient02 has none. Its "CT images" folder (1,188 files) is Elekta XVI CBCT reconstructions: I opened 148 of them, which report Manufacturer ELEKTA, model "Elekta XVI" and ImageType DERIVED/SECONDARY, at 270x270 and 410x410 with 1 mm pixels and 2 mm slices. By size, the 1,188 files are 132 slices times 5 volumes plus 132 times 4. So a planning CT appears to be missing for that patient; this rests on sizes plus the 148 opened files, and I did not open all 1,188. Center5 Patient01 has both a 512x512 series and XVI CBCT reconstructions, so the same-session CBCT volumes are a bonus there. Center5 Patient03's planning CT, opened: Philips Brilliance Big Bore, ImageType ORIGINAL/PRIMARY/AXIAL/HELIX, 512x512, 1.17 mm pixels, 2 mm slices. It has 207 slices, about 41 cm craniocaudal; the 80 slices I decoded span z -168 to +244 mm. RTSTRUCT, RTPLAN and RTDOSE (RS/RP/RD.dcm) are present per patient, and centroid files hold the planned seed positions.
corrections: The 3.6 TB figure is the UNCOMPRESSED size (about 3.52 TB summed from the 7z headers; the data paper says '3.6 Tb'). The actual download is 12 archives totalling 960.45 GB.

The Center2 sizes are wrong. The five intrafraction archives are 126.99 / 110.35 / 95.96 / 60.84 / 64.89 GB, not '110-127 GB per 4 patients'. There is also Center2_AllOtherData.7z (1.32 GB), which holds the CT, plans and logs. Center3 is 85.58 and 59.89 GB plus Center3_AllOtherData.7z (0.53 GB). Center1 113.73, Center4 222.70 and Center5 17.68 GB are confirmed.

The TROG DOI 10.58118/p5ks-zh06 is not a copy of the data. It is a HeSANDA catalogue record whose page says access is 'requested via the Health Data Australia catalogue' or by email, and it links back to the USyd handle. It carries no licence.

The angle recorded in the TIFF file names, the HND header and Frames.xml is typed 'MV gantry' in README and paper Table 1. The kV source sits 90 degrees from the MV beam, so the kV projection angle must be derived. The KIM logs' 'Gantry' column is described as the kV gantry angle.

Elekta (Center5) is imaged at 5.5 Hz, not 10 Hz (data paper; Frames.xml DeltaMs about 183 ms). Its frames are stored at 512x512 (Frames.xml Width/Height; file size 524,388 B), not the 1024x1024 the README lists. With the README's '0.4 mm at isocentre' pixel, 1024 px and 512 px cannot both hold; the true pixel pitch was not resolved.
Center4 (Trilogy) is 1024x768 with SDD 1.8 m, not 1024x774 or 1024x1024. Center1 MV frames share the kV size, and Centers 2 and 3 MV frames are 1190x1196.
'Each patient has a planning CT' is contradicted for Center5 Patient02. Its CT folder has only Elekta XVI CBCT reconstructions (DERIVED/SECONDARY, 270x270 and 410x410) and no 512x512 slices.

'Setup-CBCT projections' are not a separate labelled set. No path contains 'CBCT'. On TrueBeam they are the KIM session-0 frames (Ch1_0_*; 100,471 of 404,248 kV TIFFs, about 503 per fraction). At Elekta they sit in XVI image folders, e.g. field 'POST CB'. The README says only that the KIM-log figures mark which data points belong to the setup CBCT.

Treatment-arc kV frames are tightly collimated to about a 10 cm square around the prostate (rendered at TrueBeam Center2 Patient01 Fx01 and at Elekta Center5 Patient03 Fx01). They show the pubic symphysis and seeds and no sacrum or spine. Only the setup-CBCT sweeps (about 25% of kV frames) are wide-field pelvis, so the candidate's 'about 1 million frames' overstates the frames useful for spine work by roughly fourfold.

'No image archive was opened' is no longer true. Five blocks were decoded by HTTP range from Center5.7z and Center2_IntrafractionImages_Patient01-04.7z, and frames and CT were rendered and read. The remaining archives were checked by header listing only.

Dates: the handle gives dc.date.issued 2023-04-12, and every archive file's Last-Modified is 2023-11-30, so the files were re-uploaded then. The data paper is Med Phys 2025;52(3):1941-1949, first online 2024-11-23.
The analysis-code repository moved to github.com/Image-X-Institute/SPARK_Data_Analysis_Code and has no licence file.
Minor: Center2 Patient06 Fx04 has 2,859 .hnd kV frames at a TrueBeam site, while every other TrueBeam fraction is .tiff. I did not establish why.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real clinical kV projections of 48 living patients, not DRRs, not simulations and not MV portal images (MV frames are kept in separate MV folders). I pulled single LZMA2 blocks out of Center1, Center3 (Patient04-05), Center4 and Center5 using HTTP Range requests and rendered frames myself. They show real anatomy, genitalia, couch rails, three gold markers, and horizontal MV-scatter banding on frames taken while the beam was on. Center5 Patient01 Fx01 is one example: in the treatment-arc series, 909 of 1034 kV frames have MVOn=True. Two kinds of kV frame exist. (1) Setup-CBCT projections are full field. They are Ch1_0 in the Varian TIFFs: 503 frames at Center1 P01 Fx01 and 561 at Center3 P04 Fx01, of which about 500 were taken in rotation at about 16 Hz. At Elekta Center5 P01 Fx01 the setup series has 610 frames, preset 'Prostate Seed S20 - Spark', 120 kV, 16 mA, 20 ms, gantry -160 to 180 with MV off, at 4.6 Hz. (2) Treatment-arc frames, which are most of the roughly 1 million images, are tightly collimated to a small square on the prostate markers. That square is about 6 cm at isocentre on Varian Centers 1, 3 and 4 and about 9 cm on Elekta Center5. At Center4 (Trilogy), even the pre-arc 'kV fluoro only' rotation frames I sampled (Frame01407, Frame02529) were collimated. I found no full-field setup CBCT there.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same subject. Every patient has a planning CT with RTSTRUCT, RTPLAN and RTDOSE. I read Center5: Philips Brilliance Big Bore, HFS, 120 kVp, 512x512 at 1.17 mm, 2 mm slices, 348-412 mm craniocaudal. Sagittal and coronal reformats of Center5 Patient01 and Patient03 show the lumbar spine (L5 and above, up to about L2-L3), the sacrum, the coccyx, the pelvis and the proximal femora. A bonus the candidate missed: the CT folder of Center5 Patient01 also holds 10 reconstructed Elekta XVI CBCT volumes (132 slices, 262 mm, 1 mm pixels), and Patient02 has 1188 CT files, which suggests CBCTs as well. Center5 Patient03 and Patient04 have the planning CT only. For Centers 1 and 4, per-patient file counts (about 175-540) point to planning CT only, with a few exceptions I did not open. Caveat: the planning CT was taken before treatment, so the pelvic pose differs from each fraction. RTSTRUCTs have FemHead_L/R, and 'BONES' or 'PELVIC BONES' in 2 of the 4 Center5 patients. No vertebra labels.
verdicts.anatomy: Full-field setup projections, rendered at Center1, Center3 and Center5: in AP view I saw both femoral heads and necks, the proximal femoral shafts, acetabula, obturator foramina, pubic symphysis and rami, the pelvic inlet and the lower iliac wings. The sacrum projects inside the inlet but is largely hidden by bowel gas. A Varian lateral frame (Center1 P01, MV gantry 359) shows the distal sacrum and coccyx posteriorly next to the couch rails. L5 was not in any frame I viewed. The Varian field is 774 detector rows along SI, about 20 cm at isocentre, so it reaches roughly 10 cm above the prostate. The Elekta S20 setup field reaches roughly S1-S2 at its top edge. Treatment-arc frames show only the markers, prostate soft tissue and the edges of the pubis and femoral heads, with no sacrum. The lumbar spine appears only in the planning CT.
verdicts.counts: 48 patients by centre, from Table 1 of the Med Phys data article: Center1 9, Center2 20, Center3 5, Center4 10, Center5 4. 5 fractions each; some fractions are split into Images1/Images2. kV frames I counted from the archive headers: Center1 79,924 kV and 61,714 MV. Center4 156,957 kV (.hnd) and 122,633 MV. Center5 55,503 kV (.his) and no MV. Center3 Patient04-05 35,754 kV and 26,868 MV. Center2 and Center3 Patient01-03 were not listed. The paper's 'approximately 1 million images' is plausible for kV and MV together. The full-field subset is much smaller: about 500-610 setup frames per fraction at Centers 1, 3 and 5. I estimate at most about 100k full-field frames, but that is not measured. Sizes: the download is 0.96 TB compressed. Measured Content-Length: Center1 113.7 GB, Center4 222.7 GB, Center5 17.7 GB. Center2 image archives are 127.0, 110.4, 96.0, 60.8 and 64.9 GB, plus AllOtherData 1.3 GB. Center3 archives are 85.6 and 59.9 GB, plus 0.53 GB. The paper's '3.6 Tb' matches the uncompressed size. Uncompressed sizes I measured: Center1 452 GB, Center4 326 GB, Center5 30.1 GB, Center3 P04-05 267 GB.
verdicts.access_now: Open, with no login. The archives download directly over HTTPS from ses-data.library.sydney.edu.au/public/31090_Keall/*.7z with Accept-Ranges: bytes, so single 7z LZMA2 blocks (about 20-56 MB) can be pulled and decoded without downloading a whole archive. That is how I checked the content. The landing page ses.library.usyd.edu.au returns Cloudflare 403 to plain curl but serves a Chrome-impersonating client (curl_cffi). The TROG record (DOI 10.58118/p5ks-zh06) is only a HeSANDA metadata entry: its access is 'requested via the Health Data Australia catalogue', and it links back to the USyd copy. It is not an open mirror.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the landing page and in the DataCite rights for 10.25910/qg5d-6058. The README asks users to cite Keall et al., IJROBP 2020;107(3):530-538. The data article is Sengupta et al., Med Phys 2025;52(3):1941-1949, epub 23 Nov 2024, doi 10.1002/mp.17529, CC BY.
corrections: Most kV frames are useless for spine work. Treatment-arc intrafraction kV frames are collimated to a square of about 6 cm (Varian, Centers 1, 3 and 4) to about 9 cm (Elekta, Center5) at isocentre on the prostate markers. Only the setup-CBCT projections are full field. The candidate's 'images may be collimated' understates this.

Center4 (Varian Trilogy): the pre-arc 'kV fluoro only imaging' rotation I sampled (P01 Fx01, Frame01407 static and Frame02529 rotating) was collimated too. I found no full-field setup-CBCT projections there, so the claim of 'setup-CBCT projections on 5 linacs' is not supported for Center4.

L5 is not 'at most at the edge': it was absent from every projection I rendered, and the Varian SI field is about 20 cm at isocentre. The sacrum is only partly visible. In AP it is mostly hidden by bowel gas; in lateral the distal sacrum and coccyx show. The lumbar spine, L5 included, appears only in the planning CT.

Center5 (Elekta) frames are stored at 512x512 16-bit (Frames.xml Width/Height 512; .his 524,388 bytes = 100-byte header + 512*512*2), not the README's 1024x1024. Center4 .hnd frames are 1024x768, not 1024x774. The 1024x774 size holds only for the Center1-3 TIFFs (uint32, Matrox frame grabber).

Frame rate is not uniformly 10 Hz. The paper says 5.5 Hz on Elekta; I measured about 4.6-5.2 Hz. Varian setup rotations run at about 16 Hz (median 63 ms) and Varian treatment arcs at about 10.6 Hz (median 94 ms).

The README's 'pixel size at isocenter' of 0.388 mm and 0.4 mm times 1024 gives 397 mm and 410 mm, which are the physical widths of the Varian and XVI kV panels. These values are probably detector-plane pitch, and at isocentre the pixel would be about 1.5x smaller. This is my inference and should be checked before using the geometry for pose.

Total download is about 0.96 TB compressed, not 3.6 TB. 3.6 Tb is the paper's figure and matches the uncompressed size. Center2 per-4-patient archives are 61-127 GB (60.8, 64.9, 96.0, 110.4, 127.0), not 110-127 GB.
The TROG DOI 10.58118/p5ks-zh06 is a by-request metadata record (Health Data Australia / [e-mail withheld]), not an open copy.
Elekta model 'Synergy' is not stated in any primary source. The README says only 'Elekta', and Frames.xml StationName is 'M2Agility'.
Understated in the candidate: reconstructed XVI CBCT volumes are included for at least Center5 Patient01 (10 volumes), alongside the planning CT.

Pose metadata is thinner on Center4. The .hnd header carries only dGantryRtn and dCTProjectionAngle; SAD, SFD, blades and resolution are undefined (99999999). Elekta Frames.xml adds per-frame UCentre/VCentre and MVOn. Varian TIFF angles come from file names plus Ch1_frame_info.csv timestamps. KIM logs give per-frame 3D and 2D marker positions. Triangulation and linac logs are absent for Elekta. There are no vertebra or spine labels anywhere.
The Med Phys data article was published in issue 2025;52(3):1941-1949 (epub 23 Nov 2024).

candidate.name: RTK public patient data: Centre Léon Bérard lung patients 1-2 and POPI (Elekta XVI 4D-CBCT projections + planning CT)
candidate.why_relevant: Real clinical Elekta kV projections of the thorax, with the thoracic spine visible on the lateral views (one pass rendered them). Each projection has a 3x4 matrix, and the rigid CBCT-to-planning-CT transforms are included. A DRR can therefore be rendered at the true pose and compared pixel by pixel, which is direct material for calibrating Elekta flat-panel physics (bowtie, scatter, lag). Only 3 subjects, thorax only, no lumbar spine or pelvis.
candidate.institution: CREATIS / Centre Léon Bérard, Lyon (RTK consortium, Simon Rit)
candidate.device: Elekta Synergy XVI, offset (half-fan) detector
candidate.anatomy: Thorax (thoracic spine on lateral views)
candidate.n_images: About 655 projections per scan (CLBpatient1 CBCT.zip 669 MB, 664 entries; CLBpatient2 837 MB; POPI projections.tgz 270 MB)
candidate.pose_or_labels: geom.xml RTK circular geometry: SID 1000 mm, SDD 1536 mm, gantry angle and 3x4 matrix per projection, detector offset about -119 mm. CBCT2CT.mat/CT2CBCT.mat rigid transforms; cphase.txt; planning 4D CT; displacement fields; motion masks.
candidate.xray_kind: Raw Elekta XVI 4D-CBCT sweep projections (.his 512x512) plus pre-corrected .mha

verdicts.access_now: Open, anonymous download that works right now. The Girder API returns HTTP 200 with a Content-Length for every item, with no login, no request step and no DUA. I streamed CLBpatient1 CBCT.zip, CLBpatient2 CBCT.zip, both planningCT.zip files and POPI projections.tgz to the end; the POPI tar listing finished with exit code 0. The server ignores HTTP Range headers but supports Girder's offset/endByte parameters, which is how I pulled geom.xml and the .mat files out of the zips. I only checked headers on the DVF archives (2.72 GB, 4.02 GB, 1.45 GB), all 200. Girder's own counter for CLBpatient1 CBCT.zip shows 134 completed downloads. The full 10-phase POPI 4D CT is not on Girder. It is live at CREATIS (www.creatis.insa-lyon.fr/~srit/POPI/Images/Dicom: 4DCT-Dicom.tar 774 MB, and a 467 MB MetaImage version); the old tux.creatis links redirect there with a 301.
verdicts.licence: No licence on the data. The Girder RTK collection has an empty 'terms' field and each folder and item has empty descriptions and metadata. The Apache-2.0 licence belongs to the RTK code repository (github RTKConsortium/RTK), not to the data. The POPI-model page (github open-vv/popi-model; the repository itself has no licence) asks users to cite the Léon Bérard Cancer Center & CREATIS and Vandemeulebroucke et al., ICCR 2007, and says downloading means agreeing to that. That is an attribution request, not a licence, and it is written for the CREATIS 4D CT rather than the Girder copies. No ethics or consent statement appears in the MA-ROOSTER paper (Mory, Janssens and Rit, PMB 2016;61:6856, hal-01375767). Redistribution and derivative-use terms are therefore unstated.
verdicts.counts: Actual counts, not the candidate's 'about 655 per scan'. CLBpatient1: 656 .his files (512x512, 16-bit, 524,388 bytes each) and 656 projections with matrices in geom.xml; the 664 zip entries include non-projection files. CLBpatient2: 676 .his and 676 geom.xml projections, 685 zip entries. POPI: 644 .his in projections.tgz (file dates 2007-01-17), 644 projections in geometry.xml, 644 lines in sphase.txt. That is 1,976 real kV frames across 3 subjects, about 670 per subject. The paper says 'approximately 635 projections, 512x512, pixel 0.8x0.8 mm, 360 degrees, 5.48 fps'. Folder totals: CLBpatient1 3.84 GB, CLBpatient2 5.32 GB, POPI 1.87 GB; whole RTK collection 13.4 GB.
verdicts.anatomy: Thorax only. I looked at renders of the raw frames from an earlier pass. The thoracic spine shows on AP views for CLB1, CLB2 and POPI, and on the POPI lateral. There is no lumbar spine or pelvis. CLB1 frames contain an implanted port with metal artefact (the paper mentions metal artefacts in patient 1) and a stereotactic body frame (SBF) honeycomb mesh plus the table. The CLB1 lateral is dominated by the SBF mesh and cut off by the half-fan detector, so vertebrae are not clearly readable on it.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes for all three subjects, with caveats. CLB1 planningCT: 10-phase 4D CT, 512x512x170, 0.879x0.879x2 mm, int16, with 4D.mhd. CLB2 planningCT: 10 phases, 512x512x218, 1.365x1.365x2 mm, no 4D.mhd. That contradicts the paper's statement that both are 512x512x170 at 0.88 mm; the paper names the scanner as a Philips Brilliance Big Bore 16-slice. CLB1 and CLB2 each include CBCT2CT.mat and CT2CBCT.mat. CLB1's transform is an exact axis permutation plus a translation with zero residual rotation, which looks more like an isocentre or setup mapping than a fitted registration. CLB2's has sub-degree rotations, so it looks like a real registration, and it also ships a flipMatrix.mat that flips x. POPI has no .mat transform. On Girder it ships muCT.mha, a float attenuation volume of 360x141x482 in a permuted orientation, plus uchar masks: patient_50, mm_50, mm_50_in_cbct_coordinates, MotionMask and PatientMask. The DICOM 4D CT (10 phases, 512x512x141, 0.977x0.977x2 mm) is only at CREATIS. That POPI's CBCT and CT are the same patient rests on the RTK docs' phrase 'projections of the POPI patient'.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real clinical Elekta Synergy XVI kV projections of living patients, as raw .his frames. CLB1 and CLB2 also ship correctedProjs.mha (666 MB and 687 MB), but per the paper and the RTK docs these are log-transformed and have the SBF and table removed by forward-projecting a masked reconstruction and subtracting it. They are processed images, not detector intensities, so pixel-level physics calibration (bowtie, scatter, lag) has to start from the raw .his. POPI also includes the Elekta XVI database tables FRAME.DBF and IMAGE.DBF for rtkelektasynergygeometry.
corrections: The half-fan claim holds only for CLB1 and CLB2. POPI is not an offset-detector scan: its ProjectionOffsetX runs from -5.2 to +1.3 mm, against -113.95 to -119.3 mm for CLB1 and -112.2 to -116.4 mm for CLB2. The device field 'offset (half-fan) detector, offset about -119 mm' is wrong for POPI.
Projection counts are 656 (CLB1), 676 (CLB2) and 644 (POPI), not 'about 655 per scan'. The '664 entries' figure is the whole CLB1 zip, not the number of projections.

The planning 4D CT is on Girder only for CLB1 and CLB2. POPI's Girder folder holds a single-phase float attenuation volume (muCT.mha) and masks; the 10-phase POPI 4D CT is hosted separately at CREATIS.

Rigid CBCT-to-CT transforms exist only for CLB1 and CLB2. CLB1's is a pure axis permutation plus translation with no fitted rotation, so it may be a setup or isocentre mapping rather than a registration. POPI has no .mat and instead gives a mask and muCT resampled into CBCT coordinates.
The CLB2 planning CT is 512x512x218 at 1.365 mm in-plane, not the 512x512x170 at 0.88 mm the MA-ROOSTER paper states for both patients.

The pre-corrected .mha projections are log-transformed with the stereotactic body frame and table subtracted. They are not raw pre-corrections usable for detector-physics calibration; only the .his frames are raw.

The 'lung-cancer patients' diagnosis is not stated for these specific subjects in the primary sources I read. The paper calls them clinical CBCT acquisitions of two patients in a thoracic radiotherapy context with tumour tracking. The institution comes from the CLB folder names and the author affiliations (Centre Léon Bérard), not from an explicit statement in the paper.
Evidence URL rtkelektasynergygeometry/README does not document these patients. Its example data (item 5be973478d777f2179a26e1c, elekta.tgz, 619 MB) sits in the Catphan 503 phantom folder.

No licence exists. 'None stated' is accurate for Girder, but there is also no ethics, consent or data-use statement. The only terms are POPI's citation guideline, and the Apache-2.0 licence covers the RTK code only.
Frames also contain an implanted port with metal artefact (CLB1) and the SBF mesh plus table, which complicates pixel-by-pixel DRR comparison against a CT that may or may not include the same frame.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. I downloaded and rendered the .his frames at gantry 0, 60, 180, 240 and 270 degrees for all three subjects. They are real clinical kV chest projections, not DRRs. They show lungs with vessel detail, the heart, clavicles, ribs and the diaphragm. CLB1 has an implanted port reservoir, and the couch rails are visible at some angles. The source-to-detector distance of 1536 mm is the Elekta XVI kV imager, not the MV portal imager. Raw .his files are 100-byte header plus 512x512 uint16, and the values are inverted (air near 0). They need att = -log((65536 - raw)/65536), not -log(raw).
verdicts.paired_ct: CLB1: 10-phase 4D planning CT (planningCT/00-90.raw, 512x512x170, 0.879x0.879x2 mm, about 340 mm craniocaudal), plus CBCT2CT.mat and CT2CBCT.mat. CLB2: 10-phase 4D planning CT (512x512x218, 1.365x1.365x2 mm, about 436 mm), plus CBCT2CT.mat, CT2CBCT.mat and an extra flipMatrix.mat (x-flip) whose use is not documented. The RTK 4D ROOSTER page describes these as 'transform matrices to change from CT to CBCT coordinates and back' for the two MA-ROOSTER patients. POPI: the Kitware folder has no planning 4D CT and no CBCT2CT/CT2CBCT matrices. It has one static volume, muCT.mha (attenuation units, 360x141x482 at 0.977/2/0.977 mm, already in CBCT coordinates). Its dimensions match the POPI-model preprocessed 4D CT (482x360x141, Philips Brilliance Big Bore). It also has masks at 512x512x141. The full POPI 4D CT is hosted separately at creatis.insa-lyon.fr/~srit/POPI (returns HTTP 200). Only the RTK docs ('the POPI patient') state that the POPI CBCT and the POPI CT are the same subject. The CBCT was acquired 2007-01-17 (IMAGE.DBF); the CT acquisition date is not stated.
verdicts.anatomy: Thorax only. The projections run from the upper thorax or shoulders down to the diaphragm domes. The craniocaudal field of view at the isocentre is 512 x 0.8 mm / 1.536 = 267 mm (IMAGE.DBF MMPIX 0.518 mm at isocentre). I mapped that field onto each planning CT through CBCT2CT and rendered coronal bone MIPs with the field marked. In both CLB CTs, rib-bearing vertebrae continue about two levels below the lower edge of the field, so the lowest vertebra projected is about T10-T11. Cone magnification at the spine (about ±13 mm) does not change that. POPI's lower field edge sits just below the diaphragm dome, and the POPI CT itself ends 29 mm lower. No lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis appears in any projection. Vertebrae are visible on the lateral views, most clearly in POPI; the half-fan CLB laterals cover only part of the AP depth.
verdicts.counts: 3 patient subjects: CLBpatient1, CLBpatient2 and POPI. The same Public folder also holds Catphan 503/504, Moving Phantom, Noisy Phantom and Gate-simulation folders, which are not patient data. One CBCT sweep per subject. Projection counts: CLB1 656 .his (CBCT.zip 669,142,487 B, 664 zip entries including the folder and 7 non-projection files). CLB2 676 .his (837,461,870 B, 685 entries). POPI 644 .his (projections.tgz 269,638,195 B). Total 1,976 projections. Each geometry file has matching <Projection> counts (656/676/644), and each sweep covers about 0.4-360 degrees. CLB1 and CLB2 also include correctedProjs.mha: log-transformed, table-removed float stacks, 504x504 at 0.8 mm. POPI has no corrected stack.
verdicts.licence: None stated. The data.kitware.com RTK collection has terms "" and no licence file is present in any folder. The POPI-model page (github open-vv/popi-model) sets citation guidelines for the POPI 4D CT ('By downloading this data, you agree to follow these guidelines'): credit the Léon Bérard Cancer Center and CREATIS, and cite Vandemeulebroucke et al. 2007. Nothing states terms for the projection data.
verdicts.access_now: Open and anonymous. All three CBCT archives, both planning-CT zips, POPI projections.tgz, muCT.mha, geometry.xml and the DBF files downloaded without login on 2026-09-21 through the Girder API (api/v1/item/<id>/download). The server ignores HTTP Range requests and always sends the whole file.
corrections: Projection counts are 656 (CLB1), 676 (CLB2) and 644 (POPI), not 'about 655 per scan'. The 664 figure is zip entries; it includes the folder and 7 non-projection files.

POPI does not use an offset (half-fan) detector. Its ProjectionOffsetX is about -5.1 mm, so the detector is centred. Only CLB1 (-119.25 mm) and CLB2 (-116.3 mm) are offset. 'Detector offset about -119 mm' describes CLB1 only.

The POPI Kitware folder has no CBCT2CT.mat or CT2CBCT.mat and no planning 4D CT. It has one static attenuation volume, muCT.mha, already in CBCT coordinates, plus masks. The 4D CT is hosted separately on the POPI-model site. The claim that rigid transforms are included for all subjects is wrong for POPI.
POPI has no pre-corrected .mha projections. correctedProjs.mha exists only for CLB1 and CLB2. POPI's phase file is sphase.txt, not cphase.txt.

CLB1's CBCT2CT.mat is a pure axis permutation plus translation (0 0 1 -94.2 / 1 0 0 33.1 / 0 -1 0 -416), with no rotational registration component. CLB2's transform has about 0.8-0.9 degrees of rotation and comes with an extra flipMatrix.mat (x-flip) whose use is not documented. Whether these are accurate patient registrations or coordinate-convention alignments is not stated.

'Lung-cancer patients' is not stated in any primary source I could open. The MA-ROOSTER abstract (PMID 27588815) says 'two patients' and discusses tumour location in the free-breathing thorax. The RTK docs say only 'patient'. The diagnosis is unverified.

The per-projection 3x4 matrices come from Elekta's scanner geometry (FRAME.DBF / IMAGE.DBF via rtkelektasynergygeometry), not from a per-frame 2D/3D registration. 'A DRR at the true pose' also depends on the unverified CBCT-to-CT transforms, respiratory phase, and the unstated interval between the planning CT and the CBCT.
Raw .his intensities are inverted (air near 0, attenuating tissue near 60,000). A physics-calibration pipeline that takes -log(raw) gets the contrast backwards.

There are no vertebral labels or landmarks on the projections. The only labels are motion masks, patient masks and respiratory phase signals, plus displacement fields (DVFs.zip 2.7/4.0 GB, POPI dvf.tgz 1.45 GB). The POPI-model's manual landmarks are lung landmarks on the CT.
The rtkelektasynergygeometry evidence page links elekta.tgz in the 'Catphan 503' folder, which is phantom data, not patient data.

candidate.name: CHIRP: Collection of Head Images during RadiotheraPy (Varian TrueBeam kV projections + planning CT + CBCT)
candidate.why_relevant: Open real TrueBeam kV projections (during VMAT and setup CBCT) of the head and neck, with the cervical spine expected in the field (not viewed). Each patient has a planning CT, CBCTs and CBCT-to-CT registration files. It adds a second Varian kV chain for physics calibration. Cervical levels only.
candidate.institution: Image X Institute, University of Sydney; Blacktown Hospital
candidate.device: Varian TrueBeam OBI (XIM); planning CT Siemens Somatom Definition AS 64
candidate.anatomy: Head and neck (cervical spine expected in field; not verified)
candidate.subjects: 30 living head-and-neck cancer patients (PAT01-PAT32 excluding 08 and 27; replans for 11 and 12)
candidate.n_images: Per-patient kV archives (PAT01kVImages.7z 5.8 GB); CBCTs.7z 1.27 GB; Planning CTs 1.42 GB
candidate.pose_or_labels: Gantry angle in each XIM header; Scan.xml CBCT geometry; CBCT-to-planning-CT registration files; RTSTRUCT, plans, dose
candidate.xray_kind: kV projections during treatment + setup CBCT projections

verdicts.access_now: Open and downloadable now, with no login or request step. The SES DSpace record hdl 2123/34250 (DOI 10.25910/32wt-4973) says "Access status: Open Access" and "workflow.metadata.only No". It lists 36 dc.bitstream.url links on ses-data.library.sydney.edu.au (S3 behind CloudFront). A HEAD request to all 36 returned HTTP 200 with a Content-Length to plain curl. accept-ranges is bytes. Two access caveats: (1) The landing page and CHIRP_README.txt on ses.library.usyd.edu.au sit behind Cloudflare, which returns 403 to plain curl; the pages returned 200 when fetched with curl_cffi impersonating Chrome. The data bitstreams are not blocked. (2) Each archive is one solid LZMA 7z folder, so a single projection cannot be pulled by range request unless it lies near the start of the stream. I proved this works by range-fetching the first 12 MB of PAT29kVImages.7z, decompressing it and decoding 4 XIM files. Total download is 117,139,436,022 bytes (about 117.1 GB).
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The DataCite rightsList gives cc-by-4.0 (SPDX), and the SES dc.rights says "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0". The companion PMB paper is also CC BY 4.0 according to Crossref.
verdicts.counts:
There are 30 patients: PAT01–PAT32 with no 08 and no 27, confirmed by the README and the archive listings. Files (bytes, from HEAD):
- 30 per-patient kV archives, 1,881,207,940 (PAT29) to 5,797,799,582 (PAT01), summing to about 114.2 GB.
- Patient CBCTs.7z: 1,267,330,078.
- Patient Planning CTs.7z: 1,422,559,866.
- Patient Dose Files.7z: 160,018,409.
- Patient Structure Sets.7z: 72,328,877.
- Patient Plans.7z: 1,185,298.
- Patient Registration Files.7z: 491,047.
- CHIRP_README.txt: 2.9 KB.

Contents, from 7z header listings rebuilt from range requests:
- kV images: every kV archive holds only FxNN folders, 160 fractions in all (5–7 per patient). Each fraction has one Scan.xml and 265–896 .xim projections (mostly about 502 or about 896), 126,116 XIM in total.
- CBCTs: 30 patient folders, 14,602 DICOM files, 7.69 GB uncompressed.
- Planning CTs: 32 series (30 patients plus replans PAT11_2 and PAT12_2), 231–268 DICOM files each. The archive also contains macOS .DS_Store junk files.
- Registration files: extracted in full, 160 DICOM REG (Spatial Registration Storage) files, one per fraction.
- XIM format: 1024x768 pixels, 0.388 mm pixel size, 20-bit.
verdicts.anatomy: Head and neck. I checked PAT29 Fx01 only, decoding 4 XIM projections at gantry angles 169°, 212°, 278° and 311°. In the lateral and oblique views the upper-to-mid cervical spine (roughly C1 to C4/C5) is visible behind the mandible. Two things overlap it: the mesh of a thermoplastic immobilisation mask, and a metal mandibular reconstruction plate in this patient. The lower neck is cut off by the field edge and the shoulders. In the AP-like view the spine is largely hidden by the mandible. The field is 1024x768 at 0.388 mm on the detector. The header gives SAD about 100 cm and SID about 150 cm, so the field is roughly 26.5 x 19.9 cm at isocentre. Only one patient and fraction was viewed, so cervical coverage in other patients is not verified.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, confirmed by decoding. These are real Varian kV flat-panel projections: XIM magic "VMS.XI", ImageSourceId KVModule, ImageModeId DynamicGainFluoro, continuous mode at 14.8 fps, 100 kVp, 15 mA, 20 ms, large focal spot, titanium foil, "Full Fan V1" collimator. The rendered images show patient anatomy, a mask and a metal plate. Every per-frame header has GantryRtn and KVSourceRtn (GantryRtn + 90°). StartTime decodes to 2023-09-04. MVBeamOn is 0 and MVDoseRate is 0, so the treatment beam was off during acquisition. These are pre-treatment CBCT projections, not images taken during treatment.
corrections: REFUTED: the candidate says the data include kV projections taken 'during treatment/during VMAT'. They do not. The README says the kV images are 'projections used to create CBCT images'. The paper (section 2.4) says testing used 'kV x-ray images acquired to reconstruct the CBCT volume used for patient setup and positioning prior to treatment'. Every kV archive holds exactly one projection folder per fraction, 160 in all, matching the 160 REG files. The decoded XIM headers show MVBeamOn=0 and MVDoseRate=0. The xray_kind should be 'pre-treatment setup CBCT projection sets (MV beam off)' only.

The paper's own data availability statement (PMB 2025, 10.1088/1361-6560/adf40e) says 'The data cannot be made publicly available... available upon reasonable request from the authors.' The later SES deposit (issued 2025-08-26; S3 files last modified 2025-09-11) supersedes it. The release is real and open, but the paper's statement is out of date.
The paper analysed 17 patients and 3 fractions each. The deposit has 30 patients and 160 fractions, so the dataset is larger than the paper's cohort.

The 'registration files' are 160 rigid DICOM Spatial Registration objects, described as clinical couch shifts. They are not a curated or deformable CBCT-to-CT registration. The paper's ground truth used deformable registration, and that registration is not in the deposit.

The cervical spine is no longer only 'expected': I viewed 4 projections of PAT29 Fx01. The upper-to-mid cervical spine (about C1 to C4/C5) is visible in lateral and oblique views, with thermoplastic mask mesh and a mandibular plate overlapping it. The lower cervical spine is cut off by the field edge and shoulders. Other patients were not checked, and no spine labels of any kind are provided.
The device detail 'OBI' is my inference, not a source statement. The README says only 'Varian TrueBeam'. The XIM headers say AcquisitionSystemVersion 3.0.117.110 and ImageSourceId KVModule.
Scan.xml geometry was not opened because it sits deep inside the solid 7z streams. Its content is taken from the README only.

Access friction: the landing page and README 403 plain curl (Cloudflare), and the archives are solid LZMA 7z (about 117 GB in total; 5.8 GB for PAT01 alone). Getting a whole patient means downloading the whole archive. The per-file byte sizes above were measured, and the per-archive sizes the candidate gives are correct (PAT01 5.80 GB, CBCTs 1.27 GB, Planning CTs 1.42 GB).
Minor: the Planning CT archive contains macOS .DS_Store and ._.DS_Store files. The directory names in the listings are PAT01…PAT32; the README's 'Pat32kVImages' spelling is a typo.

xray_kind is wrong. There are no kV images taken during VMAT, only pre-treatment (setup) CBCT projections. The README defines each PATxxkVImages folder as 'kV images (projections) used to create CBCT images'. The paper abstract says its test data were 'kV x-ray images used to reconstruct the pre-treatment CBCT volume'. Each of the 160 kV fraction folders holds exactly one Scan.xml with AcquisitionType KV3D. I decoded every frame of PAT29 (2,283 frames over 5 scans) and the first 403 frames of PAT01 Fx01: MVBeamOn=0 and MVDoseRate=0 on all of them. The DataCite wording 'conventional images for VMAT treatments' is the source of the mistake.

n_images was given only as archive sizes. The actual count, from the 7z headers of all 30 archives, is 126,116 .xim projections in 160 CBCT scans. That is 5 to 7 scans per patient (first, early, middle and last fractions) and 265 to 896 frames per scan. Each scan also starts with one zero-size, 0 kV frame. The release totals 117.1 GB over 36 files. The kV archives range from 1.88 GB (PAT29) to 5.80 GB (PAT01).

There are two acquisition protocols, not one. 'Head and Shoulders' scans cover a full 360 degrees at 125 kV, 15 mA and 20 ms, half fan with the imager offset -160 mm, about 896 frames over about 61 s. 'Head' scans cover 200 degrees (21 to -179) at 100 kV, full fan, about 501 frames over about 34 s. Both use nominal SID 1500 mm, SAD 1000 mm, 1024x768 pixels at 0.388 mm and 15 fps.

Anatomy has now been viewed (the candidate said 'not viewed'). A PAT01 Head-and-Shoulders scan shows the mandible and teeth, cervical spine, shoulders, clavicles, upper ribs and lung apices, plus the mask baseplate. PAT29 Head-mode scans are centred on the skull and mandible (which has a reconstruction plate); only the upper cervical spine appears, at the bottom edge. In lateral half-fan frames the posterior spine is cut off and the shoulders hide the lower C-spine. The field at isocentre is about 26.5 x 20 cm. There is no lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis in any image. Cervical and upper thoracic is the most that is present.

The paired CT and CBCT claim is confirmed. Planning CTs are Siemens SOMATOM Definition AS neck protocols, 2 mm slices at 1.37 mm in-plane. They span 490 mm (PAT01) and 504 mm (PAT02), from above the vertex to the upper thorax. CBCTs are Varian 'Patient Verification' at 125 kV, 88 slices of 1.99 mm (173 mm). The PatientID is CHIRP01 in the planning CT, the CBCT and the REG file. The CBCT archive has 160 fraction folders across 30 patients, which matches the kV folders.

The pose is nominal, not calibrated. Each XIM header gives GantryRtn, KVSourceRtn, kV source and detector Vrt/Lat/Lng, and couch position. Scan.xml gives nominal SID, SAD, ImagerLat, start/stop angles, bowtie and couch settings. No per-projection projection matrices, flexmap or detector-calibration folders are included; each folder has only Proj_*.xim and Scan.xml. The 160 REG files are DICOM Spatial Registration 'ONLINEMATCH' rigid CBCT-to-planning-CT transforms (the couch-shift match). They are not projection-to-CT poses.

The labels are radiotherapy contours only. There are 32 RTSTRUCT sets: 30 patients plus the replans 11_2 and 12_2. Organ-at-risk contours include spinal cord, brainstem, parotids and mandible, and 29 of the 32 sets have a GTV ROI. There are no vertebra or level labels and no bone labels except the mandible. Minor issue: the PAT12 and PAT12_2 structure sets carry a hashed PatientID ('GbdsNC2z...') instead of CHIRP12.

The subject count is confirmed at 30 patients (PAT01 to PAT32 without 08 and 27). The replans 11_2 and 12_2 add planning CT, structure set, plan and dose sets only, not extra kV images. The linked paper used 17 of the 30 patients.

Access is open: all 36 files at ses-data.library.sydney.edu.au/public/34250_Gardner/ return HTTP 200 without a login. However, the landing page and README on ses.library.usyd.edu.au are behind Cloudflare, which returns 403 to plain curl; they load with Chrome TLS impersonation. Every archive is a single solid LZMA stream, so reaching any one frame means decompressing that patient's archive from the start.

Two date and device details. The landing page date is 2025-08-26; DataCite shows the DOI created 2025-08-26 and registered 2025-09-16. Scan.xml gives MachineType HET and MachineId OBK15, a TrueBeam, and the XIM header gives ImageSourceId KVModule, so these are kV images, not MV portal images.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes: real kV flat-panel acquisitions on a Varian TrueBeam. They are not DRRs, not simulated and not MV portal images. The XIM headers show ImageSourceId=KVModule, KVBeamOn=1, measured air kerma and normalisation-chamber readings, 100 or 125 kV, and MVBeamOn=0. The rendered frames show quantum noise, the immobilisation mask baseplate and couch hardware. Every image is a pre-treatment CBCT projection; none was taken during treatment delivery.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same subject. There is a planning CT for each of the 30 patients (plus replans 11_2 and 12_2): Siemens SOMATOM Definition AS, 2 mm slices, about 49-50 cm from above the vertex to the upper thorax. There is a reconstructed CBCT for each of the 160 kV scans (Varian, 125 kV, 173 mm). There is also a rigid CBCT-to-planning-CT REG file for each scan. PatientIDs match between the CT and CBCT.
verdicts.anatomy: Head and neck. Visible: skull and face, mandible and teeth, cervical spine, and in the Head-and-Shoulders scans the shoulders, clavicles, upper ribs and lung apices. How much cervical spine shows depends on the protocol. Head-mode scans show only the upper C-spine, at the bottom edge. Lateral half-fan frames cut off the posterior spine, and the shoulders hide the lower C-spine. No lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis appears in any projection, CT or CBCT.
verdicts.counts: 30 patients and 160 CBCT scans (5-7 per patient). There are 126,116 .xim projections, 265-896 per scan, of which about 160 are zero-exposure first frames. The 32 planning CT series hold 7,980 slices; the 160 CBCT reconstructions hold 14,602 slices; there are 160 REG files, 32 RTSTRUCT, 32 RTPLAN and the dose files. Download size is 117.1 GB.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0 (landing page, and the DataCite rightsList 'cc-by-4.0'). The linked PMB paper is also CC BY.
verdicts.access_now: Open. All 36 files returned HTTP 200 without a login on 2026-09-21 from ses-data.library.sydney.edu.au/public/34250_Gardner/. The landing page and README 403 plain curl behind Cloudflare but load with a browser-like TLS client. The archives are solid 7z (LZMA), so reading any frame requires streaming the patient's archive from its start.

candidate.name: Projections of Pelvis phantom CBCT (CIRS 801-P on Elekta XVI, moving-blocker scatter study; Zhao et al., PLOS One 2017)
candidate.why_relevant: Real kV CBCT sweep projections of an anthropomorphic pelvis phantom with per-view angles. The unblocked scan (Pelvis_WOB) can be reconstructed into a CBCT of the same object. The two moving-blocker scans carry lead-strip shadows, which give a measured scatter signal on real Elekta projections for checking a scatter model directly. It is the phantom counterpart to COBRA's Elekta data. There is no separate diagnostic CT. The device comes from the paper; one pass found it not stated in the figshare record. A sister record holds Catphan projections (10.6084/m9.figshare.5663467).
candidate.institution: University of Texas at Arlington / UT Southwestern (Cong Zhao, Jin, Wang)
candidate.device: Elekta Synergy XVI (per paper): 512x512 at 0.8 mm, SAD 1000 mm, SDD 1536 mm
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis (CIRS 801-P anthropomorphic)
candidate.subjects: 1 phantom, 3 scans (no blocker; blocker at two settings)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Gantry angle file per scan; SAD/SDD in paper
candidate.xray_kind: kV CBCT sweep projections (radiotherapy on-board imager)

verdicts.access_now: Open and downloadable now, with no login. The figshare API (status public, download_disabled false, not embargoed) lists 6 files. ndownloader.figshare.com/files/<id> returns 302 to a presigned S3 GET. I downloaded all three angle files in full and pulled byte ranges of two of the projection files (HTTP 206). Two quirks: the old-style landing URL returned HTTP 202 to curl (a bot challenge), though the API works; and a HEAD request on the S3 redirect returns 403 because the link is signed for GET only, so a HEAD-based link checker would wrongly report the files dead.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The figshare API shows license value 1 and DataCite shows rightsIdentifier cc-by-4.0.
verdicts.counts: 6 files, 2,124,423,080 bytes in total (DataCite gives the same size). Three scans of little-endian float32 512x512 frames: Pelvis_WOB_512x512x674_prj.raw (706,740,224 B, 674 frames), Pelvis_WB_B20G20_L_512x512x679_prj.raw (711,983,104 B, 679 frames) and Pelvis_WB_B20G60_H_512x512x673_prj.raw (705,691,648 B, 673 frames). Each byte count divided by 512*512*4 gives exactly the frame count in the file name. That is 2,026 projections in all. Each scan has a matching _ang.raw of float32 angles in degrees (674, 679 and 673 values) running from about -180 to +180 with a mean step of about 0.53 degrees, so one full 360-degree sweep per scan. Pixel values are raw intensities from 0 to 65536, with unattenuated air clipped at 65536. They are not log-normalised.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are measured kV CBCT projections of a physical CIRS 801-P pelvis phantom on an Elekta Synergy XVI, according to the paper. They are not simulated. It is a phantom, not a patient, and the images are radiotherapy on-board CBCT, not fluoroscopy. I rendered four frames: the blocker scans show lead-strip shadows, dense in B20G20 and sparse in B20G60.
verdicts.anatomy: A CIRS 801-P anthropomorphic pelvis. In a rendered frame from the unblocked scan (frame 0), lower lumbar vertebral bodies and disc spaces are visible above the sacrum and pelvis at the top of the field. I did not count the levels; it looks like roughly two or three. It is a half-fan (offset-detector) acquisition, so the phantom fills about half the detector width.
verdicts.paired_ct: Not released. The paper says a Philips multi-detector CT (MDCT) of both phantoms was acquired as the gold standard, but no CT volume is in the figshare record. The only same-object volume is one you reconstruct yourself from the unblocked Pelvis_WOB scan.
corrections: Projection count is exactly 2,026 (674 + 679 + 673), not 'about 2,030'. Files are float32 512x512 raw, 2,124,423,080 bytes in total.

'There is no separate diagnostic CT' is misleading. The paper (Section 2.4) says a Philips MDCT of both phantoms was acquired and used as the gold standard. It exists but is not in the figshare record, and the Data Availability statement names only the two projection records. Report it as acquired and unreleased, not as nonexistent.

Reconstruction is harder than the candidate implies. The pelvis scan is half-fan (offset detector) per the paper, and neither the paper text nor the figshare record gives the detector lateral offset or the rotation-centre shift. There is no air/flood scan in the pelvis record (the Catphan sister record has Air-WOB; this one does not), and the pixels are raw intensities clipped at 65536. The offset and I0 have to be estimated.

The device and geometry come only from the paper, not from the figshare record. The paper states Elekta Synergy XVI, SAD 1000 mm, SDD 1536 mm, a 360-degree sweep in about 2 min, 120 kVp and 80 mA/20 ms for the pelvis. The figshare record has a two-line description ('File names are the geometry size'), no README and no geometry file.

The paper's '512 x 512 pixels at 0.8 mm' is written as if it applied to both systems. The Catphan sister record (10.6084/m9.figshare.5663467), however, holds 1024x768x678 frames acquired on a Varian TrueBeam OBI (SDD 1500 mm, blocker simulated by manual shift), not on the Elekta. That record is 17.06 GB across 8 scans plus one air scan.

The record does not say which blocker setting each file name means. The paper says the pelvis blocker had 3.2 mm lead strips at 9.6 mm and 3.2 mm pitch. Matching B20G20 to the 3.2 mm pitch and B20G60 to the 9.6 mm pitch is my inference from the rendered strip spacing and the 1:3 gap ratio. What the _L/_H suffixes mean is not stated anywhere I found.

The figshare title is 'Projections of Pelvis phantom (CBCT)', with Cong Zhao as sole author, version 1, published 2017-12-04. The paper's affiliations are University of Texas at Arlington (Physics) and UT Southwestern (Radiation Oncology), which matches the institution claimed.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed, with one qualification: the subject is a phantom, not a patient. Paper Section 2.4 says the pelvis data were acquired on an Elekta Synergy XVI (kV on-board imager), half-fan, 120 kVp, 80 mA/20 ms. I range-downloaded 8 frames (4 WOB, 2 per blocker scan). They are measured flat-panel frames and not DRRs: the values are integer-valued float32 raw intensities, lead-strip shadows are visible in both blocker scans, there is a detector edge band at the bottom rows, and the air is pinned at exactly 65536 in every frame (11-37% of pixels). They are kV, not MV portal images. The figshare record itself names no device, kVp or phantom model. Those facts come only from the paper.
verdicts.paired_ct: No CT or CBCT volume is released. The paper says a Philips MDCT of both phantoms was acquired and used as the gold standard (Sections 2.4 and 2.5, Table 1, Figs 11/13/15). The figshare record has only 6 files, 3 x prj.raw and 3 x ang.raw, so the MDCT is not deposited. A CBCT can only come from reconstructing Pelvis_WOB yourself, which gives the same data rather than an independent volume. That also needs geometry the paper does not state: the half-fan detector lateral offset, the piercing point or flexmap, and I0 (the air region is clipped or normalised at 65536, and there is no pelvis air or flood scan).
verdicts.anatomy: I looked at rendered frames near gantry -90 and +90 degrees (AP/PA). They show the lowest one to two lumbar vertebrae at the top edge of the frame (most likely L5 and part of L4; no source names the level), plus the whole sacrum with foramina, the coccyx, iliac wing, acetabulum, femoral head and proximal femoral shaft, and the pubic symphysis. Because the scan is half-fan, the midline sits near column 400 of 512, so every frame shows one hemipelvis plus about 120 px past midline, and lateral frames are truncated. The phantom is CIRS 801-P, built from Visible Human male data. Its datasheet lists bone, cartilage, spinal cord and vertebral discs, so all frames share one anatomy.
verdicts.counts: 1 phantom, 3 circular 360-degree scans. From the file names and byte sizes (512*512*N*4 bytes, float32): Pelvis_WOB = 674 frames, Pelvis_WB_B20G20_L = 679, Pelvis_WB_B20G60_H = 673, for exactly 2,026 projections and 2,124,423,080 bytes (2.1 GB).
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, confirmed in both the figshare API and DataCite (rightsIdentifier cc-by-4.0). The paper is also CC BY.
verdicts.access_now: Open, with no login. The ndownloader.figshare.com file URLs serve directly and accept HTTP byte-range requests; I pulled single 1 MiB frames that way on 2026-09-21. The figshare record, the PLOS article (HTTP 200), the Europe PMC full text and DataCite all resolve.
corrections: ct_or_cbct_same_subject should be false for anything released. The paper says a Philips MDCT of the phantom was acquired as the benchmark, but it is not in the figshare record, which holds only 3 projection files and 3 angle files. No reconstructed CBCT is shared either. The candidate's line 'There is no separate diagnostic CT' is wrong about the study (an MDCT exists) but right that none is available.

Reconstructing Pelvis_WOB into a CBCT needs parameters that no primary source states. These are half-fan scans (paper Section 2.4), so the detector offset is essential, and neither the record nor the paper gives it. There is also no flexmap or projection matrix and no I0: the air reads exactly 65536 in every inspected frame, which is either clipping or a normalisation constant, and there is no pelvis air or flood scan. The 'measured scatter signal' use also depends on knowing I0.
Every frame is laterally truncated by the half-fan geometry. The midline is near column 400 of 512, so only one hemipelvis plus a margin is in view, which is unlike a centred fluoroscopy frame.
Total projections is exactly 2,026 (674 + 679 + 673), not 'about 2,030'.

No source says which blocker file is which setting. The paper gives two pelvis blocker settings: 3.2 mm strips at 3.2 mm pitch (robustness) and 9.6 mm pitch (boundary effect). By inference from the file names and the rendered strip spacing, B20G20 is the 3.2 mm pitch scan and B20G60 the 9.6 mm pitch scan. The _L and _H suffixes are unexplained.

The angle files carry no documentation. I read them as little-endian float32 gantry angles in degrees from -180 to +180, at a median step of about 0.55 degrees over roughly 360 degrees. That reading is my own, not stated anywhere. Pose is gantry angle only; there are no labels, landmarks or segmentations of any kind.

The 512x512 at 0.8 mm pixel size, SAD 1000 mm, SDD 1536 mm, device, phantom model and kVp/mAs come only from the paper, not from the figshare record. The paper's sentence giving 512x512 at 0.8 mm is written for both systems, yet the sister Catphan files are 1024x768, so that sentence is not accurate for the Varian data.

The sister record 10.6084/m9.figshare.5663467 (Catphan) was acquired on a Varian TrueBeam OBI with a manually shifted blocker, not on the Elekta. It is 1024x768 x 678 frames and includes an Air-WOB scan. It is not Elekta data.
The claim 'phantom counterpart to COBRA's Elekta data' is not supported by any primary source here; COBRA is not mentioned. Treat it as unverified.

The subject is one anthropomorphic phantom (Visible Human male anatomy), not a patient. The lumbar coverage is only the lowest one to two vertebrae at the top edge of the detector, and no source names the level.

candidate.name: RabbitCT C-arm cone-beam CT benchmark: Zenodo archival re-release (496 calibrated projections of a post-mortem rabbit)
candidate.why_relevant: Real C-arm CBCT projections of an animal torso (a rendered volume shows the skull, cervical and upper thoracic spine, ribs and forelimbs). Every one of the 496 views has an exact calibrated 3x4 projection matrix, and there is a reference reconstruction in the same frame. That isolates the image-formation model of a Siemens angiographic C-arm chain at a known pose. The original authors agreed to the re-release, made on 2026-07-08 after the FAU challenge site went offline. Caveats: one animal, and the 'CT' is the reconstruction from the same sweep. RabbitCT benchmarked backprojection, so the projections may already be weighted and filtered rather than raw intensities; check this before intensity calibration. The device (Artis zee) is recalled from the 2009 paper and not named in the record.
candidate.institution: Pattern Recognition Lab, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (Rohkohl, Keck, Hofmann, Hornegger)
candidate.device: Siemens Artis zee angiographic C-arm (from 2009 paper; not stated in Zenodo record)
candidate.anatomy: Whole post-mortem rabbit (spine and torso in field)
candidate.n_images: 496 projections; 512 (2.68 GB) and 1024 (4.83 GB) containers; 256^3 reference volume at 1 mm
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibrated 3x4 projection matrix per projection (world to detector, mm)

verdicts.access_now: Open now, with no login or request. Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.21267885 is status "published" with access_right "open", published 2026-07-08, and stats show 73 downloads. All five files returned HTTP 200 with their full content-length. I downloaded rabbitct_develop-v2.zip (5,206 B) and reference_256.vol (67,108,864 B) in full, and both MD5s matched the API checksums (e71fc9ab..., 1964eb95...). Byte-range reads of rabbitct_512-v2.rctd at five offsets (start, around 2.36 GB, 2.40 GB and the last 1 MB) all succeeded. The original site is gone as the record says: www.rabbitct.com does not respond and www5.cs.fau.de/research/software/rabbitct/ returns 404.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, as declared in the Zenodo metadata (license.id cc-by-4.0) and in README_data.md. The "authors' agreement" to re-release rests only on the uploader's own text in the record notes and README. The uploader shows only as Zenodo owner id 185719. The creators field lists Rohkohl, Keck, Hofmann and Hornegger, but that is metadata, not proof of who uploaded it. I found no independent statement from the authors or FAU. The original distribution terms on rabbitct.com could not be checked: the site is dead and the Wayback Machine was offline when I tried. The original RabbitCT software (GitHub mirror of code.google.com/p/rabbitct) was GPL-2.0.
verdicts.counts:
Exact sizes from the API:
- rabbitct_512-v2.rctd: 2,683,222,552 B
- rabbitct_1024-v2.rctd: 4,830,706,200 B
- reference_256.vol: 67,108,864 B (256^3 float32, values 0 to 4095)
- rabbitct_develop-v2.zip: 5,206 B (rabbitct.h, CMake files, LolaBunny.cpp)
- README_data.md: 2,450 B

Container layout, parsed from the bytes: a 24-byte header (uint32 version=2, S_x=1248, S_y=960, N=496, then two floats, 1.2076 and 24.0, not interpreted). Then 496 records, each a 96-byte float64 3x4 matrix followed by a 1248x960 float32 image. I confirmed matrices at records 0-2 and 492-495, and the records end at byte 2,377,038,360. The rest of each file matches, to the byte, uint16 reference volumes: 512^3 + 256^3 + 128^3 in the 512 file, and 1024^3 + 512^3 + 256^3 + 128^3 in the 1024 file. I saw uint16 values from 0 to 4095 in that region. That layout is inferred from the byte arithmetic; the README does not describe it.

Geometry from the matrices: source about 746-750 mm from the isocentre, rotation about world z, 0.391 degrees per view, spanning about 198 degrees. That confirms a short scan.
verdicts.anatomy: I rendered MIPs of reference_256.vol (a 256 mm cube at 1 mm). They show the skull, the cervical and upper-to-mid thoracic spine, ribs, and both forelimbs (humeri, forearms, paws). A thin metal object (needle or wire) sits in the field, along with table and holder structures. The lumbar spine and pelvis are not in the volume. The candidate's "whole rabbit" wording is wrong: the field runs from the head down to the upper thorax. One post-mortem rabbit.
verdicts.paired_ct: There is no independent CT. The only 3-D data are reconstructions from the same C-arm sweep: reference_256.vol (float32) and the uint16 reference volumes embedded in each .rctd. They share the world frame of the projection matrices. The README says the volume is a 256 mm cube centred on the origin, with voxel size 256 mm / N.
verdicts.real_xray:
The projections come from a real C-arm acquisition but are released only after preprocessing: weighted and ramp-filtered, not raw detector intensities or line integrals. I confirmed this three ways:
1. Pixel statistics: about 70% of pixels are negative and the mean is about 0. Projection 0 runs from -8.34 to 46.4; projections 1 and 2 are similar.
2. The rendered projection is an edge-enhanced relief image.
3. The shipped LolaBunny backprojector only accumulates I_n / w^2, with no filtering or weighting step.
arXiv 1401.7494 says the same: each projection "contains the filtered and weighted intensity values". Ramp filtering removes the DC component, so the data cannot calibrate intensity or image formation without an ill-posed inversion. Only the geometric side, the calibrated projection matrices, is usable as delivered.
corrections: File names are wrong in the candidate and in the record's own description. The actual files are rabbitct_512-v2.rctd, rabbitct_1024-v2.rctd and rabbitct_develop-v2.zip; the README calls this the corrected '-v2 (2012)' release.

The projections are confirmed to be pre-weighted and ramp-filtered, not raw intensities. About 70% of pixels are negative with a mean near zero, the example backprojector applies no filter, and arXiv 1401.7494 says 'filtered and weighted intensity values'. The candidate's claim that this 'isolates the image-formation model of a Siemens angiographic C-arm chain' is refuted for intensities; only the geometry (3x4 matrices) holds.

Device is not primary-sourced. 'Artis zee' appears in neither the Zenodo record, the PubMed abstract nor the two arXiv papers that use RabbitCT; only a ResearchGate listing snippet says 'Artis Zee, Siemens AG'. The 2009 paper is closed access (OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar both report closed), so I could not check its text.

Anatomy: this is not a whole rabbit. The reference volume shows head, cervical and upper-to-mid thoracic spine, ribs and forelimbs, with no lumbar spine or pelvis. A metal needle or wire object is also in the field.

The authors' agreement and the CC BY 4.0 re-licence are asserted only by an unidentified uploader (Zenodo owner 185719). I found no confirmation from the authors or FAU, and the original data terms could not be retrieved.
The .rctd containers also embed uint16 reference volumes at 128/256/512 (and 1024 in the larger file). That is why the files exceed 496 x 4.79 MB; the README does not mention it.

Short scan confirmed from the calibrated matrices: about 198 degrees over 496 views at 0.391 degrees per step, source about 746-750 mm from the isocentre, rotation about world z. 1248x960 float32 per projection.
Sizes are 2.68 GB and 4.83 GB in decimal units; the README's ~2.5 and ~4.5 GB are binary GiB. The two are consistent.

verdicts.real_xray: Real C-arm acquisitions, but not raw images. The Zenodo record calls it "a single high-resolution C-arm CT scan of a post-mortem rabbit". The archived FAU project page says: "The dataset we provide for reconstruction was acquired from a real rabbit with a real C-arm system." So these are not DRRs, not simulations and not MV portal images. However, the stored projections are FDK-preprocessed. I decoded projections 0, 1, 2, 124, 248, 372 and 495 from rabbitct_512-v2.rctd (float32, 1248x960). Each has a mean near 0 and 51–70% negative pixels (proj 0: min -8.3, max 46.4, median -0.0007), and they look edge-enhanced. That is ramp-filtered data, not intensities or line integrals. Contrast fades toward both ends of the sweep (proj 0 and 495 much fainter than 124–372), which fits short-scan (Parker-type) weighting. The bundled LolaBunny module only backprojects with a 1/w^2 weight and applies no filter, which is consistent with filtering having been done beforehand. A later paper from the same lab (arXiv:1401.3615) calls it "a filtered, high resolution CT dataset of a rabbit" and "the preprocessed dataset". Ramp filtering removes the DC term, so raw attenuation images cannot be recovered exactly.
verdicts.paired_ct: Only the reconstruction of the same 496 projections; there is no independent CT. reference_256.vol is a raw 256^3 float32 volume at 1 mm (64 MB; md5 1964eb95… matches Zenodo). Its values run 0–4095, which looks like a 12-bit scale rather than HU. The tail of each .rctd holds further uint16 volume data; from the byte counts these look like reference volumes at 128/256/512 (plus 1024 in the 1024 file), but that is an inference. By construction it shares the frame of the projection matrices.
verdicts.anatomy: I rendered MIPs and mid-slices of reference_256.vol and looked at 7 projections across the sweep. The field covers the cranial half of the rabbit: skull, cervical spine, upper-to-mid thoracic spine with ribs, shoulder girdles and forelimbs. The lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are NOT in the field in the volume or in any projection I viewed. The field also contains the patient table and a thin radiodense needle or cannula-like object.
verdicts.counts: 1 post-mortem rabbit, 1 scan, 496 unique projections of 1248x960 float32. The 1024 container is the same scan: its first record (header plus projection 0 with its matrix) is byte-identical to the 512 container's, so there are 496 images in total, not 992. Container layout: 24-byte header (uint32 2, 1248, 960, 496, then two floats 1.2076 and 24.0), then 496 records of [12 float64 matrix (96 B) + 1248*960 float32 image], then trailing uint16 volume data. From the matrices, the source sits about 746 mm from isocentre and moves from -9.2 to 188.9 degrees (about 198 degrees, a short scan).
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0 (Zenodo metadata license id cc-by-4.0). The record says it is "Re-released under CC BY 4.0 with the authors' agreement". That statement comes from the uploader (Zenodo owner id 185719), and I could not check it independently; the original RabbitCT licence terms are unknown.
verdicts.access_now: Open and without login as of 2026-09-21. The API record, README_data.md and developer zip downloaded directly. The 64 MB reference volume downloaded in full and its md5 matched. HTTP range requests into both .rctd containers worked (2.68 GB and 4.83 GB).
corrections: The projections are NOT raw X-ray images: they are FDK-preprocessed (ramp-filtered, and apparently cosine/short-scan weighted). The decoded images have mean near 0, 51-70% negative pixels and an edge-enhanced look, and fade toward the sweep ends. This contradicts the stated benefit that the data 'isolates the image-formation model of a Siemens angiographic C-arm chain'. Raw intensities or line integrals cannot be recovered exactly because ramp filtering removes the DC component. The candidate's own caveat ('may already be weighted and filtered') is confirmed, and it is disqualifying for intensity or detector calibration.

Anatomy: no lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis anywhere in the data. The field runs from the skull to about the mid-thorax with the forelimbs; 'spine and torso in field' overstates it. The candidate's own description (skull, cervical and upper thoracic spine, ribs, forelimbs) is accurate.
The 'CT of the same subject' is only the circular CBCT reconstruction of the same 496 projections. It is on an unscaled 0-4095 axis (not HU), with no independent diagnostic CT.
Count: 496 unique projections in total. The 512 and 1024 containers hold the same scan (first record byte-identical); they differ only in the embedded reference volumes.
Labels: none. There are no anatomical labels, landmarks or segmentations. Pose is per-view calibrated 3x4 matrices only.

Device: the Zenodo record and README do not name the C-arm. The 2009 Med Phys paper could not be opened (Wiley returned 403; not open access per Semantic Scholar), so I could not check that it names the device. A same-lab secondary source (Xia et al. 2012, FAU) names 'Artis Zee, Siemens AG' and describes a 200-degree short scan, which matches the ~198 degrees recovered from the matrices. It gives the width as 1240 pixels, but the container header says 1248. arXiv:1104.5243 shows an Axiom Artis zeego only as an illustration.
'Re-released with the authors' agreement' rests only on the uploader's statement in the Zenodo record; it is not independently verifiable.

The candidate lists 'Pattern Recognition Lab' as the institution. The archived project page says RabbitCT was a collaboration between the Department of Neuroradiology and the Pattern Recognition Lab at FAU.

candidate.name: TCIA CMB-MML and CMB-AML (Cancer Moonshot Biobank): Siemens AXIOM-Artis 'FL SPINE' frames, DynaCT, skeletal-survey radiographs, same-patient CT
candidate.why_relevant: The only TCIA collection outside the known list with open, real interventional spine fluoroscopy alongside spine CT. MSB-04031 (viewed) has AP and lateral thoracolumbar 'FL SPINE' vertebral-augmentation frames with bilateral transpedicular trocars and cement, plus a lumbar CT (NMS NeuViz 64) and CT-guided procedure series. DynaCT (C-arm CBCT) sessions with 'FL Angio' frames exist for MSB-02929 (AP of L5, sacrum and ilium) and MSB-09896 in MML, and MSB-07839 and MSB-07656 in AML. About five patients have spine, sacrum or pelvis CR films plus a diagnostic abdomen/pelvis CT taken 1-8 months apart. The DICOM carries positioner angles and SID/SOD, so the pose is partly recoverable. It is tiny and unlabelled, but instruments are visible. Re-query NBIA Modality=XA on each release. The passes differ on counts (13-16 FL SPINE frames; 5 vs 9 patients with X-ray plus CT). The 8sDCT XA series hold only 2-3 frames, not the sweep.
candidate.institution: NCI Cancer Moonshot Biobank (NCORP community sites) via TCIA
candidate.device: Siemens AXIOM-Artis biplane (SID 1093-1240 mm, SOD 612-750 mm, pixel 0.308 mm plane A / 0.184 mm plane B, 68-90 kVp); DynaCT; CR Philips DigitalDiagnost, Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD, GE Discovery XR656, Fujifilm; CT GE, Siemens, NMS NeuViz 64
candidate.anatomy: Thoracolumbar spine fluoroscopy; C/T/L-spine, sacrum/coccyx and pelvis radiographs; L5/sacrum/ilium DynaCT
candidate.subjects: Living patients: 4 with FL SPINE (MSB-01049, -01224, -02092, -04031; only -04031 with lumbar CT); 4 DynaCT sessions; about 5 with spine/pelvis CR + CT (MSB-00392, -03406, -05151, -05206, -05562)
candidate.n_images: About 13-16 FL SPINE frames, about 12 FL Angio frames, 4 DynaCT volumes of 386 slices, about 60-90 spine/pelvis CR films (XA 29 series in 12 patients; CR 130 series in 10 patients)
candidate.pose_or_labels: No annotations; DICOM positioner angles and SID/SOD; trocars and needles visible
candidate.xray_kind: Interventional fluoroscopy last-image-hold frames (XA), DynaCT, diagnostic CR

verdicts.access_now: Open now, with no login. The NBIA v1 REST getSeries endpoint lists every series, and getImage?SeriesInstanceUID= returns each series as a DICOM zip. About 550 MB came down anonymously on 2026-09-21, including every XA frame of 3 or fewer images in both collections, the MSB-02929 DynaCT volume (386 files, 100 MB zip) and the MSB-04031 lumbar CT. The collection page says the TCIA Data Retriever is needed, but the REST path works without it. Head imaging needs a request under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy: 33 subjects and 23.35 GB in MML, 4 subjects and 1.49 GB in AML.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. Every series returned by the API carries LicenseName 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License' (MML 1,156/1,156 series; all 29 MML XA and 9 AML XA series). Users must also follow the TCIA Data Usage Policy, cite the DOI, and include the Biobank acknowledgement sentence. Head images (MR/PT/CT) are held separately under NIH Controlled access.
verdicts.counts:
CMB-MML v11 (2026-07-02), public radiology: 110 subjects, 238 studies, 1,156 series, 49,849 images, 26.76 GB. The API count matches the page exactly.

MML XA: 29 series, 417 images, 12 patients, 268.6 MB.
- 'FL SPINE': exactly 14 frames in 13 series from 4 patients (01049 x3, 01224 x2, 02092 x2, 04031 x7).
- 'FL Angio': 12 frames from 7 patients.
