- '8sDCT Body': 2 frames (02929).
- 'XA_Chest': 3 frames.
- DynaCT: 1 volume in XA (09896). A second DynaCT volume (02929) is stored as Modality=CT, so an XA query misses it.

CMB-AML v9 (2026-07-02, DOI 10.7937/PCTE-6M66): 9 public subjects, 52 series, 2,868 images, 1.59 GB. XA is 9 series in 4 patients: 7 FL Angio frames (01723 x4, 05702, 07656, 07839), one DynaCT volume (07839, 386 slices) and one 3-frame 8sDCT series (07656). AML has no FL SPINE frames.

CR (MML): 130 series, 131 images, 10 patients. About 50 series are explicitly named C/T/L-spine, pelvis, sacrum, coccyx, L5-S1 spot or KUB. About 29 more have generic or blank descriptions (05151 'AP'/'Lateral', 05562 blank x13, 05895 AP/LATERAL). DX: 1 chest film.

Frames are 1024x1024 at about 2.1 MB each. Each DynaCT volume is about 203 MB.
verdicts.anatomy:
Opened and looked at every FL SPINE and FL Angio frame (contact sheets), plus renders of two volumes.
- Real thoracolumbar spine fluoroscopy: only MSB-04031. It has AP plane-A frames with bilateral transpedicular trocars, lateral plane-B frames with cement in the vertebral bodies, and a haemostat visible.
- Iliac-crest bone-marrow biopsies: the FL SPINE frames of MSB-01049, -01224 and -02092, and nearly all FL Angio frames (01516, 01723, 02139, 03453, 05702, 07656, 07839, 08799, 09896). Patients are prone, the needle sits in the posterior ilium, and the lower lumbar spine, sacrum and SI joints are in the field. 'FL SPINE' is the name of the organ program, not the procedure.
- MSB-02929: the FL Angio frames are AP views of the lower lumbar spine, sacrum and both ilia with a wire marker. Its DynaCT (0.49 mm isotropic, 512x512x386, prone) covers L4/L5, the sacrum and both iliac wings. The candidate's 'L5, sacrum and ilium' is confirmed.
- MSB-04031 CT_LSpine (NMS NeuViz 64, BONE kernel F60): 108 slices at 2.5 mm, 0.32 mm pixels, covering about T11/T12 to the sacrum.
verdicts.paired_ct:
Same subject: yes, but only for a few patients.
- MSB-04031: the lumbar CT is 15 days before the augmentation fluoroscopy (StudyDate 1960-04-27 vs 1960-05-12, de-identified but relative). It is pre-procedure, so it has no cement. The patient also has a CT-guided pelvic marrow biopsy CT (GE Optima CT580, 25-33 slices) about 4.5 months earlier.
- Same-session C-arm CBCT plus fluoro frames: MSB-02929 and MSB-09896 (MML) and MSB-07839 (AML).
- MSB-01049, -01224 and -02092 (FL SPINE) have no CT at all.
- CR plus CT in 5 patients, but only 2 fit 'abdomen/pelvis CT 1-8 months apart': MSB-03406 (CT CAP 25 days after the films) and MSB-05151 (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 8 months after).
- MSB-00392: CT about 23 months after the films.
- MSB-05206: its only CT is the 5 mm attenuation CT of a whole-body PET/CT, about 25 months before the films.
- MSB-05562: chest CT only, about 25 months after the films.
- MSB-03816, -05032, -05895, -06699 and -06833 have CR only.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real clinical frames from a Siemens AXIOM-Artis biplane system: ImageType DERIVED/SECONDARY 'SINGLE A' or 'SINGLE B', 'STORE MONITOR' (last-image-hold captures). The DICOM carries PositionerPrimaryAngle and PositionerSecondaryAngle. SID ranges from 1093 to 1240 mm. SOD ranges from 612 to 759 mm, but it is missing on some frames (MSB-03453 both frames, MSB-04031 FL Angio series 2, and all 8sDCT frames). The 8sDCT series hold 2-3 projection frames at 90 kVp, not the rotational sweep. There are no annotations.
corrections: DynaCT volumes number 3, not 4: MSB-02929 (MML, stored as Modality=CT, so it does not appear under Modality=XA), MSB-09896 (MML) and MSB-07839 (AML). MSB-07656 (AML) has only a 3-frame '8sDCT Body' series and one FL Angio frame, with no reconstructed volume.

FL SPINE is exactly 14 frames in 13 series from 4 MML patients; AML has none. Only MSB-04031's 7 frames show vertebral augmentation. The FL SPINE frames of MSB-01049, -01224 and -02092 are prone posterior iliac-crest bone-marrow biopsies, as the StudyDescriptions 'XR_Biopsy_BoneMarrow' / 'XA_Biopsy_Bone' say. 'FL SPINE' is the organ-program label, not the procedure. So 'thoracolumbar spine fluoroscopy' applies to one patient.

FL Angio is 12 frames in MML plus 7 in AML (19 in total). Almost all are iliac-crest marrow biopsies with the lumbosacral junction in view, not spine procedures. The two MSB-04031 FL Angio frames are the exception: they are AP/lateral thoracolumbar views.

The 'about five patients with spine/pelvis CR plus abdomen/pelvis CT 1-8 months apart' is overstated. Only MSB-03406 (25 days) and MSB-05151 (8 months) fit. MSB-00392's CT is about 23 months after the films. MSB-05206's only CT is a 5 mm PET/CT attenuation CT about 25 months before. MSB-05562 has only a chest CT, about 25 months after, and its 13 CR series have blank descriptions.

Pixel spacing on plane A depends on zoom: 0.217, 0.308 or 0.373 mm, not a fixed 0.308. Plane B is 0.184 mm. SOD runs from 612 to 759 mm (759 is MSB-05702, AML) and is missing on several frames. Fluoro kVp is 65-75.4; 90 kVp is the 8sDCT frames only.
Spine/pelvis CR is about 50 explicitly named series, plus about 29 with generic or blank descriptions. 'About 60-90' is at or above the upper bound.
The candidate gives only the MML DOI. CMB-AML is a separate record: DOI 10.7937/PCTE-6M66, v9 2026-07-02.
MSB-04031's lumbar CT (2.5 mm slices, T11/T12 to sacrum) is 15 days before the augmentation and has no cement. It is a pre-procedure pairing, not the same session.
The collection page says the TCIA Data Retriever is required, but anonymous NBIA REST getImage downloads work. This is access, not a restriction.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes. I downloaded and rendered every 2-D XA frame in both collections (41 stored, 35 unique by pixel hash) through the anonymous NBIA API. All are real Siemens AXIOM-Artis fluoroscopy last-image-hold captures, with ImageType DERIVED/SECONDARY/STORE MONITOR, so they are display captures rather than raw detector frames. They show collimator shutters, needles, trocars, a hemostat, a kyphoplasty balloon and cement. None are DRRs or MV portal images. Many carry burned-in text ('PT IS PRONE', 'LEFT', 'RIGHT') that would need masking. The five '8sDCT Body' frames (MSB-02929: 2 frames, MSB-07656: 3 frames) are real projections taken during the DynaCT sweep, at primary angles of -18.7 to 34.3 degrees. The CR films are real diagnostic skeletal-survey radiographs.
verdicts.anatomy: Every 2-D XA frame shows the lumbar spine and/or the sacrum and pelvis. MSB-04031 is the only spine procedure: AP and lateral thoracolumbar vertebral augmentation with bilateral transpedicular trocars at one level, a balloon bone tamp at a second level, and cement in two vertebral bodies on the lateral view. Three of the four 'FL SPINE' patients (MSB-01049, -01224, -02092) and all the 'FL Angio' patients are prone PA views of posterior iliac-crest bone-marrow biopsies. These frames show roughly L3/L4 to S1, the sacrum, the SI joint and the iliac wing. So the lumbosacral junction appears in about 15 of the 16 XA patients, not only in MSB-02929. The 'XA_Chest' series (MSB-03312, MSB-08058) are mislabelled: they are iliac biopsies too. I rendered the DynaCT for MSB-07839: 512x512x386 voxels at 0.493 mm isotropic, a field of about 25x25x19 cm covering L4/L5, the sacrum, both SI joints and the ilia, with the needle in place. Its header says PatientPosition HFS, but the anatomy is prone (spinous process at row 0 with an identity IOP). The MSB-04031 CT covers about T10 to the sacrum (2.5 mm slices, F60 kernel). The MSB-01723 CT covers the lower chest to the femoral heads at 5 mm.
verdicts.counts: CMB-MML v11 (2026-07-02): 110 public radiology subjects, 1,156 series and 49,849 images, matching the page. XA: 29 series in 12 patients (confirmed). They hold 417 images, of which 386 are one DynaCT; the remaining 31 are 2-D frames. CMB-AML v9 (2026-07-02): XA is 9 series in 4 patients, 396 images, of which 386 are one DynaCT; the remaining 10 are 2-D frames. There are 16 XA patients in total, with 41 stored and 35 unique 2-D frames. 'FL SPINE': 14 stored, 11 unique (MSB-01049: 3; MSB-01224: 1, stored twice; MSB-02092: 1, stored twice; MSB-04031: 6 unique of 7). 'FL Angio': 12 frames in MML (confirmed) plus 7 in AML (5 unique). There are 3 DynaCT volumes of 386 slices, not 4: MSB-02929 (stored as Modality=CT, so a Modality=XA query misses it), MSB-09896 and MSB-07839. CR: 130 series and 131 images in 10 MML patients (confirmed). About 63 of those series are spine, pelvis or KUB films, and about 41 of those are lumbar, sacral, coccygeal or pelvic. There is also 1 DX (a chest film).
verdicts.paired_ct:
A CT or CBCT of the same subject exists for 8 of the 16 XA patients:
- MSB-04031: lumbar CT on a NeuViz 64, 15 days before the augmentation, pre-cement; also a limited CT-guided marrow-biopsy CT.
- MSB-02929, MSB-09896, MSB-07839: DynaCT in the same session. MSB-07839 also has CT-guided biopsy CTs 26 and 41 days earlier.
- MSB-01723 (AML): diagnostic CT of the abdomen and pelvis, 16 days before the lumbosacral biopsy fluoroscopy.
- MSB-02139: a 38-slice CT-guided biopsy CT on the same day.
- MSB-05702 (AML): a biopsy CT 42 days later.
- MSB-03453: a biopsy CT about 1,078 days earlier.

For the CR patients, only 2 of the claimed 5 have an abdomen/pelvis CT within 1 to 8 months:
- MSB-03406: chest-abdomen-pelvis CT at 2 mm, 25 days after the films.
- MSB-05151: chest-abdomen-pelvis CT at 2 mm, 244 days after.
- MSB-00392: chest-abdomen-pelvis CT about 711 days after.
- MSB-05206: only the low-dose CT from a PET/CT (5 mm), about 770 days before.
- MSB-05562: chest-only CT, about 760 days after.

Nothing registers any X-ray to any CT.
verdicts.access_now: Open. The NBIA REST getSeries and getImage calls worked without login or token. I downloaded XA, DynaCT and CT series directly with curl on 2026-09-21. On the collection pages, head images are held separately under the NIH Controlled Data Access policy; none of the relevant series are head images.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0 on every public MML and AML series, per the NBIA LicenseName field and both collection pages. Citation is required: CMB-MML DOI 10.7937/SZKB-SW39 (Version 11), CMB-AML DOI 10.7937/PCTE-6M66 (Version 9). The Moonshot Biobank acknowledgement sentence is also requested. Head imaging is NIH-controlled.
corrections: DynaCT volumes: there are 3, not 4 (MML MSB-02929 and MSB-09896, AML MSB-07839). MSB-07656 has only 3 '8sDCT Body' projection frames plus 1 FL Angio frame, and no reconstructed volume. MSB-02929's DynaCT is stored as Modality=CT, so it does not appear in the Modality=XA query in the evidence URLs.
FL SPINE count: 14 stored images in 11 series, but only 11 unique frames. MSB-01224 and MSB-02092 each hold one image duplicated across two series, and MSB-04031 series 9 holds the same image twice.

Anatomy: 'thoracolumbar spine fluoroscopy' describes only MSB-04031. The FL SPINE frames of MSB-01049, -01224 and -02092, and every FL Angio frame, are prone posterior iliac-crest bone-marrow biopsies. They show the lower lumbar spine, sacrum, SI joint and ilium. 'FL SPINE' is a protocol name, not the procedure. The lumbosacral junction is visible in about 15 of the 16 XA patients, which makes the collection more relevant to the lumbosacral question than the candidate states.
The series labelled 'XA_Chest' (MSB-03312, MSB-08058) are iliac biopsy frames, not chest images.
CMB-AML adds 10 stored 2-D frames (8 unique) in 4 patients, plus 1 DynaCT. The candidate lists AML only for DynaCT.

'About five patients have spine/pelvis CR plus a diagnostic abdomen/pelvis CT 1-8 months apart' is refuted for 3 of the 5. It holds only for MSB-03406 (25 days) and MSB-05151 (244 days). MSB-00392's CT is about 23 months after the films. MSB-05206 has only the PET/CT's low-dose CT, about 25 months before. MSB-05562 has a chest-only CT about 25 months after.

Same-subject CT for the XA patients is broader than 'only -04031'. MSB-01723 (AML) has a full abdomen/pelvis CT 16 days before a lumbosacral biopsy frame. MSB-02139, MSB-05702, MSB-03453 and MSB-07839 have CT-guided biopsy CTs at intervals from the same day to about 3 years. MSB-02929, MSB-09896 and MSB-07839 have a DynaCT from the same session.

Geometry ranges are wider than stated. SOD runs up to 758.7 mm (MSB-05702) and is missing on several frames (MSB-03453, the 8sDCT frames, MSB-04031 FL Angio series 2). ImagerPixelSpacing is also 0.3730 and 0.2166 mm, not only 0.308 (plane A) and 0.184 (plane B), and it is missing on some frames. kVp runs from 65 to 90.

Pose: the DICOM carries PositionerPrimaryAngle, PositionerSecondaryAngle, SID and (mostly) SOD. There are no projection matrices, no detector calibration and no link from any frame to its DynaCT or CT. The MSB-07839 DynaCT header says PatientPosition HFS, but the burned-in text and the anatomy show the patient was prone, so the header's patient frame cannot be trusted for pose.
All XA frames are STORE MONITOR display captures (DERIVED/SECONDARY) with burned-in orientation text. They are processed images, not raw detector frames.
Not verified: the claim that this is 'the only TCIA collection outside the known list' with open interventional spine fluoroscopy. I searched only these two collections.

candidate.name: TCIA CT localizers (topogram/scout/surview/scanogram) in about 29-54 torso collections beyond CT Colonography
candidate.why_relevant: New fact about a known source type: the localizer route is not limited to CT Colonography (530) and COVID-19-NY-SBU (345). A strict pass counted about 1,148 more patients across 29 collections with a localizer (6 images or fewer) and a diagnostic CT (more than 20 images) in the same study. The largest are TCGA-KIRC 164, CMB-LCA 102, TCGA-BLCA 99, TCGA-OV 97, CPTAC-UCEC 73, TCGA-LIHC 71, CMB-MML 66, TCGA-UCEC 56, CMB-CRC 53, CPTAC-CCRCC 46 and TCGA-STAD 45. A looser description match found 2,697 patients in 55 collections. That gives real torso projections of the lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis from about 15 scanner models and 5 vendors, with geometry recoverable from DICOM. There are none in Spine-Mets-CT-SEG, Spinal-Multiple-Myeloma-SEG, Pelvic-Reference-Data, Pancreas-CT, KiTS and others. Caveats: localizer physics (line-scan fan beam, heavy post-processing) differs from a C-arm. Counts come from a SeriesDescription heuristic without a body-part check, some scouts are head or chest only (for example many CMB-LCA), and same-session pairing is not verified.
candidate.institution: The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCGA, CPTAC and Cancer Moonshot Biobank sites)
candidate.device: Siemens Sensation/Definition (Topogram), GE LightSpeed/VCT/Revolution/Optima (Scout), Philips Brilliance/Mx8000 (Surview), Toshiba Aquilion ONE, Fujifilm SCENARIA View (Scanogram)
candidate.anatomy: Mostly abdomen/pelvis and chest-abdomen-pelvis (lumbar spine, sacrum, pelvis); some chest or head only
candidate.subjects: About 1,148 (strict) to 2,697 (loose) living patients beyond CT Colonography
candidate.pose_or_labels: ImagePosition/Orientation and PixelSpacing in the CT patient frame; no labels
candidate.doi_or_id: TCIA NBIA public API (for example TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-BLCA, TCGA-OV, CPTAC-UCEC, TCGA-LIHC, CMB-CRC, CPTAC-CCRCC)

corrections: Scanner diversity is understated. In the 31 non-lung collections the localizers carry 103 distinct ManufacturerModelName strings from at least 8 vendors: GE 1179 series, Siemens 999, Philips 82, Fujifilm 34, Toshiba 33, Hitachi 20, NMS/Neusoft 12, Canon 2, UIH 2, and 49 with no manufacturer. The candidate's 'about 15 models and 5 vendors' is too low. Some model strings are duplicates of each other ('Definition AS+' and 'SOMATOM Definition AS+').

Same-session pairing is checkable, and in my sample it held. For 45 random patients across the 11 named collections, the localizer's FrameOfReferenceUID was identical to that of a slice from the diagnostic CT in the same study, 45 of 45. This is a sample, not all 1,146.

The per-collection strict counts depend slightly on the regex. My pass reproduced TCGA-KIRC 164, CMB-LCA 102, CPTAC-UCEC 73, TCGA-LIHC 71, CMB-MML 66, TCGA-UCEC 56 and TCGA-STAD 45 exactly. I got TCGA-BLCA 97 (claim 99), TCGA-OV 94 (claim 97), CMB-CRC 52 (claim 53), CPTAC-CCRCC 45 (claim 46) and CT COLONOGRAPHY 528 (claim 530). COVID-19-NY-SBU was 344 (claim 345).

The total depends on which collections are excluded. Across all 156 collections, the strict rule (localizer of 6 images or fewer plus a CT series of more than 20 in the same study) finds 1,746 patients in 49 collections beyond CTC and COVID-19-NY-SBU. The candidate's ~1,148/29 figure matches only after the lung and phantom collections are dropped, which gives 1,146 patients in 31 collections. The dropped set includes ACRIN-NSCLC-FDG-PET 205, NSCLC Radiogenomics 93, RIDER Lung PET-CT 60, TCGA-LUAD 54, Anti-PD-1_Lung 42 and TCGA-LUSC 35.

Resolution is coarse compared with a C-arm. Siemens topograms are 512x512 at 1 or 2 mm per pixel, and many CPTAC, CMB and TCGA-LIHC/UCEC/STAD topograms are at 2 mm, where a lumbar body spans about 15-20 px. GE scouts are 0.545 x 0.597 mm (anisotropic). GE lateral scouts at 10 mA are visibly very noisy (for example CMB-MML MSB-00667).

Some localizer images are duplicates, so 'several thousand localizer series' overstates independent views. Some Siemens series add a DERIVED/SECONDARY 'CSA RESAMPLED' copy (TCGA-KIRC CW-5589, TCGA-LIHC DD-A11C). Philips Surview series add 'PS' (presentation-state) copies of the same image (TCGA-BLCA G2-A3VY).

Geometry is not uniform. Siemens and GE headers carry DistanceSourceToDetector and DistanceSourceToPatient (for example 1040/570, 1085.6/595, 949/541) plus ImageOrientationPatient, ImagePositionPatient and PixelSpacing. The Philips Brilliance Surview I opened has no SID or SOD.

BodyPartExamined cannot serve as the anatomy filter. TCGA replaces it with the organ (KIDNEY, OVARY, BLADDER, UTERUS, STOMACH, LIVER), CPTAC often tags torso topograms CHEST, and many CMB values are null. Coverage has to be checked from the pixels.

The licence claim is right for the torso set only. Those 2,412 localizer series are all CC BY 3.0 or CC BY 4.0. Elsewhere in the archive MIDRC-RICORD-1A is CC BY-NC 4.0. CMB collections keep head images in a separate 'NIH Controlled Data Access Policy' (Limited) subset; the public API returns only the CC BY 4.0 public part.

Access: the landing pages say 'Download requires TCIA Data Retriever'. In practice the public NBIA v1 REST endpoints (getSeries, getImage, getSOPInstanceUIDs, getSingleImage) served all 45 sampled localizer series and the paired CT slices with HTTP 200 and no login or token. There are no labels.

Confirmed from pixels: in a rendered random sample of 45 patients, most AP localizers run from chest or abdomen through the lumbar spine to the iliac crests or the full pelvis and proximal femora. Exceptions: CMB-LCA MSB-02861 is chest only and ends at the upper abdomen. CMB-LCA MSB-06387 and CMB-CRC MSB-03554 are lateral chest or upper-body views with little or no lumbosacral coverage.
Confirmed negatives: Spine-Mets-CT-SEG, Spinal-Multiple-Myeloma-SEG, Pelvic-Reference-Data, Pancreas-CT and C4KC-KiTS (TCIA's name for KiTS) have no series of 6 images or fewer at all.
verdicts.access_now: Open and downloadable now with no login. The public NBIA v1 REST API returned HTTP 200 for getSeries on all 156 collections and for getImage on 45 of 45 sampled localizer series; getSingleImage also returned 45 paired CT slices. The collection landing pages describe the status as 'Public, Complete' (TCGA-KIRC) or 'Public, Ongoing' (CPTAC-UCEC, CMB-MML, CMB-LCA) and point to the TCIA Data Retriever, but the REST API works directly. Localizer files are small: 0.1-4 MB per series and about 5 GB for all 31 non-lung collections (TCGA-KIRC 0.53 GB, CMB-LCA 0.78 GB, CMB-CRC 0.45 GB, TCGA-BLCA 0.36 GB). The paired diagnostic CTs are much larger; the whole TCGA-KIRC collection is 91.56 GB.
verdicts.anatomy: In the 45 sampled patients the AP views were mostly chest-abdomen-pelvis or abdomen-pelvis: lumbar spine in nearly all, and the sacrum, pelvis and proximal femora in most. Laterals are often noisy, and some cover the chest only. CMB-LCA is lung-cancer imaging and includes chest-only and head scouts (BodyPartExamined CHEST 117 and HEAD 48 of 341). The header body-part field is replaced by the organ name in TCGA and is unreliable in CPTAC and CMB, so coverage must be checked from the pixels.
verdicts.counts: Strict rule: a CT series matching topogram, scout, surview, scanogram, localizer or locator with 6 images or fewer, plus a CT series of more than 20 images in the same study. Across all of TCIA: 2,618 patients in 51 collections. Excluding CT COLONOGRAPHY (528) and COVID-19-NY-SBU (344): 1,746 patients in 49 collections. Excluding the lung and phantom collections as well: 1,146 patients in 31 collections and 2,412 localizer series. Largest: TCGA-KIRC 164 (296 series), CMB-LCA 102 (341), TCGA-BLCA 97 (132), TCGA-OV 94 (123), CPTAC-UCEC 73 (119), TCGA-LIHC 71 (150), CMB-MML 66 (100), TCGA-UCEC 56 (187), CMB-CRC 52 (217), CPTAC-CCRCC 45 (59), TCGA-STAD 45 (49), CMB-BRCA 39.
verdicts.licence: Set per collection in the NBIA metadata. The TCGA collections are CC BY 3.0 Unported; CPTAC and CMB are CC BY 4.0 International. All 2,412 non-lung localizer series fall under one of these two. Elsewhere in the archive MIDRC-RICORD-1A is CC BY-NC 4.0. CMB head images sit in a separate Limited subset under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy, which the public API does not return.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, in the same study. In 45 of 45 sampled patients the localizer's FrameOfReferenceUID matched a slice from the study's diagnostic CT, so the scout's ImagePositionPatient and ImageOrientationPatient are in the CT patient frame. Siemens and GE headers also give the source-to-detector and source-to-patient distances; the Philips header I opened does not.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real X-ray scanned-projection radiographs acquired by the CT tube: ImageType ORIGINAL/PRIMARY/LOCALIZER at 80-130 kVp and 10-80 mA. They are line-scan fan-beam images, not C-arm cone-beam images, and are post-processed. Resolution is 0.55-2 mm per pixel, and the low-mA GE laterals are very noisy.

Confirmed. I downloaded 60 localizer series anonymously from the NBIA API: 12 hand-picked and 48 drawn at random from the strict torso pool. They are CT Image Storage objects (SOP 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.2), and almost all are ImageType ORIGINAL\PRIMARY\LOCALIZER, with kVp, mA and DistanceSourceToDetector/Patient filled in (GE 949/541 mm, Siemens 1040/570, SOMATOM Force 1085.6/595). Rendered, they are real scanned projection radiographs, not DRRs and not MV portal images. Exceptions:
- A few series are DERIVED\SECONDARY: CPTAC-UCEC C3N-02635 ('DERIVED SECONDARY OTHER'), TCGA-LIHC G3-A3CK and one image of TCGA-UCEC A2F4. TCGA-KICH KM-8440 is ORIGINAL\SECONDARY. These may be reprocessed copies.
- The geometry is a CT line scan (fan beam across, parallel along the table), not a C-arm cone beam.
verdicts.paired_ct:
Confirmed on a sample. In all 12 hand-picked studies, whose FrameOfReferenceUID I compared, the localizer and the thin or axial CT series in the same study share one FrameOfReferenceUID and were acquired 1 to 25 minutes apart. That makes them the same subject in the same session, which is stronger than the candidate's 'pairing not verified' caveat. Caveats:
- TCGA paired CTs from the 1990s and 2000s are often 5 mm slices (some 2.5 or 1.25 mm).
- CMB-MML 'diagnostic CT' studies are often CT_Biopsy_BoneMarrow slabs of 30 to 33 slices (for example MSB-02628 and MSB-07917). They do not cover the lumbar spine and sacrum, even though they pass the '>20 images' rule.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar spine and pelvis appear in roughly 44 to 46 of the 48 randomly sampled patients from the 30 non-lung collections, usually chest to pelvis or abdomen to pelvis, AP with some laterals. Chest-dominant or no-pelvis views were CMB-LCA MSB-00556 and TCGA-LIHC G3-A3CK. Across all 2,423 strict localizer series in that subset, BodyPartExamined still reads CHEST 384 and HEAD 86, so a patient counted may have only a chest or head localizer. CMB-LCA is mixed: I sampled chest-only scouts, and by study description about 29 of its 103 patients are chest or head only.
verdicts.counts:
I reproduced the strict rule (description matches topo, scout, surview, scanogram or locali; 6 images or fewer; a CT of more than 20 images in the same study) on getSeries?Modality=CT for all 155 public non-NLST collections.
- Excluding CT COLONOGRAPHY and COVID-19-NY-SBU: 49 collections and 1,731 patients. This includes lung and PET collections, phantoms (RIDER PHANTOM PET-CT, QIBA CT-1C) and synthetic or test sets (MIDI-B).
- Restricted to 30 non-lung torso collections: 1,137 patients, 2,423 localizer series and 3,812 images. This agrees with the candidate's ~1,148 in 29.
- Per collection (mine, with the candidate's in brackets): TCGA-KIRC 162 (164), CMB-LCA 103 (102), TCGA-BLCA 97 (99), TCGA-OV 94 (97), CPTAC-UCEC 73 (73), TCGA-LIHC 73 (71), CMB-MML 66, TCGA-UCEC 56, CMB-CRC 53, TCGA-STAD 45, CPTAC-CCRCC 43 (46).
- By the same rule, CT COLONOGRAPHY has 722 patients and COVID-19-NY-SBU 344.
- The loose figure of 2,697 patients in 55 collections is not reproducible: it depends on the regex. My loose pass gave 2,174 patients in 55 collections excluding those two.
verdicts.licence: Confirmed for all 30 torso collections: TCGA-* are CC BY 3.0 Unported; CPTAC-*, CMB-* and VAREPOP-APOLLO are CC BY 4.0. Collections outside the subset that are CC BY-NC (NSCLC-Radiomics, MIDRC-RICORD-1A/1B, Phantom FDA) or have no licence (MIDI-B) must stay excluded.
verdicts.access_now: Open. getSeries, getSOPInstanceUIDs, getSingleImage and getImage (series zip) all worked on 2026-09-21 with no login.
corrections: Headline counts need correcting. My reproduction gives 1,137 patients, 2,423 localizer series and 3,812 images in 30 non-lung torso collections, which is close to the stated ~1,148 in 29. The 'loose 2,697 patients in 55 collections' could not be reproduced, and a loose match also takes in phantoms (RIDER PHANTOM PET-CT, QIBA CT-1C) and synthetic or test sets (MIDI-B), which are not living patients.

'About 15 scanner models and 5 vendors' is understated. The strict torso subset has about 103 ManufacturerModelName strings from GE, Siemens, Philips, Toshiba, Fujifilm, Hitachi, Canon, UIH, Neusoft and NMS; 47 series have no manufacturer.
'n_images: several thousand localizer series' should read about 2,423 series and 3,812 images in the strict torso subset.

ImageCount 2 does not mean AP plus lateral. Several Siemens topogram series hold duplicate images with identical IOP and IPP (CPTAC-UCEC C3L-05848 and C3L-05849, CPTAC-CCRCC C3N-01648, TCGA-KIRC B8-A54G with 4 copies). Siemens topograms are mostly AP only, while GE scouts are often AP plus lateral.
Resolution varies. Siemens topograms are often stored at 512x512 with 1 mm pixels (2 mm on a SOMATOM Force) or at 1024x1024. GE scouts are about 888 columns at 0.545x0.597 mm.
Some localizers are DERIVED\SECONDARY or ORIGINAL\SECONDARY rather than ORIGINAL\PRIMARY (CPTAC-UCEC C3N-02635, TCGA-LIHC G3-A3CK, TCGA-KICH KM-8440, TCGA-UCEC A2F4), so filter on ImageType.

Anatomy is not guaranteed for every patient. Even inside the torso subset, 384 localizer series say CHEST and 86 say HEAD. CMB-LCA is partly chest-only: roughly 29 of 103 patients by study description, and one of two sampled scouts had no pelvis.
The '>20-image diagnostic CT' rule does not guarantee lumbar or sacral CT coverage. CMB-MML pairs are often 30-to-33-slice bone-marrow biopsy slabs, and many TCGA CTs are 5 mm.
Same-session pairing is verified on a sample, not unverified as stated. In all 12 studies checked, the localizer and the CT share a FrameOfReferenceUID and were acquired minutes apart.

Pose: IOP, IPP and PixelSpacing put the image plane in the CT frame, and DistanceSourceToDetector/Patient are present. The projection model is a vendor-specific hybrid (fan beam across, parallel along z), not a C-arm pinhole pose. There are no labels.
The candidate's own 'CT Colonography (530)' figure is low under this rule: the strict rule gives 722 CTC patients.

Negative claims are confirmed: Spine-Mets-CT-SEG, Spinal-Multiple-Myeloma-SEG, Pelvic-Reference-Data, Pancreas-CT and C4KC-KiTS have no series of 6 images or fewer. The NBIA name is 'C4KC-KiTS'; 'KiTS' returns nothing.

candidate.name: TCIA small same-patient radiograph/fluoroscopy + CT overlaps (VAREPOP-APOLLO, TCGA-BLCA, TCGA-KIRC, COVID-19-AR, CMB-PCA, CMB-CRC; LIDC-IDRI chest)
candidate.why_relevant: This is the result of scanning all public NBIA collections for RF, XA, CR and DX series that share a patient with a CT. VAREPOP-APOLLO: AP-7CQ6 has a portable abdomen AP (Carestream DRX-Revolution) one day before an abdomen/pelvis CT (Siemens Edge), plus 11 barium fluoroscopy series. AP-SNKW has abdomen and hip films with CT. AP-2CM3 has a C-spine series but only a chest CT. The other collections contribute COVID-19-AR (1-2 patients with abdomen/pelvis DX + CT), TCGA-BLCA (7-10 patients with abdominal DX/CR + CT), TCGA-KIRC (1 CR urogram) and CMB-PCA (1 voiding cystourethrogram + CT). LIDC-IDRI (290 patients) is chest only. There is no pose, there are no labels, and the CT may be from another date. These are small additions to the known COVID-19-NY-SBU route. The scan also confirms that TCIA holds no hidden large film-plus-CT torso cohort beyond CMB-MML and the localizers. Patient counts differ between passes.
candidate.institution: TCIA (VA APOLLO, UAMS, TCGA, CMB sites)
candidate.device: Carestream DRX-Revolution, GE Revolution XRd, Samsung DGR, Oehm und Rehbein DX; Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD (RF); Siemens CT
candidate.anatomy: Abdomen/pelvis with lumbar spine; hip; cervical spine (one patient, no neck CT); chest (LIDC-IDRI)
candidate.subjects: About 5-15 living patients outside the chest; 290 chest-only (LIDC-IDRI)
candidate.n_images: Tens of films; 11 barium fluoroscopy series; LIDC-IDRI 569 chest radiograph series
candidate.pose_or_labels: none
candidate.xray_kind: Diagnostic radiographs (CR/DX); GI barium fluoroscopy (RF, 2 fps); voiding cystourethrogram

verdicts.access_now: Open now, no login needed. I pulled 60+ series anonymously through the NBIA v1 API (getImage?SeriesInstanceUID=...), which returns a zip of DICOMs plus a LICENSE file. That covers every film series named in the candidate plus the omitted CMB-AML, CMB-LCA and TCGA-UCEC ones. The TCIA collection pages say bulk download 'requires TCIA Data Retriever', but single series come straight from the API. All the DOIs resolve (HTTP 200) to TCIA collection pages. VAREPOP-APOLLO's page reads 'Public, Ongoing', Version 3, updated 2025/10/02: 41 subjects, 279 studies, 1,549 series, 235,421 images, 129.1 GB (the API's FileSize values sum to 108 GB). One subject (AP-2BGA) was removed over facial features, and the collection is still ongoing, which may explain why patient counts differ between passes. Dates are shifted (LongitudinalTemporalInformationModified), which is why they fall in the 1950s to 1970s. The film series are small: the 54 relevant film series I downloaded come to 680 MB.
verdicts.licence: From the API's LicenseName field, and for VAREPOP-APOLLO also from the LICENSE file inside the zip. VAREPOP-APOLLO, CMB-PCA, CMB-CRC, CMB-AML, CMB-LCA and COVID-19-AR: CC BY 4.0. TCGA-BLCA, TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-UCEC and LIDC-IDRI: CC BY 3.0 Unported. The TCIA Data Usage Policy also applies (no re-identification) and citation is required.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, all real acquisitions (checked by rendering every series). They are mostly diagnostic CR/DX films. The true fluoroscopy is: the VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-7CQ6 barium esophagram (Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD, 51 frames over 11 series); the CMB-PCA voiding series (GEMS Precision 500D, 11 images, circular field); 3 unique mobile C-arm frames in CMB-CRC MSB-06489 (GE OEC 'Surgery VAS 15 31 cm FPD Motorized', SID 1000, positioner angles recorded); and the omitted CMB-AML Siemens AXIOM-Artis biopsy frames. The TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC 'projection urogram' CR images are real plain films taken during CT urography, carrying 'CTU 20MIN' and 'POST VOID' markers; they are not CT-derived projections. Several TCGA-BLCA G2-A3VY IVP series are linear tomograms, not plain projections.
verdicts.anatomy: The AP-7CQ6 RF frames show the pharynx, cervical spine, thoracic esophagus and GE junction, not the abdomen or lumbar spine, even though BodyPartExamined says ABDOMEN. Films that show the lumbar spine and pelvis: the AP-7CQ6 abdomen AP; the AP-SNKW abdomen AP x2, pelvis AP and hip AP/frog; COVID-19-AR-16424111 and -16434453; TCGA-G2-A2EK/A2EL/A3VY; TCGA-CW-6088; CMB-PCA MSB-08178; CMB-CRC MSB-02381. The CMB-CRC MSB-06489 C-arm frames show the thoracolumbar spine. AP-2CM3 has cervical films and shoulder films. LIDC-IDRI is chest only. Among the omitted items, the CMB-AML MSB-01723 prone fluoroscopy frames show L4 to S1 and the iliac crest with a biopsy needle.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same patient, different date in most cases. Checked intervals: AP-7CQ6 abdomen AP 1 day before a non-contrast abdomen/pelvis CT (Siemens SOMATOM Definition Edge, 1.5 mm MPR). Its esophagram has no CT covering the neck or chest; the 'HEAD W/O & WITH CONT' study holds only a topogram. AP-SNKW abdomen/pelvis CT 1975-09-14: 3 months after the abdomen films and 25 days after the pelvis/hip films. A CT labelled 'CHEST WITH CONT' but tagged ABDOMEN falls 9 days before the pelvis film. AP-2CM3 has chest CTs only; its 'PET/CT skull-thigh' is a single topogram. COVID-19-AR-16424111: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 2 days before the films (Philips Brilliance 64, 744-slice thins). COVID-19-AR-16434453: CT PE chest only. TCGA-G2-A2EL: KUB 3 days after an abdomen CT. TCGA-G2-A3VY: CT urogram about 1 month before the IVP. TCGA-G2-A2EK: nearest CTs about 3 months before and 7 weeks after. TCGA-CW-6088 and TCGA-D1-A2G5: plain films from the same session as the CT urogram, same day. CMB-CRC MSB-02381: abdomen films the same day as a 5-mm abdomen/pelvis CT. CMB-CRC MSB-06489: only 5-mm limited liver-biopsy CTs, 11 days before and 25 days after. CMB-PCA MSB-08178: first CT about 10 months after the films. CMB-AML MSB-01723 (omitted): abdomen/pelvis CT 16 days before the fluoroscopy. CMB-AML MSB-07839 (omitted): a same-session Siemens DynaCT cone-beam volume (386 images, 203 MB). No pose ground truth and no labels anywhere.
verdicts.counts: Patients whose non-chest films share a patient with a CT, from my own scan of every public NBIA RF/XA/CR/DX series (RF 12, XA 41, CR 12,660, DX 3,836): COVID-19-NY-SBU 51, CMB-MML 9, VAREPOP-APOLLO 4, CMB-AML 3, TCGA-BLCA 3, CMB-CRC 2, COVID-19-AR 2 (my keyword filter first reported 0 because the study name includes 'W PA CHEST'), CMB-LCA 1, CMB-PCA 1, TCGA-KIRC 1, TCGA-UCEC 1. Of the 4 in VAREPOP-APOLLO, 2 have torso films; AP-2CM3 has cervical films and AP-ANXW has elbow and knee films. Outside COVID-19-NY-SBU and CMB-MML this makes about 12 usable torso patients in the named collections, or 17 including those omitted. LIDC-IDRI has 290 radiograph series (237 DX + 53 CR) in 290 patients, 569 images, all chest. RF exists in only two collections (VAREPOP-APOLLO 11 series, CMB-PCA 1). The claim that TCIA hides no large film-plus-CT torso cohort beyond COVID-19-NY-SBU and CMB-MML holds.
corrections: The 11 VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-7CQ6 RF series are a barium esophagram (StudyDesc 'ESOPHAGUS RAPID SEQUENCE FILMS'). They show pharynx and cervical spine, thoracic esophagus and GE junction, not abdomen or lumbar spine, despite BodyPartExamined=ABDOMEN. That is 51 frames in total, 1-18 per series. The patient's CTs are abdomen/pelvis only (the head CT study is just a topogram), so the fluoroscopy has essentially no CT covering its anatomy.

AP-7CQ6 abdomen AP confirmed. DICOM modality is CR, from a Carestream DRX-Revolution, 80 kVp, 0.139 mm pixels. It was taken 1 day before a non-contrast abdomen/pelvis CT on a Siemens SOMATOM Definition Edge.

TCGA-BLCA: 10 patients have some film plus a CT, but only 3 have abdominal films: G2-A2EK (portable Fuji CR), G2-A2EL (Agfa CR 35 KUB) and G2-A3VY (IV pyelogram with tomography, GE; many of its 8 series are linear tomograms). The other 7 have chest films only. '7-10 patients with abdominal DX/CR + CT' is wrong; the number is 3.

TCGA-KIRC CW-6088 has 4 CR films, not 1: 3 on 1995-02-26 and 1 on 1999-10-11. They are real plain films taken during CT urography (markers 'CTU 20MIN', 'POST VOID'), each on the same day as the CT urogram.

COVID-19-AR: only 16424111 has abdomen films (supine and upright, Philips MobileDiagnost wDR) with an abdominal CT, a chest/abdomen/pelvis CT 2 days earlier. 16434453's abdomen and pelvis films pair only with a CT PE chest.

CMB-CRC is named but not described. It contributes MSB-02381, supine and erect abdomen DX (Samsung GM85) on the same day as a 5-mm abdomen/pelvis CT. It also contributes MSB-06489: 3 unique real mobile C-arm frames (GE OEC FPD, SID 1000, positioner angles recorded) of the thoracolumbar spine during a liver biopsy, filed twice under two study descriptions (6 entries, 3 images). The nearest CTs are 5-mm limited biopsy scans 11 days before and 25 days after.
CMB-PCA MSB-08178: one RF voiding series of 11 images (GEMS Precision 500D) plus 4 DX abdomen images (GE). The first CT comes about 10 months after the films.
LIDC-IDRI: 569 is the image count, not the series count. It has 290 series (237 DX + 53 CR) in 290 patients, all chest, CC BY 3.0.

Omitted: CMB-AML (CC BY 4.0). It has 3 patients with Siemens AXIOM-Artis fluoroscopy frames taken during prone bone-marrow biopsy, showing L4 to S1 and the iliac crest with a needle. MSB-01723 has an abdomen/pelvis CT 16 days earlier (2 unique frames, each filed twice). MSB-07839 also has a same-session DynaCT cone-beam CT (386 images, 203 MB). These are the only real fluoroscopy frames of the lumbosacral junction with a same-patient CT among these TCIA collections.

Also omitted: CMB-LCA MSB-09794, upright lateral thoracic-spine DX with a chest/abdomen/pelvis CT 4 weeks earlier; and TCGA-UCEC D1-A2G5, 3 CT-urogram plain films taken the same day as an abdomen CT (CC BY 3.0).

Device list is partly wrong. 'GE Revolution XRd' and 'Samsung DGR' do not appear on the relevant films; 'GE Revolution XRd' may be a misreading of the chest-only GE 'Revolution XQi'. Actual film devices: GE 'Thunder Platform', GE Revolution XQi (chest only), Samsung GM85, Samsung GC85A (chest only), Philips MobileDiagnost wDR, Fujifilm CR, Agfa CR 35, Konica Minolta CS-7, GEMS Precision 500D, GE OEC C-arm, Siemens AXIOM-Artis, Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD, Carestream DRX-Revolution, Oehm und Rehbein. The paired CTs also include Philips Brilliance, GE LightSpeed/Optima/Revolution EVO and Toshiba Aquilion, not only Siemens.

AP-2CM3 confirmed: 7 cervical-spine DX series (5 distinct views plus 2 duplicates) and 3 shoulder views, with chest CTs only; its PET/CT 'skull-thigh' study is a single topogram. AP-SNKW's films are 3 months (abdomen) and 25 days (pelvis/hip) from the abdomen/pelvis CT. AP-ANXW's films are elbow and knee, which is irrelevant.

Access detail: the TCIA pages route bulk download through the TCIA Data Retriever, but per-series anonymous download through the NBIA v1 API works now. VAREPOP-APOLLO is 'Public, Ongoing' (Version 3, 2025/10/02) and has dates shifted, so its patient list can change between passes.

Scope: every claim below was re-derived from the public NBIA v1 API without a login (getSeries per collection, getSeries per modality across all collections, getPatientByCollectionAndModality for CT). I downloaded about 60 X-ray instances through getImage and rendered them. Nothing was taken from the candidate's own summary.

VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-7CQ6 is confirmed. It has one abdomen AP taken 1974-12-24 (modality CR, not DX; Carestream DRX-Revolution; ImageType DERIVED/PRIMARY; 3032x2520 at 0.139 mm) and a CT 'ABDOMEN & PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST' on a SOMATOM Definition Edge on 1974-12-25. The render shows the thoracolumbar and lumbar spine plus the upper pelvis.

VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-7CQ6 barium fluoroscopy is refuted as lumbar or pelvic material. The 11 RF series have StudyDesc 'ESOPHAGUS RAPID SEQUENCE FILMS', so they are an esophagram. The renders show the pharynx, neck and cervical spine in AP and lateral views; there is no lumbar spine. The BodyPartExamined tag reads ABDOMEN and is wrong. The series are multi-frame (2 to 18 frames per series checked), 768x768 at 0.169 mm, CineRate 4, SID 1236 to 1244 and SOD 706, from a Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD. This patient has no CT covering the neck; the only CTs are abdomen/pelvis and head.

VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-SNKW is confirmed and understated. It has 8 real films: 2 Carestream abdomen AP (1975-06-14) and 6 Siemens Fluorospot Compact FD CR films (1975-08-20: abdomen supine x2, abdomen upright, pelvis AP, hip AP, hip frog). The lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are visible. The CT abdomen & pelvis is dated 1975-09-14, 25 days after the Fluorospot films. There are also chest CTs and PET/CT.

VAREPOP-APOLLO AP-2CM3: 'only a chest CT' is wrong. The patient also has a PET/CT 'SKULL-THIGH' CT (Biograph64_mCT, 1977-11-18), which covers the neck at low dose. The C-spine DX films (Oehm und Rehbein, 1978-03-10) were taken about 4 months later. None of this is lumbar.

VAREPOP-APOLLO totals: 7 patients have X-ray and all 7 have CT, but only 2 (AP-7CQ6 and AP-SNKW) have lumbar or pelvic films. There are 75 X-ray series and 79 instances (RF 11, CR 44, DX 20). The licence is CC BY 4.0.

TCGA-BLCA '7-10 patients with abdominal DX/CR + CT' is refuted. 10 patients have any X-ray plus CT, but most of those films are chest. Only 3 carry abdominal films. TCGA-G2-A3VY has an IV pyelogram with tomography: 8 DX series, 41 images, GE Thunder Platform, 2003-09-22, with a CT urogram on 2003-08-19. TCGA-G2-A2EL has an AP scout/KUB (Agfa CR 35, 2000-12-22) with a CT abdomen on 2000-12-19. TCGA-G2-A2EK has 1 CR tagged ABDOMEN that renders as a portable chest/upper abdomen, with no useful lumbar view. Several of the A3VY images are linear tomograms, not plain projections. The licence is CC BY 3.0.

TCGA-KIRC is 1 patient (TCGA-CW-6088) with 4 CR instances, not 1: three on 1995-02-26 and one on 1999-10-11. Each is a real Fuji CR plate (burned-in 'CTU 20MIN' and 'POST VOID'), not a CT reprojection, despite the description 'projection urogram'. Each was taken on the same day as a CT urogram. The lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are visible.

COVID-19-AR is confirmed at 2 patients, but only 1 is truly paired. COVID-19-AR-16424111 has 2 abdominal DX films (Philips MobileDiagnost wDR, 2012-02-10) 2 days after a CT chest/abdomen/pelvis. COVID-19-AR-16434453 has 3 abdominal/pelvic DX films (2012-02-27), but its only CT is a CT PE chest from 7 days earlier, which does not cover the pelvis. Of 262 X-ray series in the collection, 256 are chest.

CMB-PCA MSB-08178 is confirmed. The RF VCUG has 11 images (GE Precision 500D, spot images, no pixel spacing, circular field over the pelvis, sacrum and lower lumbar spine). There are also 2 DX abdomen series with 4 images (GE Thunder Platform, SID 1000 and SOD 934). All are dated 1956-10-31. The nearest CT abdomen/pelvis is 1957-08-21, about 10 months later.

CMB-CRC appears only in the candidate's ID list, and its content was not described. MSB-02381 has 2 abdomen DX films (Samsung GM85) on the same day as a CT AbdPelvis (1959-04-04). One of them shows the lumbar spine and upper pelvis; the one labelled 'erect' is mostly chest. MSB-06489 has 2 XA series with 6 images from a GE 'VAS 15 31 cm FPD Motorized' mobile C-arm, logged under US liver biopsy. These are real intraprocedural fluoroscopy of the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spine with a catheter loop, and the header carries positioner angles and SID 1000. The nearest abdominal CTs are 11 days before (1959-09-25) and 25 days after (1959-10-31).

The candidate missed CMB-AML (doi 10.7937/PCTE-6M66, CC BY 4.0), which is the most fluoroscopy-like item found. It holds Siemens AXIOM-Artis 'FL Angio' images from prone iliac bone-marrow biopsies with the needle in view; L4-L5, the sacrum and the SI joints are visible. MSB-01723 has 4 images and a CT Abd/Pel 16 days earlier. MSB-05702 has 1 image and a CT biopsy 11 days later. MSB-07839 has 1 image plus a 386-slice DynaCT cone-beam volume of the pelvis from the same session, with CT biopsy scans 10 and 26 days earlier. A fourth patient, MSB-07656, has fluoroscopy but no CT; its '8sDCT Body' series is only 3 monitor captures, not a volume. All of these fluoroscopy frames are DERIVED/SECONDARY 'STORE MONITOR' captures.

Also missed: TCGA-UCEC TCGA-D1-A2G5 has 3 Fuji CR post-CT-urogram KUB films (lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis visible) on the same day as a CT abdomen (1992-04-22). CMB-LCA MSB-09794 has thoracic-spine DX films with chest-abdomen-pelvis CTs.

LIDC-IDRI: '569 chest radiograph series' is wrong. It is 290 X-ray series (237 DX and 53 CR) holding 569 images from 290 patients. Every one of those patients has CT, and all films are chest. The licence is CC BY 3.0, not 4.0.
Pose and labels: none, confirmed. Some RF and XA headers carry SID, SOD and positioner angles, but no calibrated pose or registration to the CT is provided. No annotations accompany the X-rays.

Dates: most X-ray/CT pairs are days to months apart. Same-day or next-day pairs exist only for AP-7CQ6 (1 day), TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC (same day), CMB-CRC MSB-02381 (same day) and the CMB-AML DynaCT (same session). All dates are de-identification-shifted.

The claim that TCIA holds no other large film-plus-CT torso cohort is supported, but only for public NBIA collections. Across every public NBIA collection, patient overlap between X-ray and CT is: COVID-19-NY-SBU 439 (52 with a non-chest body part), LIDC-IDRI 290 (chest only), COVID-19-AR 22, ACRIN-NSCLC-FDG-PET 10 (chest only), TCGA-BLCA 10, CMB-MML 9, VAREPOP-APOLLO 7, RIDER Pilot 5 (chest only), CMB-AML 3, CMB-CRC 3, CMB-LCA 2, Pseudo-PHI 2 (a synthetic de-identification test set), and CMB-PCA, TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC 1 each. Restricted collections and IDC-only data were not checked.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. Every X-ray checked is a real acquisition; none are DRRs. The CR and DX films are ORIGINAL or DERIVED/PRIMARY with vendor detector tags (Carestream, Siemens Fluorospot, Fuji, Agfa, GE Thunder, Philips MobileDiagnost, Samsung). The RF and XA images are real fluoroscopy: the APOLLO esophagram, the CMB-PCA VCUG, the CMB-CRC GE mobile C-arm and the CMB-AML Siemens AXIOM-Artis. The CMB-AML frames are STORE MONITOR last-image-hold captures. The TCGA-KIRC 'projection urogram' images are Fuji CR plates with burned-in 'CTU 20MIN', not CT reprojections. Some TCGA-BLCA IVP images are linear tomograms.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, the same subjects have CT, but CT dates are usually days to months away from the films. The closer pairs are: AP-7CQ6 abdomen AP with a CT abdomen/pelvis 1 day later; TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC post-CT-urogram KUBs on the same day as the CT; CMB-CRC MSB-02381 abdomen DX with a same-day CT AbdPelvis; COVID-19-AR-16424111 with a CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 2 days earlier; CMB-AML MSB-07839 with a same-session DynaCT cone-beam volume of the pelvis (386 slices) plus CTs 10 and 26 days earlier. AP-SNKW's CT abdomen/pelvis is 25 days after its films. CMB-PCA's CT is about 10 months after the VCUG. COVID-19-AR-16434453 has only a chest CT, which does not cover its pelvic films. AP-7CQ6's esophagram has no neck CT at all.
verdicts.anatomy: The lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are visible in rendered films from AP-7CQ6 (1 abdomen AP), AP-SNKW (abdomen, pelvis and hip films), TCGA-G2-A3VY (IVP), TCGA-G2-A2EL (KUB), TCGA-CW-6088 and TCGA-D1-A2G5 (post-CT-urogram KUBs), COVID-19-AR-16424111 and -16434453, CMB-PCA MSB-08178 (abdomen DX and VCUG) and CMB-CRC MSB-02381. CMB-CRC MSB-06489's C-arm frames show the lower thoracic and upper lumbar spine. CMB-AML fluoroscopy shows L4-L5, the sacrum, the SI joints and the iliac crests. The 11 APOLLO barium series are neck and esophagus only, with no lumbar spine. AP-2CM3 is cervical spine and shoulder. LIDC-IDRI is chest only.
verdicts.counts: About 15 patients outside the chest have lumbar or pelvic-region X-ray plus CT: VAREPOP-APOLLO 2, TCGA-BLCA 2 to 3, TCGA-KIRC 1, TCGA-UCEC 1, COVID-19-AR 2 (only 1 with an abdominal CT), CMB-PCA 1, CMB-CRC 2 and CMB-AML 3. Lumbar or pelvic images total roughly 90. That includes about 22 true fluoroscopy frames: 11 VCUG, 6 GE C-arm and 5 CMB-AML frames from the 3 CT-paired patients, plus 1 cone-beam volume. The APOLLO esophagram (11 series of 2 to 18 frames) is not lumbar material. LIDC-IDRI adds 290 chest series (569 images) from 290 patients. There are no poses and no labels.
verdicts.licence: The NBIA series metadata gives CC BY 4.0 for VAREPOP-APOLLO, COVID-19-AR, CMB-PCA, CMB-CRC, CMB-AML and CMB-LCA. It gives CC BY 3.0 for TCGA-BLCA, TCGA-KIRC, TCGA-UCEC and LIDC-IDRI.
verdicts.access_now: Open. The series lists and pixel data were downloaded through the public NBIA v1 API (getSeries and getImage) with no login or token. The DOIs resolve to the TCIA collection pages for VAREPOP-APOLLO, CMB-AML, CMB-PCA and CMB-CRC.

candidate.name: US-X Complete phantom data (TUM CAMP): Loop-X lateral X-ray + co-registered CBCT of two lumbar phantoms
candidate.why_relevant: A Loop-X lateral projection and a CBCT from the same device, which the paper says are 'inherently co-registered', for two lumbar phantoms (one L1-L5 plus sacrum, one 3D-printed). Paired ultrasound is also included. It is a new device type in the collection. It is small, and the LRZ share could not be listed (JavaScript-only page), so the X-ray count is unknown.
candidate.institution: Technical University of Munich (CAMP)
candidate.device: medPhoton Loop-X
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine L1-L5 + sacrum
candidate.n_images: not stated (lateral X-ray + CBCT per phantom)
candidate.pose_or_labels: X-ray and CBCT co-registered by the device; vertebra segmentations

corrections: The share and the phantom files exist and can be downloaded now without a login, but the files hold no real X-ray image and no CBCT volume. The paper's own sentence 'Code and data can be found at github' is accurate only for derived data: two 4.1 MB HDF5 files of masks, point clouds and matrices.

real_xray=true is wrong for what was released. The Loop-X lateral radiograph was acquired, but only a 256x256 binary vertebral-body mask from it is published (GT_Xray_segms, values 0 or the level id 20-24, about 2,400-2,750 foreground pixels). No X-ray intensities are released, so for this project the release contains zero real X-ray images.

ct_or_cbct_same_subject / 'co-registered CBCT' is not released as a volume. Each phantom file has only a 4096-point cloud per vertebra (complete_pcds, taken from the CBCT, normalised to about +/-0.45), a 4096-point ultrasound partial cloud (incomplete_pcds), a 4x4 inverse transform (scale about 133) and a 3x4 projection matrix. There is no CBCT and no ultrasound volume in the share.
The sacrum is not in the release. Each phantom file has exactly five entries, verLev20 to verLev24 (L1-L5). The paper's appendix says phantom 1 contains the sacrum, but no sacrum data was shared.

The two phantom files contain the same GT_Xray_segms array and the same proj_matrices, byte for byte. Their complete_pcds and incomplete_pcds differ: the shapes are measurably different, with a chamfer of about 0.035-0.042 in normalised units, roughly 5 mm. So at most one distinct X-ray mask set is released for two phantoms, and which phantom it belongs to is not stated. The cause is unknown.

n_images is not an unknown count. The share lists exactly five files. Two are phantom files (phantom2_with_vertlabelmap_polluted.h5 and phantom_with_vertBodylabelmap.h5, 4,104,192 bytes each). Three are synthetic VerSe20-derived splits: Verse2020_VertBodyLabelmap_train.h5 at 536,796,756 bytes, val at 176,378,854 and test at 171,053,328. The total is about 892 MB. The candidate said the share 'could not be listed'. It can, through the Sync+Share wapi endpoint.

Licence: no data licence is stated anywhere, not in the README, the paper or the share. The GitHub repo has no root licence (the API reports license=null). The only LICENSE files are MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2021 PL', inherited from the MVP_Benchmark code the repo adapts. They cover code, not the data. The VerSe-derived synthetic files presumably carry VerSe's terms, but this is not stated.

Device is correct: medPhoton Loop-X for the X-ray and the CBCT, and a Siemens ACUSON Juniper 5C1 ultrasound probe on a KUKA iiwa. Phantom 2 is a 3D print of VerSe 2020 subject 818, not an independent anatomy. Its CT and masks already exist in VerSe.

Not a new real-X-ray source for task A. What was released is shape-completion training data: masks and point clouds. Treat it as a derived-label set for two phantoms. It is not a radiograph plus CBCT pair.
verdicts.access_now: Open now with no login or request. The LRZ Sync+Share link is live, and the files download directly from https://syncandshare.lrz.de/dl/fi5STHyTaLSYSwwC42iDog/<file>. Both phantom files were downloaded on 2026-09-21 as valid HDF5 files, and a range request on the VerSe test file returned 206. The network weights sit on a second live LRZ link (fi4hJgCvKggP1vhPAFpECJ). What can be downloaded is derived data only: masks, point clouds and matrices. No raw X-ray or CBCT is shared.
verdicts.licence: No data licence is stated in the README, the paper or the share. The repo has no root licence (GitHub license=null). The subfolders carry MIT licences, 'Copyright (c) 2021 PL', inherited from the MVP_Benchmark code, and these cover code only. The arXiv preprint is under the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence.
verdicts.counts: The share holds five HDF5 files, about 892 MB in total. Two are phantom files of 4,104,192 bytes each. Each has five vertebrae (L1-L5, ids 20-24), and for each vertebra: one 256x256 X-ray vertebral-body mask, a 4096x3 complete point cloud from the CBCT, a 4096x3 partial point cloud from the ultrasound, a labelmap point array, a 3x4 projection matrix and transforms. The X-ray masks and projection matrices are identical across the two phantom files. The other three are synthetic VerSe20 splits (train 536.8 MB, val 176.4 MB, test 171.1 MB); the paper gives 149 lumbar samples split 60/20/20. The release has zero real radiograph images and zero CBCT volumes.
verdicts.real_xray: Acquired but not released as an image. The paper describes one Loop-X lateral projection per phantom. The share contains only a binary vertebral-body segmentation made from it, 256x256 per level, and the same array appears in both phantom files.
verdicts.paired_ct: A Loop-X CBCT was acquired and is inherently co-registered with the X-ray, according to the paper. It is not released as a volume. Only 4096-point per-vertebra surface clouds taken from it are shared, along with transforms and a projection matrix. Phantom 2 is a 3D print of VerSe20 subject 818, so its source CT and masks are already public through VerSe.
verdicts.anatomy: The released data covers only lumbar L1-L5, as five entries per phantom. The sacrum is described in the paper's phantom 1 appendix but is absent from the data. Both subjects are phantoms: one commercial L1-L5 plus sacrum with softer discs, and one 3D-printed from VerSe20 subject 818.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, according to the paper, and only for the phantom test data. Sec. 3.1 says: 'We also acquire paired lateral X-ray and cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans using a Loop-X system (medPhoton)… Since the system acquires both X-ray and CBCT images, they are inherently co-registered.' These are real projections of physical phantoms, not of humans. All training data is simulated: VerSe20 segmentation points are projected onto a mid-sagittal plane, so it is not even a DRR. The released files contain NO X-ray pixel data. For each phantom there is only a 256x256 label map per vertebra ('GT_Xray_segms', values 20-24) and a point cloud lifted from it ('labelmaps', 4096x3).
verdicts.paired_ct: The paper says a CBCT was acquired on the same Loop-X for each phantom, and that the CBCT and the X-ray are co-registered by the device. The CBCT volume is not released. Only 'complete_pcds' is: 5 vertebrae x 4096-point ground-truth surface point clouds per phantom, which the paper says were extracted from the CBCT. It also includes 'inverse_trafo_matrices', which map the normalised points back to a mm frame. I did not verify the CT-X-ray pairing from the data. The X-ray-side arrays (GT_Xray_segms, proj_matrices, trafos_to_RIA, transl_vectors) are byte-identical in the two phantom files, but the CBCT-derived complete_pcds differ, with a mean symmetric nearest-neighbour distance of about 2 mm. So either both phantoms reuse one X-ray, or the phantom2 file carries a copy of phantom 1's X-ray products. The source does not explain which.
verdicts.anatomy: Paper appendix A.1 describes the two phantoms. Phantom 1 is 'the five lumbar vertebrae L1-L5 and the sacrum as well as intervertebral disks from a different, softer material'. Phantom 2 is 'a 3D printed version of the volumetric annotations of lumbar vertebrae from subject 818 in the VerSe 2020 dataset', which is lumbar only with no sacrum stated. The released data covers L1-L5 only (labels 0-4, ids verLev20-verLev24, X-ray label values 20-24). No sacrum, pelvis or disc appears in any released array. I rendered the label map: it is a lateral view of whole vertebrae (bodies plus posterior elements), with L1 at the bottom of the image.
verdicts.counts: 2 phantoms and 0 human subjects. The paper reports 10 phantom vertebrae in total ('a total of 10 vertebrae from the two lumbar phantoms'). It implies one lateral X-ray and one CBCT per phantom ('a single lateral X-ray') but never gives an image count. The LRZ share is listable through its /wapi/filelink API. It holds exactly 5 files: phantom_with_vertBodylabelmap.h5 (4.1 MB), phantom2_with_vertlabelmap_polluted.h5 (4.1 MB), and Verse2020_VertBodyLabelmap_{train,val,test}.h5 (537/176/171 MB, synthetic, 149 VerSe20 lumbar spines in total). Each phantom file holds 5 vertebrae. None of the files contains a raw X-ray, CBCT or ultrasound image.
verdicts.licence: No data licence is stated anywhere I could see (README, LRZ share, paper). The GitHub repo has no top-level licence (the API returns license=None). ShapeCompletion/LICENSE is MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2021 PL', inherited from the MVP_Benchmark code, and covers code, not data. The arXiv paper carries the arXiv perpetual non-exclusive licence.
verdicts.access_now: Open, no login. The page https://syncandshare.lrz.de/getlink/fi5STHyTaLSYSwwC42iDog/ needs JavaScript, but the listing is at https://syncandshare.lrz.de/wapi/filelink/MjRKdnZUVjJFdWtYVE1ndnBWc0Jn?action=getFiles&ID=fi5STHyTaLSYSwwC42iDog&json=1. Files download from https://syncandshare.lrz.de/dl/fi5STHyTaLSYSwwC42iDog/<filename>. The /download/ resourceURL path returns a login page. On 2026-09-21 both phantom h5 files downloaded and are valid HDF5.
corrections: The released data does NOT contain the Loop-X X-ray images or the CBCT volumes. Both phantom files are point-cloud HDF5s. Their keys are incomplete_pcds (ultrasound partial point clouds, 5x4096x3), complete_pcds (CBCT-derived GT point clouds, 5x4096x3), labelmaps (X-ray segmentation lifted to 3D, 5x4096x3), GT_Xray_segms (5x256x256 label maps), proj_matrices (5x3x4), trafos_to_RIA, inverse_trafo_matrices, transl_vectors, labels, number_per_class and datasets_ids. A spine-fluoroscopy project gets no radiograph pixels and no CT/CBCT volume.

Anatomy 'L1-L5 + sacrum' applies only to physical phantom 1 as the paper appendix describes it. Phantom 2 is a 3D print of VerSe20 subject 818's lumbar annotations, and the paper does not state a sacrum for it. The released arrays contain L1-L5 only (ids verLev20-24). There is no sacrum, pelvis or lumbosacral junction.

'Vertebra segmentations' is only partly right. The released X-ray label map covers whole vertebrae (body plus posterior elements), although the paper text says 'we segment vertebral bodies semi-automatically from the X-ray scan'. The CBCT side is released only as point clouds, with no voxel segmentation.

The X-ray-derived arrays are byte-identical in the two phantom files: GT_Xray_segms, proj_matrices, trafos_to_RIA and transl_vectors. The CBCT-derived complete_pcds differ, with a mean symmetric NN distance of about 2 mm per vertebra. Either one X-ray serves both phantoms or the phantom2 file duplicates phantom 1's X-ray. The source does not say which, so treat phantom 2's X-ray pairing as unverified.

A pose exists but is undocumented: one 3x4 projection matrix, repeated for all 5 vertebrae and identical in both files. Its third row is [0.9999, -0.014, 0.0011, 705.88], which points the viewing axis roughly along left-right and fits a lateral view. No README or paper text defines its units or image frame.
X-ray count: the paper implies one lateral X-ray per phantom but gives no number. The released files contain 0 X-ray images and one 256x256 segmentation per vertebra.
Subjects: 2 phantoms and no human subjects. The training 'X-rays' are simulated by projecting VerSe20 segmentation points onto a plane, not by DRR rendering, and are not real acquisitions.
Licence: no data licence stated. The only licence file is MIT for code inherited from MVP_Benchmark (Copyright 2021 PL).

The test config refers to datasets/phantom_with_vertBodylabelmap_polluted.h5, which is not on the share. The share has phantom_with_vertBodylabelmap.h5 (no '_polluted') and phantom2_with_vertlabelmap_polluted.h5.

Confirmed: arXiv:2511.15600, submitted 2025-11-19, 'Accepted at the Workshop on Shape in Medical Imaging at MICCAI 2025', Springer DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-06774-6_17, TUM (Navab group). Device is medPhoton Loop-X. The LRZ share is openly downloadable, so the earlier 'could not be listed' note is resolved.

candidate.name: FAU Surgical-Device-Detection: real intraoperative spine CBCT-sweep projections with implant labels and calibrated matrices
candidate.why_relevant: The assets folder holds real clinical intraoperative projections from two spine cases (S260_Spine03, S264_Spine04) and two ankle cases. Each case has 19 views, every 20th frame of a CBCT sweep (v020-v380). There are ground-truth implant masks and keypoints, and the C-arm's calibrated 3x4 matrix for every view. It is a small but real NEED B set: spine intraoperative X-ray with screw labels and known pose. The matrix XML is Siemens-style (m_cadStudyUID, XCUData), and the 976x976 float TIFFs suggest a Cios Spin (inferred, not stated). There is no CT volume, and 19 views is too few for a usable reconstruction. Pretrained Faster/Mask R-CNN implant detectors are on HF (joshua-scheuplein). The Sci Rep manuscript is not yet indexed.
candidate.institution: FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (Joshua Scheuplein)
candidate.device: Mobile 3D C-arm, Siemens-style matrices (Cios Spin inferred)
candidate.anatomy: Thoracolumbar spine with pedicle screws (2 cases); ankle (2 cases)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Per-view calibrated 3x4 projection matrices; GT device masks/keypoints

corrections: The core claim is false: the shipped projections are SIMULATED, not real clinical X-ray. The README (both main and tag v1.0.0) says: 'All reported quantitative results are based exclusively on evaluations using real clinical data. Due to data privacy restrictions, these clinical images cannot be shared publicly. Therefore, this repository includes simulated example cases (provided as TIFF files)'. The candidate's real_xray should be false.

The shipped GT file is assets/ground_truth/implant_detection_simulated_test_gt.json. Every one of its 8022 image entries points to '/mnt/azureml/.../2025-07-Implant-Detection-V9-Simulated/Images/...'. All four shipped cases (S260_Spine03, S264_Spine04, S267_Ankle15, S279_Ankle05) are inside that Simulated dataset, 191 views each (v010 to v390 in steps of 2).

I rendered S260_Spine03_v100.tiff (976x976 float32, range 0.014 to 0.985). It looks like a DRR-style render: thoracic vertebrae and ribs, with screws, towers, tulips and a curved K-wire composited over them. Nothing in the source says it is a patient acquisition.
'Living patients: 2 spine + 2 ankle' is refuted. These are simulated cases. The real clinical test scans are not released, and no request route is given.

'Per-view calibrated 3x4 matrix for every view' needs correcting. The repo has ONE file, assets/projection_matrices/C_arm_Proj_Mats.xml. It holds 400 matrices (M0 to M399) plus I0_VALUES for a single sweep (m_cadStudyUID L-182593-L) and is shared by all four cases. It is not a separate calibration for each case. The real-looking Siemens geometry was used to simulate the images and does not show the images are real.

The GT PNGs under assets/ground_truth/<case>/ are 1410x1410 RGBA visualisation overlays (boxes, class names, coloured masks, keypoints; about 62k unique colours), not label masks. The machine-readable GT is the COCO JSON: 67,514 annotations, 4 keypoints each, RLE masks, 5 categories (screw, tulip_short, tower, tulip_long, wire).
The COCO JSON annotates 42 simulated cases (8022 images), but TIFFs ship for only 4 of them (76 images). The other 38 cases (7,258 images) are annotations only, with no pixels.

Cios Spin is not stated anywhere. The only device evidence is a code comment in utils/projection_matrix.py ('siemens standard (compensate siemens detector flip)') and the Siemens-style XML tags. The nKV field reads 1109, which is implausible as a kV value.
The candidate calls the spine cases 'thoracolumbar'. The source never states the level, and the rendered S260 view shows ribs (thoracic).
Licence mismatch: the code and the Zenodo record are Apache-2.0, but both HF checkpoints (joshua-scheuplein/Implant-Detector-Faster-R-CNN and -Mask-R-CNN) are tagged cc-by-nc-4.0.
The Sci Rep manuscript is not found on Crossref or by web search as of 2026-09-21. Zenodo describes the record only as accompanying the manuscript.

Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20696581 (published 2026-06-15, 0 downloads) has one file, Surgical-Device-Detection-v1.0.0.zip, 1,027,550,738 bytes, md5 8ed67d6cc03bbabfba09638953bf5e28; a HEAD request returns HTTP 200. The same content is on GitHub main / tag v1.0.0 (690 tree entries, about 1.11 GB of blobs). The real clinical intraoperative images are not available at all: the README says they 'cannot be shared publicly' for data-privacy reasons and gives no request route.
verdicts.licence: The repository and the Zenodo record are Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file, and GitHub spdx Apache-2.0). The pretrained HF checkpoints are CC-BY-NC-4.0.
verdicts.counts: 4 simulated cases (2 spine, 2 ankle), each with 19 TIFF views v020 to v380 (976x976 float32, 3,810,576 bytes each, 72.4 MB per case): 76 images in total, 38 of them spine. There are also 76 GT overlay PNGs, one COCO GT JSON (58.7 MB; 8022 simulated images across 42 cases, 67,514 annotations, 5 classes), 152+152 files of model predictions, 80+80 triangulation-result files (about 613 MB), 1 XML with 400 projection matrices, 2 detector configs, and figures.
verdicts.real_xray: No. The README says the example cases are simulated, the GT JSON's source dataset is named '2025-07-Implant-Detection-V9-Simulated', and the render looks like a DRR with composited implants. The real clinical data behind the reported results is withheld.
verdicts.paired_ct: None is released. The simulated projections presumably come from some volume plus implant models, but the repo never says what it was, and no CT is shipped.
verdicts.anatomy: Simulated spine views with pedicle screws, tulips, towers and K-wires. The rendered S260 view shows thoracic vertebrae and ribs, and the level is not stated. The two ankle cases are also simulated.

corrections: The images are NOT real acquisitions. The repo README says: 'All reported quantitative results are based exclusively on evaluations using real clinical data. Due to data privacy restrictions, these clinical images cannot be shared publicly. Therefore, this repository includes simulated example cases (provided as TIFF files)'. The candidate's 'real clinical intraoperative projections' and 'real_xray: true' are directly contradicted by the primary source.

The ground-truth file is named assets/ground_truth/implant_detection_simulated_test_gt.json. Every image entry in it points to '.../INPUT_dataset_dir/2025-07-Implant-Detection-V9-Simulated/Images/...'. Its info block reads 'Automatically generated COCO json file for Detectron2.'

I rendered S260_Spine03 and S264_Spine04 (v020, v120, v200). They look like forward projections of a finite reconstructed volume with virtual implants: the anatomy stops at hard rectangular volume edges with air outside, and the screws, towers, tulips and K-wires float in non-surgical orientations, crossing each other and running past the body. device_triangulation.py fixes volume_shape=(512,512,512) and voxel_size=0.313 mm, which fits simulation from a 3D C-arm volume. That these are simulated from CBCT is my reading of the renders and constants; it is not stated in words.

'Living patients: 2 spine + 2 ankle' is not supported. No source says the scenes are living patients, and what is released is simulated. The source volumes behind the simulations are not described or released.

Pose: there is one projection-matrix file, assets/projection_matrices/C_arm_Proj_Mats.xml, holding 400 matrices (M0-M399). device_triangulation.py loads that same file for every scene. So it is one shared nominal 400-view trajectory, not a calibration per case per acquisition. The header shows m_cadStudyUID 'L-182593-L' and XCUData nKV 1109. 'Siemens-style' is a fair description, but Cios Spin is not stated anywhere.

Labels: the COCO JSON has RLE segmentation masks, bounding boxes and 4 keypoints per device (tip, tip_direction, head, head_direction). There are 5 classes: screw, tulip_short, tower, tulip_long, wire. The per-view *_gt.png files are overlay previews, not mask files. All labels are simulation ground truth, not annotation of real images.

The GT JSON covers 42 simulated scenes, 8022 images and 67,514 annotations, at 191 views per scene (v010-v390, step 2). Six scenes are spine (S018_Spine05, S038_Spine03, S260_Spine03, S263_Spine05, S264_Spine04, S274_Spine01). The rest are ankle, foot, knee, wrist and elbow. Image files are released for only 4 scenes x 19 views = 76 TIFFs (38 spine). The count of 76 is right, but they are simulated.

Anatomy: the scene names say 'Spine', and vertebral bodies are faintly visible in the renders. No source gives a level or region, so 'thoracolumbar' is not supported. I could not identify lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis in the frames I rendered.
Licence: the code is Apache-2.0 (GitHub spdx and Zenodo). The pretrained checkpoints on HF (joshua-scheuplein/Implant-Detector-*-R-CNN) are CC-BY-NC-4.0, not Apache.

Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20696581 is a Software record ('Surgical-Device-Detection: v1.0.0', 2026-06-15, one zip of about 1.03 GB). It is a snapshot of the GitHub repo, not a dataset deposit. It names the Scientific Reports manuscript but gives no DOI for it.

For this project it does not serve need B. There is no real intraoperative X-ray, and the only pose is a shared nominal trajectory applied to simulated frames. At most it is a simulated-implant example set, and simulated DRR-like data are already available here.
verdicts.real_xray: No. The README says the released TIFFs are 'simulated example cases' and that the real clinical images cannot be shared. The GT dataset is named '2025-07-Implant-Detection-V9-Simulated'. The renders show projections of a finite volume with randomly placed virtual implants. The real clinical test data behind the reported metrics are not released.

The GT JSON describes 42 simulated scenes, 8022 images and 67,514 device annotations (6 spine scenes), but images are released for only 4 scenes.
