Every case contains a 602-frame rotational acquisition (XA multi-frame, PositionerMotion DYNAMIC) with per-frame PositionerPrimaryAngleIncrement starting at -119.7 deg and stepping about 0.4 deg per frame, covering roughly 240 deg. The runs also carry SID 1200 mm, SOD 760 mm, ImagerPixelSpacing 0.616 mm and a magnification factor of 1.579. That is 10 runs and 6,020 projection frames, each paired with its own CBCT reconstruction.

Only some fluoroscopy carries geometry. On the 8 NeuAngio 43C cases, the frames are 217 single-frame 1024x1024 12-bit Secondary Capture images (ImageType DERIVED). The one header I read had no SID, SOD or positioner-angle tags. The 2 NeuAngio 33F cases contain 30 multi-frame XA 'Fluoro' cines, 978x978 at 15 fps and 29-57 frames each (about 1,310 frames, estimated from file sizes), and these do carry SID, SOD, kVp and positioner angle. Two further 43C multi-frame files (192 MB and 128 MB) were not inspected because of the 429.

Anatomy is now verified by rendering, not just inferred from the name. I rendered one Secondary Capture frame, one 33F fluoroscopy frame, two spin frames and two CBCT slices. They show an anthropomorphic skull phantom with a radio-opaque cerebral vessel tree, mostly in one hemisphere, and a catheter. Protocol is 'Head-Cerebral', PatientSex is O, and patient names are test-like ('test_y_left_1', 'H_random_21'). There is no spine target. It is off-target for spine fluoroscopy, as flagged.

No pose or registration labels ship. Apart from DICOM, the zip holds only a README.txt (153 bytes: the description plus 'CC-BY 4.0'), a vendor 'info' XML per series and one dose-summary screenshot (Modality OT) per study. The only pose information is the DICOM positioner and geometry tags. The field pose_or_labels should be 'none as files; DICOM geometry tags only'.
Institution: the record gives the affiliation only as 'Northeast university' and the contact as a qq.com email. 'Shenyang, China' is an inference that the record does not state.
No paper is linked. The DataCite relatedIdentifiers are empty and the SciDB papers list is empty, so there is no methods description of the phantom or the acquisition protocol.

Confirmed as stated: DOI 10.57760/sciencedb.32821 resolves (302) to the SciDB detail page. There is one file, HeadPhantom_2D3D_TrainingDataset.zip, of 5,370,184,583 bytes, version V1. It was issued 2025-12-05 and the DataCite state is findable. Keywords are '2d-3d registration', 'head' and 'style transfer'. The licence is CC BY 4.0 in DataCite, in the SciDB copyRight field and in the README.
Could not check: the claim that only DataCite surfaces this dataset. The SciDB landing page itself loads (HTTP 200, title '10-case CT and X-ray DICOM dataset for 2D–3D registration').
verdicts.access_now: Open now, with no login. The anonymous download URL returns HTTP 200 for the whole 5.37 GB zip and supports byte ranges. I verified this by listing the zip directory and decoding DICOM through range reads. Only the file-tree browsing API asks for a login ('User Not Login'). The download host rate-limits: it returned HTTP 429 after a few hundred range requests and was still doing so more than 10 minutes later.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. It appears in the DataCite rightsList (cc-by-4.0), in the SciDB copyRight field and in the README.txt inside the zip.
verdicts.counts: There is one file: HeadPhantom_2D3D_TrainingDataset.zip, 5,370,184,583 bytes, 4,619 zip entries. It holds 10 studies: 8 on NeuAngio 43C and 2 on NeuAngio 33F. Per study there is one CBCT reconstruction (376 or 512 slices, 512x512 at 0.493 mm, 4,032 slices in total) and one 602-frame rotational run with per-frame angles (6,020 frames in total). The 43C studies add 217 single-frame 1024x1024 Secondary Capture fluoroscopy images and two further multi-frame files that were not inspected. The 33F studies add 30 multi-frame fluoroscopy cines at 978x978, about 1,310 frames. Each study also has a dose-summary screenshot, and each series has a vendor 'info' XML.
verdicts.anatomy: An anthropomorphic head phantom: a skull with a radio-opaque cerebral vessel tree and a catheter, under protocol 'Head-Cerebral'. I verified this by rendering fluoroscopy frames, spin frames and CBCT slices. There is no spine target, so it is off-target.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, but it is a C-arm CBCT, not a CT. Each case has a CBCT reconstructed on the same angiography C-arm from its own 602-frame rotational run (DerivationDescription 'CONTRAST-3D Recon From 2D XRay Angiography'). The rotational run is included along with its per-frame angles, SID 1200 mm and SOD 760 mm. No separate registration or pose files ship.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real X-ray acquisitions of a physical phantom on Neusoft NeuAngio 43C and 33F angiography C-arms, not simulations. The 33F fluoroscopy cines and all rotational runs are native XA multi-frame DICOM with geometry tags. The 43C fluoroscopy frames are stored as DERIVED Secondary Capture, and the one header I read had no geometry tags.

corrections: ANATOMY CONFIRMED BY RENDERING, OFF-TARGET: I rendered a CBCT mid-slice and a 2-D frame for every case. All 10 show the same vascular skull phantom: a skull, mandible and teeth, a contrast-filled tube network over one hemisphere, and a metal bead. Every series uses protocol 'Head-Cerebral'. No lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis appears anywhere. The candidate's 'not verified' can now read 'verified'.

THE 'CT' IS A C-ARM CBCT, NOT A DIAGNOSTIC CT: each volume's series is 'GCT_20sGCT', with DerivationDescription 'CONTRAST-3D Recon From 2D XRay Angiography'. It is stored under the CT Image SOP class but with Modality XA, and its FrameOfReferenceUID comes from that session's 602-frame rotational spin. Same phantom, same session, same C-arm: yes. Conventional CT: no.

SUBJECTS: probably one phantom, not 10. The 'cases' are 10 imaging sessions whose patient names encode how the phantom was repositioned: test_x_up_1, test_x_down_1, test_y_left_1, test_z_left_1, test_z_right_1, test_random_1/2/3 (NeuAngio 43C, 2024-10-10), and H_random_21/22 (NeuAngio 33F, 2024-10-12). The vessel pattern looks the same in all 10. They are not independent subjects.

DEVICE IS STATED in the DICOM headers, so 'not stated' is wrong: Neusoft Medical Systems NeuAngio 33F (2 sessions) and NeuAngio 43C (8 sessions), detector type DIRECT, source-detector distance about 1200 mm, source-patient distance 760 mm. On the 33F, imager pixel spacing is 0.308 mm and the field of view is 300 mm.

'NATIVE DICOM FLUOROSCOPY' IS ONLY PARTLY TRUE. Native multi-frame XA fluoro cines (SOP 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.12.1, pulsed, 15 fps, 65-70 kVp) exist as 15 runs in each of the two 33F sessions (631 and 679 frames, 978x978). The 43C sessions have only one run in each of two sessions: 78 frames at 1294x952, and about 52 frames (inferred from file size). The other 217 2-D images, all in the 43C sessions, are 8-bit Secondary Capture screen captures (SOP 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.7, ConversionType WSD, 1024x1024, letterboxed) with no geometry tags.

COUNTS WERE NOT LISTED; FROM THE ZIP CENTRAL DIRECTORY: 4,619 entries, 8.99 GB uncompressed. They comprise 10 CBCT volumes (2x512 + 8x376 slices = 4,032 slices), 10 rotational spins of 602 projection frames each (6,020 frames with per-frame angles, -119.7 deg onward), 32 native XA fluoro cines (about 1,440 frames), 217 secondary-capture frames, 10 dose-summary screenshots, 153 vendor 'info' XML files and one README.

POSE/LABELS: there are none. The README says only what the abstract says. No annotation, pose, landmark or registration ground-truth file exists. Implicit geometry is present: the native XA cines and spins carry positioner primary/secondary angles, source-detector and source-patient distances, and Table Motion STATIC. The spins also carry per-frame angle arrays and private NeuAngio arrays (0019,1003/1005). Secondary captures carry no geometry.

ACCESS CONFLICT RESOLVED: open, no login. The versionList API returns shareStatus PUBLIC with protectMonth 0. The direct download URL returns HTTP 200 anonymously with content-length 5,370,184,583 and accepts range requests. It returns HTTP 429 after bursts of requests. The 'User Not Login' reply comes from a SciDB file-query API endpoint, not from the download.
INSTITUTION: the primary metadata says only 'Northeast university', with no city. 'Northeastern University, Shenyang' is an inference and no primary source states it.
No associated paper is linked (referenceLinks and papers are empty). A web search does surface the SciDB page directly, so it is not 'only DataCite'.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real acquisitions of a phantom on Neusoft NeuAngio 33F/43C flat-detector angiography C-arms. The dose reports log 16 pulsed fluoro events at 65 kV plus one 20 s, 120 kV rotational 'GCT' spin per session. There are no DRRs or MV portal images. However, 217 of the 2-D frames (in the 8 NeuAngio 43C sessions) are 8-bit secondary-capture screen grabs, not native XA.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, but it is a C-arm cone-beam CT reconstructed from the same session's 602-frame rotational spin on the same device ('CONTRAST-3D Recon From 2D XRay Angiography', 512x512, 0.37 mm voxels in the 33F sessions, 0.49 mm in the 43C sessions). It is not a separate diagnostic CT. It shares a frame of reference with the spin. The fluoro runs have C-arm angles but no frame-of-reference UID.
verdicts.anatomy: A head (skull) phantom with a contrast-filled vessel tree, protocol 'Head-Cerebral', verified by rendering a CBCT slice and a 2-D frame for all 10 sessions. No lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis.
verdicts.counts: Probably one phantom, imaged in 10 repositioned sessions. They contain 10 CBCT volumes (4,032 slices), 10 spins of 602 frames (6,020 projections with angles), 32 native XA fluoro cines (about 1,440 frames), 217 secondary-capture frames and 10 dose screenshots. The zip is 5.37 GB compressed, 8.99 GB uncompressed, 4,619 entries.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated in DataCite rightsList (cc-by-4.0), in the SciDB copyRight field, and in the README inside the zip.
verdicts.access_now: Open. The direct download works anonymously (HTTP 200/206, no login, range requests supported); shareStatus is PUBLIC with no embargo. The server rate-limits with HTTP 429 after bursts.

candidate.name: NIT Warangal / NIMS Hyderabad intraoperative lumbar Ziehm C-arm AP/LAT + preoperative CT with L1-L5 centroids (2D-3D-sci-registration)
candidate.why_relevant: This matches the task exactly. Living patients have real intraoperative lumbar C-arm AP and lateral frames, a same-patient preoperative CT, and level-named vertebra centroids in both modalities: L1-L5 and sometimes D11/D12, in 3D (LPS mm) on the CT and in 2D pixels on every X-ray. The centroid .mrk.json files and registered 6-DoF poses (EPnP + CMA-ES; PDE in results/, mean 1.63 mm) are already public. The CT and X-ray NRRDs must come from the authors. The README says 'contact the authors', and the manuscript says de-identified data are available on reasonable request. It adds a device not yet in the collection (Ziehm Vision FD; SID 1110 mm, 0.2 mm/px, 1024x1024 in the pipeline's camera model). The README reports 9 patients and 51 sets; the manuscript evaluates 2 patients and 13 projections. Caution: the patient folder names in the public repo look like real personal names, which matters for any DUA.
candidate.institution: National Institute of Technology Warangal; Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Hyderabad, India (Raghu Gangolu)
candidate.device: Ziehm Vision FD mobile C-arm (as assumed by the pipeline)
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine L1-L5 (plus T11/T12 'D11/D12' on some)
candidate.n_images: 51 AP/LAT C-arm sets (mostly 3 AP + 3 LAT per patient), about 100 X-rays
candidate.pose_or_labels: Public: 3D CT centroids + 2D X-ray centroids by level; registered 6-DoF poses per set (results/newdata)
candidate.licence: MIT (code and annotations); images and CT not released
candidate.published: Repo created 2026-07-15, updated 2026-08-28; paper under review at Scientific Reports

verdicts.access_now: Only partly downloadable. The CT and raw X-ray volumes are not released. .gitignore excludes *.nrrd/*.dcm/*.nii, the README says 'CT NRRDs and X-ray NRRDs are not included... contact the authors or obtain the clinical data through your institution', and the manuscript's data statement says data 'will be made available upon reasonable request subject to ethics and data-governance constraints'. That statement is a promise, not a release, and there is no request channel, DUA or form. Downloadable now: 60 Slicer centroid JSONs, 10 results JSONs, a 9.0 MB report PDF and 54 overlay PNGs. The PNGs are 3072x1024, 125.2 MB in total. Each holds the real C-arm frame as a 1024x1024 8-bit panel with markers and burned-in scanner text drawn over it, next to a DRR, so the X-ray pixels are in practice public in degraded form. The CT is visible only as rendered DRRs. The repo has no releases, no tags and no DOI, and holds one commit (b501c8b3, 2026-07-15).
verdicts.licence: A LICENSE file carries MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2026 Raghu Gangolu, National Institute of Technology Warangal'. It covers 'this software and associated documentation files'. There are no separate data terms and no DUA, and the images and CT are not licensed at all because they are not released. Whether MIT legitimately covers patient-derived annotations is doubtful: the manuscript's ethics protocol number reads '[to be inserted]'.
verdicts.counts: Checked against the git tree. There are 9 patient folders with 9 CT centroid files and 51 X-ray centroid files: 24 AP and 27 LAT. Swaroop has LAT only (3). Each 'SET' folder is one image, so there are 51 annotated frames, not about 100. At least one frame is duplicated: the RASVANTI AP-SET-2 and AP-SET-3 overlays have identical X-ray pixels and identical centroids. Swaroop LAT-SET-1 and LAT-SET-2 also look like the same frame (0.3% of pixels differ). That leaves at most about 49 distinct frames. There are 54 overlay PNGs, which includes 3 stale Swaroop AP overlays with no AP centroid files. all_results.json also holds an 'ARJUN (baseline)' entry with 5 projections that has no data folder. The manuscript (main.tex) is a different cohort: 'A Two-Patient Feasibility Study' of Arjun (5 AP JPEG frames with Labelme 2-D annotations) and Ramulamma (8 TIF/DICOM frames, no 2-D annotations), 13 projections. Neither patient's annotations are in data/.
verdicts.anatomy: Label totals across all 60 files: L3 60, L4 58, L5 55, L2 51, L1 34, D12 13, and S1 once (SHRILATHA's CT, which has no L1). D11 appears nowhere. Many frames carry only 3 levels: every JYOTHI AP frame has L3-L5 only, and several NAYEEMA frames have L3-L5 only. The frames are intraoperative with pedicle screws in place (BIKNA AP shows instrumentation at several levels), and the preoperative CT has none, which the manuscript acknowledges as a metal mismatch.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, a same-patient preoperative CT exists: each patient has a CT CENTROID.mrk.json in LPS mm. The CT volumes are not public.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. The overlays show real clinical C-arm frames with burned-in scanner text: kV, mA, fluoro time, mGy, W/L, 'Dr.' / 'Neurosurgery', patient IDs such as PAT3381 and PAT3815, and acquisition dates and times such as '..7.03.2026 15:40:14' and '07.07.2026 10:21:58'.
corrections: The candidate says about 100 X-rays. Each SET folder holds one image, so there are 51 annotated frames (24 AP, 27 LAT). At least one is an exact duplicate (RASVANTI AP-SET-2 = AP-SET-3, same pixels and same centroids) and one is a near duplicate (Swaroop LAT-SET-1 and LAT-SET-2), leaving at most about 49 distinct frames.

The candidate says 'registered 6-DoF poses per set' are public. They are not. The results JSONs store only best_pose_delta, a 6-vector offset from the EPnP pose, and it is all zeros on 41 of the 51 new-patient projections because the safety net reverted to EPnP. They also store per-vertebra deformation vectors. An absolute pose would have to be re-derived by EPnP from the public centroids under the assumed intrinsics.

The mean PDE of 1.63 mm is not an independent accuracy. It is the reprojection residual of the same 2-D centroids that EPnP was fitted to, measured in detector-plane mm (pixel error x 0.2 mm), and CMA-ES left the EPnP pose unchanged on most sets.

Ziehm Vision FD is an assumption, not the confirmed device. src/generic_patient_loader.py says 'Ziehm Vision FD assumed - no DICOM metadata'. The manuscript names no device, calls the SID and pixel spacing 'nominal', and lists 'No calibrated geometry' as a limitation. The burned-in overlay text does not show a vendor name.
D11 appears in no file. D12 appears on 13 files and S1 on one CT (SHRILATHA, whose CT has no L1).

The X-ray pixels are not entirely unreleased. The 54 public overlay PNGs include each real frame at 1024x1024 8-bit with markers and burned-in text on top. They are usable for viewing, not as raw or calibrated data.

The manuscript's 2 patients (Arjun, Ramulamma) do not overlap with the 9 README patients, and their annotations are not in data/. The README's 9 patients / 51 sets appear in no paper text in the repo.

The 'updated 2026-08-28' date is only GitHub's updated_at metadata. pushed_at is 2026-07-15, and the repo has one commit. 'Under review at Scientific Reports' comes only from the README BibTeX and could not be verified.

The privacy concern is worse than folder names. The overlays carry burned-in patient IDs (PAT3381, PAT3815), acquisition dates and times, and a department header. The folder names (BIKNA, JYOTHI, NAYEEMA BEGUM, RASVANTI, SARKHI, SHRILATHA, SHRINIVAS, Swaroop, VIJAYALAXMI) and the script names (swaroopa, ramulamma, arjun) look like real personal names. This contradicts the manuscript's 'Patient data have been de-identified', and the ethics protocol number is '[to be inserted]'.

The manuscript's authors are from NIMS Orthopaedics, while the overlay header reads 'Neurosurgery'. The manuscript is also inconsistent on design: the abstract says 'retrospective feasibility evaluation' and the introduction says 'prospectively collected'.
The X-ray .mrk.json files declare coordinateSystem 'LPS' and units 'mm', but the values are pixel (u,v,0). A consumer that trusts the header would misread them.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. I viewed all 51 public overlay PNGs (results/newdata/<patient>/<SET>_overlay.png; panel 1 is the native 1024x1024 X-ray). All are real intraoperative C-arm frames, not DRRs. Each shows burned-in console text (kV, mA, fluoro time, mGy, frame counter, 'Dr. Neurosurgery'), and most show surgical instruments, retractors, K-wires, pedicle screws and rods, with circular iris collimation on many. Caveats: (1) They are display-type captures with burned-in text. Many are display-rotated ('R 72/90/103/106 deg'), so some frames in XRAY-AP folders show the spine horizontal. (2) Metal that is absent from the preop CT is present in most frames. (3) Ziehm Vision FD is not established for the nine README patients. generic_patient_loader.py says 'Ziehm Vision FD assumed - no DICOM metadata'. Ziehm, SID 1110 mm and 0.2 mm/px are sourced only for the separate Ramulamma DICOMs (ramulamma_loader.py cites private tag 0019,1014). ramulamma_testing_loader.py gives 0.2977 mm/px from an NRRD header, which contradicts 0.2.
verdicts.paired_ct: Stated, not verifiable. README: one 'Preop CT (NRRD)' per patient, never published; only the CT-side CENTROID.mrk.json (LPS mm) is public. Panel 3 of each overlay is a DRR rendered from that CT, and it lines up plausibly with the X-ray in e.g. BIKNA, JYOTHI and Swaroop. So a CT existed on the authors' side and appears to be the same patient's, but pairing cannot be checked independently. The published PDE cannot confirm it either (see the pose corrections). data_loader.py names Siemens-style series ('L_Spine 1.0 B60s/I26s') for the manuscript patients.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar spine. X-ray centroid labels are L1-L5 plus D12 only; D11 appears in no public file (only in code). Many sets have only 3-4 levels, e.g. JYOTHI AP sets are L3-L5. CT label sets differ by patient: SHRILATHA's CT has S1,L5-L2 and no L1; several CTs add D12. Sacrum, SI joints and iliac wings are visible in several AP frames (JYOTHI AP 1-3, NAYEEMA AP-1, SHRILATHA AP-1, SARKHI AP). But S1, sacrum and pelvis are never annotated on any X-ray, and the lumbosacral junction is out of field in many frames (e.g. BIKNA L5 at v=994 of 1024).
verdicts.counts: README cohort: 9 patients and 51 sets. One set folder holds one image NRRD and one centroid file (_discover_sets takes nrrds[0]), so 51 sets = 51 X-ray images, not ~100. That is 8 patients x (3 AP + 3 LAT) plus Swaroop with 3 LAT only. Duplicates: RASVANTI AP-SET-2 and AP-SET-3 are pixel-identical frames (mean abs diff 0.0) with byte-identical centroid JSONs. Swaroop LAT-SET-1 and LAT-SET-2 are the same frame (diff 0.31, same frame counter). So there are at most 49 unique frames. The manuscript's 2 patients (Arjun: 5 AP JPEGs of varying size, Labelme 2D labels; Ramulamma: 8 TIF/DICOM frames of 85 TIF + 107 DICOM, no 2D labels) are NOT among the nine. Their annotations are not in the repo; only Arjun's scores appear in all_results.json as 'ARJUN (baseline)'. The loader docstring names three more patients (MANGTA, NARSIMHA, SAMRAJYAM) that are also absent.
verdicts.licence: A root MIT LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2026 Raghu Gangolu, NITW') covers the repository. It is a generic software licence that says nothing about the annotation JSONs or overlay images, and no data licence or DUA exists. CT and X-ray NRRDs are not released. The public overlays carry patient identifiers (below), so redistribution is questionable whatever the MIT file says.
verdicts.access_now: Public now: the centroid .mrk.json files (2D X-ray centroids stored as pixel (u,v,0) despite a 'LPS mm' header), results JSONs, 51 overlay PNGs showing the real frames, and the registration_report.pdf (not opened). Images and CT: README says 'contact the authors or obtain the clinical data through your institution'; the manuscript says 'upon reasonable request subject to ethics and data-governance constraints'. There is no formal process, and the manuscript's ethics protocol number reads '[to be inserted]'.
corrections: The '~100 X-rays' figure is wrong. Each set is one image (one NRRD plus one CENTROID.mrk.json per folder), so 51 sets = 51 X-rays, and Swaroop has LAT only.
The 51 contain duplicates. RASVANTI AP-SET-2 and AP-SET-3 are pixel-identical frames with byte-identical annotations; Swaroop LAT-SET-1 and LAT-SET-2 are the same frame. At most 49 unique frames.

The manuscript's '2 patients / 13 projections' are not a subset of the nine. They are two different patients (Arjun, Ramulamma) whose data and 2D annotations are not in the repo. Ramulamma has no 2D annotations at all.

No registered absolute 6-DoF pose is published. results.json stores only 'best_pose_delta' relative to an unsaved EPnP initialisation, and it is all zeros in 46 of 56 projections (safety-net revert). A pose can be recomputed from the public centroids, but only under assumed nominal intrinsics.

The 'mean PDE 1.63 mm' is circular. It is the EPnP/SQPNP reprojection residual on the same 2D centroids used to fit the pose (0.0 mm wherever only 3 landmarks exist). It is not an independent registration accuracy, and it cannot confirm CT/X-ray pairing.

The Ziehm Vision FD device, SID 1110 mm and 0.2 mm/px are ASSUMED for the nine README patients (loader docstring: 'Ziehm Vision FD assumed - no DICOM metadata'). They are sourced only for the separate Ramulamma DICOMs. Another loader reads 0.2977 mm/px from an NRRD header. The manuscript calls SID 'source-to-isocenter', the code 'source-to-image'.
Only D12 appears in any public label file, never D11. SHRILATHA's CT lacks L1 and has S1. Many X-ray sets annotate only 3-4 levels.
Sacrum and pelvis are visible in several AP frames but never annotated on X-ray. No S1 or pelvic landmark exists in any 2D label.
Frames are display captures with burned-in text and arbitrary display rotation. Most contain pedicle screws, rods, retractors or K-wires that are absent from the preop CT.

Identifiers are exposed publicly, beyond the folder names. Overlay PNGs show burned-in patient IDs (e.g. PAT3381, PAT3815, PAT3258, PAT3060), acquisition dates and times (29.11.2025 to 07.07.2026) and, in at least one frame, what looks like age/sex ('27 M'). This contradicts the manuscript's 'Patient data have been de-identified'. The ethics protocol number is '[to be inserted]'.
'Updated 2026-08-28' is GitHub metadata only. The repo has a single commit (b501c8b, 2026-07-15), and pushed_at is 2026-07-15.
The manuscript contradicts itself on design: the abstract says 'retrospective', the introduction says 'prospectively collected'.

candidate.name: Hohai University / Changzhou lumbar intraoperative X-ray + CT (LineReg; Shen et al., Med Phys 2026)
candidate.why_relevant: This is semantic edge-guided single-view 2D/3D registration. Ten patients have preoperative lumbar CT and intraoperative X-rays. The paper uses 90 real clinical registration samples and 710 edge-annotated images (real X-rays plus DRRs) with vertebral-body edge masks. The GitHub repo is code only, and 'Dual-view registration on Real X-rays' is still unchecked on its roadmap. The article is not open access, the Wiley page is Cloudflare-blocked and the data statement was not read. Email the authors. It may share a data source with ABLSpineLevelCheck (same university and city).
candidate.institution: Hohai University, Changzhou; Changzhou No.2 and Third People's Hospitals (Shen A, Jiang J, et al.)
candidate.device: not stated
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine
candidate.n_images: 90 real registration samples; 710 edge-annotated images (mixed real and DRR)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Vertebral-body edge masks; registration GT (mTRE)

corrections: Access is 'not released', not 'unknown'. No CT, X-ray, edge mask or pose file is downloadable anywhere I could find. The only availability sentence in the abstract is 'The code for the proposed method is available at github.com/shenao1995/lineReg'. It says nothing about data.

I found no data availability statement on the public record, which is not proof that none exists. The Wiley page loads (HTTP 200) when curl_cffi impersonates chrome131; the default chrome, safari, firefox and edge fingerprints get 403, so the page is not simply Cloudflare-blocked. What it shows publicly is the abstract, a Conflict of Interest statement ('no conflicts of interest'), the Supporting Information and the references. The page's own metadata says format-viewed=abstract. The full text sits behind a subscription (OpenAlex oa_status=closed; Europe PMC 'Subscription required', isOpenAccess=N, hasData=N), so a statement in the body text was not read. The PDF link returned the HTML paywall page.

The Supporting Information (mp70385-sup-0001-SuppMat.pdf, 262.1 KB, downloaded and read) contains only ablation tables and figures: ESegMamba beta and epochs, CMA-ES Cov, Sigma and alpha. It has no data statement and no description of acquisition or device.
The GitHub repo has no licence at all (GitHub API license=null), so default copyright applies. 'Code only' describes its contents, not a licence.

Repo contents (about 49 MB, default branch master): Python code (lineReg_main.py, line_infer.py, reg_process_vis.py, utils.py); three AttUNet .pth weights of 8.0 MB each; a 12.9 MB GIF; two small PNGs; .idea and __pycache__ files. The weights are named AttUNet, not ESegMamba, so the published edge network's weights do not appear to be there. I checked the file trees of the 20 most recent commits (2024-05 to 2026-05) and found no CT, X-ray, mask or pose files in any of them. The README tells users to put their own Data/case1/ct.nii.gz and ct_seg.nii.gz in place.

The README roadmap marks only 'Single-view registration on simulated X-rays' as done. 'Dual-view on simulated' and 'Dual-view on Real X-rays' are unchecked, and single-view on real X-rays is not listed at all. So the released code demonstrates simulated data only.

Hospital affiliation: the paper lists 'The Third Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, Changzhou' (Nong L, Chen Q), which is Changzhou No.2 People's Hospital. No 'Third People's Hospital' appears. The candidate omitted an industry partner: Tuodao Medical Technology Co., Ltd., Nanjing (Wang F, Wu X), a spine-robot company. That makes data sharing less likely. The corresponding author is Junfeng Jiang (Hohai, College of AI and Automation); the address is shown as [email protected] on the page. Grant: Jiangsu BE2022718.

The ABLSpineLevelCheck link is plausible but unproven. The paper cites it as ref 36 (Jiang J, Shuai L, Zeng Q, BIBM 2024), and its first author is this paper's corresponding author. Nothing I read states that the two share a data source.

Dates: issue date March 2026 (Med Phys 53(3): e70385). First published online 15 March 2026 per Wiley and Crossref. Received 2025-04-13, accepted 2026-02-26. The candidate's '2026-03-01' is the issue or print date.

'10 living patients' and 'each has preoperative CT and intraoperative X-rays' go further than the abstract. The abstract says 710 images 'comprising X-rays and DRRs derived from 10 patients', split 4:1 by patient into 568 train and 142 test, and '90 real clinical samples' plus 300 simulated. The real/DRR mix within the 710 is not given, and neither is how real-data ground truth was obtained. On real data the abstract reports 'mean in-plane translation error ~1.5 mm', not mTRE; mTRE is stated for the method comparisons.
Device and C-arm model are not given in the abstract or the supplement. The body text was not read.
verdicts.access_now: Not downloadable. The paper exists (PMID 41833531, DOI 10.1002/mp.70385) but only code is released. No data repository, DOI or accession is cited in the abstract, the supplement or the GitHub repo. No data availability statement is visible on the public Wiley page; the full text is paywalled and was not read. The author's other repos (RadGS_Reg, LineRegWeb, PayerSeg_Revised, FlowReg) were listed; RadGS_Reg was also checked and ships no data either. The only route is to email the corresponding author, Junfeng Jiang (Hohai University). A Tuodao Medical industry co-authorship makes release unlikely.
verdicts.licence: No data licence, because no data is released. The code repo has no licence file (GitHub license=null, default copyright). The article is subscription-access under Wiley VOR terms and the Wiley TDM licence 1.1.
verdicts.counts: From the abstract: 10 patients; 710 edge-annotated images (X-rays plus DRRs, mix unstated), split 568 train / 142 test by patient; 300 simulated and 90 real clinical registration samples. Nothing is released.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, within the study: '90 real clinical samples' of intraoperative X-rays, with about 1.5 mm in-plane translation error reported on real data. None are released.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, within the study: preoperative lumbar CT registered to intraoperative X-rays for the same patients. Not released.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar spine, with vertebra-level registration (code targets L1-L5 via labels 21-25 in a user-supplied segmentation).

verdicts.real_xray: Partly confirmed. The abstract (Europe PMC, and the Wiley page reached with Safari TLS impersonation) says the aim is "aligning preoperative CT with intraoperative X-rays". It reports 2D/3D registration "on 300 simulated samples and 90 real clinical samples", and says "On real clinical data" the in-plane translation error was about 1.5 mm. So the 90 are real, not DRRs. No accessible source names the device or says whether these are C-arm fluoroscopy frames or radiographs. The 710-image edge set is described as "comprising X-rays and Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs", and the real/DRR split is not stated. The sister JCAD paper has the same author list and hospital (10.3724/SP.J.1089.2024-00438). It describes its own real data as intraoperative AP and lateral X-rays, 976x976 at 0.3 mm, focal length 1124 mm, with extrinsics from an optical tracking system. That points to a navigated or robotic C-arm setup, but it is a different paper with 8 CTs, and the overlap with this one is not stated.
verdicts.paired_ct: Preoperative CT, not CBCT, per the abstract. Same-subject pairing is implied, not stated per patient. The 90 real clinical samples are registered to CT and follow "the same patient-specific split" as the 10 patients. The abstract does not say that all 10 patients have real intraoperative X-rays.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar spine only. The Purpose says "single-view lumbar spine 2D/3D registration", the MeSH major topic is Lumbar Vertebrae, and the repo code targets L1-L5 from a multi-label CT segmentation. The sacrum and pelvis are not mentioned in the abstract, the supporting information, the repo, or either sister paper (CJIG 2025, JCAD). Whether S1 or the pelvis appears in the field of view is unknown.
verdicts.counts: 10 patients. 710 images for edge segmentation (X-rays plus DRRs, split not stated), 568 train and 142 test on a 4:1 patient split. Registration: 300 simulated samples and 90 real clinical samples. The number of distinct real X-ray exposures is NOT stated. In the sister JCAD paper a "sample" is one single-vertebra crop (8 patients gave 16 samples and 32 AP+lateral images), so 90 samples could come from far fewer frames.
verdicts.licence: No licence. The GitHub API reports license: null and the repo has no LICENSE file, so even the code is all-rights-reserved by default. The repo holds code plus three AttUNet .pth weight files and no data. The article is closed access (OpenAlex oa_status closed; Europe PMC "Subscription required").
verdicts.access_now: No data access. No data availability statement appears on the Wiley abstract page, which shows the abstract, a COI statement, supporting information and references. The full text is paywalled and was not read. The supporting information (mp70385-sup-0001-SuppMat.pdf, retrieved) has only ablation studies and no dataset description. The released lineReg code registers only against a DRR rendered at a known ground-truth pose. The README roadmap marks "Single-view registration on simulated X-rays" done and leaves dual-view simulated and "Dual-view registration on Real X-rays" unchecked. The only route is to email the corresponding author, Junfeng Jiang ([e-mail withheld], listed in the JCAD paper). Two co-authors are from Tuodao Medical Technology, a spinal-robot company, which may limit release; this is inferred, not stated.
corrections: Affiliations: the only hospital listed is 'The Third Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, Changzhou' (Nong L, Chen Q), which is Changzhou Second People's Hospital. No 'Third People's Hospital' is named. Also missing from the candidate: Tuodao Medical Technology Co., Ltd., Nanjing (Wang F, Wu X), an industry co-affiliation. Grant: Jiangsu Province Key Research Program BE2022718.
'90 real registration samples' are samples, not images. The abstract gives no count of distinct real X-ray frames. In the same group's JCAD paper a sample is one single-vertebra crop.
The real/DRR split of the 710 edge-annotated images is not stated anywhere accessible. The abstract only says the set comprises 'X-rays and Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs'.

Ground truth on real data is unverified. The abstract reports mTRE for method comparison, but for real clinical data it reports only 'mean in-plane translation error of approximately 1.5 mm'. How the real-data reference pose was obtained is not stated in any accessible source for this paper. The sister JCAD paper used optical-tracking extrinsics, but it is not shown that this paper did.

'Ten patients have preoperative lumbar CT and intraoperative X-rays' is a paraphrase. The abstract says the images are 'derived from 10 patients'. It does not say all 10 have real intraoperative X-rays, and it never says 'living'; it says 'clinical'.

'Vertebral-body edge masks' is only partly supported. The abstract says 'vertebral body edges' are used as semantic features and gives Dice/mIoU for their segmentation, but who annotated the edges and how is not stated. In the CJIG and JCAD sister papers, radiologists labelled the edges on DRRs.
The device is not stated, and neither is fluoroscopy versus radiograph. The registration is single-view.
Sacrum and pelvis: never mentioned. Anatomy is the lumbar spine only; the code parses L1-L5 labels.
Licence is not 'code only'. The repo has NO licence (GitHub license null) and contains AttUNet weights. It has no data, and the only registration code released is simulated.

The Wiley page is not fully blocked. curl_cffi with impersonate='safari' returns 200 for the abstract page and the supporting information; the full text is still subscription-only. No data availability statement is visible.

Two earlier papers by the same authors give a stated data picture. The CJIG 2025 paper (10.11834/jig.240001; Hohai plus Changzhou First People's Hospital) used 10 CTs for simulated DRRs, and its real data was one patient's CT and ONE intraoperative AP X-ray. The JCAD paper (10.3724/SP.J.1089.2024-00438; same authors and hospital as the Med Phys paper) used 8 CTs with intraoperative AP and lateral X-rays, 16 single-vertebra samples and 32 images. Neither has a data-sharing statement. Whether the Med Phys cohort of 10 overlaps them is not stated.

The link to ABLSpineLevelCheck is speculation. That paper (BIBM 2024, 10.1109/bibm62325.2024.10822817) shares only the corresponding author, Junfeng Jiang of Hohai University. No source says the data source is shared.
Publication date confirmed: print 2026-03-01, Med Phys 53(3):e70385, PMID 41833531, indexed 2026-03-16.

candidate.name: SJTU Med-X / Tongji / TAOiMAGE calibrated standing biplanar lumbar radiographs + CT (Yu, Tsai et al.; Med Phys 2026)
candidate.why_relevant: Living-patient lumbar radiographs from a calibrated biplanar DR system, a new device class. The same-patient CT is segmented and registered into the X-ray geometry (repeatability under 0.3 mm and 0.7 degrees), giving a gold-standard 6-DoF pose per vertebra. Several postures are covered: flexion, extension, bending and rotation. One subject has lumbar sacralization, relevant to LSTV. The data statement says available from the corresponding author on reasonable request; code is public. Counts differ by version: Med Phys has 64 (48 non-pathological at Centre 1 plus 16 pathological at Centre 2, Third Hospital of Hebei Medical University); arXiv has 50 subjects drawn from 225 CTs, with a 144-pair test set from 8 subjects. The group also runs dual-fluoroscopic spine kinematics studies on the same hardware.
candidate.institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of BME / Med-X; Shanghai Tongji Hospital; TAOiMAGE Medical Technologies (Tsung-Yuan Tsai)
candidate.device: TAOiMAGE Golden Eye / Eagle Eye biplanar X-ray (3072x3072, 0.139 mm); CT United Imaging uCT760
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine L1-L5
candidate.subjects: 64 living (Med Phys) / 50 (arXiv) with CT + biplanar X-rays; 270 further CTs for shape models
candidate.n_images: 2 views per posture, multiple postures per subject
candidate.pose_or_labels: CT-to-biplanar registered vertebral poses; 7 landmarks per vertebra

verdicts.access_now: Not downloadable. The paper exists (Med Phys 2026;53(8):e70570, online 22 Jul 2026, PMID 42482570, PMC13389557), but no data release exists. Med Phys data statement, verbatim: "The datasets generated or analyzed during the study are not publicly available due to privacy and ethical restrictions regarding patient confidentiality but are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request." The arXiv v3 statement says only "Data will be made available on request." The paper lists three corresponding authors ([e-mail withheld], [e-mail withheld], [e-mail withheld]), but the statement says "the corresponding author" without naming one. I searched Zenodo, DataCite, figshare and Hugging Face and found no deposit. Crossref has no dataset relation. Europe PMC tags the record "supporting_data", but that tag is a text-mined link to arXiv:1904.04514 (the HRNet paper), not a dataset. The only public thing is code: github.com/ywx0314/lumbar_multitask. It was created 2025-10-21, last pushed 2026-04-22 and is 52 KB. It holds training and test scripts, an HRNet network, losses and stray .pyc files. It has no data, no weights, no releases, and no train.txt, test.txt or testGuangzhou.txt split lists (the configs point to a missing data/ folder).
verdicts.licence: No data licence, because no data was released. The code repo has no LICENSE file; its README says only "Copyright (c) 2024. by Wanxin Yu", which in practice means all rights reserved. The article is (c) 2026 AAPM under Wiley VOR/TDM terms. PMC places it in the Wiley Open Access Collection, but its metadata sets pmc-prop-open-access to no.
verdicts.counts: Med Phys: 270 separate lumbar CTs (512x512, 0.812 mm, 1.0 mm slices, from several centres, used for the shape models and 810 DRR pairs). Centre 1: 48 subjects without pathology, each with CT and biplanar X-rays. They performed flexion, extension, left/right bending and left/right rotation at three ranges each, giving 864 biplanar pairs (48 x 18). Centre 2: 16 pathological patients (compression, prior fusion, spondylolisthesis), each with CT and ONE standing biplanar pair. The test set is 144 Centre-1 pairs plus the 16 Centre-2 pairs. arXiv v3: 225 CTs (uCT760), with calibrated biplanar X-rays for "50 of the participants", so the 50 are a subset of the 225. There are about 18 pairs per participant. Two subjects (one L2-L3 fusion, one sacralization) form a special test set. Of the other 48, 8 subjects give the 144 test pairs and 40 subjects give 720 train/val pairs. I could not work out from the text whether the two abnormal-count subjects are counted within Med Phys's 48 or sit on top of them (Med Phys moves them to Supplement S4).
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar L1-L5 only, no sacrum or pelvis labelled. arXiv: 7 landmarks per vertebra (superior and inferior endplate centres, both transverse-process tips, both pedicle centres, spinous-process tip). Med Phys refers to the same landmark types but I did not find it stating a count. In the sacralization case the sacralized segment was annotated as L5.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, for every X-ray subject (Centre 1 and Centre 2). A surgeon segmented L1-L5 on each subject's own CT and registered it to that subject's biplanar images using a custom MATLAB 2D-3D program (repeatability under 0.3 mm and under 0.7 degrees, cited as a gold standard). This gives per-vertebra poses, but they have not been released.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are radiographs of living subjects taken on calibrated biplanar DR systems (TAOiMAGE Golden Eye and Eagle Eye, 3072x3072, 0.139 mm pixels, calibration accuracy 0.05 mm, 78 kV / 40 mA, 0.16 mSv per pair, mostly low-dose mode). They are static biplanar radiographs, not fluoroscopy sequences.
corrections: Centre 2 is NOT identified as the Third Hospital of Hebei Medical University in the Med Phys paper; Hebei appears only as co-author Zhiyong Hou's affiliation. The paper never names either centre. Two indirect clues point elsewhere: the public code's test config reads test list 'testGuangzhou.txt', and the second IRB number, ZE2024-232-01, has the format Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine uses (corresponding author Shudong Chen is there). So Centre 2 is probably Guangzhou, but this is unconfirmed. Centre 1 is Shanghai Tongji Hospital according to arXiv's IRB statement (2021-011-SK).
The United Imaging uCT760 CT scanner is named only in arXiv v3, which covers the 225-CT cohort. Med Phys names no scanner and describes its 270 CTs as coming from several centres.
In arXiv, the 50 X-ray subjects are a subset of the 225 CT participants. In Med Phys, the 270 CTs are described as a separate dataset, distinct from the 64 CT+X-ray subjects.
The range of postures (flexion, extension, bending, rotation at three ranges) applies to Centre 1 only. The 16 Centre-2 pathological patients each have a single standing biplanar pair.

The sacralization subject is documented in arXiv's special test set and in Med Phys Supplement S4. Med Phys does not say whether that subject is among the 64, so the claim that it is part of the 64-subject cohort is unverified.

'Code is public' is true, but the repo has no licence, no weights and no data or split files. Its README gives a different paper title and wrong author names in the BibTeX (Zhaoyang Zhu, Chen Wang instead of Zhemin Zhu, Cong Wang).
Europe PMC's 'supporting_data' tag on this record is not a dataset. It is a text-mined link to arXiv:1904.04514 (the HRNet paper).
I did not verify the claim that 'the group also runs dual-fluoroscopic spine kinematics studies on the same hardware'; neither paper says so.

Access caveat: PMC now answers automated requests with a reCAPTCHA or cookie wall, and Wiley returns 403. The Med Phys full text I quote comes from the PMC HTML fetched earlier in this session plus NCBI efetch front matter. The 594.4 KB supplement (MP-53-0-s001.pdf) was not retrieved, so Supplement S4 (the fusion and sacralization cases) was not read.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real acquisitions from living people. Med Phys section 2.1 describes simultaneous biplanar radiographs taken on calibrated TAOiMAGE Golden Eye / Eagle Eye systems (3072x3072, 0.139 mm, 78 kV / 40 mA, 0.16 mSv per pair, mostly low-dose mode, lead shielding outside the imaged area). Rendered raw frames (Med Phys Fig 7, Supp Figs S4/S5) show real body habitus, bowel gas and fusion hardware. These are static radiographs, not fluoroscopy: the word "fluoroscopy" does not appear in either version. Beware that the Med Phys training set ALSO includes 810 synthetic DRR pairs made from the 270 SSM CTs, and the ground-truth "signal isolation" targets are DRRs of the registered CT. Only the 880 clinical pairs are real.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes for the X-ray cohort. In Med Phys, all 48 Centre-1 subjects "underwent both lumbar CT and biplanar radiography", and each of the 16 Centre-2 patients had "a lumbar CT scan and a single pair of standing biplanar radiographs". arXiv v3 gives the CT scanner as United Imaging uCT760 (120 kV, 1.0 mm), which Med Phys does not name. The 270 CTs (Med Phys) or 175 CTs (arXiv) used for the shape models have no X-rays. It is also not stated how long after the CT the X-rays were taken; the CT is supine and the radiographs are weight-bearing or in motion.
verdicts.anatomy: Labels cover L1-L5 only: the CT segmentations, the shape models and the 7 landmarks per vertebra. Neither text mentions sacrum, pelvis or ilium. The raw AP and lateral frames, however, visibly include the lower ribs down through the iliac wings, sacrum and hip joints (AP) and the sacrum (lateral), so the lumbosacral junction is in the field of view but unlabelled. LSTV content is one sacralisation case (arXiv: two special subjects, one with L2-L3 fusion and one with lumbar sacralisation). The sacralised vertebra was annotated as L5 and the model failed on it (Supp S4).
verdicts.counts: Med Phys 2026: 48 Centre-1 subjects (non-specific low back pain, no osseous abnormality, age 23.9 +/- 2.1) doing 6 movements (flexion, extension, left/right bend, left/right twist) at 3 ranges each, 864 biplanar pairs in total (18 per subject). Plus 16 Centre-2 pathological patients (age 62.9) with 1 standing pair each, for 880 real pairs (1760 images) from 64 CT-paired subjects. Also 270 independent CTs (SSM only) and 810 DRR pairs. Test set: 144 Centre-1 pairs plus 16 Centre-2 pairs. arXiv v3: 225 CTs, of which 50 have biplanar X-rays (about 18 pairs each) and 175 build the SSM. The two special cases (fusion, sacralisation) are a separate test set; of the other 48, 8 subjects give 144 test pairs and 40 subjects give 720 train/validation pairs.
verdicts.access_now: Not public. Med Phys: "not publicly available due to privacy and ethical restrictions ... available from the corresponding author on reasonable request". arXiv v3: "Data will be made available on request." Corresponding authors listed: Tsung-Yuan Tsai ([e-mail withheld]), Yan Yu ([e-mail withheld]), Shudong Chen ([e-mail withheld]). The GitHub repo ywx0314/lumbar_multitask holds network code only (train/test/dataset loaders, no data, no weights listed).
verdicts.licence: No data licence (data by request only). The code repo has no licence file (GitHub license = null; the README says "Copyright (c) 2024 Wanxin Yu"), so it is all-rights-reserved by default. Europe PMC reports that the article is not in the open-access subset (OpenAlex: green OA copy on PMC, licence null). COI: Tsai received research support from TAOiMAGE, and co-author Zhu is a TAOiMAGE employee.
corrections: The '<0.3 mm translation, <0.7 deg orientation repeatability' was NOT measured on this dataset or on TAOiMAGE hardware. Both versions cite it from Li G et al., Eur Spine J 2009 (Med Phys ref 32), an older dual-fluoroscopic study, so it cannot be quoted as this dataset's pose accuracy.

Per-vertebra 'gold-standard 6-DoF pose' comes from a custom MATLAB program in which the CT L1-L5 models are adjusted 'until it matched the corresponding contours' (arXiv v3). This is a registration done by the authors, not an independent tracker or fiducial measurement. The calibration accuracy of 0.05 mm (bead-box DLT plus bundle adjustment, Supp S1) is for the imaging geometry, not for the pose.

Landmarks (7 per vertebra: superior/inferior endplate centres, left/right transverse-process tips, left/right pedicle centres, spinous-process tip) were annotated in 3D on the CT by one orthopaedic surgeon and projected into the X-rays. They were not marked on the radiographs.

These are static biplanar radiographs, not fluoroscopy. Neither source uses the word. The claim that the group runs dual-fluoroscopic spine kinematics 'on the same hardware' appears in no source examined and is unverified.

The identity of Centre 2 is not stated. Linking it to the Third Hospital of Hebei Medical University is an inference from one author's affiliation. The second IRB number (ZE2024-232-01) and corresponding author Chen (Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine) point to another possible site.

Anatomy: the labels are L1-L5 only and the sacrum and pelvis are never mentioned, but the raw frames do show them. So the 'lumbar spine L1-L5' description is right for the labels and understates the field of view.
Not all images are standing. Centre 1 has flexion, extension, bending and twisting at three ranges each. Only Centre 2 (16 pairs) is described as standing.
The sacralisation case is n=1, labelled L5 and a model failure. Whether it sits inside the Med Phys 48/16 split is not stated (arXiv held it out, together with the fusion case, beyond the 48).
The Med Phys data also includes 810 DRR pairs (synthetic), which must not be counted as real X-rays.
The CT scanner model (uCT760) comes from arXiv v3 only. Med Phys gives CT as 512x512, 0.812 mm, 1.0 mm slices for the SSM set and does not name the scanner for the paired CTs.

candidate.name: Southeast University / Bond-Star Medical in-house spine CT + real PA C-arm X-rays (Perlove PLX118F; Chen, Kong et al.)
candidate.why_relevant: Fifteen clinical spine CTs (5 cervical, 5 thoracic, 5 lumbar), each with a real PA X-ray from a Perlove PLX118F mobile C-arm (1024x1024, 0.19959 mm/px, SID 1011.7 mm) and a ground-truth extrinsic matrix. It is a Chinese C-arm model not covered elsewhere. A related paper (arXiv 2402.02498) has 465 in-house CTs used for simulation only. No data statement was found, and the group's WACV 2026 paper used only public data, so the set has never been released. The corresponding author is Youyong Kong.
candidate.institution: Southeast University, Nanjing; Bond-Star Medical Technology; 117th Hospital of PLA
candidate.device: Perlove PLX118F mobile C-arm
candidate.anatomy: Cervical, thoracic and lumbar spine
candidate.pose_or_labels: Ground-truth extrinsic matrix per X-ray

verdicts.access_now: Not downloadable, and no route to request it. The data exist only as an in-house set described in papers. arXiv 2402.05642 v3 (HTML and the 9-page PDF) has no data availability statement, no ethics statement and no offer to share on request. The only related code repo, github.com/m1nhengChen/CMAES-reg, is the ISBI 2025 version of this paper: code and a PDF only, no data, no releases, no licence. Its README says results are "evaluated on simulation data". The SOPI and cdreg repos also hold code only. Searches of Zenodo (Perlove, PLX118F), Hugging Face and the author's other GitHub repos found nothing. The group's two newest papers use only public data: arXiv 2509.06890 (WACV 2026) uses DeepFluoro, Ljubljana and CTSpine1K, and arXiv 2607.23343 (July 2026) has a data availability statement naming only DeepFluoro and Ljubljana. So the set has never been released. Asking the corresponding author, [e-mail withheld], is the only possible route, and no paper offers it.
verdicts.licence: None. The data are unreleased and the paper gives no licence. The arXiv licence (non-exclusive, perpetual) covers only the paper text. The CMAES-reg, SOPI and cdreg repos have no licence file (GitHub API license: null).
verdicts.counts: arXiv 2402.05642: fifteen spine CTs (five cervical, five thoracic, five lumbar). Each has one PA X-ray at 1024x1024 with a ground-truth extrinsic matrix, and the table labels them Subject #1 to #15. The group's other papers give different numbers. ICASSP 2024 SOPI (arXiv 2305.06252) used 146 CTs for simulation plus a real set of "CTs and corresponding lumbar fluoroscopy from 5 acquisitions". ISBI 2024 (arXiv 2402.02498) used 465 CTs "from collaborating institutions", simulation only. Med Phys 2025 (PMID 40400109) says it evaluated on "52 real x-ray images". ISBI 2025 (the CMAES-reg PDF) used 52 VerSe CTs, simulation only. No file list and no sizes exist anywhere.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, according to the paper. Section 4.1 describes real PA X-rays and calls them "real orthopedic spine surgery clinical data". The cervical discussion refers to "preoperative and intraoperative imaging", so the X-rays are intraoperative. A log transform (Beer-Lambert) is applied to invert the intensities.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes. Each of the 15 CTs is paired with one PA X-ray. The CTs were resampled to 1.0 mm isotropic and cropped or padded to 256 cubed. Registration used a segmentation of the vertebrae as the volume, made with the SpineCLUE automatic method (arXiv 2401.07271), not the raw CT.
verdicts.anatomy: Cervical (5), thoracic (5) and lumbar (5) spine. Only PA views, one per subject. The ICASSP 2024 real set was lumbar only (5 acquisitions).
corrections: Access is not 'unknown'. There is no data availability statement, no request route and no release anywhere, so 'not available' is the right value.

The 117th Hospital of the PLA is not in arXiv 2402.05642. It comes from the Med Phys 2025 paper (Mingying Li, per OpenAlex). PubMed lists that author as 'Department of Radiology, The 903rd Hospital of the People's Liberation Army, Hangzhou', which appears to be the renamed 117th Hospital. Neither paper says this hospital supplied the 15-case set.
Bond-Star Medical Technology is thanked only as a funder ('supported in part by'). No paper states it supplied data or is an institution holding the set.
'15 living patients' is not stated. The paper says 'fifteen spine CT scans' and labels them Subject #1 to #15 as clinical surgical data. It does not say these are 15 distinct patients.

The C-arm geometry is nominal device specs, not a per-image calibration. The paper says the intrinsics 'simulate a Perlove PLX118F mobile C-arm', giving 0.19959 mm/px, SID 1011.7 mm and a 1024x1024 detector. How the ground-truth extrinsics were obtained is never described.

The Med Phys 2025 paper (10.1002/mp.17896) reports 52 real X-ray images, not 15. It is closed access (OpenAlex oa_status closed; Wiley returned 403), so its device, anatomy and any data statement could not be checked.
arXiv 2402.02498 lists the device as 0.199 mm/px and 1012 mm (rounded), and uses it only as the simulation geometry for 465 CTs. That paper does state IRB approval and written consent.

The ISBI 2025 published version of this CMA-ES work (the CMAES-reg PDF) dropped the 15 real cases and used 52 VerSe CTs simulated with Perlove intrinsics. The 15-case real set appears only in the arXiv preprint.
The candidate is right on these points: corresponding author Youyong Kong, the 5/5/5 split, PA views, one extrinsic matrix per X-ray, the Perlove PLX118F, and no public release.

verdicts.real_xray: Stated as real, but no image is shown. arXiv 2402.05642 section 4.1 says the Perlove PLX118F mobile C-arm "generates the X-ray images in this work". The abstract calls the data "real orthopedic spine surgery clinical data", and the paper applies a Beer-Lambert log transform to the raw X-rays. It attributes the cervical failures to head position differing "during preoperative and intraoperative imaging", which points to intraoperative acquisitions. There are no DRRs and no MV portal images in the test set. Each subject has one PA frame, not a fluoroscopy sequence. The 9-page PDF has no embedded raster images, so I could not look at an X-ray to confirm it is real.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, per subject. "Each scan has a corresponding X-ray with Postero-Anterior (PA) views", and the conclusion calls them "paired CT and X-ray images". The volume is a preoperative diagnostic CT, not a CBCT. The CTs were resampled to 1 mm isotropic and cropped or padded to 256^3.
verdicts.anatomy: Five cervical, five thoracic and five lumbar spine scans (Table 1: cervical #1-5, thoracic #6-10, lumbar #11-15). The lumbar spine is present in 5 subjects. No source says whether the sacrum or pelvis is in the field of view; the images are described only as spine ROI crops. The ICASSP 2024 paper's 5 real cases are "lumbar fluoroscopy", with CTs cropped to the lumbar spine.
verdicts.counts: arXiv 2402.05642: 15 CTs and 15 PA X-rays, one per scan. ICASSP 2024 (arXiv 2305.06252): 146 CTs from "several partner hospitals" for training and validation, plus "a set of CTs and corresponding lumbar fluoroscopy from 5 acquisitions". These may overlap the 15. ISBI 2024 (arXiv 2402.02498): 465 CTs "from collaborating institutions", tested on simulated X-rays only. Med Phys 2025 (doi 10.1002/mp.17896; PubMed 40400109 abstract): "evaluated on 52 real x-ray images". That is the largest real-image count this group has stated. The paper is closed access, so its number of subjects and anatomy are unknown.
verdicts.licence: No data statement in 2402.05642, 2305.06252 or 2402.02498. The GitHub repos m1nhengChen/SOPI and m1nhengChen/cdreg hold code only; their READMEs say nothing about data. The Med Phys 2025 paper is closed access (OpenAlex oa_status closed), so I could not read its data availability statement. The group's later papers use only public data: WACV 2026 (arXiv 2509.06890) uses DeepFluoro, Ljubljana and CTSpine1K, and arXiv 2607.23343 uses DeepFluoro and Ljubljana. That fits a set that was never released. I found no statement that it is private or restricted, so the licence is unknown, not confirmed closed.
verdicts.access_now: Not publicly downloadable as far as any primary source shows. The only route would be asking the corresponding author, Youyong Kong ([e-mail withheld], the address printed in arXiv 2402.05642).
corrections: Institution: arXiv 2402.05642 lists Southeast University affiliations only. Bond-Star Medical Technology appears only in the acknowledgement as a funder ('supported in part by'), not as a data source or affiliation.

'117th Hospital of PLA' comes from OpenAlex's institution normalization. The raw affiliation on the Med Phys 2025 paper (PubMed 40400109) is 'Department of Radiology, The 903rd Hospital of the People's Liberation Army, Hangzhou'. It belongs to one co-author (Mingying Li) of the Med Phys paper, not of 2402.05642. No source names the hospital that acquired the 15 CT/X-ray pairs.

'15 living patients' is not stated. The paper says 'fifteen spine CT scans' and 'real orthopedic spine surgery clinical data'. That these are 15 distinct living patients is an inference. No ethics or consent statement appears in 2402.05642; the IRB statement is in the ISBI paper 2402.02498.
n_images understates the group's real X-ray set. The Med Phys 2025 abstract reports 52 real X-ray images. ICASSP 2024 separately reports 5 real lumbar fluoroscopy acquisitions with CT.

Ground-truth extrinsic matrix: 2402.05642 says only 'For each X-ray, the ground truth extrinsic matrix is provided'. It does not say how the pose was obtained (fiducials, tracking or manual registration), so its accuracy is unknown. The mTRE landmark set is not described either (neither count nor how it was obtained).
Labels: no vertebra-level labels or 2-D annotations are stated. The CT spine segmentations were made automatically (SpineCLUE, ref 18), not annotated by hand.
Sacrum and pelvis coverage is not stated anywhere. Only 5 of the 15 subjects are lumbar, and each has a single PA frame.
The images cannot be inspected: 2402.05642 has no figures (the PDF has no embedded images), so 'real' rests on the text alone.
Access 'unknown' is right in that no data availability statement was found. The Med Phys data statement could not be read because the paper is closed access.

candidate.name: Manipal (MIT / Kasturba Medical College) thoracolumbar intraoperative C-arm + preoperative CT, Ziehm 9-inch image intensifier
candidate.why_relevant: Four adolescent trauma patients, imaged prone, have a preoperative CT (Philips, T5-L4) and intraoperative AP fluoroscopy from a Ziehm 9-inch image-intensifier C-arm (66-86 kV). Vertebral centroids and levels (T11-L3) are marked in both the CT and the X-ray. The image-intensifier chain adds device variety. There is no data statement. The group's later pedicle-screw 2D-3D paper is cited in the xvr Nature paper.
candidate.institution: Manipal Institute of Technology; Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, India (Naik, Bhat et al.)
candidate.device: Ziehm 9-inch image-intensifier C-arm
candidate.anatomy: Thoracolumbar spine T11-L3
candidate.pose_or_labels: Vertebral centroids with level identity in CT and X-ray; pose by registration

corrections: Access is not 'unknown'. Nothing has been released and there is no route to request it. The PMC full text and the Springer page (fetched 2026-09-21) have no Data availability section and no supplementary files. The Declarations cover only ethics, consent and conflicts, and no repository, request contact or code link appears. So the data is neither downloadable nor offered on request.

The same group's other papers point the same way. The companion J Imaging 2022 paper (PMC9324544) says 'Data Availability Statement: Not applicable.' Their Eur Spine J 2026 paper (10.1007/s00586-025-09342-6) says: 'The data involved in this study is taken with approval from the Kasturba Medical College and Kasturba Hospital Institutional Ethics Committee which cannot be shared publicly.' Treat this cohort as private to the institution.

Licence: the CC BY 4.0 licence applies to the article's text and figures only. No dataset licence exists. The only openly licensed images are the processed X-ray/DRR panels in the figures (for example Fig. 11, with centroids overlaid). These are figure reproductions, not raw fluoroscopy or CT.

n_images: each of the 4 datasets used one AP intraoperative X-ray as its reference image. The paper never says how many frames were acquired in total. Each X-ray has 3 marked centroids (3 consecutive levels between T11 and L3), so about 12 2-D landmarks in all.

Pose labels are weaker than 'pose by registration' suggests. There were no fiducials, no tracker and no ground-truth pose. The fine ICP/CMA-ES stage minimises mPDE on the same three centroid pairs it then reports. The final mPDE of 0.33-0.47 mm is therefore a fitting residual, not an independent accuracy. Validation beyond that was a visual DRR match and feedback from three surgeons.

Only partly verified: the article says 'adolescent patients ... who had undergone spinal injuries, specifically in the thoracolumbar region'. It also says the data included scans 'specifically acquired for diagnosis purposes and spinal fusion surgeries'. So 'trauma' fits, but the exact ages and aetiology are not given. The ethics statement names ICMR standards but gives no IEC number in this paper; the J Imaging companion gives IEC No 128/2019.

Device, confirmed: 'Ziehm's 9-in. C-arm - Image Intensifier system', prone patients, 66-86 kV and 3.3-3.8 mA, AP view with no gantry rotation. The companion J Imaging paper is a different 2-patient set taken on a Philips BV Endura and a Ziehm 8000. Do not merge the two cohorts.

xvr link, confirmed: the xvr Nature paper (s41586-026-11045-x) cites Naik et al., J Imaging 8:185 (2022) as its reference 12. It does not cite this MBEC paper, and nothing shows xvr used this group's data.
verdicts.access_now: None. Nothing can be downloaded and nothing is offered on request. The article has no data availability statement, supplementary material or repository link, on either PMC or Springer. The group's 2026 Eur Spine J paper states that their Kasturba data 'cannot be shared publicly'. Zenodo and figshare searches for the authors found no release. The only route would be a cold approach to the authors (Naik / Anitha H, MIT Manipal; Bhat, KMC Orthopaedics), and a release is unlikely because the ethics committee restricts it.
verdicts.licence: The article is CC BY 4.0 (confirmed from the PMC OA licence field and the licence text on the article page). That covers the text and figures only. No licence has been issued for any data, and the group's later papers say it cannot be shared publicly.
verdicts.counts: 4 patients (datasets 1-4), 4 preoperative CT volumes cropped to T5-L4, one AP intraoperative X-ray per patient as the reference, 3 centroids per X-ray. Table 2 lists pCT sizes: 512x512x243 at 0.56x0.56x3 mm (T12-L2); 512x512x242 at 0.47x0.47x3 mm (T11-L1); 512x512x244 at 0.44x0.44x3 mm (L1-L3); 512x512x211 at 0.58x0.58x3 mm (T12-L2). No file sizes exist because no files were released.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same subject. Preoperative diagnostic CT on a Philips scanner, patient supine, 120-140 kVp, 300-400 mA, 3 mm slices. The intraoperative fluoroscopy was taken prone, so the two differ in patient position. Vertebral centroids were marked manually in the CT (checked in the axial, coronal and sagittal planes), with the T12/L1 transition or the floating ribs as the level landmark.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. Real intraoperative AP fluoroscopy from a Ziehm 9-inch image-intensifier C-arm, taken during pedicle screw insertion with the patient prone, at 66-86 kV and 3.3-3.8 mA. Only processed figure panels are publicly visible.
verdicts.anatomy: The CT covers the thoracolumbar spine, cropped T5-L4. The X-ray fields show T11-L3 (three consecutive levels per patient). Adolescent spinal-injury patients undergoing fusion.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes. The images are real intraoperative fluoroscopy. The paper says "target localization was performed on real X-ray images acquired for four patients" on a "Ziehm's 9-in. C-arm - Image Intensifier system", with patients prone during pedicle screw insertion, at 66-86 kV and 3.3-3.8 mA. The view is AP only, and the C-arm was not rotated. I looked at Figs 4 and 11. The right-hand column of Fig 11 shows genuine image-intensifier frames, with circular field edges, a radiopaque marker instrument and patient soft tissue. The DRRs in the other columns are the paper's own simulated images and are not part of the data. There are no MV or portal images. The exact Ziehm model is not named.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, a diagnostic preoperative CT of the same patient. It is not a CBCT. Table 2 pairs each dataset's pCT (512x512x211-244 voxels, 0.44-0.58 x 0.44-0.58 x 3 mm) with the levels in that patient's intraoperative X-ray. The CT was a Philips scanner at 120-140 kVp and 300-400 mA, acquired SUPINE. The fluoroscopy was acquired PRONE. T5-L4 is the range that was CROPPED for the DRR database. The paper says "complete axial pCT images" were collected, and 211-244 slices at 3 mm is roughly 63-73 cm of coverage. The Discussion says "pelvis regions were excluded from the preoperative CT" when building the DRR database, which implies the full scans may include the pelvis, but this is not stated for each case. The follow-up J Imaging 2022 paper (PMC9324544) reuses the dataset-2 CT (512x512x242, 0.47x0.47x3) to register L3-L5, so that CT reaches at least L5.
verdicts.anatomy: Thoracolumbar spine only in the fluoroscopy. The levels are: dataset 1 T12-L2, dataset 2 T11-L1, dataset 3 L1-L3, dataset 4 T12-L2. Each image contributes three vertebrae. Ribs are visible, and the paper uses the floating ribs and the T12/L1 transition as its landmark. None of the fluoroscopic images in this paper contain L4, L5, the sacrum or the pelvis. The CT was cropped to T5-L4 for the experiments, and its full extent is not stated.
verdicts.counts: Four living patients, described as "adolescent patients ... who had undergone spinal injuries, specifically in the thoracolumbar region". No ages or sex are given. There are four pCT volumes. The number of X-ray images is not stated. The text says the AP view was the reference image, and Fig 11 shows one AP frame per dataset, so in effect four AP images were used. The introduction mentions that multiple images are taken in surgery, but no other images are reported or used.
verdicts.licence: The article is CC BY 4.0, but that covers only the published text and figures. There is no data licence. The MBEC paper has no data availability statement and no supplementary material. The follow-up J Imaging paper states "Data Availability Statement: Not applicable."
verdicts.access_now: None. The data has not been released: there is no repository, no supplementary file and no statement of access on request. The only way to get it would be to write to the corresponding author (Shyamasunder N Bhat, Kasturba Medical College, [e-mail withheld]). The only material usable now is four downsampled AP frames in the CC BY figures (Fig 11, 752x1094 composite), with centroid overlays burned in.
corrections: 'Imaged prone' applies only to the fluoroscopy. The pCT was acquired supine (Philips, 120-140 kVp, 300-400 mA, 3 mm slices).

'CT T5-L4' is the cropped range used for the DRR database, not the acquired extent. The paper says the complete axial pCT was collected, 211-244 slices x 3 mm is about 63-73 cm, and the Discussion says the pelvis was excluded from the pCT for the DRR database. The follow-up J Imaging paper uses the same dataset-2 CT volume for L3-L5.

The fluoroscopy covers only T11-L3, three vertebrae per image (T12-L2, T11-L1, L1-L3, T12-L2). No image in this paper shows L4, L5, the sacrum or the pelvis, so it does not cover the lumbosacral junction.
n_images is not stated. The paper uses one AP reference image per patient (Fig 11), so four AP images in effect. There are no lateral views in this paper.

The labels are three manually marked vertebral centroids per image, in both CT and X-ray. The authors say marking varies by up to 2 mm. Level identity is given only as per-dataset ranges in Table 2. No label files are released.

There is no ground-truth pose: no fiducials, no tracker, no calibration phantom. The 'pose' is a 6-DOF fit of a C-arm model to the same three centroid pairs used to score it, so the final mPDE of 0.33-0.47 mm is a fit residual, not a validation. The authors say out-of-plane parameters were poorly constrained, and the source-to-detector initial guess was set manually.
Access is not 'unknown': it is unreleased. There is no data availability statement, no supplementary material and no repository. The CC BY 4.0 licence covers the article only.

The device model is not named beyond 'Ziehm's 9-in. C-arm - Image Intensifier system'. The follow-up J Imaging paper names a Philips BV Endura and a Ziehm 8000 for its two patients, which gives 65-76 kV, a CT current of 200-300 mA (against 300-400 mA here), and 1024x1280 X-rays at 0.23 mm, with AP and lateral views.

'Adolescent trauma' matches the text ('adolescent patients ... spinal injuries ... thoracolumbar region'). The paper also says the datasets were 'acquired for diagnosis purposes and spinal fusion surgeries'. No ages are given.

The xvr citation is confirmed, but for the follow-up paper, not this one. Nature s41586-026-11045-x, reference 12, cites Naik, Hoblidar, Bhat, Ampar and Kundangar, J. Imaging 8, 185 (2022), doi 10.3390/jimaging8070185. The MBEC paper is not cited there.

The bibliographic details are confirmed: Med Biol Eng Comput 60(8):2271-2289, epub 2022-06-10, doi 10.1007/s11517-022-02600-5, PMID 35680729. Ethics is given only as ICMR standards plus informed consent, with no committee number in this paper. The follow-up gives IEC No 128/2019.

candidate.name: Fourth Medical Center of PLA General Hospital pelvic-fracture intraoperative AP + inlet X-rays + CT (Ju et al., Sci Rep 2025)
candidate.why_relevant: Eight living pelvic-fracture patients have real intraoperative AP and inlet pelvic X-rays with same-patient CT and 3D points of interest. The method assumes a known relative C-arm pose between the two views, but there is no ground-truth pose on the real images. It is small. Requests go to the corresponding author (Jingxin Zhao). Code is at github.com/TUYaYa1/Points-of-Interest-tracking-network. It may overlap the MetaPose private set from the same hospital.
candidate.institution: Beijing University of Technology; Fourth Medical Center, Chinese PLA General Hospital
candidate.device: not stated
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis and sacrum
candidate.n_images: 8 real intraoperative X-rays + CT per patient
candidate.pose_or_labels: 3D POIs on CT; tracked POIs on X-rays; registration results

verdicts.access_now: Not downloadable. There is no repository record. The data availability statement on both Nature and PMC reads, in full: "Correspondence and requests for data and materials should be addressed to Jingxin Zhao." That is a line telling readers who to write to, not an offer to share. The paper does not say "upon reasonable request" and names no conditions, DUA or repository. Corresponding email: [e-mail withheld]. Ethics approval (Chinese PLA General Hospital, No. S2022-781-01) was retrospective with consent waived because the data were anonymised; nothing is said about sharing outside the study. Zenodo searches for the dataset, POITT and the repo name return 0 hits. The only public artefact is the code repo github.com/TUYaYa1/Points-of-Interest-tracking-network: 4 files totalling 12 KB (Requirements.txt, unet_cbam.py, Unet_cbam_train.py, Unet_CBAM_test.py). It has no README, no licence, no data and no weights, and the scripts load np.load('your path') placeholders. Created 2025-05-20, last push 2025-06-24.
verdicts.licence: No data licence, because no data were released. The article is open access under CC BY-NC-ND (4.0, per the PMC BioC licence field), and that covers the article only. The GitHub code has no licence file, so it defaults to all rights reserved.
verdicts.counts: The paper says CT and X-ray images were collected from 8 patients in two views (pelvic AP and inlet). The real-image counts are inconsistent. The dataset section says "we utilize 8 real intraoperative X-ray images", which is 8 images in total, not 8 per patient, and a two-view method would need 16 for 8 patients. Table 4, the real X-ray results, reports only 5 cases (AP and inlet each), so at most 5 patients' real image pairs are evaluated. The simulation counts also disagree. The abstract says 300 pairs of simulated DRRs per patient. The methods and supplement say 3000 paired DRRs per patient (2700 train, 300 test), made with DeepDRR under random rotations of U(-8,8) degrees and translations of U(-15,15) mm. No file sizes, formats or image resolutions are given for the real X-rays or the CTs.
verdicts.anatomy: Pelvis. The 3D POIs were marked in 3D Slicer on bony landmarks such as the anterior superior iliac spine, anterior inferior iliac spine and pubic symphysis. Supplementary Fig. 2 shows three POIs per image. No sacral or vertebral landmark or label is described. The sacrum is only incidentally in the field of view, so calling it "Pelvis and sacrum" overstates it, and nothing here is spine-level.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, per the paper: a preoperative CT for each of the 8 patients, used to make DRRs and to hold the 3D POIs. Not released.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, per the paper: real intraoperative pelvic X-rays in AP and inlet views, which the paper calls "real intraoperative X-ray images" and "clinical real X-ray images". The C-arm make and model are not stated anywhere, including the supplement. The geometry in Supplementary Table 2 (source-detector distance 1160 mm, source-isocenter 1000 mm, pixel size 0.194, 1536 detector, fx/fy 5979.38) is the DeepDRR simulation setting, not a measured real-device calibration. There is no ground truth on the real images: the paper says "only SSIM and NCC are used as metrics due to the lack of real labels". The POIs on the real X-rays are network predictions, not annotations. The method assumes a known relative C-arm pose between the two views, which the paper lists as a limitation, and no real-image pose is recorded.
corrections: n_images '8 real intraoperative X-rays + CT per patient' is wrong. The paper says '8 real intraoperative X-ray images' in total, and Table 4 evaluates only 5 real cases (AP + inlet each). CT is per patient (8 patients).
Abstract and methods disagree on the DRR count: the abstract says 300 pairs per patient, the methods and supplement say 3000 per patient (2700 train / 300 test).
Anatomy 'Pelvis and sacrum' overstates it. The labelled POIs are pelvic landmarks (ASIS, AIIS, pubic symphysis). No sacral or vertebral labels are described.

pose_or_labels: the 'tracked POIs on X-rays' are model outputs, not ground truth. The paper states the real X-rays lack labels, and there is no real-image C-arm pose. Only the 3D POIs on CT, marked manually in 3D Slicer, are true annotations. No registration results are released as files.

Access is less than 'on request': the statement only says requests should be addressed to Jingxin Zhao ([e-mail withheld]). It makes no commitment to share, and no repository or DUA is named. Consent was waived for a retrospective anonymised study, and nothing addresses sharing outside it.

Licence: the article is CC BY-NC-ND. The data have no licence because they were not released. The GitHub repo has no licence, no README, no data and no weights (4 Python files, 12 KB, placeholder paths).
Device is 'not stated' for the real C-arm. The geometry in the supplement is the DeepDRR simulation setting only.
Dates: received 21 July 2024, accepted 7 July 2025, published 18 July 2025. Sci Rep 15, article 26183. PMID 40681637.

Institutions confirmed: College of Computer Science and Beijing Key Laboratory of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, Beijing University of Technology; Department of Orthopaedics, The Fourth Medical Center, Chinese PLA General Hospital.
The claim that it overlaps the 'MetaPose private set from the same hospital' is unverified. I found no primary source for MetaPose's institution or data in this check.
