candidate.name: Giessen/Jena canine biplanar fluoroscopy of the lumbosacral junction with CT of the same dogs (Front Vet Sci 2021, plus companion craniocervical studies); raw videos held in the Jena Collection of X-ray Movies
candidate.why_relevant: Merged record: the Giessen paper and the Jena video archive are one dataset. The paper supplies the CT and the solved poses; the archive holds the raw video. Four living German Shepherds were filmed on a treadmill with biplanar C-arm fluoroscopy of the pelvis, sacrum, L6 and L7. Each bone was tracked by scientific rotoscoping, and the same dogs had helical CT of the whole spine and pelvis, so every tracked frame has a CT-to-frame pose. The Jena lab corrects distortion with a perforated-metal grid and calibrates 3-D space with a steel-sphere cuboid, so the projection geometry can be recovered. In the archive, subproject szeb_subproject_00000167 ('Dog vertebral column Giessen') holds films 606 and 612-615, each with 90-174 files (raw Roentgen_A/B_VisarioG2.avi biplanar videos plus per-day calibration films), recorded 2015-2018. The metadata can be read through an open Solr index behind a proof-of-work gate, but file downloads return HTTP 403 without login. The archive also has beagle and dachshund films and one canine cadaver lumbar/thoracic mobility film (024) with calibration-body films; the archive has no CT for these. Companion studies with the same setup cover the craniocervical junction in Chihuahuas and Labradors (10.3389/fvets.2021.709967) and in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels (PLOS ONE 2023); they have CT of the head, spine and pelvis. All three papers say raw data 'will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation'. The archive says to contact Prof. Martin S. Fischer ([e-mail withheld]). The subjects are dogs, which have 7 lumbar vertebrae.

verdicts.access_now: The raw data cannot be downloaded now. I tested on 2026-09-22 after passing the site's proof-of-work gate (mod_repudiator, 18-bit SHA-256). The film pages and Solr metadata are public. Every file request through MCRFileNodeServlet returns HTTP 403 Forbidden without login. That includes a German Shepherd AVI in film 606, a protocol .txt in film 606, and an AVI in film 024, which is "published" with a "Public Domain from 2017-12-05" date. Subproject 167 also carries a public-domain date (2020-02-25), but its films 606 and 612-615 are in state "new" and worldReadableComplete is false. The archive page says "Bei Interesse an den Videos nehmen Sie bitte Kontakt auf zu: Prof. Dr. Martin S. Fischer, [e-mail withheld]". The two Frontiers papers say only "will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation". That is a promise, not a release. Openly downloadable today (CC BY supplements only): (1) The lumbosacral paper's supplement, Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip, 39.3 MB: Video_1-4.MP4 plus Data_Sheet_1.docx. Video 3 is a real single-view lumbar/pelvic fluoroscopy clip at 640x426, 25 fps, 76 s, downsampled H.264. Videos 1 and 4 are rotoscoped bone-model overlays. Video 2 is the live camera. The docx holds only timing-of-occurrence tables. (2) The 709967 companion: 8 MP4s. (3) PLOS ONE S1 File: a 61 MB zip of 10 MP4s. (4) Eight transcoded HLS preview streams on subproject 167, e.g. 'Schaeferhund LS Trab 63Grad.avi' at 1080x720, 25 fps, about 17.6 s, single view. None of these contains CT, poses or calibration images.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbosacral paper: pelvis, sacrum, L6 and L7 of four living German Shepherds at walk and trot, in two oblique views 63 degrees apart. Film 606 metadata: 'versch. Hunde in Schritt/Trab/Stand/Halsbewegung/auf Box steigend' (various dogs at walk, trot and stand, neck movement, stepping onto a box). Companions: craniocervical junction (skull, C1, C2). Film 024: cadaver spine, lumbar and thoracic focus. Film 468: beagles. Film 469: dachshunds. Dogs have 7 lumbar vertebrae.
verdicts.counts: Archive (Solr facets): 623 films, 56,566 data files, 17,432 derivates (confirmed). Subproject 167 derivates: 606=174, 612=90, 613=109, 614=98, 615=0. Data files: 606=660, 612=350, 613=395, 614=370, 615=0. Each derivate holds Roentgen_A and Roentgen_B X-ray AVIs plus two live-camera AVIs named 00-50-C2-*. Film 606 (German Shepherd): 323 X-ray AVIs totalling 1.93 GB, median 6.2 MB, max 16.4 MB, 42 under 200 KB; 326 live-camera AVIs; 11 protocol .txt files. All subproject 167 files together are about 9.2 GB. A 1536x1024 frame is about 1.5 MB uncompressed, so these AVIs must be compressed or short; 'raw' is not verified. Paper: strides analysed were walk n=6 and trot n=9 across the four dogs. Dog films tagged body region spine: 7 (024, 468, 469, 606, 612, 613, 615); 614 (Cavalier) is tagged Whole body. Film 468: 4 beagles, 38 films including 3 calibration. Film 469: 3 dachshunds, 28 films including 3 calibration. Film 024: 12 derivates, 24 AVIs, 0.04 GB, including calibration-body films 07 and 11.
verdicts.licence: The articles are CC BY 4.0: Frontiers 709966 and 709967, PLOS ONE 0278665. That covers their supplementary MP4s. No licence is stated for the archive data on the archive site, and the Lizenzen field on the wissenschaftliche-sammlungen portal record is empty. 'Public Domain from' dates appear in the archive metadata, but they do not grant download access (403).
verdicts.paired_ct: The same dogs had CT: Philips Brilliance 16-slice, 120 kV, 1 mm. The lumbosacral paper says '200 mA'; PLOS ONE says '200 mAs'. The CT is not released anywhere. It is not in the paper supplements and not in the Jena archive, which holds only .avi and .txt files. The rotoscoping poses are not released either. The paper reports only derived rotation curves, and its data sheet gives timing tables as percent of the stride cycle.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real biplanar image-intensifier fluoroscopy recordings of living dogs. I confirmed this visually: supplementary Video 3 and the public German Shepherd lumbosacral preview stream both show a real lateral-oblique fluoroscopy of the canine lumbar spine and pelvis. Only single-view, transcoded clips are openly reachable.
corrections: PMC8417724 in the evidence list is the craniocervical companion (10.3389/fvets.2021.709967), not the lumbosacral paper. The lumbosacral paper is PMC8427507 (Schaub, Kelleners, Schmidt, Eley, Fischer).

'The paper supplies the CT and the solved poses' is false. Neither is released. The lumbosacral paper's data statement is only 'The raw data supporting the conclusions of this article will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation.' Its supplement is 4 MP4s plus a docx of timing tables.
'Every tracked frame has a CT-to-frame pose' overstates it. Rotoscoping covered only the analysed strides (walk n=6, trot n=9 across four dogs), was done by one person, and the poses are unpublished.

The lumbosacral paper says 'shutter speed was set to 500 μs'; it gives no frame rate. The 500 fps comes from the archive record for film 606 ('A+B 63Grad, 500fps, 1536mal1024'). The lumbosacral paper gives CT as 200 mA, not 200 mAs (PLOS ONE says 200 mAs).

The lumbosacral paper does not describe distortion correction or 3-D calibration. The perforated-metal-sheet and steel-sphere cuboid description (120x100 mm, 1 mm spheres at 10 mm) comes from the archive's general fluoroscope page. That page says calibration images 'are available for each project', but they sit inside the 403-gated files.

'All three papers say without undue reservation' is wrong. Only the two Frontiers papers say it. PLOS ONE 2023 says 'All relevant data are available in the paper and its Supporting Information files. Additional Xray videos are available on https://www.x-ray-movies-jena.de/' — yet the site's files return 403.

'Films 606 and 612-615, each with 90-174 files' is wrong for 615 (French Bulldog). It has 0 derivates and 0 indexed files, although its description claims 96 files. Derivate counts are 174/90/109/98/0 and data-file counts are 660/350/395/370/0. Each derivate includes two live-camera AVIs as well as the A and B X-ray AVIs.

The AVIs are small: median about 6 MB, max 16.4 MB, and about 12% of X-ray files are under 200 KB. At 1536x1024 these must be compressed or very short clips. 'Raw' and 'high-resolution' are not verified.

Access status: file downloads returned 403 today, even for film 024, which is state 'published' with a 'Public Domain from 2017-12-05' date. Films 606 and 612-615 are in state 'new', and worldReadableComplete is false for all of them.

The public metadata does not document which files in film 606 belong to the paper's four German Shepherds. Film 606 covers 'various dogs' over 11 recording days (27.07.15 to 23.04.16), including neck movement and stepping onto a box. The protocol .txt files that might map them are also 403.

The candidate omits some open material. The four CC BY supplementary MP4s download openly (39.3 MB zip), and Video 3 is a real single-view fluoroscopy clip at 640x426, 25 fps, 76 s. The companion papers add 8 MP4s and 10 MP4s (61 MB zip). Public transcoded HLS previews exist, e.g. the German Shepherd LS trot preview at 1080x720, about 17.6 s. None has CT, poses or calibration.
Film 468 is beagles (4 dogs, 38 films) and film 469 is dachshunds (3 dogs, 28 films). Both are state 'submitted' and both include 3 calibration films. The archive has no CT for any of these.
The collection portal names a second contact besides Prof. Fischer: Dr. Bettina Hesse (Sammlungsbetreuung, collection curator).

Confirmed as stated: archive totals of 623 films and 56,566 data files; hardware (Neurostar base, 400 mm image intensifiers, SpeedCam Visario g2 up to 1536x1024 and 2000 fps, SID 520-750 mm); 63-degree planes at 100 kV and 75 mA; four German Shepherds; L6, L7, sacrum and pelvis; 709967 cohort of 8 Chihuahuas and 3 Labradors with CT of head, spine and pelvis; subproject 167 with films 606 and 612-615; the proof-of-work-gated open Solr index.

The paper does not supply the CT or the solved poses. The lumbosacral paper (Schaub et al. 2021, 10.3389/fvets.2021.709966, PMC8427507) releases only summary tables (Data_Sheet_1.docx holds time-of-occurrence means and SDs per dog) and 4 MP4 videos. Its data statement reads: 'The raw data supporting the conclusions of this article will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation.' CT volumes, bone meshes and per-frame 6-DoF poses are not published anywhere I could find.

Poses do not exist for 'every tracked frame'. Only selected strides were rotoscoped: 6 walk and 9 trot per dog (Fig 4/5 captions; supplementary Table 1 says 'analyzed in all four dogs during walking (n = 6) and trotting (n = 9)'). The paper also says 'the sacrum was defined as a fixed connection with the pelvis', so there is no separate sacrum pose. The published motion is relative to the adjoining caudal bone. Reported accuracy is about 1.5 deg for rotation and 0.1 cm for translation.
The lumbosacral paper states the CT as '120 kV, 200 mA, and a slice thickness of 1 mm', not 200 mAs. The 200 mAs figure comes from the PLOS ONE paper.

The lumbosacral paper gives no X-ray frame rate. It gives only a 500 microsecond shutter, 100 kV / 75 mA and 63 deg planes, and 500 pics/s for the light cameras. '500 fps, 1536x1024' comes from the archive's film-606 metadata and from the companion craniocervical paper, which states 500 Hz.

None of the three papers mentions the perforated-metal undistortion grid, the steel-sphere cuboid or the 520-750 mm source-to-intensifier range. These come from the archive's 'The Fluoroscope' page, which describes the facility in general, not this study. That page also says 'The images of the calibration cube and the perforated metal sheet are available for each project.'

Not all three papers say data 'will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation'. The two Frontiers papers do. PLOS ONE (Nickel 2023) says: 'All relevant data are available in the paper and its Supporting Information files. Additional Xray videos are available on https://www.x-ray-movies-jena.de/'. Its S1 File is a 61 MB zip holding only 10 MP4 videos.

The lumbosacral paper does not cite the Jena archive (the x-ray-movies URL appears 0 times in PMC8427507). The link from the paper to the archive is inferred. Only film 606 fits it: topic 'Schaeferhund', 'A+B 63Grad, 500fps, 1536mal1024', dated 27 Jul 2015 to 23 Apr 2016. Its metadata still says 'versch.Hunde in Schritt/Trab/Stand/Halsbewegung/auf Box steigend' (various dogs; includes neck motion and stepping onto a box), gives no dog count and names no study.

Films 612-615 are not German Shepherd lumbosacral data. Their topics are 612 Labrador, 613 Chihuahua, 614 Cavalier and 615 French Bulldog. Film 615 has derCount 0, meaning no files. So the claim of films '606 and 612-615, each with 90-174 files' is wrong: the counts are 606=174, 612=90, 613=109, 614=98, 615=0 derivates.

The per-day calibration films are noted as 'Kal' only in films 612-615. Film 606's notes list only 'Dateien' plus one 'Protokoll' per day. Its 660 indexed files are 160 Roentgen_A and 163 Roentgen_B AVIs, 326 files named by MAC address (00-50-C2-1D-7E-F9 / -7F-85, probably the two light cameras) and 11 Protokoll.txt files. None is named as a calibration file.

I could not confirm the X-ray AVIs are 'raw'. The 323 Roentgen AVIs in film 606 total about 1.9 GB, median 6.2 MB each, which is far too small for uncompressed 1536x1024 at 500 fps. The site says only that files are saved 'without any post-processing or correction of the distortions'. Codec and frame count are unknown because downloads return 403.

The claim that the companion studies all have CT of head, spine and pelvis holds only for 709967 ('head, complete spine, and pelvis'). PLOS ONE states CT of 'the head and entire spine', with no pelvis. The companion papers image the craniocervical junction, not L7-sacrum.
The evidence list mislabels PMC8417724: it is the craniocervical paper (709967), not the lumbosacral one. The lumbosacral paper is PMC8427507 (PMID 34513974).

The claim of 'no CT' for the beagle, dachshund and cadaver films is true only of the archive, which holds videos only. The lumbosacral paper cites Wachs' scientific-rotoscoping study of three beagles (ref 17), a method that needs CT bone models, so CT may exist outside the archive. This is unverified.
Subjects are dogs (canine lumbosacral junction: L6, L7, sacrum, pelvis), not humans. The paper calls L6/L7 'the last two lumbar vertebrae', which is consistent with 7 canine lumbar vertebrae.
verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. These are real biplanar image-intensifier X-ray videos of living dogs, not DRRs and not MV portal images. The paper describes 'biplanar X-ray high-speed videography (Neurostar Siemens AG ... Visario Speedcam)', two C-arms at 63 deg, 100 kV / 75 mA, 500 microsecond shutter. I looked at frames from the paper's Supplementary Video 3 (640x426, 25 fps, 1912 frames, raw X-ray) and from the archive's public preview stream 'Schaeferhund LS Trab 63Grad' (17.6 s, up to 1080x720). Both show real circular-field image-intensifier fluoroscopy of the caudal lumbar spine, pelvis and tail of a trotting dog. Supplementary Videos 1 and 4 show rendered CT bone models overlaid on the X-ray, and Video 2 is a light-camera view. The site says the fluoroscope uses constant rather than pulsed radiation.
verdicts.paired_ct: Stated in the paper but not released. It says 'CT images of the complete spine and pelvis were acquired using a 16-slice helical scanner (Brilliance Philips ...) ... 120 kV, 200 mA, and a slice thickness of 1 mm' for the same four dogs, and that CT-derived bone models of the pelvis, sacrum, L6 and L7 were matched to the X-ray in Maya. No CT, mesh or pose file is published, and the data are available only on request from the authors. The archive holds no CT. The companion paper 709967 has CT of head, spine and pelvis for 8 Chihuahuas and 3 Labradors. PLOS ONE has CT of head and spine for CKCS, Chihuahuas and Labradors. Neither is released.
verdicts.anatomy: Canine lumbosacral junction. Pelvis, sacrum, L6 and L7 were modelled, with the sacrum fixed rigidly to the pelvis. The images are oblique-lateral views at 63 deg. The frames I viewed show the caudal lumbar vertebrae, the pelvis overlap and the tail. The companion studies target the skull, C1 and C2. The archive also lists 'LS' and 'THL' preview clips for Labrador, Cavalier, Chihuahua and French Bulldog in subproject 167, but no paper I found reports lumbosacral tracking or pelvis CT for those dogs apart from the 709967 cohort. All subjects are dogs, not humans.
verdicts.counts: Lumbosacral paper: 4 German Shepherds (1 female, 3 male, 22 +/- 6 months), with 6 walk and 9 trot strides rotoscoped per dog. Companion studies: 8 Chihuahuas and 3 Labradors (709967); 8 CKCS, 8 Chihuahuas and 3 Labradors at walk (PLOS). Archive: 623 film records and 56,566 data files overall (Solr numFound). There are 79 dog film records, 7 of them tagged spine (024, 468, 469, 606, 612, 613, 615); 614 is tagged whole-body. Film 606 (German Shepherd, 63 deg) has 174 derivates and 660 files: 160 Roentgen_A and 163 Roentgen_B AVIs (about 1.9 GB total), 326 light-camera AVIs and 11 protocols. Which of these are the 4 study dogs is not identified. Films 612/613/614/615 are Labrador/Chihuahua/Cavalier/French Bulldog with 90/109/98/0 derivates.
verdicts.access_now: Open now (CC BY): the lumbosacral paper's 4 supplementary MP4s through Europe PMC supplementaryFiles (39 MB zip: one raw single-view X-ray clip, two rotoscoping overlays, one light-camera clip) and the summary tables. PLOS S1 zip has 10 craniocervical videos. The archive shows a public HLS preview (about 17.6 s, 25 fps) of 'Schaeferhund LS Trab 63Grad' on the subproject-167 page. Metadata is readable once the site's two-stage SHA-256 proof-of-work is solved. Raw archive files return HTTP 403: I tested MCRFileNodeServlet for a film-606 derivate and for a film-024 derivate. The archive says to contact [e-mail withheld]. CT, meshes and poses are on request from the Giessen authors only.
verdicts.licence: The articles are CC BY 4.0 (Frontiers 709966 and 709967, and PLOS ONE). No licence is stated for the raw videos, CT or poses. The archive has a 'Public Domain from' date field (film 024: 2017-12-05; film 606 and the other Giessen films: none), but film-024 files still return 403, so that field does not mean the files are openly downloadable.

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN5: Iguana Lung Ventilation (rib kinematics), public collection 'All Iguana Lung Ventilation Data'
candidate.why_relevant: A fully open, calibrated biplanar X-ray set of a trunk (ribs and vertebrae) with CT of the same individuals: CT volumes for Iguana01-05, CT log sheets, and bone and marker meshes. Every recording day has undistortion-grid and calibration-cube TIFFs per camera, taken before and after the recordings. Raw .cine files are 2.2 GB each. Anonymous range requests returned HTTP 206 for a calibration TIFF, a .cine and a CT zip. The animal is non-mammalian (reptile).
candidate.institution: Brown University, Keck XROMM facility (Brainerd, Moritz)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; Phantom cameras, 70 kV, 200 mA, 60 fps, pulsed 4 ms, SID 156 cm
candidate.anatomy: Thorax: ribs, vertebrae
candidate.subjects: Living animals: 5 green iguanas, plus frozen-specimen precision trials
candidate.n_images: 61 data trials plus 8 calibration trials, 385 files
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibration grid and cube per camera per day (DLT recoverable in XMALab); marker-based and markerless XROMM

verdicts.access_now: You can download it now without an account from the legacy XMAPortal site, which is read-only. It works one file at a time, and only once the PHP session is set. First GET the collection page and then that file's page (larequest.php?request=Collection_exploreFile&fileID=N&collectionID=38). Then larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N returns the real file and supports byte ranges. I checked the first bytes of five files this way: a calibration TIFF (1760x1760, 3,097,892 B), a .cine (Vision Research CINE, 762 frames, 1760x1760, 2,360,398,376 B), an AVI (1024x1024 uncompressed, 2,146,488,320 B), the CT zip Iguana01_CTscan.zip (864,429,095 B) and a CT log PDF. The same download URL without that session returns HTTP 206 with a 48-byte text body, 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.', so an HTTP 206 on its own proves nothing. The new portal (xma.xromm.brown.edu/datasets/ab9c96b5-5c3f-5df3-a2f3-687fd81f9a7c) lists the dataset but says 'Sign in to an XMAPortal account to view and download data'. The legacy banner says the old site stays up read-only only 'for a few months' after the 2026-06-29 migration, so anonymous access may end.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the legacy collection page: 'This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.' The new-portal dataset page shows no licence in its server-rendered HTML; its only notice is a site footer, '© 2026 Brown University. All rights reserved.' The associated JEB article is under the Company of Biologists user licence, not CC.
verdicts.counts: Legacy collection 38: 69 trials (61 data, 8 calibration), 5 individuals, 1 species, 385 files. On the new portal the same dataset reads 67 trials and 755 files, which does not reconcile with the legacy counts. File types: 116 .cih, 104 .avi, 86 .cine, 38 .tif, 18 .zip, 12 .xml, 8 .chd, 3 .pdf. Total about 304 GB: video (XMovie) about 301.5 GB, 3D volumes about 1.7 GB, processed zips about 0.67 GB, calibration about 0.2 GB.
verdicts.anatomy: Green iguana trunk. Mesh names cover ribs, sternum, cervical C2–C4, trunk vertebrae (V1–V10, vert15–18) and S1–S2. Mesh zips exist only for Ig02, Ig03 and Ig05; there are none for Ig01 or Ig04. The animal is a reptile, not a mammal.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, for all five animals, as DICOM. Ig01: 3 series of 1,193 slices (824 MB). Ig02: 257 slices (57.5 MB). Ig03: 617 .dcm (147 MB). Ig04: 1,118 slices (256 MB). Ig05: 484 slices (115 MB). There is also Ig04_Rib02.zip (1,768 .slice files, 340 MB, no subject tag, format not identified). Ig02 includes an Amira label field (ORTHO-IGUANA2-labels.am) and Ig05 includes a .rois_series.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real biplanar research X-ray videos of living animals, stored as raw camera files: Phantom .cine for 2009–2013 and Photron uncompressed .avi plus .cih for 2008. No DLT coefficients, marker tracks or rigid-body kinematics are shipped. The only processed data are six zips of undistorted frames for three Ig05 trials. Any pose would have to be recomputed in XMALab from the calibration images, and those are missing for 15 trials.
corrections: The claim that every recording day has grid and cube TIFFs per camera, before and after, is false. 2008-12-21 and 2008-12-22 (Ig02, 9 data trials) and 2009-06-16 (Ig03, 6 data trials) have no calibration trial in the collection; trial numbers 37 and 38 are absent from the listing. The three 2008 calibration days (080610, 080612, 080618) have a single cube and a single grid TIFF per camera, with no before/after pair. The 2009-07-28 calibration is .cine, with cube before and after but grid before only (comment: 'no grid after'). The 2010-06-21 calibration is .cine plus one TIFF. Only 111205, 111212 and 130916 have before/after TIFFs per camera, and 111205 carries mislabelled category and camera fields.

The claim that raw .cine files are 2.2 GB each is false. The 70 video .cine files range from 217 MB to 3 GB, and the 2009-06-16 Ig03 trials are 217–775 MB. All 30 of the 2008 data trials (Ig01 and Ig02) are Photron uncompressed AVI at 1024x1024, 104 files of 114 MB to 2 GB split into -00/-01/-02 segments with .cih headers, not .cine.
Not all data trials are biplanar. Six Ig01 trials on 2008-06-18 (Ig01_080618_02 to _07) have camera-1 video only.

The device and settings claim holds only for Ig05 (2011-12-05 and 2011-12-12). Per-file metadata for other days: Ig04 Phantom 65 kV, 200 mA, SID 127 cm, 5 ms pulse. Ig03 2009-07-28 Phantom 45 kV, 320 mA, SID 108 cm. Ig03 2009-06-16 Phantom 100 mA, kV blank. Ig01 2008 Photron 125 fps, 90 kV, 3–4 mA, no pulse listed. Ig02 2008 Photron 125 fps, 85 kV, 20 mA. Not all cameras were Phantom and not all recordings were 60 fps.
Bone and marker meshes exist only for Ig02, Ig03 and Ig05, and the Ig03 set has no marker mesh (its trials are markerless). Ig01 and Ig04 have CT but no meshes.

The evidence URL larequest.php?request=view3dvolFilesPublicStudy, which has no parameters, returns only 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or institution is empty.' and is dead as given. The working 3D-volume listing is larequest.php?request=CollectionView3dvolFiles&StudyID=5&instit=BROWN&collectionID=38.

Anonymous range requests do not prove access by themselves. Without the session set by the file page, the download endpoint returns HTTP 206 with a 48-byte error body. I got real content only after visiting the file page first, and confirmed it by the files' first bytes.

The citation is wrong on the portal and in the candidate. The paper is J Exp Biol 2016;219(Pt 3):404–411, PMID 26596531, not '(2015) 219(3), 404-414'. The recordings span 2008-06 to 2013-09, not 'Study 2011'.
Access is not permanent. The new portal requires sign-in to download, and the legacy anonymous route is described as temporary ('a few months' after 2026-06-29).
A metadata error: trial Ig05_111205_01 is dated 2012-11-05 in the listing, while its siblings are 2011-12-05.
No pose or labels are released: no DLT coefficients, 2-D or 3-D marker tracks, or XROMM transforms. The 'Processed Files' tab holds only six zips of undistorted frames for Ig05_111212_01 to _03.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. These are real in-vivo biplanar X-ray video recordings, not DRRs. I pulled frames of Ig05 trial 1 from both cameras through the new portal. They show image-intensifier footage with a circular field, a live standing iguana, a forelimb, the rib cage, the vertebral column and implanted tantalum beads. The grid_before_cam01.tif calibration image is a real undistortion-grid exposure through an image intensifier. The recording hardware changes across the study, as the paper says ('biplanar C-arm fluoroscopes or ... custom-made biplanar videoradiography'). The 2008 data (Ig01, Ig02) are Photron FASTCAM-1024PCI .avi files: 1024x1024 at 125 fps with a 1/500 s shutter, according to the .cih header. The Ig03 June 2009 data came from a Phantom v9.1 (1200x1200, 30 fps, from the .xml header). The Ig03 July 2009 data are Phantom .cine at 1808x1800 and 60 fps. The Ig04 and Ig05 data are Phantom .cine at 1760x1760 and 60 fps, 762-777 frames per cine.
verdicts.paired_ct: Confirmed at the level of the subject, but the CT was taken after death, not during the X-ray sessions. The 3D Vol listing has one CT per animal: Iguana01_CTscan.zip, ct_scan_Ig02.zip, Iguana03_CTscan.zip, Iguana04_CTscan.zip and Iguana5.zip. The paper says the animals were killed after video collection and 'CT scans of the trunks were collected at Rhode Island Hospital (Philips...; 80 kV, 0.625 mm)'. I checked two archives by range request. Ig05 contains a 479-slice DICOM series whose header reads GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS LightSpeed16, not Philips; it is 80 kVp, 0.625 mm slices, 0.307 mm pixels, about 299 mm long, collected Feb 2012 after the Dec 2011 recordings. Ig02 contains a 257-slice DICOM series. Bone and marker OBJ meshes exist for Ig02, Ig03 and Ig05. There is an Amira label field (ORTHO-IGUANA2-labels.am) for Ig02. Ig04_Rib02.zip holds an unidentified stack of .slice files. There are no model files for Ig01 or Ig04.
verdicts.anatomy: The imaged region is the pectoral end of the trunk of a reptile. In the frames I saw, this is the head/neck base, shoulder and forelimb, cervical and anterior dorsal ribs, sternum and the vertebral column. The paper animated 'the first dorsal rib ... with various combinations of additional cervical and dorsal ribs'. The models agree: cervical ribs C2-C4, dorsal ribs D1-D5 with sternal segments, sternum, and vertebrae V3-V10. In the Ig05 models 'S1/S2' are sternal ribs, not sacral vertebrae. There is no pelvis or sacrum model and no hindlimb bone model. I could not identify a pelvis or sacrum in the frames I inspected. Squamates have no mammalian-style lumbar region, and nothing lumbosacral is targeted or labelled.
verdicts.counts: Subjects: 5 live green iguanas (Ig01-Ig05). The paper says Ig01 'did not yield useful data; only data from Ig02-Ig05 are reported'. The two 'precision test' trials are frozen specimens of Ig02 and Ig03, the same animals and not extra subjects. The legacy study overview says 8 calibration trials, 61 data trials and 385 files. The collection's trial table lists 67 trials: 8 calibration and 59 data, including the 2 frozen-specimen trials. The new portal lists 67 trials and 755 files, including 190 transcoded .mp4 files. Trial files break down as 86 .cine, 104 .avi segments, 116 .cih, 38 .tif, 12 .xml, 8 .chd, 18 .zip and 3 .pdf. One camera view of one trial runs about 600-780 frames. The 2008 trials are split into 2 GB .avi chunks. The 7 Ig01 trials from 2008-06-18 have camera-1 video only, so they are single-plane.
verdicts.access_now: Open without login on the new portal. I confirmed HTTP 206 on anonymous range requests to https://xma.xromm.brown.edu/api/v1/files/<uid> for: the Iguana5.zip CT archive, where I read its central directory and extracted DICOM headers; the calibration TIFF grid_before_cam01.tif (trial 64); and the .cine files Ig4Cam1Trial1, Trial01_Cam01 and Trial2Cam1, where I read their headers. The legacy xmaportal.org pages are read-only and show no anonymous download control; Collection_exploreFile returns 'StudyID and/or Institution is empty'.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0 is stated on the legacy collection page: 'This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'. I found no licence statement on the new-portal dataset page; the only licence there is the publisher's licence for the JEB article, in its Crossref metadata.
corrections: Anatomy is the pectoral end of the trunk of a reptile: cervical ribs C2-C4, dorsal ribs 1-5, sternum and vertebrae up to about V10. No lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis is imaged as a target, modelled or labelled, and I saw none in the frames I inspected. For a lumbosacral/pelvic fluoroscopy project, the anatomy does not match.

Claim that every recording day has grid and cube TIFFs per camera, before and after: refuted. The Ig02 days (2008-12-21, 2008-12-22) and the Ig03 day 2009-06-16 have no calibration trial in the collection. The 2008 calibrations have one grid and one cube frame per camera, with no before/after pair. The 2009-07-28 calibration is marked 'no grid after' and is .cine, not TIFF. The 2010-06-21 calibration is mostly .cine. Only the 2011-12-05, 2011-12-12 and 2013-09-16 calibrations have full before/after TIFF sets.

Device string 'Phantom cameras, 70 kV, 200 mA, 60 fps, pulsed 4 ms, SID 156 cm': I found no primary source for these as single values, and SID 156 cm and the 4 ms pulse appear nowhere I checked. The paper gives ranges: 60-125 fps, 70-90 kV, 4-20 mA (C-arms) or 100-200 mA (videoradiography). The file headers show mixed hardware: Photron FASTCAM-1024PCI at 125 fps in 2008, Phantom v9.1 at 30 fps in June 2009, and Phantom at 60 fps in July 2009, 2010 and 2011. Early data were recorded on biplanar C-arm fluoroscopes, not the Keck XROMM facility.

Pose/labels: the collection holds no per-frame pose, rigid-body transforms, 2D marker tracks, XMALab projects or Maya animation files. Calibration exists only as raw grid and cube images for 8 of the 11 recording days. The only processed data are undistorted JPEG sequences for 3 Ig05 trials, bone and marker OBJ meshes (Ig02, Ig03, Ig05), one Amira label field for the Ig02 CT, and intercostal muscle-strain XLS files. Any pose would have to be derived from these by the user.
Subjects: 5 animals, but Ig01 yielded no usable data according to the paper, so 4 were analysed (Ig02-Ig05). The frozen-specimen precision trials are Ig02 and Ig03 after death, not extra specimens.
Counts: the collection table lists 67 trials (8 calibration + 59 data), not 61+8=69. The new portal lists 755 files, including 190 transcoded mp4. The 385-file figure is the legacy study count.
The CT is post-mortem and not simultaneous with the X-ray video. The Ig05 CT DICOM header says GE LightSpeed16, which contradicts the paper's 'Philips'.

'Raw .cine files are 2.2 GB each' holds only for some trials. Sizes range from 217 MB to 3 GB. All 2008 video is Photron .avi in 2 GB chunks, not .cine. The 2008-06-18 Ig01 trials have one camera only.
Article year: the portal says 2015, which is the online date. The issue is J Exp Biol 219(3):404-411 (2016), doi:10.1242/jeb.127928. The portal citation's page range '404-414' is also off.

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN40: Pelvic Mobility in Turtles (all data public)
candidate.why_relevant: Calibrated biplanar X-ray of the pelvis, sacroiliac joint and shell, with CT of the same individuals and the per-frame bone poses already solved. Files include rigid-body transform CSVs (AbsTforms), per-individual Maya scenes, CT marker coordinates and an SI-joint JCS, which together give a known CT-to-world pose for every frame. The CTs cover Es03, Es08, Pc01 and Pc04, plus pelvis, femur and shell OBJ meshes. There are calibration trials per day. Trials include cadaver 'puppet' manipulations and live walking and swimming. Anonymous download of the Es03 CT returned HTTP 206. Companion study BROWN36 (collection 10, CC BY 4.0) covers the pectoral girdle and shell of other individuals, with CT. The animals are non-mammalian (turtles).
candidate.institution: Brown University / Clemson University (Mayerl, Blob, Brainerd)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 100 kV, 100 mA, 150 fps, SID 120 cm
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis, sacroiliac joint, femur, plastron and carapace
candidate.subjects: 10 individuals of 2 species; cadaver manipulations plus living animals

verdicts.access_now: Open and anonymous, no login. Checked 2026-09-22 on the legacy portal, which is now read-only. Its banner says new work belongs on xma.xromm.brown.edu and that the legacy site stays up read-only "for a few months", so the links may stop working. The bare download link (larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N) does not work alone: without a session it returns a 48-byte text body, "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.", with HTTP 200, or 206 for a range request. Once a cookie jar has visited the study or collection page, real bytes come back. Es03.zip (fileID 50173) served 216,172,683 bytes as a zip of 1,067 DICOM slices. May6Es03Trial14Cam01.cine (fileID 50569) served 944,782,380 bytes as a Phantom cine. The RAR archive May5Es03_Animations_and_Data.rar (fileID 56775, 107,381,434 bytes) served range reads that listed its contents.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The public collection page for collectionID=42 ("All data from the Study, Pelvic Mobility in Turtles", created 2026-06-29 by Beth Brainerd) states this and links creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Companion study BROWN36 is collectionID=10, also CC BY 4.0 (confirmed).
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. The raw biplanar X-ray videos are Phantom .cine files, category XMovie, one per camera. The cited trial May6Es03Trial14 has two cine files of about 901 MB each. The Cam01 header gives 305 frames of 1760x1760 at 8-bit, uncompressed. The collection holds 175 XMovie files, plus 5 visible-light VisMovie cines. The paper gives the cameras as Phantom v10 at 1760x1760, with two Imaging Systems and Service generators.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same individuals. The 3D Vol tab lists 33 files: CT zips for all 7 individuals that have trials (Pc01, Pc04, PcX01, PcX02, PcX03, Es03, Es08), not only the 4 named. Several are flagged by the authors: Pc01's PC01_15cm.zip is "DO NOT USE", four Pc04 items are "OLD", and the "Hospital" scans are "for shell" only. The Es03 CT (8 cm scan, standard kernel) is DICOM stored as .slice files: Animage Fidex scanner, 448x448 matrix, 1,067 slices, 0.185436 mm isotropic, 110 kVp, patient name "Turtle". OBJ meshes (pelvis, femur, plastron, carapace, markers) exist only for Pc04, Pc01 and PcX01. No standalone meshes were listed for Es03, Es08, PcX02 or PcX03.
verdicts.anatomy: Turtle pelvic girdle, femur and shell (plastron and carapace). There is a sacroiliac-joint JCS, but only for Pseudemys walking scenes. No vertebral level labels or spine annotations were found. The animals are non-mammalian, and their thoracic vertebrae are fused to the carapace.
verdicts.counts: The study overview lists 10 calibration trials, 89 data trials, 10 individuals, 2 species and 387 files. Only 7 individuals appear in the trials. Per the paper, 5 were live (3 Pseudemys concinna, PcX01–03, and 2 Emydura subglobosa, Es03 and Es08); Pc01 and Pc04 are cadaver or frozen specimens. The public collection's All Files listing has 354 rows totalling about 284 GB: 175 XMovie, 5 VisMovie, 33 3DVOL, 27 ProcData, MISC (e.g. BigCube_framespec_65mm.csv) and calibration grid and cube TIFFs. That is 354 against the 387 claimed. Trials break down as 8 puppet trials (2014-06-18, Pc04 and Pc01, dead specimens), 2 frozen-specimen "wave" trials (Pc04), and live treadmill walking, swimming and breathing trials on 2015-05-05, 05-06 and 05-08.
corrections: The acquisition parameters are wrong. The paper gives walking at 100 mA, 68–85 kVp, 100 frames/s, 1/500 s shutter, and swimming at 100 mA, 90–100 kVp, 150 frames/s, 1/1000 s shutter. '100 kV, 150 fps' fits only the right view during swimming. SID 120 cm was not found in the paper's methods as retrieved and is unverified.

An 'HTTP 206' status does not prove the file is available. The bare downloadfileXsendfile URL returns a 48-byte error text ('Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.') with 206 on a range request. Real bytes come back only after the session cookie is set by visiting the collection page. Downloading with the cookie did return the real Es03 CT zip (216,172,683 bytes of DICOM).

The 'AbsTforms' rigid-body transform CSVs exist only for Trial01, a cadaver Pc04 puppet trial: Trial01RBM2xyzptsfixedAbsTforms.csv and Trial01xyzptsswappedAbsTforms.csv. The author's note on the first says the femur animation 'is messed up' when played in Maya. No per-frame transform CSVs were found for the live walking or swimming trials.

For live trials the solved motion is inside per-day, per-individual RAR archives, as Maya ASCII scenes (e.g. May05Es03AllFIles_Animated_10Hz.ma, about 169 MB) plus joint-angle CSVs (PelvicMotion_rx/ry/rz, Femur_shell_rx/ry/rz). The GCV files are 'smoothed to 100 points' per cycle and filtered (10 Hz walking, 15 Hz swimming). These are cycle-normalised angles, not per-frame CT-to-world poses. A per-frame pose would have to be pulled out of the Maya keyframes. That step was not verified.

CTmarkerCoordinates.csv (840 B) is described by the authors as a 'rough draft of CT Marker Coordinates -- needs to be redone. Marker models were poor quality.' Trial01.ma is described as a 'preliminary animation done at Brown with ugly bone models and innaccurate CT marker coordinates'.
The SI Joint JCS.zip (92.2 MB) is described as 'JCS placed at SacroIliac joint for walking Maya scenes for all three cooters', which means Pseudemys walking only, not Emydura and not swimming.

CT coverage is wider than claimed and uneven in quality. There are CT zips for Pc01, Pc04, PcX01, PcX02, PcX03, Es03 and Es08, but Pc01's CT is flagged 'DO NOT USE', several Pc04 items are 'OLD', and the hospital scans are for the shell only. OBJ meshes exist only for Pc04, Pc01 and PcX01.

Calibration material is raw per-day grid TIFFs (XCalibGrid) and cube TIFFs (XCalibObject: small cube in several poses plus big cube), with a cube framespec CSV. No solved camera calibration or DLT file was seen as a standalone file. Calibrated cameras may sit inside the Maya scenes, but that was not verified.
File count: the study overview says 387 files, but the public collection's All Files listing has 354 files (about 284 GB). The '33 3D-volume' and '27 processed' counts are confirmed.

Individuals: the portal says 10, but only 7 appear in trials. The paper reports 3 live P. concinna and 2 live E. subglobosa, plus one previously euthanised frozen specimen used for the precision analysis.

The data were acquired on 2014-06-18 and 2015-05-05 to 05-08. The paper is J Exp Biol 219(17):2650–2658 (2016). The paper states that the X-ray video and CT data are available from xmaportal.org. The public CC BY collection was created 2026-06-29.
The legacy xmaportal.org is in read-only mode during migration to xma.xromm.brown.edu, and its banner says it will remain available only 'for a few months'. The cited URLs may stop working.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. These are real biplanar high-speed X-ray videos from the research XROMM rig at Brown, recorded through an image intensifier. They are not DRRs or simulations. Each trial has Cam01/Cam02 .cine files with a Phantom 'CI' header (for example May6Es03Trial14Cam01.cine, 944,782,380 bytes, 305 frames). The portal's JPG export decodes to 1760x1760 greyscale frames with a circular intensifier field and a lead 'F' marker. The frames I pulled from May5Es03Trial15 Cam01 show the whole live turtle (head, shell, limbs, bead markers) walking on a treadmill. The per-file metadata for May6Es03Trial14Cam01 gives FrameRate 150, Shutter 1000, kV 100, mA 100, SID 120 cm, so the stated device parameters hold for that file. I did not check them for every trial. There are also 5 visible-light 'VisMovie' cam3 videos, which are not X-ray.
verdicts.paired_ct: Confirmed, and more complete than the candidate says, but with quality caveats. The 3D Vol tab lists 33 files, and every individual that appears in the trials has a scan: Es03, Es08, Pc01, Pc04, PcX01, PcX02 and PcX03. The candidate names only Es03, Es08, Pc01 and Pc04. Es03.zip (216,172,683 bytes) holds 1,067 DICOM .slice files. The header reads ANIMAGE FIDEX, Brown University, 2015-05-07, 0.185436 mm pixels, 110 kVp. That makes it a veterinary cone-beam CT taken between the May 6 and May 8 recording days, so it is CBCT rather than conventional CT. There are separate 'Hospital' CT scans 'for shell models'. Caveats: PC01_15cm.zip is marked 'DO NOT USE', all 2014 Pc04 scans are marked 'OLD', and CTmarkerCoordinates.csv says 'rough draft ... needs to be redone. Marker models were poor quality.' Two files in the 3D Vol category are actually undistorted TIFF frames labelled 'WRONG PLACE'.
verdicts.anatomy: Turtles, not humans or mammals. The species are Emydura subglobosa (Es, pleurodire) and Pseudemys concinna (Pc, cryptodire). The frames show the whole small animal (Es03 weighs 0.61 kg): shell, head, limbs and markers. Turtles have no lumbar spine, because the trunk vertebrae are fused to the carapace. The study targets the pelvic girdle, femur and shell, and 'SI Joint JCS.zip' is a joint coordinate system at the sacroiliac joint, but only 'for walking Maya scenes for all three cooters' (Pseudemys). I did not visually confirm the sacral vertebrae in any frame. For a human lumbosacral fluoroscopy task the anatomy transfers nothing. The only use is as a methods or geometry testbed.
verdicts.counts:
The overview page says 10 calibration trials, 89 data trials, 10 individuals, 2 species, 387 files and 1 collection. What is actually listed:
- Trial 99 in the full trial list is an empty placeholder titled 'I didnt mean to upload this'. So there are 88 real data trials, and the public collection (collectionID=42) lists 98 trials: 88 data plus 10 calibration.
- Only 7 individuals appear in trials or files: Pc01, Pc04 (dead specimens), PcX01, PcX02, PcX03, Es03, Es08. I could not find the other 3 of the claimed 10.
- The All Files table, with Show All on, lists 354 files, not 387: 175 X-ray cine movies, 65 XCalibObject images, 20 XCalibGrid images, 33 3DVOL, 27 ProcData, 29 MISC and 5 VisMovie.
- The 175 movies are 87 two-camera trials plus one Cam01-only trial.
- Trials by type: 7 cadaver 'puppet' trials (2014), 2 frozen-specimen 'wave' trials, live treadmill walking, swimming, and 3 breathing trials.
- Frame counts I saw: 305 per camera (May6Es03Trial14) and 1,000 per camera (May5Es03Trial15).
verdicts.access_now: Open and anonymous. No login is needed, but download links only work once the session cookie has been set by visiting the study pages. Without it the server returns 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.' With the cookie, ranged GETs to downloadfileXsendfile returned HTTP 206 for Es03.zip (Content-Range total 216172683), for a 944 MB cine, and for its JPG zip. The site banner says the legacy portal is read-only and that new work is on xma.xromm.brown.edu.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The collection page 'All data from the Study, Pelvic Mobility in Turtles' (collectionID=42, created 2026-06-29 by Beth Brainerd) states it is 'licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'. The study description also says 'License: CC BY 4.0'. Companion collection BROWN36 (collectionID=10) is also CC BY 4.0.
corrections: CT coverage is understated: PcX01, PcX02 and PcX03 also have CT (Fidex CBCT and/or hospital scans), so all 7 individuals with trials have volumes, not only Es03, Es08, Pc01 and Pc04.
The Es03 'CT' is an Animage FIDEX cone-beam CT (DICOM header), not a conventional CT. Shell models come from separate hospital CT scans.

Pc01's CT (PC01_15cm.zip) is labelled 'DO NOT USE', and the 2014 Pc04 volumes and meshes are all labelled 'OLD'. CTmarkerCoordinates.csv is a 'rough draft ... needs to be redone. Marker models were poor quality.'
'89 data trials' includes trial 99, an empty placeholder named 'I didnt mean to upload this'. There are 88 real data trials, and the public collection lists 88 data plus 10 calibration trials.
'10 individuals' could not be confirmed: only 7 individuals appear in any trial or file listing.
'387 files' could not be confirmed: the All Files table lists 354 files.
Rigid-body AbsTforms CSVs exist only for Trial01, a Pc04 cadaver puppet trial (two versions). The claim that transforms 'together give a known CT-to-world pose for every frame' is not supported.

Processed live-animal data is one RAR per individual per day for May 5 and May 6 only (10 files). Each holds Maya ASCII scenes 'AllTrials_Animated_15Hz' (filtered at 15 Hz) plus JCS rotation CSVs for femur-shell and pelvic motion, with _GCV files 'smoothed to 100 points'. None of these are per-frame 4x4 pose CSVs.
These trials have no processed files: all May 8 trials, the Trial03/04/06/07 cadaver trials, and the frozen-specimen wave trials.
The SI-joint JCS covers only 'walking Maya scenes for all three cooters' (Pseudemys), not every individual or behaviour.
Anatomy: turtles have no lumbar spine (trunk vertebrae are fused to the carapace), and I did not visually confirm the sacral vertebrae in any frame.
Device parameters (100 kV, 100 mA, 150 fps, SID 120 cm) are confirmed only in the metadata of one file (May6Es03Trial14Cam01). I did not check them per trial.
Two '3DVOL' files (Cam1/Cam2 Undistort.rar) are actually undistorted TIFFs for Trial05, labelled 'WRONG PLACE'.

I could not read the JEB full text (the publisher returns Cloudflare 403, including through chrome impersonation). I confirmed the paper's existence and its XROMM/species description from the Europe PMC abstract (PMID 27340204). No paper-level count per species was checked.

candidate.name: XMAPortal XMA7 (SVROM): Snake Intervertebral Mobility, cadaveric ball python, public collection 2
candidate.why_relevant: The most spine-like of the XROMM collections: calibrated biplanar X-ray of a vertebral column, region by region (cervical, anterior thoracic, posterior thoracic, sacral), with high-resolution CT of the same cadaver specimens for each region (about 10-11 GB each). It has grid and Lego-cube calibrations. Anonymous download of a 503 MB camera AVI returned HTTP 206. The public collection has no processed poses yet. The animal is non-mammalian (snake).
candidate.institution: XMA portal (PI Manafzadeh; study leader Margulis-Ohnuma)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 81 kV, 100 mA, 50 fps, pulsed 2 ms, SID 124 cm
candidate.anatomy: Vertebral column: cervical, anterior and posterior thoracic, sacral/cloacal regions
candidate.subjects: Cadavers: 3 ball pythons, plus lizard specimens with CT only
candidate.n_images: 158 data trials plus 7 calibration trials in the study; 86 trials in the public collection
candidate.pose_or_labels: Undistortion grids and calibration cube per session; no processed pose files yet

verdicts.access_now: Can be downloaded now without an account, though the portal's own interface asks you to sign in. On 2026-09-22, an anonymous GET to the new portal's file API (https://xma.xromm.brown.edu/api/v1/files/<fileUID>) returned HTTP 206 and real bytes for three things: SVROM02RUN_1_Cam01.avi (RIFF/AVI H264 header, Content-Range 0-1023/526673374), a grid TIF (II* header) and the CT zip mm3663_svrom02_cervical_01.zip (PK header, total 11302211209 bytes). A plain full GET of a 2.8 MB AVI returned 200 with the complete file. The fileUIDs are embedded in the public page https://xma.xromm.brown.edu/datasets/6c79d524-178d-590b-8c55-796a8ced3158/files. That web page, however, says 'Sign in to an XMAPortal account to view and download data'. So the interface route needs a free account, and the open API may be unintended and could close later. The legacy xmaportal.org page is in read-only migration mode. It shows no download control to an anonymous visitor, and its Collection_exploreFile links return 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty'.
verdicts.licence: The legacy collection page says CC BY 4.0 ('This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License', linked to creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0). The new portal's dataset pages show no licence text at all (grep for 'licen' finds nothing). No publication is linked on either portal (legacy field blank; new-portal JSON has "publications":[]). The description says only 'accompanying Margulis-Ohnuma et al. submission', and a web search found no published paper.
verdicts.counts:
The public collection has 86 trials: 82 data trials (44 from SVROM02, 38 from SVROM03) and 4 calibration sessions, all recorded 2025-05-15. The study overview lists 158 data trials, 7 calibration trials and 3 individuals, but only 2 of those individuals are in the public collection. It holds 270 files, about 261.4 GB (decimal):
- 164 X-ray AVIs (82 trials x 2 cameras), 54.5 GB, 260,918 frames in total
- 8 undistortion-grid TIFs (4 sessions x 2 cameras)
- 74 calibration-object TIFs (smallLegoCubeV2 and tinyCube)
- 8 small MISC files (cube framespec .csv and .ref)
- 16 CT zips, 206.7 GB: 8 python (10.8-11.5 GB each) and 8 lizard (13.5-15.4 GB each)

18 of the AVIs are 'quick shot' trials of only 13-18 frames (SVROM02RUN_49-51, SVROM03RUN_43-48). The processed-files tab is empty on both portals. The all-datasets listing says '524 files', but the file table itself lists 270.
verdicts.anatomy: A cadaveric ball python vertebral column, manipulated region by region. The portal labels the regions cervical, antThoracic, postThoracic and sacral; it says 'sacral', not 'cloacal'. Each python CT has a field of view of about 31 x 32 x 37 mm (1699 x 1721 x 2000 voxels at 18.5 um), so each scan covers only a short segment within its region. The lizard CTs (Calotes, Paroedura, chameleon, Elgaria, named after pitch/yaw/roll poses) are not attached to any individual. The study itself records '1 species'.
verdicts.real_xray:
Yes. These are real biplanar videofluoroscopy frames of cadaver manipulations, 2048x2048 at 50 fps, stored as lossy 8-bit H.264 (yuv420p) inside AVI; the portal also holds MP4 transcodes. Acquisition settings differ between the two cameras:
- Camera 1: 81 kV, 100 mA, SID 124
- Camera 2: 70 kV, 100 mA, SID 122
- Both: pulsed, pulse width 2, shutter 2000, magnification 3
verdicts.paired_ct:
Yes, same specimen, but the CT is raw projection data, not a reconstructed volume. There is one zip per python per region (SVROM02 and SVROM03 x cervical, antThoracic, postThoracic, sacral). I read the central directory of mm3663_svrom02_cervical_01.zip through range requests. It holds 1501 TIFs of 8,000,126 bytes each (2000x2000 16-bit), plus .xtekct, .ctprofile.xml and .ctinfo.xml. The .xtekct file shows a Nikon XT H 225 scanner (CT Pro 5.4) with these settings:
- Projections=1500, AngularStep 0.24 deg
- Detector 2000x2000 at 0.2 mm, SrcToObject 56.6 mm, SrcToDetector 612.1 mm
- 200 kV / 110 uA, voxel size 0.0185 mm

The ctprofile says Reconstruct=false. The user has to run FDK reconstruction (for example with a toolkit that reads Nikon xtekct files). I did not check whether each CT's short field of view covers the same vertebrae that the X-ray trials show.
corrections: The CT zips hold raw Nikon XT H 225 micro-CT projections (1500 projection TIFs plus .xtekct reconstruction parameters, Reconstruct=false), not reconstructed high-resolution CT volumes. The user must reconstruct them. Each has a field of view of about 31x32x37 mm at 18.5 um, so it covers a short segment, not a whole region.
The public collection contains 2 ball pythons (SVROM02, SVROM03), not 3. The third individual counted in the study overview is not in collection 2.
The kV and SID in the candidate are camera 1 only. Camera 2 is 70 kV at SID 122 cm; camera 1 is 81 kV at SID 124 cm. Both are 100 mA, 50 fps, pulsed, pulse width 2, magnification 3.

Access has a caveat. The new portal's interface says 'Sign in to an XMAPortal account to view and download data'. Anonymous download works only through the direct API URL /api/v1/files/<fileUID> (206 confirmed for AVI, TIF and CT zip). The legacy xmaportal.org page offers no anonymous download and is being retired to read-only.
The CC BY 4.0 licence appears only on the legacy xmaportal.org collection page. The new-portal dataset page shows no licence.
No publication is associated: the publications field is empty on both portals, and the description says only 'accompanying Margulis-Ohnuma et al. submission'. It is unpublished.
The portal labels the region 'sacral'. 'Cloacal' is not in the source.
The lizard CT zips (8 files, 13.5-15.4 GB each) are not linked to any individual, and the study metadata says 1 species. 'Lizard specimens' comes from the file names only.
The X-ray videos are lossy 8-bit H.264 in AVI, not raw frames. 18 of the 164 AVIs have only 13-18 frames ('quick shot' trials).
Total size is about 261 GB: 54.5 GB of video and 206.7 GB of CT. On the legacy site, collection 2 CT sizes are shown in GiB (10.0-10.7), while the new portal shows 10.8-11.5 GB.

Subjects: the study has 3 individuals (SVROM01, SVROM02, SVROM03; 'Study Overview' page shows 3 Individuals, 1 Species), but the PUBLIC collection contains only 2 ball pythons, SVROM02 and SVROM03. All SVROM01 trials (recorded 2025-05-14) and the three 2025-05-14 calibrations are marked Public = No. Only the 2025-05-15 session is public.

The '3DVOL' CT zips are NOT reconstructed volumes. Each SVROM zip holds 1501 raw 2000x2000 16-bit TIFF cone-beam projections (_0001 to _1501; Projections=1500) plus Nikon .xtekct, .ctprofile.xml and .ctinfo.xml reconstruction parameters. The user has to run the FDK reconstruction. I rendered projection 0376 of svrom02_sacral and it is a transmission radiograph of a snake segment in a tube, not a slice. Scanner is Nikon/X-Tek (Reflection Rotating 225 head; recon PC named YALE-RECON2), 200 kV, 110 uA. Target voxel size is 18.5 um for svrom02_cervical (1699x1721x2000) and 36.6 um for svrom02_sacral (963x976x2000). That makes the sacral FOV only about 35x36x73 mm, a short segment per region.

CT same subject is confirmed only by the portal's metadata: each SVROM zip is tagged Subject SVROM02 or SVROM03 and named by region (8 CTs = 2 snakes x 4 regions). Radiopaque marker beads appear in both the fluoroscopy frame and the CT projection. The CT projection shows a cut or excised segment coiled in a tube, so the CT was not taken in the pose of any fluoroscopy frame. The CT was scanned after sectioning; the scan date relative to the videos is not stated.

Lizards: the 8 lizard 3DVOL zips (Calotes, Paroedura, chameleon, Elgaria; names end in pitch/yaw/roll) have no subject assigned, and the study lists 1 species. 'Lizard specimens with CT only' is inferred from filenames only. mm3663_chameleon_elgaria_yaw is also raw projections (2001 TIFFs, 145 kV, 54 um voxel). No lizard X-ray video exists in the collection.

Anatomy: this is a snake. There is no lumbar spine, no mammalian sacrum and no pelvis. The portal's 'sacral' region label is the authors' term for a snake body region. For a human lumbosacral/pelvic fluoroscopy project it gives no anatomical coverage, only a generic real-fluoro plus same-specimen-CT plus calibration registration testbed.

Processed Files tab is empty. There are no bone poses, no tracked marker coordinates, no CT segmentations and no meshes. Calibration material is confirmed: an undistortion grid TIFF per camera per session (XCalibGrid), smallLegoCubeV2 and tinyCube calibration-object TIFFs (XCalibObject), small_lego_cube_v2_framespec.csv and a .ref file, for 4 sessions (preAM, postAM, prePM, postPM). The preAM calibration comment says 'do not use frame 3'.

Access caveat: files download anonymously, including HTTP 206 range requests, but only after a session cookie is set by visiting the collection or file page. A bare downloadfileXsendfile link without the cookie returns a 48-byte 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty' page. The legacy portal is in read-only legacy mode. The new portal (xma.xromm.brown.edu) lists the same dataset as legacyStudyID XMA:7 with 86 trials and 270 files.

Frame counts are not given by the portal. SVROM02RUN_1_Cam01.avi is H.264 2048x2048, 1801 frames at 50 fps (about 36 s), 526,673,374 bytes. Eleven of the 82 public data trials (SVROM02RUN_49-51, SVROM03RUN_43-48, 'twisted snake and taped down, quick') are only 1.2-3.3 MB per camera, so they are very short clips. Only cam1 of one trial was decoded; the resolution of cam2 was not checked.
'Pulsed 2 ms': the metadata says Radiationtype=pulsed, Pulsewidth=2, ShutterSpeed=2000 with no unit stated. MagLevel=3. The unit is not confirmed as ms.
No associated publication is listed. The description says only 'accompanying Margulis-Ohnuma et al. submission'.
verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. I decoded frame 0 of SVROM02RUN_1_Cam01.avi (from a 4 MB range download). It shows a circular image-intensifier field with a ball python head and cervical vertebrae, radiopaque marker beads and manipulation hardware. That is a real fluoroscopic acquisition, not a DRR or a simulation, and not MV portal imaging. Per-file metadata: 81 kV, 100 mA, 50 fps, ShutterSpeed 2000, SID 124 cm, MagLevel 3, pulsed, Pulsewidth 2 (unit not stated). There are two cameras (cam1, cam2) per trial, and the videos are cadaver manipulations.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same specimen by metadata. There are 8 CTs: SVROM02 and SVROM03, each with cervical, antThoracic, postThoracic and sacral, and each tagged with its subject. The same marker beads are visible in the X-ray and CT. However, the files are RAW Nikon micro-CT projections (1500 projections plus 1, 2000x2000 uint16 TIFF) with .xtekct geometry, and no reconstructed volume is included. Voxel size is 18.5-36.6 um. Each CT covers an excised short segment in a tube, not the pose of any video frame. No CT exists for SVROM01, which is not public anyway.
verdicts.anatomy: Snake (ball python) vertebral column by region. The portal labels are cervical, antThoracic, postThoracic and 'sacral'. There is no lumbar spine, no mammalian sacrum and no pelvis. The 'sacral' label is a snake body region. The lizard CTs (Calotes, Paroedura, chameleon, Elgaria) are CT only and have no fluoroscopy.
verdicts.counts: Study: 158 data trials, 7 calibration trials, 3 individuals, 1 species, 500 files. Public collection 2: 82 data trials (44 SVROM02, 38 SVROM03) plus 4 calibration trials = 86 trials and 270 files, the same on the legacy and new portals. That is 2 cameras x 82 AVIs = 164 videos. A typical full trial is about 1800 frames per camera (SVROM02RUN_1 cam1 has 1801 frames at 2048x2048). Eleven trials are very short, 1-3 MB. The collection also holds 16 CT projection zips: 8 snake and 8 lizard, 10.0-14.4 GB each.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. This is stated on the collection page ('This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License').
verdicts.access_now: Open, with no login. Tested 2026-09-22: the metadata txt downloaded, the AVI returned HTTP 206 on a range request, and range reads of a 10.8 GB CT zip worked. A session cookie from first visiting the collection or file page is required, otherwise the download link returns a 48-byte error. The legacy portal is read-only and the dataset is mirrored on xma.xromm.brown.edu (XMA:7).

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN71: Archosaur Hindlimb ROM Data (intact cadaveric alligators and guineafowl, with pelvis CT)
candidate.why_relevant: Calibrated biplanar X-ray of intact cadavers with the pelvis in the field, and CT of the same specimens: pelvis scans plus whole-body scans of 34-54 GB. There are grid and Lego-cube calibrations per session. Anonymous download of ALLROM01pelvis.zip returned HTTP 206. It can test 2D/3D pose recovery through thick soft tissue. The focus is hindlimb, but the pelvis is imaged. The animals are non-mammalian.
candidate.institution: Brown University (Manafzadeh, Gatesy)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 70 kV, 200 mA, 30 fps, pulsed 2 ms, SID 129 cm
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis, hip, knee, ankle in intact bodies
candidate.subjects: Cadavers: 2 alligators and 2 guineafowl (the study lists 8 individuals of 5 species)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Grid and calibration cube per session; ROM poses published (PNAS 2021, Nat Commun 2024)

verdicts.access_now: Downloadable NOW, anonymously, no account, no request form. Collection page loads (HTTP 200) and the download endpoint larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=<id> serves the bytes: I pulled ALLROM01pelvis.zip in full (185,585,901 B, 200, ~42 MB/s) and byte-ranged into the 57.5 GB micro-CT zip (206 Partial Content, Accept-Ranges works, Content-Range .../57552842074). Three access frictions, all real but not blocking: (1) the download URL only works inside a session that has first loaded a collection page — a cold deep link returns the 48-byte body "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty", so a scraper must set the cookie by fetching CollectionView3dvolFiles first; (2) the site carries a banner: "This website is in a legacy read-only mode. New work should be completed on xma.xromm.brown.edu" (a new portal at that host is live, HTTP 200; the legacy HTML also contains commented-out banners saying the old site goes read-only 29 Jun 2026 and stays up "for a few months"), so these exact URLs have a stated expiry and there is no DOI or landing-page redirect for the data; (3) the three 34–54 GB micro-CT zips were written WITHOUT ZIP64 records — the EOCD reports 4549 entries and a central-directory offset of 1,717,581,615 in a 57.5 GB file (true offset wraps mod 2^32), so a strict unzip may refuse them and a tolerant extractor or manual offset unwrapping is needed. Total collection volume ~1.44 TB (X-ray video 1.19 TB + 3D volumes 250.7 GB).
verdicts.anatomy: Hindlimb ROM is the subject, but the pelvis is genuinely in the field, and in the alligator so is the vertebral column. I rendered first frames from four cines (2 alligator individuals, 1 guineafowl): circular image-intensifier field, real transmission images through intact soft tissue, showing trunk/tail vertebrae, pelvis, femur and distal limb with implanted zirconia beads. Trial comments confirm framing varies by trial ("pelvis centered", "Hip ~centered", "MT often out") — many trials are framed on knee/ankle with the pelvis partly or wholly out. Note raw cines are transmission-like (background bright, bone darker) and carry II pincushion distortion; undistortion grids are supplied but not applied. CT side: I rendered MIPs and mid-slices of ALLROM01pelvis (809 slices, 480x480, 0.1706 mm isotropic) — it is an INTACT body segment with skin and soft tissue showing presacral vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, sacrum, caudal vertebrae, both ilia and proximal femora, with bright bead markers. Micro-CT projections of a "bottle" file show a soft-tissue block containing spine/pelvis and beads inside a plastic jar, not clean bones and not a whole body. All anatomy is non-mammalian (Alligator mississippiensis, Numida meleagris).
verdicts.counts: Collection 14 (BROWN71): 132 trials = 115 Data + 17 Calib (candidate's "132 trials" correct), 420 files (correct), 0 processed files. By category: 230 XMovie .cine (~1193 GB), 136 XCalibObject .tif, 34 XCalibGrid .tif, 10 MISC (5 Lego-cube framespec .csv + 5 .ref), 10 3DVOL .zip (250.7 GB). Cines are 1760x1760, 8-bit, 1800 frames each in the four I parsed, 30 fps header — so roughly 3.85e5 individual X-ray frames, ~1.9e5 synchronised biplanar pairs (1.1934e12 bytes / 1760^2). Individuals in this collection: ALLROM01 (26 data trials), ALLROM02 (30), GFROM01 (29), GFROM02 (30). Parent study BROWN71 overall: 26 calib + 189 data trials, 8 individuals, 5 species, 682 files, 3 collections. Recording dates 2018-05-24 to 2019-11-16 (one post-calib trial dated 2019-12-12).
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the collection record itself: "This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" with a link to creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ and a request to follow CC attribution best practice. Authors Gatesy, S. and Manafzadeh, A.; created 2020-08-26, last modified 2024-02-20. No separate LICENSE file, no machine-readable licence metadata, no DOI on the data record itself.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same individuals, but not what the candidate says. Two different modalities and only one individual has DICOM. ALLROM01 has four Animage FIDEX (veterinary cone-beam) DICOM series: ALLROM01pelvis (2018-06-06, 809 slices, 480^2, 0.1706 mm, KVP 110 in header, InstitutionName "Brown University", PatientName "ROMtests"), ALLROM01limb (2018-06-06, 384^2, 0.2133 mm), ALLROM01rPelvis and ALLROM01rLimb (both 2019-04-08, 480^2/0.1705 mm and 448^2/0.1827 mm) — i.e. scanned days to weeks after each video session, with the beads still in place, body intact with soft tissue. The other three individuals (ALLROM02, GFROM01, GFROM02) have NO DICOM at all: only the six "bottle" zips, which are Nikon XT H micro-CT projects — 2500 raw 2000x2000 16-bit projection TIFFs plus a VGStudio .vol reconstruction and .xtekct geometry (VoxelsX/Y/Z 1853/1844/1998 at 0.06276 mm = ~116 x 116 x 125 mm field, SrcToObject 368.4 mm, SrcToDetector 1174 mm, 120 kV, 125 uA, 0.1 mm Cu filter, 2500 projections, 0.144 deg step). HU is not calibrated in either (CBCT/micro-CT). Registration-grade pairing is therefore possible in principle (same specimen, same beads) but must be built by the user.
verdicts.real_xray: Real, not synthetic, and verified at pixel level. I decoded Phantom .cine headers and rendered frames: 1760x1760 8-bit, 1800 frames per trial, 30 fps, circular II field with physical letter/number markers in the beam, soft-tissue attenuation and implanted radiopaque beads visible. Biplanar (cam1/cam2 per trial, 2 files per trial for 115 data trials). Acquisition per PNAS SI: two Varian G-1086 tubes with Dunlee TH9447QXH590 image intensifiers, W. M. Keck Foundation XROMM Facility, Brown University. These are cadaveric manipulations, not in vivo motion, and not clinical C-arm fluoroscopy.
corrections: 'Whole-body scans of 34-54 GB' is wrong. The 34.7-53.6 GB 'bottle' zips are Nikon XT H micro-CT projects with a ~116 x 116 x 125 mm reconstructed field (VoxelsX/Y/Z 1853/1844/1998 at 0.0628 mm, from the .xtekct file) — a body segment in a jar, not a whole body. I rendered three raw projections: a soft-tissue block containing spine and pelvis with beads, inside a plastic container. Their bulk is 2500 raw 2000x2000 projection TIFFs plus a VGStudio .vol, not a large field of view.

'Pelvis scans plus whole-body scans' overstates CT coverage. Only ONE of the four individuals (ALLROM01) has pelvis/limb DICOM CT; ALLROM02, GFROM01 and GFROM02 have micro-CT projection projects only, with no DICOM anywhere in the collection.

'ROM poses published (PNAS 2021, Nat Commun 2024)' is not a data release. The Processed Files tab of this collection is EMPTY: no XMALab 2-D marker tracks, no rigid-body transforms, no solved calibration (no DLT coefficients or camera matrices), no bone meshes, no joint-coordinate systems, no joint-rotation tables. The PNAS data-availability statement deposits only 'calibration images, X-ray videos, and CT files' (BROWN20, BROWN58, BROWN71); the PNAS SI Appendix names no Dryad/Zenodo/figshare deposit. What is provided is per-session raw calibration IMAGES (grid + 4 Lego-cube pairs per camera) plus the cube framespec .csv and .ref — the calibration must be solved by the user in XMALab, and the poses must be re-tracked.

The device line's single values are a range in the only primary source (PNAS 2021 SI Appendix): 65-85 kV, 200 mA, magnification level 0, 2 ms pulse width, Varian G-1086 tubes, Dunlee TH9447QXH590 intensifiers, 118-130 cm SUBJECT-to-image distance (not source-to-image distance), and 30-50 fps with 1/1000 s shutter, 1760x1760, 125-300 us EDR. I could find no primary source anywhere on the portal or in the papers for the specific '70 kV' or 'SID 129 cm'. The 30 fps is consistent with the cine header of ALLROM01cam1RUN01 (FrameRate 30, 1800 frames).

CT technique in the SI (90 kV, 0.1 mA, 0.173 mm, 480x480, FIDEX) does not match the shipped DICOM headers (KVP 110, tube current 31, SliceThickness 0.17062, 480x480). Small, but the published methods and the released files disagree on kV.

The SI states specimens were 'disarticulated' before CT; the released ALLROM01pelvis volume is NOT disarticulated — the render shows an intact trunk segment with skin, soft tissue, ribs, gastralia, vertebral column, both ilia and proximal femora. Whatever was disarticulated, what shipped is an intact-body scan.

'Anonymous download returned HTTP 206' is true but incomplete: the endpoint only serves bytes to a session that has already loaded a collection page; cold, it returns a 48-byte error. Any automated fetch must prime the cookie.

Access has a stated shelf life: the portal is in 'legacy read-only mode', new work is directed to xma.xromm.brown.edu, and the record carries no DOI, so both evidence URLs are expected to break. I could not find this collection on the new portal (no public search/API endpoint responded).
The three >4 GB zips lack ZIP64 records (EOCD offsets wrap mod 2^32), so strict unzip implementations may fail on them.

The Nature Communications 2024 data-availability statement does NOT cite this collection: it points to StudyID=20 collection 15 (guineafowl CT and in vivo XROMM) and says the emu CT is 'available on request directly from' J. R. Hutchinson. Only the portal's own association links that paper to BROWN71 collection 14. The PNAS 2021 statement does cite BROWN71.
One of the 17 calibration trials in this collection (20180716RATROMpre, 2018-07-16, small Lego cube) belongs to a rat session with no archosaur data in the collection — it pads the trial count.

Framing caveat for a spine use case: the X-ray videos are aimed at the hindlimb. The pelvis is in the field in many alligator trials and the presacral/caudal column is often visible, but trial comments ('MT often out (pelvis centered)', 'Hip ~centered') show framing shifts trial to trial; there is no per-frame record of what is in the field.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, confirmed by looking at the frames. I downloaded the start of three raw Phantom .cine files and rendered frames: ALLROM01cam1RUN06, GFROM01cam1RUN01 and ALLROM02cam1RUN01. Each is an image-intensifier acquisition: circular vignetted field, quantum noise, a lead 'F' marker, and tantalum beads visible in the bones. They are not DRRs, not simulated and not MV portal images. The format is 1760x1760 8-bit, uncompressed, with 1800 stored frames in each of the three files sampled. There are two cameras per trial (cam1/cam2), so the setup is biplanar. The X-ray settings differ between sessions. ALLROM01RUN06 (2018-05-24) is 30 fps, 70 kV, 200 mA, SID 129, pulsed 2 ms. GFROM01RUN01 (2019-04-12) and ALLROM02RUN01 (2019-11-16) are 50 fps, 85 kV, 200 mA, SID 120, pulsed 2 ms.
verdicts.paired_ct:
Yes. Each CT is tied to the same individual through the IndividName and IndividID fields in the per-file metadata. There are two kinds of CT.
(1) ALLROM01 has four DICOM zips: pelvis, rPelvis, llimb and rLimb. I downloaded ALLROM01pelvis.zip in full: 185,585,901 bytes, 809 slices. Header: Modality CT, Manufacturer ANIMAGE (a Fidex-type CBCT), 110 kV, 480x480 pixels, 0.1706 mm isotropic, so about 82x82x138 mm. StudyDate is 2018-06-06, between that animal's X-ray sessions of 2018-05-24 and 2019-02-04. MIPs show presacral vertebrae, both sacral vertebrae, the ilia, the proximal caudal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia and implanted tantalum beads.
(2) GFROM01, GFROM02 and ALLROM02 each have two Nikon XT H micro-CT 'bottle' scans (33.7-53.6 GB per zip). I checked only ALLROM02bottle1. Its xtekct file gives 120 kV, 125 uA, 0.1 mm Cu filter, 2500 projections, 1853x1844x1998 voxels at 0.0628 mm, so about 116x116x125 mm. The zip holds the raw projection TIFFs, a .vol reconstruction and VGStudio projects. Every CT was acquired after the X-ray session of the same specimen: GF01 2019-09-19, GF02 2019-10-31, AL02 2019-11-27.
verdicts.anatomy: This is non-mammalian anatomy. The rendered alligator frame (ALLROM01RUN06) shows the trunk: the vertebral column crossing the sacral and pelvic region, plus both hindlimbs with beads. The guineafowl frame shows the pelvis/synsacrum region and the limb. Trial comments put the hip at the centre of the field ('Hip ~centered'), and the pelvis CT contains the alligator's presacral-sacral-caudal junction. There is no human-type lumbar spine or sacrum. The alligator has 2 sacral vertebrae; the guineafowl has a fused synsacrum. The imaging targets the hip, knee and ankle; the spine is incidental.
verdicts.counts: The collection page lists 132 trials: 115 data trials and 17 calibration trials. The file listing shows 420 files: 230 XMovie cines (about 1.19 TB), 136 XCalibObject, 34 XCalibGrid, 10 MISC and 10 3DVOL. There are 4 individuals: ALLROM01, ALLROM02, GFROM01 and GFROM02. Assuming about 1800 frames per cine, the collection holds roughly 400k X-ray frames. That total is an estimate from 3 sampled files, not a stated figure. The parent study BROWN71 lists 8 individuals, 5 species, 189 data trials, 26 calibration trials and 682 files. The other individuals (a quail, a rat and loons) are not public.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The collection page states this directly: 'This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.'
verdicts.access_now: Open, and no login is needed, but a session cookie is. Called without a cookie, downloadfileXsendfile does return HTTP 206, but the body is a 48-byte error ('Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.'). After I visited the CollectionView page with a cookie jar, the full ALLROM01pelvis.zip, ranged reads of the 57.5 GB bottle zip and the cine files all downloaded as application/octet-stream. The portal banner says the site is now in 'legacy read-only mode' and that new work belongs on xma.xromm.brown.edu, so these URLs may move. The bottle zips have truncated, non-zip64 local-header offsets (made on macOS). I found the xtekct entry only after adding 3x2^32 to the recorded offset, so a standard unzip may fail on the 34-54 GB files.
corrections: Device parameters vary by session. The candidate's '70 kV, 200 mA, 30 fps, pulsed 2 ms, SID 129 cm' matches only the 2018-05-24 ALLROM01 session I checked. GFROM01 (2019-04-12) and ALLROM02 (2019-11-16) are 85 kV, 200 mA, 50 fps, SID 120 cm.

'Whole-body scans' is not stated anywhere. The 33.7-53.6 GB files are two Nikon XT H micro-CT 'bottle' scans per specimen. The one I opened (ALLROM02bottle1) covers about 116x116x125 mm at 0.063 mm voxels, and each zip is mostly raw projections plus a .vol reconstruction. Treat these as regional scans (about 12.5 cm each) until the other scans are checked.
Pelvis scans exist only for ALLROM01 (ALLROM01pelvis and ALLROM01rPelvis, Animage CBCT DICOM, 0.17 mm). The other three specimens have only the Nikon bottle scans.

The claim that an anonymous download returned HTTP 206 is misleading on its own. Without a session cookie the 206 carries a 48-byte error page. A real download works anonymously only after a CollectionView page has set a Webportal cookie.

No poses or labels are distributed. The Processed Files tab of collection 14 is empty: no XMALab marker points, no rigid-body transforms, no solved calibrations. The PNAS 2021 Data Availability statement lists only 'Calibration images, X-ray videos, and CT files' on XMAPortal. The 'ROM poses published' claim has no downloadable per-frame pose in any primary source I could find. Tantalum beads are visible in the frames and in the CT, so users could solve poses themselves with XMALab. The Lego-cube calibration is raw images plus a framespec CSV.
The Nat Commun 2024 paper's data statement cites the guineafowl CT and in vivo XROMM in BROWN20 collection 15, not these cadaver ROM trials. It is only loosely a source for this collection.
Calibration trial 26 (20180716RATROMpre) belongs to a rat session whose data trials are not public. So only 16 of the 17 calibration trials pair with the public data trials.

The CT was acquired after the X-ray sessions, sometimes weeks later (ALLROM01 CT 2018-06-06 against X-rays of 2018-05-24 and 2019-02-04), in a different body posture. Pairing needs per-bone rigid registration, for example using the beads, not a single volume pose.
The anatomy is reptile and bird. Any 'lumbosacral' relevance to human spine fluoroscopy is by analogy only.

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN21: Morphology and Function of Wild and Domesticated Turkeys (CT plus XROMM standing-posture data)
candidate.why_relevant: Calibrated biplanar standing-posture X-ray of the pelvis (synsacrum) and hindlimb, with CT and pelvis/femur meshes of the birds that were X-rayed (e.g. BBWRed5). There are calibration trials per day. The frames are near-static. The animals are non-mammalian (bird).
candidate.institution: Brown University (Stover, Brainerd, Roberts)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 105 kV, 200 mA, 30 fps, SID 145 cm
candidate.xray_kind: Biplanar videofluoroscopy (posture trials on a force plate)
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis/synsacrum, femur, tibiotarsus, tarsometatarsus
candidate.subjects: Living animals: 85 CT-scanned; posture X-ray on a subset
candidate.n_images: 70 data trials plus 7 calibration trials; 638 files
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibration per day; Maya measurement scenes

verdicts.access_now: Open, and downloadable today with no login from the legacy XMAPortal. The legacy site is in read-only mode and its banner says it will stay up "for a few months". Downloads use larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N, and they only work after the collection page has set a PHP session cookie.
