A bare request returns "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty." I downloaded these without logging in: a 3,097,892-byte calibration TIF (fileID 45329, 1760x1760 8-bit), byte ranges of three .cine movies, and the zip central directory of the BBWRed5 CT, which holds 948 entries, almost all .dcm slices. The replacement portal lists the same dataset (xma.xromm.brown.edu/datasets/8fec2361-9ac0-5367-940d-429fe2cdc319, legacyStudyID BROWN:21) but says "Sign in to an XMAPortal account to view and download data", so access there needs a free account. The collection is about 56 GB in total (listed sizes summed): 40.4 GB of 3D volumes and meshes, 11.1 GB of X-ray cines, 1.6 GB of calibration TIFs, 1.8 GB misc and 0.76 GB of Maya scenes.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The legacy collection page states it ("This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License"). The new portal's dataset page shows no licence for the dataset; the only licence fields there belong to the two papers in their Crossref metadata.
verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. The files are Phantom .cine biplanar image-intensifier movies: 1760x1760, 8-bit, 30 fps (FrameRate16=30 read from the cine setup header), with 19 frames in BBWRed5 01 and 30 in Teal1 01. I rendered frame 0 of BBWRed5 01 cam1, BBWRed5 01 cam2 and Teal1 01 cam1. They are real radiographs with a circular field of view. The tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus show clearly. The pelvis/synsacrum is faint or lost inside the dense body silhouette of the heavy broad-breasted bird, and the wild bird's body is partly out of the field. The 138 XMovie cines are 69 posture trials x 2 cameras.
verdicts.paired_ct: Only partly true. Six birds were X-rayed: BBWRed5, BBWBlue7, BBWYellow13, RedPink21, TealPink24 and Teal1. The JEB paper says "Three female turkeys from each strain". All six have pelvis, femur, tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus meshes (.obj/.wrl at several resolutions). Only BBWRed5 has a CT volume I could identify by name ("BBW red 5.zip", 168.9 MB, DICOM, 946 slices). None of the 183 CT zips is labelled with the other five birds' names. The other CTs are longitudinal growth scans of other birds, 2 to 20 weeks old.
verdicts.anatomy: Meshes cover the pelvis (the synsacrum is part of these meshes), femur, tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus, and some birds also have vertebrae meshes. In the posture X-ray frames I checked, the hindlimb bones are clear and the pelvis is at most faint. The subjects are birds (Meleagris gallopavo, turkey), not mammals.
verdicts.counts: The study overview says: 7 calibration trials, 70 data trials, 85 individuals, 2 species, 638 files, 1 collection. Collection 43 lists 612 files, not 638: 353 3DVOL, 138 XMovie, 72 XCalibObject, 12 XCalibGrid, 23 MISC, 14 ProcData. Of the 70 "data trials", 69 are posture trials; the 70th (#77) is only a summary spreadsheet, "Turkey Locomotion Data.xlsx". Posture trials per bird: BBWRed5 10, BBWBlue7 10, RedPink21 13, TealPink24 11, BBWYellow13 13, Teal1 12, recorded 2014-12-01 to 2014-12-03. Estimated total from cine sizes: about 3,700 frames across both cameras, roughly 1,850 biplanar pairs. There are also 4 wand calibration cines of 443 MB each and plumb-line TIFs. The 3D Vol tab has 183 CT zips covering about 84 distinct subject labels.
corrections: File count: collection 43 (the candidate URL) lists 612 files. The 638 figure is the whole study BROWN21, from the study overview.
'70 data trials' includes a summary spreadsheet counted as trial #77. There are 69 X-ray posture trials, each with a cam1 and cam2 .cine (138 movies).

'85 CT-scanned' is not what the source says. The study overview says '85 Individuals'. The 3D Vol tab has 183 CT zip archives covering about 84 subject labels, most of them repeat growth scans of the same birds.
The same-bird CT claim holds in full only for BBWRed5, whose DICOM zip I opened and read. The other five X-rayed birds have bone meshes only; I found no CT volume labelled with their names.

Device settings: 30 fps is confirmed from the cine header, and the camera metadata reads 'Phantom'. I found no primary source for 105 kV, 200 mA or SID 145 cm. The portal's SID field is empty and the JEB methods give no kV, mA or SID.

Pose labels: there are per-day calibration cube and grid TIFs, plumb-line TIFs and wand cines. The Maya .mb files are CT measurement scenes for other birds (bbw 5/6/7, pilgrim 1-3, wild 63/65/66) plus 'BBW Wild dorsal pelvis' and 'leg comparison'. I found no per-trial rotoscoped pelvis/femur pose files and no XMALab point files, only a centre-of-mass results spreadsheet.
Metadata errors on the portal: the trials 'BBW Yellow13 01-13' give BBWBlue7 as their individual, and the trials named 'Wild TealPink21' give TealPink24.

The third evidence URL (request=view3dvolFilesPublicStudy) depends on a session. A fresh request returns 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or institution is empty.' The working URL is request=CollectionView3dvolFiles&StudyID=21&instit=BROWN&collectionID=43.
Direct file-download URLs fail without a session cookie from an earlier page view. No login is needed.
The legacy portal is read-only and temporary. The new portal (xma.xromm.brown.edu) requires a free account to view or download and shows no dataset licence.
Dates: X-ray trials are 2014-12-01 to 2014-12-03; the collection was created 2026-06-29. The 2012-2017 range was not verified; the only year labels I saw on CT files were 2013 and 2014.

Relevance caveat: the subjects are birds, and in the frames I rendered the pelvis/synsacrum is barely visible through the body mass. For pelvis work, the useful X-ray content is weaker than the description suggests.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. The data trials are Phantom CINE files, two per trial (cam1 and cam2). I downloaded four of them anonymously and parsed the headers: 1760x1760 pixels, 8-bit, with the circular field and vignetting of an image intensifier. Two trials were rendered, BBWRed5 01 (19 frames per camera) and Wild Teal1 12 (30 frames per camera, the last 3 dark because the beam was off). Both show real radiographic anatomy: a living turkey standing, with gizzard grit, ribs and hindlimb bones. These are not DRRs, not simulation and not MV portal images. The file metadata page lists 30 fps, shutter 1000, 105 kV, 200 mA, SID 145 cm and pulsed radiation. Frames are near-static: the mean absolute difference between consecutive frames is about 0.8-1.0 grey levels.
verdicts.paired_ct: Partly confirmed. The JEB 2018 methods say: "Each turkey was CT scanned to create 3D bone models of the pelvis and femora". The six birds X-rayed for posture (BBWRed5, BBWBlue7, BBWYellow13, RedPink21, TealPink24, Teal1) all have meshes in the collection (pelvis, femur, tibiotarsus, tarsometatarsus; .obj/.wrl). A raw CT volume is listed under a posture bird's name only for BBWRed5: 'BBW red 5.zip', 177 MB. Its zip directory holds hundreds of .dcm slices. The other five posture birds have meshes only. The DICOM UIDs embed a Unix time of about 2015-05-07, against X-ray dates of 2014-12-01 to 03. That may only be the export time, so the gap between CT and X-ray is unknown.
verdicts.anatomy: Non-mammalian: domestic and wild turkey, Meleagris gallopavo. There is no lumbar spine and no mammalian sacrum; the avian pelvis is fused to a synsacrum. The rendered frames clearly show the distal hindlimb (tibiotarsus, intertarsal joint, tarsometatarsus), ribs, gizzard and body soft tissue. In the broad-breasted white bird (BBWRed5) the pelvic region is almost opaque with soft tissue. In the two trials I rendered I could not pick out the synsacrum or pelvis with confidence. The paper says the pelvis pose was rotoscoped from these videos, so the pelvis is at least partly in the field of view.
verdicts.counts: Study overview: 7 calibration trials, 70 'data' trials, 85 individuals, 2 species, 638 files. The collection lists 612 files. Only 69 of the 70 data trials are X-ray; trial 77 is the 'Turkey Locomotion Data Summary' xlsx. That gives 138 X-ray cine files (69 trials x 2 cameras). Six birds were X-rayed: BBWRed5 10 trials, BBWBlue7 10, BBWYellow13 13, RedPink21 13, TealPink24 11, Teal1 12. This matches the paper's 'three female turkeys from each strain'. Estimated frames from file sizes: about 3,770 across both cameras, or about 1,880 biplanar pairs, at 10-30 frames per clip. I checked the header of 4 files only. The 85 'individuals' are study-wide. They include CT-only growth-series birds, scout scans and dead or dissected specimens, not 85 living birds that were CT-scanned.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0, stated on the collection page ('This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License').
verdicts.access_now: Open, no login needed. An anonymous curl with a session cookie from any public page downloaded cine files (HTTP 206 range served, full 58.9 MB and 92.9 MB files) and the CT zip (HTTP 200, 177,054,547 bytes). File URLs have the form larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N. The site banner says the portal is in legacy read-only mode and is moving to xma.xromm.brown.edu, so these URLs may not last.
corrections: Pose/labels refuted: no rotoscoped pelvis or bone poses for the posture trials are published. The 14 ProcData files are Maya morphology-measurement scenes for other birds (bbw 5/6/7, pilgrim 1-3, wild 63/65/66, plus a dorsal pelvis and a leg comparison) and the locomotion xlsx. 'COM results_with table.xlsx' holds only 2-D centre-of-mass coordinates, distances and ratios for 3 trials per bird. What does exist is calibration: cube images (XCalibObject), undistortion grids (XCalibGrid), plumb-line images with beads, and Day-2 force-plate wand cines.
The 'Maya measurement scenes' are not X-ray registration scenes and are not for the six X-rayed birds. I could not establish whether 'bbw 5' is the same bird as BBWRed5.
'70 data trials' should be 69 X-ray posture trials plus 1 non-X-ray summary trial. '638 files' is the study-wide count; the collection lists 612.

'85 CT-scanned living animals' is not stated anywhere. The overview says '85 Individuals'. The 3D Vol list includes scout scans (about 1.4 MB each), repeated growth time points and specimens labelled 'dead' or 'leg dissection'.
'Posture X-ray on a subset' is exactly 6 birds: 3 broad-breasted white (Red5, Blue7, Yellow13) and 3 wild (RedPink21, TealPink24, Teal1).
Raw CT volume for the same subject exists only for BBWRed5 ('BBW red 5.zip', DICOM). The other five posture birds have surface meshes only.
Portal metadata errors: the 13 'BBW Yellow13' trials are tagged with individual BBWBlue7, and the 'Wild TealPink21' trials are tagged TealPink24.
Dates: the X-ray trials were acquired 2014-12-01 to 2014-12-03 and both papers were published in 2018. 'Published 2012-2017' is unsupported.
The anatomy is avian (synsacrum): there is no lumbar spine and no mammalian sacrum. In the rendered BBW frames the pelvis is buried in soft tissue; the distal hindlimb bones are what shows clearly.

Evidence URL 'larequest.php?request=view3dvolFilesPublicStudy' returns 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or institution is empty.' without a session. Use request=CollectionView3dvolFiles&StudyID=21&instit=BROWN&collectionID=43 instead. Public trialID=1 is 'BBWRed5 01', not a calibration trial.

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN68: Quail Hip ROM (cadaveric common quail)
candidate.why_relevant: A small, clean cadaver set: biplanar X-ray of the hip and pelvis, pelvis CT of each specimen, and grid plus Lego-cube calibration with a framespec CSV. Anonymous CT download returned HTTP 206. The animals are non-mammalian (bird) and small. No licence is stated.
candidate.institution: Brown University (Manafzadeh, Gatesy)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 85 kV, 200 mA, 10 fps, SID 124 cm
candidate.xray_kind: Biplanar videofluoroscopy of cadaver ROM manipulation
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis, hip, femur
candidate.n_images: 38 data trials plus 7 calibration trials, 157 files
candidate.pose_or_labels: Grid plus Lego-cube calibration with framespec; ROM poses published

corrections: Access is open but depends on a session. Individual files download without login, but only after you open the study page, which sets a PHP 'Webportal' cookie. Tested 2026-09-22: a ranged GET for CT fileID 78478 returned HTTP 206 with a real ZIP (341,020,238 bytes). A cine (fileID 77966, 1,858,591,820 bytes) also returned 206. The framespec CSV (fileID 77998, 696 B) and a calibration TIF (fileID 77926, 1760x1760 8-bit) returned 200. The same download URL sent without the cookie returns 48 bytes of text: 'Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty.' The portal's own notice says batch download is for logged-in users only.

No pose or label data is released. The Processed Files tab shows 'Showing 0-0 of 0 files' and Collections is 0. The paper measured 20,627 hip poses from 3 markers per bone (ilia and femora) using XMALab and Maya, but its data accessibility statement lists only 'calibration images, X-ray videos and CT files'. The Royal Society figshare supplement has only three methods PDFs, four figure PDFs and two MP4 movies (CC BY 4.0). There are no marker coordinates, transforms or pose tables. 'ROM poses published' is true only as figures. Only the raw calibration material (grid and Lego-cube TIFs, framespec CSV, .ref) is there to calibrate yourself.

No licence anywhere. The legacy study pages carry none. The paper says '(c) 2018 The Author(s). Published by the Royal Society. All rights reserved.' The new portal footer says '(c) 2026 Brown University. All rights reserved.' The file listing (viewAllFilesMetadata) marks all 151 files 'File Public = No', even though they download anonymously. Treat the terms of reuse as unknown. Only the figshare supplement is CC BY 4.0.

File count: the overview says 157 files, but the listing shows 151. These are 76 .cine X-ray movies (2 cameras x 38 data trials), 12 grid TIFs, 48 Lego-cube TIFs, 12 MISC (framespec CSV and .ref) and 3 CT zips. Total is about 120 GB, of which about 119.2 GB is cine: most are 1.7 GB each, a few about 0.95 GB.
Calibration trials: of the 7, trial 45 is labelled 'empty trial'. That leaves 6 real ones, pre and post on each of 3 days.

Acquisition metadata is incomplete. The per-file metadata gives FrameRate 10, kV 85, mA 200, SID 124 for QROM01. For QROM02, SID is blank. For the QROM03 cines sampled, kV, mA and SID are all blank. The paper gives 75-85 kV (not a fixed 85), 200 mA, magnification level 3, 2 ms pulses, Varian G-1086 tubes, Phantom v10 cameras, 1760x1760 at 10 fps and 1/1000 s shutter.

The CT is not of the specimen as filmed. Per the paper and the file comments, the specimens were disarticulated after video collection and the CT was taken of pelves and femora only: Animage FIDEX, 90 kV, 0.173 mm isotropic, 480x480. The files are DICOM (CT Image Storage) renamed '.slice' inside each zip. QROM03 has 1,771 slices: 812 at the zip root plus two 481-slice subvolume folders. The free vertebral column that was present during filming was not CT-scanned. Only the synsacrum, fused into the bird pelvis, would appear.

Specimen preparation: all muscles were removed, keeping the vertebral column, pelvis, femora and hip joint capsule. These are skeletonised bird preparations, not soft-tissue-covered cadavers, so image contrast is far from clinical fluoroscopy. Whether the vertebral column is in the X-ray field of view was not checked visually.

Durability risk: the legacy xmaportal.org site shows 'This website is in a legacy read-only mode', and a notice left in its HTML says it will stay read-only 'for the next few months'. 'Quail Hip ROM' did not appear in the public dataset list fetched from the replacement portal (xma.xromm.brown.edu/datasets, 49 datasets on the page fetched). Other Manafzadeh/Gatesy sets do appear, such as 'Archosaur Hindlimb ROM Data'. The candidate's URLs may stop working.

Frame count is not stated anywhere. The cine header for QROM01cam1RUN01 says 600 stored images (60 s at 10 fps). Dividing total cine bytes by 3.1 MB per frame estimates about 38,000 frames across both cameras, roughly 19,000 biplanar pairs. That is an estimate, not a count.
verdicts.access_now: Open without login, one file at a time. Open the study page first to get the session cookie, then fetch larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N. Range requests work (HTTP 206). Batch download needs a login. The site is legacy and read-only, and the study was not found on the replacement portal.
verdicts.licence: None stated for the imaging data. Every page and the paper say 'All rights reserved', and the listing flags all files 'File Public = No'. Only the figshare supplement (methods PDFs, figures, movies) is CC BY 4.0.
verdicts.anatomy: X-ray preparations: vertebral column, pelvis and femora with all muscle removed and the hip capsule kept; markers in the ilia and femora. CT: disarticulated pelvis (with the fused synsacrum) and femora only. No CT of the free vertebral column.
verdicts.counts: 3 quail cadavers. 38 data trials. 7 calibration trials, one of them empty. 151 files listed (the overview says 157): 76 cine at 1760x1760, 10 fps, about 119 GB; 60 calibration TIFs; 12 misc; 3 CT zips of 183.6, 325.5 and 325.2 MB. Total about 120 GB. The paper reports 20,627 measured poses, not released.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same specimen, but scanned after disarticulation and covering only the pelvis and femora. DICOM (renamed .slice), Animage FIDEX, 0.173 mm isotropic, 480x480, 90 kV. QROM03 has 1,771 slices in 3 stacks.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. Real biplanar pulsed X-ray video: Varian G-1086 tubes, Phantom v10 cameras, 75-85 kV, 200 mA, 10 fps, stored as uncompressed .cine.

Yes, confirmed. These are real biplanar fluoroscopic acquisitions, not DRRs or simulations. Paper (PMC5998106): two Imaging Systems and Service units with Varian G-1086 tubes, Phantom v.10 cameras, 1760 x 1760, 10 fps, 1/1000 s shutter. File metadata for QROM01cam1RUN01.cine (fileID 77967) gives FrameRate=10, ShutterSpeed=1000, kV=85, mA=200, SID=124, MagLevel=3, pulsed, Pulsewidth=2. I parsed the header of a downloaded range of that file: Phantom 'CI' cine, 1760x1760, 8-bit, ImageCount 600.
verdicts.paired_ct: The CT is of the same subject, but only partly matches what the fluoroscopy shows. The 3D Vol tab lists three zips of DICOM slices, one per individual: QROM01_dis.zip (183.6 MB), QROM02 dis.zip (325.5 MB) and QROM03 dis.zip (325.2 MB). Each file's metadata reads 'CT image stack for the disarticulated pelvis and femora of individual QROMxx'. Paper: 'Following video data collection, specimens were disarticulated and computed-tomography scans (90 kV, 0.1 mA, 0.173 mm slice thickness, 480 x 480; FIDEX CT, Animage) were taken of the pelves and femora.' A decoded slice header confirms Modality CT, Manufacturer ANIMAGE, StationName FIDEX, KVP 90, 0.173074 mm isotropic, 480x480, StudyDate 20171017 (after the 2017-10-08 X-ray session for QROM02), with about 800 slices per zip. So the CT was taken after the X-ray, of disarticulated bones, and does not include the vertebral column. FIDEX is a veterinary cone-beam scanner; that comes from my own knowledge, not from the source.
verdicts.anatomy: Bird (Coturnix coturnix) pelvis, hip and femora. The paper says the specimens were 'dissected to isolate the vertebral column, pelvis and femora' with all muscles removed, so the vertebral column was still attached during the X-ray trials. No source says whether it falls inside the X-ray field of view; the trials are framed on the hip. There is no mammalian lumbar spine or separate sacrum; birds have a synsacrum. The CT covers only the pelves and femora.
verdicts.counts: 3 cadaveric individuals (QROM01-03), 1 species. 38 data trials (8, 11 and 19 per individual), each with 2 cine files (cam1 and cam2), so 76 cine files totalling about 119 GB. A 60 s trial has 600 frames per camera; from file sizes, roughly 41,000 single-camera frames, or about 20,600 biplanar pairs. The paper reports 20,627 measured hip poses. There are 7 calibration trials, but trial 45 is an 'empty trial' with no files, so 6 carry files. Each of those 6 has 12 files: 2 grid TIFs, 8 LegoCube TIFs and 2 framespec/ref files, 72 in all. With the 3 CT zips, the full public listing shows 151 files. The overview page says 157; I could not find the other 6.
verdicts.access_now: Open, no login. Byte-range requests to downloadfileXsendfile return HTTP 206 anonymously for a CT zip (fileID 78480, 341,334,436 bytes) and for a cine (fileID 77966, 1,858,591,820 bytes). The legacy xmaportal.org site is read-only and points to xma.xromm.brown.edu. I could not find the study on the new portal without its JavaScript search.
verdicts.licence: None stated for the data. No licence or terms text appears on the study overview, the trials page or the portal documentation. The article itself (PMC5998106) is '(c) 2018 The Author(s) Published by the Royal Society. All rights reserved.' The ethics statement says the animals were obtained as cadavers and no IACUC policy applies.
corrections: kV: the paper gives 75-85 kV, not a fixed 85 kV. Per-file metadata for QROM01RUN01 does say 85 kV, 200 mA, 10 fps, SID 124, but other trials may differ.
File count: the public listing shows 151 files (76 cine, 72 calibration, 3 CT), not 157. The 157 on the overview page could not be matched to a listing.

Calibration: 7 calibration trials are listed, but one (trial 45, 'empty trial') has no files, so only 6 are usable. Trials 11, 23, 24 and 44 use a modified 'invertedCube' framespec CSV, not the v1 framespec.

Pose: the claim that ROM poses are published is refuted as released data. The Processed Files tab shows 0 of 0 files: no XMALab marker tracks, rigid-body transforms or Maya animations are released. The paper reports 20,627 measured hip poses, but only as figures and ROM maps. I did not check whether the Royal Society supplementary material has pose tables.

Markers: the paper says three 0.8 mm zirconium oxide beads per bone were press-fitted into the ilia and femora. Poses could therefore be re-derived in XMALab from the released calibrations and videos. No labels or segmentations are provided.

CT: it is of the same subject but not the same state. It was scanned after the X-ray trials, of disarticulated pelves and femora only (vertebral column excluded), on an Animage FIDEX at 90 kV, 0.173 mm isotropic, 480x480.

Anatomy: the X-ray specimens kept the vertebral column (paper: 'dissected to isolate the vertebral column, pelvis and femora'). No source says whether it is in the X-ray field of view, and the CT does not include it. There is no human-like lumbar spine or sacrum; this is an avian synsacrum and pelvis.

Dates: the study was created on the portal 2017-09-18, X-ray sessions ran 2017-09-18, 2017-10-08 and 2017-10-14, and the paper was published in 2018 (Proc R Soc B 285:20180727, PMID 29794053, PMC5998106).
Licence: no data licence was found anywhere, and the article is 'All rights reserved'. Reuse terms are unknown, not open.

candidate.name: XMAPortal BROWN63: Boa constrictor data for Capano et al. 2022 (rib kinematics)
candidate.why_relevant: Calibrated biplanar X-ray of a rib cage, with 4.9 GB .cine files per camera and Maya scenes. In the public collection the CT of the same animals is available only as cleaned OBJ meshes. The micro-CT volumes are in the non-public part of the study, so obtaining them means asking the PI. The animal is non-mammalian (snake).
candidate.institution: Brown University (Capano, Brainerd)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM (Keck facility)
candidate.anatomy: Ribs and vertebrae
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibration per session; marker-based XROMM Maya scenes

corrections: Existence and open access are confirmed. I downloaded bc02_clean_objs.zip (7,400,095 bytes) with no login and got HTTP 200 with an attachment header. A range request on 20Dec16_Bc01_trial03_cam01.cine returned 206, with a total size of 5,275,284,328 bytes. The header reads Vision Research CINE, grayscale, 1760x1760, 1703 frames.
'4.9 GB .cine files per camera' is true of trial03 only. The 40 .cine files (20 data trials x 2 cameras) range from 3.1 to 6.6 GB, and their listed sizes add up to about 186 GB.
'Maya scenes' (plural) is wrong. The public collection holds exactly one Maya file, 122017_trial03_flat.mb (23.7 MB, belonging to trial 26).

The pose labels are not released. The collection's Processed Files tab is empty: no XMALab marker 2-D/3-D tracks and no rigid-body transforms. This is despite the paper saying it generated both in XMALab. Only calibration material is public: 122 calibration TIFFs (a Lego-cube object plus a grid for each camera) and 11 frame-spec .csv / 11 .ref files. Getting bone poses would mean re-tracking the implanted markers yourself.

'Micro-CT volumes' is not what the paper says. It describes 'a Fidex Animage veterinary scanner at Brown University (110 kV, variable mA, 0.173 mm slice thickness)'. This is a veterinary flat-panel CT; my note that it is generally described as cone-beam is from memory and was not checked in the primary source. The study also lists 'FHL microCT scan' files, but those are for pBC03/pBC04, which appear to be preserved specimens and not the three XROMM animals.

The raw CT is not downloadable, which confirms the candidate's caveat. The study-level 3D Vol listing shows 60 files, among them bc01/bc02/bc03 anterior/posterior CT zips of about 118 to 190 MB each. Their metadata page says 'Only file metadata is available.' The public collection's 3D Vol tab has only bc01/02/03_clean_objs.zip (19.7, 7.1 and 9.8 MB). Inside the bc02 zip are 11 OBJ meshes of the anterior/posterior vertebrae and ribs.

The paper's data availability statement says the raw 'X-ray video data and CT scan data' are available at this exact URL (Brown63). For the CT that promise is only partly kept: what was released is meshes, not volumes.

The collection contains 31 trials (11 calibration, 20 data) and 189 files from 3 individuals: bc01, bc02_aka_37_6 and bc03_aka_37_11. The whole study is larger (152 data trials, 30 calibration trials, 5 individuals, 797 files), but the rest is non-public and listed as metadata only.

Access is at risk. The legacy xmaportal.org site shows a banner saying it is in 'legacy read-only mode', new work belongs on xma.xromm.brown.edu, and it will stay read-only 'for a few months'. I did not check whether the new portal, a JavaScript single-page app, carries this collection, so the listed URL may stop working.

I could not verify 'Keck facility' as the device from the main text of the paper; it may be in the supplement. There is no DOI; the only identifier is the permanent XMAPortal ID Brown63, collection 6.

The anatomy is a snake's trunk: vertebrae and ribs over the vascular lung (about 35% of snout-vent length, SVL) and the saccular lung (about 50% SVL), with implanted radio-opaque markers. There is no lumbar region, no sacrum and no pelvis, so this is not mammalian spine anatomy.
verdicts.access_now: Open now with no login, through the legacy XMAPortal (xmaportal.org/webportal). The download endpoint larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N works anonymously once you have a session cookie from the collection page, and it supports byte-range requests. Only the 189 public-collection files can be downloaded. The raw CT volumes and the other ~130 data trials are metadata only, so getting them means asking the PI (Brainerd). The legacy site is read-only and being migrated to xma.xromm.brown.edu, and I did not check whether the new portal serves this collection.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 4.0. The collection page says: 'This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.' Only the public collection is covered by this.
verdicts.counts: 31 trials (11 calibration, 20 data), 189 files, 3 boas. By type: 40 .cine (about 186 GB total, 3.1 to 6.6 GB each; one checked file has 1703 frames at 1760x1760), 122 calibration .tif (about 3 MB each), 11 .csv, 11 .ref, 1 Maya .mb (23.7 MB), 1 LabChart .adicht (105.5 KB), and 3 OBJ-mesh zips (36.6 MB). The whole study, mostly non-public, has 152 data trials, 30 calibration trials, 5 individuals and 797 files, plus 60 files in 3D Vol.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real biplanar X-ray videos of living boas, recorded in Dec 2016, May 2017 and May 2018. The .cine header I retrieved is a real Vision Research recording: grayscale, 1760x1760, 1703 frames.
verdicts.paired_ct: The CT is of the same animals (bc01/02/03), but only as cleaned OBJ surface meshes of the vertebrae and ribs. The raw CT volumes (Fidex Animage veterinary CT, 0.173 mm slices, per the paper) are listed in the study but marked 'Only file metadata is available'. No DICOM or NIfTI volume is public, even though the paper's data availability statement says the CT scan data are available.
verdicts.anatomy: A snake's trunk: vertebrae and ribs at the vascular lung (about 35% SVL) and the saccular lung (about 50% SVL), with at least three radio-opaque markers implanted in each tracked bone. Non-mammalian: no lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed real, in vivo biplanar X-ray video (not DRR, not simulated, not MV portal). The 40 XMovie files are Phantom .cine; I range-fetched the header and a mid-trial frame of 20Dec16_Bc01_trial03_cam01.cine (5,275,284,328 bytes): CINE v1, 1703 frames, 1760x1760, 8-bit, 3,097,600 B/frame. The rendered frame shows a circular image-intensifier field with a snake trunk, vertebral column, ribs and implanted radio-opaque bead markers — an image-intensifier fluoroscopic frame, not a render. Capano et al. 2022 (Methods) describe marker-based XROMM from biplanar X-ray video analysed in XMALab. NOT VERIFIED from any primary source: the candidate's "Keck facility" attribution and the biplanar kV/mA/frame-rate settings — the paper's main text gives no X-ray tube or frame-rate parameters (FrameRate16 field in the cine header reads 60, which I do not trust as the true acquisition rate); acquisition details are only in the unchecked supplement.
verdicts.paired_ct: No CT/CBCT volume is in the public collection. The collection's 3D Vol tab holds exactly three files: bc01/bc02/bc03_clean_objs.zip (19.7/7.1/9.8 MB). I downloaded bc02_clean_objs.zip without logging in: 24 entries, all .obj surface meshes (aVert01, aVert02, pVert01, pVert02, aRib01L, aRib02L/R, pRib01L, pRib02L/R), i.e. two vertebrae + associated ribs in each of the anterior and posterior marked regions. Capano et al. 2022 state the meshes were segmented in Horos from CT collected on a Fidex Animage veterinary scanner at Brown (110 kV, variable mA, 0.173 mm slice) — so mesh geometry is CT-derived for the same animals, but the volume itself is withheld. The paper's Data Availability sentence ("X-ray video data and CT scan data are available ... under permanent ID Brown63" with this exact collection URL) is contradicted by what the collection actually serves. The study-level (non-public, metadata-only) 3D Vol list has 60 zips including many bc01/bc02/bc03 scans (77-283 MB each: postOp, anterior/posterior, rangeofmotion, BC01_Saccular_CT) whose contents are not stated anywhere — obtaining them means asking the PI. The two entries explicitly annotated "FHL microCT scan" belong to pBC03/pBC04, which are NOT the three XROMM animals, so the candidate's "the micro-CT volumes are in the non-public part" is wrong on both counts: same-subject scans were a veterinary CT, not micro-CT, and the micro-CT rows are other specimens.
verdicts.anatomy: Snake trunk only: precloacal vertebrae and their ribs, at roughly 35% SVL (vascular lung region) and 50% SVL (saccular lung region) per Capano et al. 2022. No lumbar spine, no sacrum, no pelvis, no femur — Serpentes have no sacrum or lumbar region, and boa pelvic vestiges sit near the cloaca, far outside these trunk fields. Mesh filenames (aVert/pVert, aRib/pRib 01-02) and the rendered frame both confirm rib cage + vertebral column only. Zero transfer value for a lumbosacral/level-identification project on human anatomy; the only conceivable use is a marker-based-XROMM calibration exemplar.
verdicts.counts: Confirmed exactly: 31 trials (20 Data + 11 Calib) and 189 files in the public collection; 3 individuals (bc01, bc02_aka_37_6, bc03_aka_37_11 = boa01 11.6 kg, boa02 3.4 kg, boa03 6.1 kg in the paper, all adult females). File breakdown I tallied from all four pages of the All Files tab: 40 XMovie .cine (2 cameras x 20 data trials, ~186 GiB total, 3.1-6.6 GiB each), 100 XCalibObject + 22 XCalibGrid TIFFs, 23 MISC (9 distinct calibration framespec/.ref files reused across sessions + 1 Maya .mb), 1 AuxData (.adicht LabChart, 105.5 KB), 3 3DVOL mesh zips. "n_images" is frames, not files: the one cine I parsed has 1703 frames; at ~3.1 MB/frame the 186 GiB implies roughly 6e4 frames total (~3e4 biplanar pairs), an estimate, not a stated figure. The parent study is larger than the collection (5 individuals, 152 data trials, 797 files) but the rest is marked Public=No.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: Overstated. Per-session calibration IMAGES exist (lego-cube and grid TIFFs for 11 calib trials, plus framespec .csv and .ref geometry files), but no solved calibration (no camera matrices/distortion files), no XMALab marker tracks, and no rigid-body transform CSVs. The Processed Files tab of the collection is EMPTY. There is exactly ONE Maya scene in the whole collection — 122017_trial03_flat.mb (23.7 MB), attached to trial 26 only — so "marker-based XROMM Maya scenes" (plural, implying per-trial animations) is refuted; 19 of 20 data trials ship raw video with no animation. No anatomical labels, no segmentations, no landmark annotations of any kind; the only per-frame ground truth is the implanted beads visible in the images.
verdicts.licence: Confirmed CC BY 4.0: the collection page states "This public data collection is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" linking creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, with an attribution-best-practices link. Authors listed as Brainerd, B. and Capano, J.; created 2019-10-04, last modified 2022-03-10. Note the licence covers the public collection only; the 60 study-level 3DVOL scans are not public and carry no stated terms.
verdicts.access_now: Open and working as of 2026-09-22 with no login: I downloaded bc02_clean_objs.zip (7,400,095 B) and byte-ranged into a 4.9 GiB .cine over plain HTTPS. Mechanics: the download endpoint is larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=NNN and it depends on PHP session state — you must first GET a collection/trial page with StudyID=63&instit=BROWN in the same cookie jar or the server returns the 48-byte string "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty." The server honours HTTP Range (206), so single frames can be pulled without the full 186 GiB. Caveat: the site banner says it is "in a legacy read-only mode" and that new work belongs on xma.xromm.brown.edu; a migration notice with a 2026-06-29 read-only date says the legacy site stays up "for the next few months", so this access route is time-limited and the files should be mirrored now if wanted.
corrections: Species/anatomy make it useless for the stated lens: this is a Boa constrictor trunk (precloacal vertebrae + ribs at ~35% and ~50% SVL). Lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are absent and cannot be present — snakes have no sacrum.

'The micro-CT volumes are in the non-public part of the study' is wrong as stated. The same-subject scans were a Fidex Animage VETERINARY CT (110 kV, 0.173 mm slice, Capano et al. 2022 Methods); the only rows annotated 'FHL microCT scan' in the non-public study-level 3D Vol list are pBC03/pBC04, which are not the three XROMM animals.

ct_or_cbct_same_subject=true is only half true. The public collection serves NO volumetric CT — just three zips of cleaned .obj surface meshes. The meshes are CT-derived for the same animals (paper: segmented in Horos from the Fidex scans), so same-subject CT geometry exists, but the volume requires a request to the PI.

The paper's Data Availability claim is contradicted by the portal: it says 'X-ray video data and CT scan data are available' at this exact collection URL, and the collection contains no CT scan data. Treat the paper's statement as unreliable, not as evidence that CT is downloadable.

'Marker-based XROMM Maya scenes' (plural) is refuted: exactly one .mb file exists in the collection (122017_trial03_flat.mb, trial 26). The Processed Files tab is empty — no XMALab marker tracks, no rigid-body transforms, no solved camera calibrations. Only raw calibration images (cube/grid TIFFs + framespec/.ref) are present.

'pose_or_labels: Calibration per session' overstates what ships: calibration OBJECT IMAGES per session, not calibration solutions. No pose file of any kind is downloadable; pose must be re-derived by tracking the implanted beads in XMALab.

'Biplanar videofluoroscopy' at the 'Keck facility' — biplanar X-ray video is confirmed by the paper and by the two per-trial cam1/cam2 .cine files, but I found no primary source naming the Keck facility; the paper's Methods and Acknowledgements do not mention it. Device/beam parameters (kV, mA, frame rate) are not stated in the main text either.

'31 trials, 189 files' is correct but 11 of the 31 trials are calibration, not data; only 20 trials carry X-ray video (40 .cine, ~186 GiB). n_images in the sense of frames is unstated; I measured 1703 frames at 1760x1760 8-bit in one cine and estimate ~6e4 frames overall — an inference, not a published number.

Access is currently open but expiring: xmaportal.org is in announced legacy read-only mode migrating to xma.xromm.brown.edu, and the download endpoint needs a session cookie seeded by a StudyID=63&instit=BROWN page request. Any pipeline keyed to these URLs will break.

candidate.name: XMAPortal ULIVERPOOL1 and ULIVERPOOL2: rainbow trout and frogfish vertebral kinematics (Camp 2021)
candidate.why_relevant: Open biplanar X-ray of a vertebral column, CT of the same fish after marker implantation, STL models of each vertebra, and grid plus Lego-cube calibrations in air and in water. The fish are small, so the value is for checking pose-recovery methods, not anatomy.
candidate.institution: University of Liverpool (Ariel Camp)
candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; 50 kV, 100 mA, SID 117 cm
candidate.anatomy: Vertebral column, neurocranium
candidate.subjects: Living fish: 3 trout; 6 frogfish in the companion study
candidate.n_images: Trout: 62 data trials plus 15 calibration trials; frogfish: 123 plus 33
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibration grids and cube; vertebra meshes

verdicts.access_now: Downloadable NOW, anonymously, no login, from the legacy portal — but on a deadline. I pulled bytes with plain curl: `downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=337` served 20189021_strike04_cam1.cine (1,260,420,488 B, CINE header reads 1024x1024 grayscale, 601 frames) and fileID=1387 served 20190430_strike02_cam1.cine (8,382,470,936 B, 3997 frames); fileID=2063 served Trout OM2_CTscans_20190121.zip (313,138,771 B, 1088 DICOM). Range requests work, so partial pulls are cheap. Session quirk: larequest.php stores StudyID in the PHP session, so you must hit CollectionView -> Collection_exploreTrial -> Collection_exploreFile with a cookie jar before the download URL, otherwise it returns the string "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty." Every cine also has a pre-converted "<name>.cine-JPG.zip" (e.g. 484 MB for the 7.8 GB frogfish cine), so frames can be had without a CINE reader. Totals of the file tables: trout collection 73 files ~39.4 GB (36 XMovie = 38.3 GB, 7 3DVOL = 1.03 GB, 25 calibration tifs, 5 MISC); frogfish 99 files ~259.2 GB (38 XMovie = 258.2 GB, 25 3DVOL = 0.99 GB, 31 calibration tifs, 5 MISC). THE DEADLINE: xmaportal.org now carries a banner "This website is in a legacy read-only mode... New work should be completed on xma.xromm.brown.edu", with a commented-out earlier banner saying the site went read-only 2026-06-29 and stays "available as read-only for the next few months". Both datasets have already migrated (xma.xromm.brown.edu/datasets/76a541a7-1f9b-55be-8dae-8eeda6504557 trout, /datasets/f8fba055-f1fc-548b-aa72-46ff2ab79f60 frogfish, both public pages), but on the new portal every file tab says "Sign in to an XMAPortal account to view and download data", and /signup says "XMA Portal is not currently allowing sign ups through the portal. Please email support to request an account: [e-mail withheld]" with an institution dropdown limited to member institutions (Wayne State is not on it). So the honest statement is: open today on the legacy host, on request (email Brown IT for an account) once it is retired. Mirror anything you want before that.
verdicts.anatomy: Fish vertebral column plus neurocranium, in vivo, during feeding strikes — not human, not a spine-radiograph analogue. Trout Oncorhynchus mykiss (62 vertebrae, small and near-identical centra, 776-998 g, 340-375 mm standard length); frogfish Antennarius commerson (large, morphologically varied vertebrae, 368-577 g, 192-230 mm). Meshes are per-vertebra: trout OM1 neurocranium + V1-V24 (26 STL), OM2 + V1-V27 (29), OM3 + V1-V25 (27); frogfish AC1 v1-v18 as loose STLs, AC2 24 STLs, AC4 20 STLs. Marker-based XROMM: 0.5-0.8 mm tantalum beads implanted in neurocranium and epaxial muscles, so the fluoroscopic frames contain implanted metal beads throughout. Value for this project is pose-recovery / biplanar-calibration method checking, as the candidate says — not level naming, and not anatomy transferable to human spine.
verdicts.counts: The candidate's counts are the STUDY-level totals, not what is released. explorePublicMetadataStudy shows study ULIVERPOOL1 holding 76 trials (62 Data + 14 Calib listed; the study overview banner says 62 data / 15 calibration / 3 individuals / 418 files) and ULIVERPOOL2 holding 155 trials (123 Data + 32 Calib; overview says 123 / 33 / 6 individuals / 977 files). The PUBLIC collections are a subset: trout collectionID=1 has 24 trials (18 Data + 6 Calib) and 73 files; frogfish collectionID=2 has 23 trials (19 Data + 4 Calib) and 99 files. Movie counts corroborate: 36 trout cines = 18 data trials x 2 cameras, 38 frogfish cines = 19 x 2. Individuals in the public collections: OM1, OM2, OM3 and AC1, AC2, AC4 — three each, matching the paper. Frame counts are large but only strike windows are usable: sampled cines carry 601 (trout, 500 fps) and 3997 (frogfish, 1000 fps) frames at 1024x1024; the paper analysed 20 of 30 trout strikes and all 18 frogfish strikes.
verdicts.licence: No CC licence, as the candidate says — confirmed verbatim on both collection pages: "Terms of use: Derivative work should attribute this data collection and the publication Camp, 2021. Contact Ariel Camp ([e-mail withheld]) for potential collaborations and help using the dataset." Note the paper itself is CC BY (Europe PMC license field) but that covers the article, not the deposit; do not inherit it. There is no dataset DOI — the cited identifiers are the portal handles ULIVERPOOL1 and ULIVERPOOL2; doi:10.1098/rspb.2021.1091 is the paper. No redistribution permission is stated, so a rehosted copy is not covered by anything written down.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same-subject CT exists and is downloadable, but it is post-mortem microCT, not clinical CT, and one of the six subjects is an empty file. The paper's methods: fish were euthanised and frozen before CT on a PerkinElmer Quantum GX microCT, 512x512, 0.172 mm slice thickness; scans are post-marker-implantation, so the tantalum beads are in the volume. Trout OM2 and OM3 ship 4 individual scans each as DICOM (1088 slices, ~300 MB per fish) plus a stitched TIFF stack for OM2 (972 slices, valid TIFF, II*\0). Frogfish AC1 (958), AC2 (820) and AC4 (1202) ship valid stitched TIFF stacks. DEFECT I verified by downloading it: OM1's only CT file, Stitiched_Trout972Tiff.zip (1.4 MB compressed, 513 MB uncompressed, 972 members), contains 972 files that are entirely zero bytes — no TIFF magic, zero non-zero bytes in any of the 972 members. That is why it compresses 345x. So OM1 has meshes but no usable CT. Second defect, the kind this project keeps getting burned by: in OM1's mesh zip, files OM1_V7.stl through OM1_V24.stl carry embedded 80-byte STL headers one greater than their filename ($v8b in OM1_V7.stl ... $v25b in OM1_V24.stl), while V1-V6 match; OM2 and OM3 are self-consistent. OM1's vertebra numbering is therefore ambiguous by one from V7 caudally, and either the filename or the header is wrong. Also empty: frogfish AC1_CT markers.stl and AC1_neurocranium.stl are both 84 bytes, i.e. a binary STL header with a triangle count of 0.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes — real biplanar high-speed X-ray video (not DRR, not simulation), two Phantom M120 cameras behind two Imaging Systems and Service X-ray machines, fish feeding in a 10x36x41 cm tank corridor. But the technique numbers in the candidate are wrong/mixed. Per-file portal metadata (downloadfileMDtxt, and the file page labels the field "SID (cm)") across the two collections: trout data trials kV 60/80/85/90, mA 200 uniformly, SID 117 on 49 files and 107 on 12, FrameRate 500, ShutterSpeed 1000, continuous radiation, MagLevel 0; frogfish kV 70/80/85, mA 200 or 250, SID 110 on all 69 flagged files, FrameRate 1000, ShutterSpeed 800. "50 kV, 100 mA" appears only as free-text comments on the trout CALIBRATION grid and Lego-cube images, never on a data trial. The paper states 500 fps 1/1000 shutter (trout) and 1000 fps 1/4000 (frogfish); the frogfish ShutterSpeed field reads 800, which does not agree with the paper's 1/4000 — unexplained, I did not resolve it. The paper gives no kV, mA or SID at all.
corrections: SUBJECT COUNT WRONG: the candidate says '6 frogfish in the companion study'. The paper used THREE adult Commerson's frogfish — AC1 368 g/192 mm, AC2 429 g/205 mm, AC4 577 g/230 mm — and the public frogfish collection contains exactly those three. The '6 Individuals' figure is the private study-level banner on studyOverview_public&StudyID=2, which counts fish that were never released.

NOT A COMPANION STUDY: trout and frogfish are both in the SAME paper (Camp 2021, Proc R Soc B 288:20211091, 'A neck-like vertebral motion in fish'); ULIVERPOOL1 and ULIVERPOOL2 are two deposits for one article. The companion paper is a different one — Jimenez & Camp 2023, J Exp Biol 226, doi:10.1242/jeb.245788, which is listed only on the TROUT collection.

TRIAL COUNTS ARE STUDY-LEVEL, NOT RELEASED: '62 data trials plus 15 calibration' and '123 plus 33' are the private study totals. Downloadable: trout 18 data + 6 calibration trials (24 trials, 73 files, ~39.4 GB); frogfish 19 data + 4 calibration trials (23 trials, 99 files, ~259.2 GB). About two thirds of the trout trials and five sixths of the frogfish trials are not public.

TECHNIQUE STRING WRONG: '50 kV, 100 mA, SID 117 cm' mixes two things. 50 kV / 100 mA is written only on trout calibration images; data trials read kV 60-90, mA 200 (trout) and kV 70-85, mA 200-250 (frogfish). SID is 117 cm on most trout files but 107 cm on 12 of them, and 110 cm — not 117 — for every frogfish file. The paper itself states none of these numbers; they exist only in the portal's per-file metadata.

ONE CT IS AN EMPTY FILE: trout OM1's sole CT archive (Stitiched_Trout972Tiff.zip) unpacks to 972 TIFFs that are 100% zero bytes. Downloaded and checked all 972 — not a header problem, no data at all. So 'CT of the same fish after marker implantation' holds for OM2, OM3, AC1, AC2, AC4 but NOT for OM1. Two frogfish STLs (AC1_CT markers.stl, AC1_neurocranium.stl) are likewise 84-byte empty binary STLs.

MESH LABEL AMBIGUITY IN OM1: OM1_V7.stl through OM1_V24.stl have embedded STL headers reading v8b through v25b — off by one against their filenames, while V1-V6 agree and OM2/OM3 are clean. Anyone using these meshes as per-level ground truth inherits an unresolved one-level offset in that fish.

NO PROCESSED KINEMATICS ARE RELEASED: the 'Processed Files' tab is empty for both collections (zero file rows). The per-individual metadata xlsx names XMALab projects, xyzpts files, CT-locator files and rigid-body transform files — one entry literally reads 'MISSING' — but none of those are in the deposit. What you get is raw video, calibration images, CT and meshes; marker tracks, camera calibrations and the rigid-body transforms behind the published angles are not there. The candidate's 'pose_or_labels: calibration grids and cube; vertebra meshes' is accurate as far as it goes, but there is no pose ground truth to score against.

THE PAPER'S FROGFISH LINK IS DEAD: the data availability statement prints https://xmaportal.org/webportallarequest.php?... (missing the slash before larequest.php) — 404. The trout link resolves. The working frogfish URL is https://xmaportal.org/webportal/larequest.php?request=CollectionView&StudyID=2&instit=ULIVERPOOL&collectionID=2 .

ACCESS IS TIME-LIMITED: open anonymous download is a property of the LEGACY host, which is in read-only mode and being retired (banner names xma.xromm.brown.edu as the successor; an earlier banner in the page source dates the read-only switch to 2026-06-29 and gives the legacy site 'a few months'). Both datasets are already on the new portal but every file view there demands sign-in, and self-service sign-up is disabled — accounts must be requested from [e-mail withheld], with an institution list that does not include Wayne State. Treat 'open' as 'open until the legacy host goes away'.

COULD NOT VERIFY: whether the new portal holds a good copy of OM1's CT (file listings there are behind the login), and whether the frogfish ShutterSpeed=800 metadata or the paper's stated 1/4000 s is correct. I did not check the 26 files I sampled against every remaining file — the empty-archive check covered OM1's CT fully, the STL header check covered OM1 and OM2 fully, OM3 was not checked.

verdicts.real_xray: Real. Biplanar high-speed X-ray video of live, unanaesthetised fish feeding — not DRR, not simulated, not MV portal. Paper methods (PMC8385379): "X-ray machines (Imaging Systems and Service) generated images, which were recorded by two Phantom cameras (M120, Vision Research) at 1024 x 1024 resolution, 500 fps and 1/1000 shutter speed (trout) or 1000 fps and 1/4000 shutter speed (frogfish)". I downloaded the first bytes of 20189021_strike01_cam1.cine (fileID 293) anonymously: Content-Length 2,027,991,296 and the Vision Research CINE magic "CI," — genuine raw camera files, two per data trial (cam1/cam2). Calibration frames are real 1 MB TIFFs of a perforated grid and of a Lego cube in air and in water. Exposure: trout calibration files are annotated "kV = 50, mA = 100"; frogfish files are annotated 70-85 kV and 200-250 mA.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, with one serious defect. Each fish was euthanised and frozen after filming and scanned on a Quantum GX microCT (PerkinElmer, Liverpool Centre for Preclinical Imaging), 512x512, 0.172 mm slices; the per-individual metadata workbooks give "Voxel Size = 172 microns, FOV = 86, kV = 90, mA = 88". The CT is post-marker-implantation, so the tantalum beads seen in the X-ray videos are also in the CT. Verified real content by parsing the zip central directories after anonymous ranged downloads: Trout OM2_CTscan_20190121_stitched.zip = 1683 entries, 444.6 MB uncompressed, ~290 KB compressed per 528,166-byte slice; AC1_CTsitched_WTNorm_Tiffs.zip = 1920 entries, 383.3 MB uncompressed, ~285 KB per 399,610-byte slice. OM2 and OM3 also have "4 individual scans, post-marker implantation" (294-299 MB each). BUT trout OM1 has no per-scan CT at all, only Stitiched_Trout972Tiff.zip (1,490,824 bytes), and I downloaded and opened it: all 972 TIFFs are byte-identical zero fills (528,166 B uncompressed, 529 B compressed each, first four bytes 00 00 00 00, zero non-zero bytes anywhere). OM1's CT deposit is empty, and OM1 is the individual carrying 8 of the 18 public trout trials. OM1's bone-model STLs (52 MB) are present and intact.
verdicts.anatomy: Fish. Neurocranium plus the cranial part of the vertebral column; per-vertebra STL meshes are "Neurocranium and vertebrae 1-24" (OM1), "1-27" (OM2), "1-25" (OM3), and 18 numbered vertebra STLs for frogfish AC1. No lumbar spine, no sacrum, no pelvis or hip — those structures do not exist in teleosts, and nothing in the deposit shows a pelvic girdle. CT FOV is 86 mm per scan with four scans stitched, i.e. roughly the head and cranial third of a 345-375 mm trout; frogfish (192-230 mm standard length) are covered more completely. Human-relevant anatomy: none.
verdicts.counts: Public collections, counted off the portal pages: trout ULIVERPOOL StudyID=1 collectionID=1 = 18 data trials + 6 calibration trials, 73 files, 3 individuals (OM1 8 trials, OM2 6, OM3 4). Frogfish StudyID=2 collectionID=2 = 19 data trials + 4 calibration trials, 99 files, 3 individuals (AC1 9 trials, AC2 5, AC4 5). The "62 data + 15 calibration / 3 individuals" and "123 data + 33 calibration / 6 individuals" figures are STUDY totals on the overview pages; the private-metadata listing for study 1 shows all 77 trials flagged Public = No, and only the collection subset is served. The paper used 3 trout and 3 frogfish (OM1/OM2/OM3, AC1/AC2/AC4), and analysed 18 frogfish strikes and 20 of 30 trout strikes. No image or frame count is published anywhere; each trial is two multi-thousand-frame .cine movies (0.4-2.1 GB per camera per trial), so "n_images" as trials is a category error.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: No pose, no labels. Both collections' "Processed Files" tabs are empty, and neither All-Files list contains an .xma project, an xyzpts CSV, a camera-calibration file or a rigid-body transform. What ships is: raw .cine videos, undistortion grids, Lego-cube calibration images, one framespec CSV and one refpoints .ref, per-individual metadata .xlsx, CT stacks, and STL meshes of neurocranium, markers and individual vertebrae. The metadata workbooks name the missing artefacts explicitly as row labels — "XMALab Project", "Calibration (XMA file)", "xyzpts File", "CT locators File", "Rigid Body Tform File", "Animated Scene" — with values such as 20190409_strike03_xyzpts100Hz_ref.csv and AC1_ctlocators_nc1234, none of which are deposited. The figshare supplement (10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5565693) holds only two movies and three figures, no kinematics. So a user must redo undistortion and 3D calibration in XMALab from the grid/cube images and re-track from scratch; there is no ground-truth 6-DoF pose to score a pose-recovery method against.
verdicts.licence: No CC licence, as the candidate says. Terms of use on both collection pages: "Derivative work should attribute this data collection and the publication Camp, 2021. Contact Ariel Camp ([e-mail withheld]) for potential collaborations and help using the dataset." The paper itself is CC BY (Europe PMC licence field "cc by"), but that covers the article, not the deposit. There is no dataset DOI; doi:10.1098/rspb.2021.1091 is the article DOI. The only dataset identifiers are the portal's "permanent identifiers ULIVERPOOL1 (trout) and ULIVERPOOL2 (frogfish)".
verdicts.access_now: Open, no login, but on a site announced for retirement. I fetched every page and downloaded files anonymously over plain curl: Trout OM1 metadata.xlsx came back complete (45,701 B, valid xlsx), OM1 bone models zip 54,526,268 B, a .cine 2,027,991,296 B, and ranged reads work once a session cookie from a collection page is held (a bare download request without that cookie returns a 48-byte "Sorry, the StudyID and/or Institution is empty."). Download URL form: larequest.php?request=downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=NNNN. Every page now carries a banner: "This website is in a legacy read-only mode. New work should be completed on xma.xromm.brown.edu", with commented-out banner drafts saying the site transitioned to read-only on 2026-06-29 and will remain "for a few months". xma.xromm.brown.edu is live (HTTP 200). So the candidate's evidence URLs are working today but are not durable, and I could not confirm that these two collections have been migrated.
corrections: OM1 trout CT is an empty deposit: Stitiched_Trout972Tiff.zip (fileID 2069, 1,490,824 B) unpacks to 972 TIFFs that are every one of them entirely zero-filled (528,166 B uncompressed, 529 B compressed, identical, magic 00 00 00 00). No other OM1 CT file exists in the collection, so the trout individual with 8 of the 18 public trials has no usable CT. OM2/OM3/AC1/AC2/AC4 CT zips are real (verified by central-directory parse).

"6 frogfish in the companion study" is wrong for what is served: the paper used three Commerson's frogfish (AC1 368 g/192 mm, AC2 429 g/205 mm, AC4 577 g/230 mm) and the public collection contains only AC1, AC2, AC4. The "6 Individuals" figure is the private study-level count.

"62 data trials plus 15 calibration" (trout) and "123 plus 33" (frogfish) are study-level totals of mostly non-public trials. The public collections hold 18 data + 6 calibration (trout, 73 files) and 19 data + 4 calibration (frogfish, 99 files). The study-1 metadata listing marks all 77 trials Public = No.

"n_images" conflates trials with images. No frame or image count is stated in any primary source; each data trial is two .cine movies of 0.4-2.1 GB, and the metadata workbooks list only per-trial digitised ranges such as 1-300 or 75-200.

SID 117 cm is unsupported. I found no source-image distance in the collection pages, the trial pages, the per-individual metadata workbooks (searched: no 'SID', 'distance', 'source', 'magnif' strings) or the paper, which names only "X-ray machines (Imaging Systems and Service)" and Phantom M120 cameras. Treat the SID as unknown.

"50 kV, 100 mA" is trout-only, and comes from file comments on calibration images, not from a stated protocol. Frogfish calibration files are annotated 70 kV/200 mA, 80 kV/250 mA and 85 kV/250 mA at 1000 fps, 800 shutter. CT exposure is separate: 90 kV, 88 mA as written in the workbooks.

"pose_or_labels: Calibration grids and cube; vertebra meshes" understates the gap: there is no pose at all. Both Processed Files tabs are empty; no XMALab project, camera calibration, 2D point (xyzpts) or rigid-body transform file is deposited, although the metadata workbooks name each of them. The figshare ESM contains only figures and movies. Pose-recovery methods cannot be scored against this deposit without re-calibrating and re-tracking.

Anatomy claim needs the explicit negative: no lumbar spine, no sacrum, no pelvis, no hip. Fish; meshes cover neurocranium and vertebrae 1-24/1-27/1-25 (trout) and 18 vertebrae (frogfish AC1). Nothing here is human-like spinopelvic anatomy.

"doi_or_id: doi:10.1098/rspb.2021.1091" is the article DOI; there is no dataset DOI. The dataset identifiers are ULIVERPOOL1 and ULIVERPOOL2. Note also that the paper's own frogfish data link is typo'd ("xmaportal.org/webportallarequest.php", missing the slash) and does not resolve; the candidate's frogfish URL (StudyID=2&collectionID=2) is the working one.
"published: 2018-2021" is acquisition 2018-08-30 to 2019-07-10 (trout autumn 2018, frogfish spring-summer 2019), article 2021, collection last modified 2024-03-08 (trout) and 2026-06-22 (frogfish).

Link durability: xmaportal.org is in legacy read-only mode and directs new work to xma.xromm.brown.edu, with banner text stating the legacy site remains only "for the next few months". I could not confirm these two collections exist on the new portal.
A second publication reuses the same trout collection and is not mentioned in the candidate: Jimenez & Camp 2023, J Exp Biol 226(20), doi:10.1242/jeb.245788.

candidate.name: XMAPortal non-public trunk studies with same-individual CT (BROWN42 monitor lizard, BROWN29 tegu, BROWN10 alligator thorax, BROWN88 boa, BROWN45 turkey ventilation, BROWN46 mouse, BROWN27 rat)
candidate.why_relevant: The portal's metadata shows calibrated biplanar trunk X-rays and CT of the same animals in each of these studies, but the files are gated (metadata only). BROWN46 (whole-body mouse, with CT) and BROWN27 (rat, partly public) are the mammalian ones. The access route is the PI, mostly Brainerd ([e-mail withheld]).
