candidate.device: Biplanar XROMM; CT on a Fidex scanner
candidate.anatomy: Ribs, vertebrae, thorax; mouse whole body
candidate.pose_or_labels: Calibration trials per day; marker-based XROMM
candidate.doi_or_id: XMAPortal BROWN42, BROWN29, BROWN10, BROWN88, BROWN45, BROWN46, BROWN27

verdicts.access_now: NOT downloadable now, and there is no documented request route. All seven named studies browse as metadata only: opening any file record returns the portal's own text "Only metadata available for this study. File download not available." I verified this on BROWN42 (file 38295) and on BROWN27 trial 8, which is one of the trials flagged Public=Yes — so even the "Yes" rows in a "Partial" study do not yield files. The legacy portal's stated route to non-public data is registration ("Contact Kia Huffman to become a registered user") plus the PI/study leader granting study access; nowhere does the portal or xromm.org publish a policy under which an outside group may request a gated study, so "on request" is an inference, not a stated offer. Brainerd is genuinely the contact of record (new-portal dataset records give contactPerson [e-mail withheld]). Two further access facts: xmaportal.org is now in "legacy read-only mode" and is stated to remain available as read-only only "for the next few months", with new work at xma.xromm.brown.edu; that successor portal redirects /studies to sign-in and exposes only 49 public datasets, among which only BROWN:45 (the chicken-egg collection) and BROWN:63 appear from this candidate set — so the metadata browsing being relied on here may not survive the migration. One thing IS downloadable right now with no login: the BROWN63 public collection (see licence/corrections).
verdicts.anatomy: Verified per study from trial-level genus/species records. BROWN42 Varanus (Savannah monitor), "marker-based rib kinematics", breathing plus treadmill walking — trunk, correct. BROWN29 Tupinambis merianae, tegu lung ventilation — trunk, correct. BROWN10 Alligator mississippiensis, "marker-based and markerless XROMM of thorax, intercostal EMG and ventilation volumes" — thorax, correct. BROWN88 Boa constrictor, "fluoromicrometry of costocutaneous mm and XROMM skeletal kinematics" — trunk, correct. BROWN45 turkey rib kinematics (plus Gallus gallus eggs as a second species) — trunk, correct. BROWN27 is NOT trunk: it is "exploring forelimb posture and its relationship to pronation and supination in rats", markerless walking, and its 3D models are humerus/radius/ulna/skull/sternum. BROWN46 is a rodent behaviour assay (exploring, grooming, climbing out of a box) — whole-body framing is plausible but the portal never says "whole body", and the animals are rats, not mice.
verdicts.counts: Calib/data trials, individuals, total files, 3D-Vol entries, from each study's Overview and 3D Vol tabs: BROWN42 12/51, 3 individuals, 408 files, 8 3DVOL (CT zips 116.6-376.8 MB pre- and post-bead for Ve01 Willie, Ve02 Maja, Ve03 Flip, plus one OBJ set). BROWN29 17/91, 8 individuals, 632 files, 60 3DVOL (CT zips 79.5-422.9 MB; many are postmortem or excised-rib scans, plus per-bone OBJs). BROWN10 10/80, 7 individuals, 387 files, 22 3DVOL (CT zips 169 MB-3.5 GB incl. muscle-fibre reconstructions, plus scan-log PDFs). BROWN88 22/131, 5 individuals (bc01-bc04, bc08), 857 files, exactly 1 3DVOL (2022APR12_bc02_8cm_CTscan.zip, 258.6 MB). BROWN45 10/58, 4 individuals, 509 files, 11 3DVOL (Me18, Me23, Me49 turkeys plus an egg scan). BROWN46 4/34, 4 individuals, 215 files, 17 3DVOL (Fidex scans 345.7 MB-1.4 GB for Female1/2, Male1/2). BROWN27 11/51, 9 individuals, 197 files, 30 3DVOL (CT of Evan/Floyd/Pink/Rudy 170.7-189.5 MB plus STL/OBJ forelimb meshes). So "50-300 trials per study" and "3-8 individuals" are close: data trials run 34-152 and individuals 3-9. X-ray files are large: .cine 1.6-5.3 GB per camera per trial (BROWN10, BROWN29, BROWN46), .avi 220-297 MB (BROWN27, BROWN88).
verdicts.licence: No licence at all is stated for any of the seven gated studies — the records carry no terms-of-use text, and their Overview "Publications" sections are empty, so there is no paper data-availability statement attached on the portal either. A licence appears only on public data collections: the BROWN63 collection states "licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" with an attribution request. So "licence: Not public" is right for the seven, but the candidate misses that an adjacent boa collection is CC BY 4.0.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same-individual CT is real but uneven, and it is not always in-vivo. Individual names in the 3D Vol tab match the trial subjects for BROWN42 (3/3: Willie, Maja, Flip, scanned before and after bead implantation, "Fidex, 15 cm FOV"), BROWN45 (3/3 turkeys Me18, Me23, Me49), BROWN46 (4/4 rats), BROWN27 (4 of 9), BROWN10 (5 of 6 individuals appearing in trials; Ag2L5 has none), BROWN29 (Tu03-Tu07, Tegu01, Tegu02). BROWN88 is the weak one: five animals in the trials, one CT file, for bc02 only. Many of the scans are explicitly postmortem or of excised parts ("postMortem", "excisedRibs", "Dead scan from 5/23", "Left Thorax Stnd ... 8 cm of thorax only"), so a paired scan is often a cadaveric or partial-FOV scan of that animal, not a live whole-body CT. Scanner: Fidex is named in BROWN42/27/46 comments, but BROWN63's scans say "FHL microCT", so "CT on a Fidex scanner" is not uniform.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes — real X-ray, not renders. The trials are Phantom .cine or .avi X-ray movies from two cameras (cam1/cam2) with per-day calibration trials (cube and grid TIFFs plus a framespec .csv and .ref), and per-file kV/mA metadata (e.g. 87 kV, 320 mA; BROWN10 filenames carry "66kV_100mA"). One caveat: BROWN46's rat trials use four cameras (cam1-cam4), so "biplanar" is not accurate for that study. I confirmed the imaging is genuine by downloading the first 1024 bytes of a public .cine (magic "CI" Phantom header, Content-Range total 5,275,284,328 bytes).
corrections: REFUTED - BROWN46 is not a mouse study. Every CT-scanned individual in it (Female1, Female2, Male1, Male2) records Genus Rattus, Species norvegicus, weights 266-370 g. The four trials named 'mouse_mag*' (strain 'probably C57BL6') carry no individual, no species and no CT. So the claim 'BROWN46 (whole-body mouse, with CT)' and the 'mouse whole body' anatomy both fail; the mammalian CT-paired animals here are rats.

REFUTED as stated - 'access: on request' is not documented. The portal's file pages return 'Only metadata available for this study. File download not available.', and the only documented route to non-public data is becoming a registered user (contact Kia Huffman) with the PI/study leader granting access. Neither xmaportal.org nor xromm.org publishes any data-request policy for outside groups. Emailing Brainerd is a reasonable guess, and she is the contact of record, but the portal never offers it.

MISSED - the boa lung-ventilation study is BROWN63, not BROWN88, and it is partly OPEN, not gated. Its public collection 'Boa constrictor data for Capano et al., 2022' (31 trials, 189 files) is CC BY 4.0 and downloads with no login today: I pulled bc02_clean_objs.zip in full (7,400,095 bytes, cleaned rib and vertebra OBJs) and the first 1 KB of 20Dec16_Bc01_trial03_cam01.cine (5,275,284,328 bytes, HTTP 206). It contains raw biplanar .cine X-ray of snake trunk, calibration TIFFs and cube/grid specs, and per-bone meshes for bc01-bc03. Raw CT volumes are NOT in the public collection - only the derived OBJ meshes.

CORRECTION - BROWN88 gives same-individual CT for only one of five animals (a single 258.6 MB file for bc02, against trials on bc01-bc04 and bc08), so listing it as a same-individual-CT study overstates the pairing.

CORRECTION - BROWN45's public part is not the turkey data. Its one public collection is 'Chickens in Ovo' (3 trials, 33 files, Gallus gallus eggs), which is also the only BROWN:45 entry on the new portal. All turkey ventilation trials are Public=No.

CORRECTION - BROWN27 is a forelimb study ('forelimb posture and its relationship to pronation and supination in rats'), not a trunk study, and its 'partly public' status is empty in practice: 16 trials show Public=Yes, but opening one (trial 8, Floyd Trial 1, two 220 MB .avi) still returns 'Only metadata available for this study. File download not available.' It has no public collection and no public dataset on the new portal.

CORRECTION - the legacy listing's own flags are: BROWN42 No, BROWN10 No, BROWN88 No, BROWN29 Partial, BROWN45 Partial, BROWN46 Partial, BROWN27 Partial. But in the three 'Partial' studies I checked trial by trial, BROWN29 and BROWN46 have zero public trials, so 'Partial' does not imply any retrievable data.

CORRECTION - much of the paired CT is postmortem or partial ('postMortem', 'excisedRibs', 'Dead scan', 'Left Thorax Stnd ... 8 cm of thorax only'), so 'Living animals' describes the X-ray trials, not necessarily the CT. Scanner is not uniformly Fidex either: BROWN63's scans are labelled FHL microCT.

RISK - xmaportal.org is in 'legacy read-only mode' and is stated to remain available only 'for the next few months'; the successor xma.xromm.brown.edu requires sign-in for everything except 49 public datasets, of which only BROWN:45 (eggs) and BROWN:63 come from this candidate set. The metadata browsing this candidate is built on may not survive migration.

UNVERIFIED - no publication is listed on any of the seven studies' Overview pages, so I found no paper data-availability statement backing these records; the only publication tie-in is the BROWN63 collection title naming Capano et al., 2022. I did not attempt to fetch any gated file by direct URL, since that would be probing access control rather than testing a published route.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real acquisitions — not DRRs, not simulations, not MV portal images. Every one of the seven studies holds "XMovie" files recorded as cam1/cam2 pairs (.cine from Phantom high-speed cameras, or .avi), alongside XCalibObject/XCalibGrid images from cube-and-grid calibration trials. I verified by decoding an actual file rather than trusting the metadata: BROWN27 fileID 21561 ("Floyd Trial1_cam1.avi", 230,696,448 B) downloads anonymously and ffprobe reports rawvideo, pal8, 1024x1024, 30 fps; the extracted frames show a live rat walking through a circular image-intensifier field with the classic II vignette, overexposed background and a lead step-wedge in the corner. That is undoubtedly a real fluoroscopic/videoradiographic acquisition. Note the per-study camera counts: in BROWN88 and BROWN46, cam3/cam4 files are visible-light ("VisMovie") — in BROWN46 some cam3/cam4 files are nevertheless filed under "XMovie", so the 94 "X-ray" files in that study over-counts the true X-ray files.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same-subject CT exists, but NOT for every animal in every study — the candidate's "CT of the same animals in each of these studies" is too strong. Counting 3DVOL volume archives (excluding OBJ/STL meshes) against individuals that actually have data trials: BROWN42 monitor lizard 3/3 (Willie, Maja, Flip; pre-bead and post-bead Fidex scans); BROWN46 rodent 4/4; BROWN45 turkey 4/4 (incl. the chicken-egg "individual"); BROWN29 tegu — scans for all six trial individuals plus two extra animals (Tu04, Tu07) that have no trials; BROWN10 alligator 5/7 (Ag2L5 and the turkey Me49 have trials but no CT); BROWN27 rat 4/9 individuals (Evan, Floyd, Pink, Rudy have CT volumes; Taylor, Harry have none; FrozenRat2015 has OBJ meshes only); BROWN88 boa 1/5 — a single "2022APR12_bc02_8cm_CTscan.zip" against five snakes with X-ray trials. CT geometry is regional, not whole-body, in the reptile studies: BROWN42 comments say "Fidex, 15 cm FOV" and "8 cm FOV"; BROWN29 says "8 cm of thorax only". The scanner is confirmed Fidex/ANIMAGE for four studies only (stated in comments for BROWN42 and BROWN10; DICOM Manufacturer = ANIMAGE read directly from BROWN27 and BROWN46 files) and is not stated for BROWN29, BROWN45, BROWN88.
verdicts.anatomy: All seven are non-human animals; none contains a human lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis. By study: BROWN42 savannah monitor — marker-based rib kinematics, breathing and treadmill walking (ribs, vertebrae, pectoral girdle); BROWN29 tegu — rib/sternum/vertebra ventilation, with OBJ models of vertebrae, sternal and vertebral ribs; BROWN10 alligator — thorax, ribs, sternum, spine models, intercostal EMG; BROWN88 boa — rectilinear locomotion, costocutaneous muscle fluoromicrometry plus skeletal kinematics (a boa has no lumbar region, no sacrum and no pelvis; its one CT is an 8 cm scan); BROWN45 turkey — rib/sternum kinematics, plus a chicken-egg embryo sub-study; BROWN27 rat — explicitly FORELIMB locomotion (models are humerus, radius, ulna, scapula, skull, sternum), and the public X-ray frames I rendered show head, cervicothoracic spine and forelimb, with the lumbar region trailing out of the circular field; BROWN46 — freely moving rodents exploring a box, no markers. Only the two rodent studies have CTs that actually reach lumbar vertebrae, which I confirmed by pulling and rendering slices: BROWN46 "Female 2" (384x384, 0.2163 mm isotropic, 110 kVp, 1446 slices = 313 mm craniocaudal, i.e. whole body) shows a lumbar-type vertebra with an abdominal gas-filled gut at slice 690 and tail/hind feet by slice 992; BROWN27 "Floyd" (480x480, 0.1731 mm, ~800+ slices, ~140 mm) shows an abdominal slice with a lumbar vertebra at slice 785. There is no human-like lumbosacral junction anywhere in this candidate.
verdicts.counts: Measured from the portal's own metadata tables (not from the candidate's estimate). Data trials / calibration trials / individuals / total files / X-ray movie files: BROWN42 51/12/3/408/100; BROWN29 91/17/8/632/178; BROWN10 80/10/7/387/149; BROWN88 131/22/5/857/263; BROWN45 58/10/4/509/135; BROWN46 34/4/4/215/94; BROWN27 51/11/9/197/104. Totals across the seven: 496 data trials, 86 calibration trials, 40 individuals, ~3,200 files, 1,023 X-ray movie files. Frame counts are not published anywhere on the portal, so the number of X-ray IMAGES cannot be stated from primary sources; individual .cine files run 200 MB to 5.9 GB, and the one file I decoded was 1024x1024 at 30 fps.
verdicts.access_now: Mixed, and more open than the candidate says. (1) Metadata browsing for all seven is open with no login, via explorePublicMetadataStudy / viewAllFilesMetadata / view3dvolFilesMetadata (send cookie showAllFiles=1 to defeat the 50-row pagination). (2) The All Studies table marks Public Access = "Partial" for BROWN27, BROWN29, BROWN45, BROWN46 and "No" for BROWN10, BROWN42, BROWN88. (3) Files flagged public do download anonymously — I verified HTTP 206 responses carrying real bytes for BROWN27 fileID 21561 (rat X-ray AVI, 230 MB; RIFF/AVI magic) and 22345 (rat CT, 181 MB zip of ANIMAGE DICOMs), BROWN29 24971 (1.87 GB .cine), BROWN46 51399 (214 MB zip of 1446 DICOM slices), BROWN45 64247 and 64359. You must first hit studyOverview_public for that StudyID to seed the PHP session, then request downloadfileXsendfile&fileID=N with the same cookie jar. Public subsets: BROWN27 = 22 rat X-ray AVIs + Floyd's CT + calibration TIFFs + 2 Maya scenes; BROWN45 = chicken-egg trials only (not turkeys); BROWN29 = one .cine; BROWN46 = one CT stack. (4) Everything else needs an account — the Documentation page says to contact Kia Huffman to become a registered user, and gives no PI email; access to a non-public study is then at the study's discretion. (5) Risk: xmaportal.org is in "legacy read-only mode" and migrating to xma.xromm.brown.edu. The new portal is live, requires sign-in to view or download data, and its public dataset list contains none of these seven studies.
verdicts.licence: None stated. I found no licence, terms-of-use or data-use statement on the all-studies page, the study overviews, the file pages, the Documentation page or the Contact page. "Not public" as a licence label is wrong for four of the seven, where the portal itself serves files to anonymous users; but "openly licensed" would be equally wrong, because nothing grants any reuse right. Fully public studies on this portal (e.g. BROWN5 Iguana Lung Ventilation) carry a Publications block with a DOI and a named Public Data Collection; none of the seven candidate studies has either.
corrections: 'The files are gated (metadata only)' and licence 'Not public': refuted for 4 of 7. The All Studies table marks BROWN27/29/45/46 as Public Access = Partial, and their public files download anonymously with no login — verified with HTTP 206 responses carrying real data (BROWN27 fileID 21561 Floyd Trial1_cam1.avi, 230,696,448 B, valid RIFF/AVI; fileID 22345 Floyd.zip, 181,228,776 B, zip of ANIMAGE DICOMs; BROWN46 fileID 51399, 214,289,551 B; BROWN29 fileID 24971, 1,874,070,780 B; BROWN45 fileIDs 64247/64359). Only BROWN10, BROWN42 and BROWN88 are fully closed.

'CT of the same animals in each of these studies': refuted as a blanket claim. BROWN88 has five boas with X-ray trials and exactly ONE CT (bc02). BROWN27 has CT volumes for 4 rats (Evan, Floyd, Pink, Rudy) but data trials for 7 individuals — Taylor and Harry have no 3D file at all, FrozenRat2015 has OBJ meshes only. BROWN10 has CT for 5 of its 7 trial individuals (Ag2L5, and the turkey Me49, have none). Only BROWN42, BROWN45, BROWN46 and BROWN29 cover every trial individual.

'BROWN46 (whole-body mouse, with CT)': the species claim is not supported and looks wrong. The study is 'Rodent Behavioral Assay'; only the 2014-12-09 pilot trials are labelled mouse ('strain probably C57BL6', with no individual assigned). The four CT'd individuals (Female1, Female2, Male1, Male2) carry DICOM PatientName 'Rats', and the trunk cross-section I measured on a mid-stack slice is ~39 mm dorsoventral — the same as the known Sprague-Dawley rat Floyd in BROWN27 (38.9 mm), roughly double a mouse. The 'whole-body' half of the claim IS supported: 1446 slices at 0.2163 mm = 313 mm craniocaudal.

'Calibrated biplanar trunk X-rays' in each study: BROWN27 is forelimb, not trunk — the study is 'Rat Forelimb Locomotion', the 3D models are humerus/radius/ulna/scapula/skull/sternum, and the public frames I rendered show head, cervicothoracic spine and forelimb with the lumbar region out of the circular field. BROWN46 is a behaviour assay of rodents exploring a box, with no markers and no processed data.

'About 50-300 trials per study': measured range is 34-131 data trials (plus 4-22 calibration trials). BROWN46 has 34 data trials, below the stated floor; no study reaches 300. X-ray movie FILES run 94-263 per study.

'Living animals, 3-8 per study': individuals run 3 to 9 (BROWN27 has 9 individuals, 7 of them with data trials). Also, not all data are in vivo — BROWN27 includes 4 'FrozenRat2015' data trials and a 'Dead Rat' Maya scene, BROWN29's CTs are largely postMortem/postOP, BROWN45 has 'Dead scan' CTs, and BROWN45's only public trials are chicken eggs (in-ovo embryos), not turkeys.

'Pose or labels: calibration trials per day; marker-based XROMM': calibration is real (Cal Before/Middle/After per day, XCalibObject + XCalibGrid, DLTcoefs/MayaCam/undistortion files), but there are NO image-level labels of any kind — no boxes, no landmarks on frames, no per-frame ground truth. Processed 3D pose exists for a minority of trials: BROWN42 19 of 51 trials with xyzpts, BROWN10 3 trials of marker points plus 5 Maya/XMALab scenes, BROWN27 4 scenes, BROWN29 4 .xma files, BROWN45 2 files, and BROWN88 and BROWN46 have ZERO ProcData files. 'Marker-based' is also not uniform: BROWN10 lists Markerless trials, BROWN27's method column is Markerless throughout. The portal's own Documentation warns that the Processed Data section is 'still a bit of a wilderness'.

'Published 2012-2022': unverified from primary sources. The Publications section on each of the seven Overview pages is EMPTY (contrast BROWN5, which lists Brainerd et al. 2015 with a DOI and a public data collection). The years quoted match portal study-creation dates (BROWN10 2012-02-06 through BROWN88 2022-03-31), which is not a publication date.

'The access route is the PI, mostly Brainerd ([e-mail withheld])': the email address appears in no primary source I could open. The Documentation page directs account requests to Kia Huffman; no PI email is published anywhere on the portal. Brainerd is listed as a PI on all seven, which is supported, but the contact route and address are not.

'Device: CT on a Fidex scanner': verified for four studies only — comments name Fidex in BROWN42 and BROWN10, and I read Manufacturer = ANIMAGE (Fidex's maker) directly from BROWN27 and BROWN46 DICOM headers. Not stated for BROWN29, BROWN45 or BROWN88.

Anatomy relevance not flagged in the candidate: all seven are non-human animals, so none provides a human lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis. The boa study has no sacrum, pelvis or lumbar region as a matter of anatomy; the reptile CTs are explicitly regional (BROWN29 '8 cm of thorax only'; BROWN42 '15 cm FOV' / '8 cm FOV'). The only CTs that reach lumbar vertebrae are the two rodent studies, confirmed by rendering slices.

Access risk omitted: xmaportal.org displays a banner saying it is in 'legacy read-only mode' and that new work moves to xma.xromm.brown.edu. The new portal is live but requires sign-in to view or download data, and none of these seven studies appears in its public dataset listing. Any access plan built on the legacy URL may expire.

candidate.name: Utah Hive: Standing Anterior Pelvic Tilt vs Proximal Femur Shape in Cam Morphology (CT plus standing pelvis/femur poses from biplane videoradiography; frames not released)
candidate.why_relevant: Kept as a lead even though the searcher marked it 'neither'. The open release has CT or synthetic CT for 32 living adults, pelvis and femur meshes, landmarks, and rigid transforms from native imaging space to the lab frame taken from biplane videoradiography during static standing. That is a solved in-vivo pelvis pose for each CT. The biplane X-ray frames and the calibration are not released; the README says additional data were collected but not included. The underlying data would meet NEED A (human pelvis, dual fluoroscopy, same-subject CT, known pose). As released, the package has no X-ray images, and the only route is to ask Anderson and Atkins for the frames. This is a separate record from the earlier Utah Hive record cftes-sc590.
candidate.institution: University of Utah Orthopaedic Research Laboratory (A. Anderson, P. Atkins)
candidate.device: Utah biplane videoradiography (dual fluoroscopy); CT or MRI-derived sCT
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis, proximal and distal femur
candidate.subjects: 32 living adults (symptomatic cam, asymptomatic cam, controls)
candidate.pose_or_labels: 4x4 pelvis and femur transforms in the lab frame during static standing; landmarks
candidate.licence: CC BY (README); record lists CC BY 3.0

verdicts.access_now: Fully open, no login, downloadable now. API says access.record=public, access.files=public, embargo inactive, status "open". Anonymous HTTPS GET of the 5.05 GB zip returns HTTP 200 with content-length 5048151035 and content-md5 c401900c9da6f91cf5f50b5ceff3964c; I streamed the entire object (5,048,151,035 bytes received) to enumerate it. Two practical notes: the server ignores Range (a byte-range request returns 200 and restarts from byte 0), so there is no resume for the 5 GB download; and the parent record has allow_user_requests=false and allow_guest_requests=false, i.e. Hive exposes no "request access" mechanism at all — for anything not in the zip the only route is email to the PI ([e-mail withheld], listed in the record's hive:contact_email and in the README). Record HTML page returns 200; DOI 10.7278/S5d-6yyb-3qjg 302-redirects to it. Stats at time of check: 50 views, 34 downloads.
verdicts.anatomy: Hip/pelvis and knee. Per-subject volumes: hip (full pelvis + proximal femurs) and knee. Surfaces are proximal femur, IPSILATERAL HEMIPELVIS, and distal femur (LS-DYNA .k); no sacrum, no spine, no acetabular cartilage surfaces. I decompressed one hip CT (Cam03_Hip_CT.nii.gz: 512x512x313, 0.658x0.658x1.0 mm, float64, sform only) and rendered coronal and sagittal MIPs: the FOV contains both hemipelves, both proximal femurs, the whole sacrum and roughly the lower three lumbar vertebrae (~L3-L5). So the released volumes do contain lumbosacral bone even though no spine mesh or label is provided. Landmarks (.xlsx) are femoral/acetabular joint centres, knee axis/midpoint, ASIS/PSIS bilaterally, iliac crests and trochanters (last two only for the Cam and N groups) — pelvic landmarks only, no vertebral landmarks.
verdicts.counts: Record has exactly 2 files: 20260223_PelTiltCamMorphology_Anderson.zip (5,048,151,035 B = 4.70 GiB) and ANDERSON_README_20260223.txt (16,397 B); total_bytes 5,048,167,432. Full enumeration of the zip (streamed, every local header read): 593 entries, 389 regular files + .particles sets, under three trees — Participant_data (289 entries), FemurSSM (167), PelvisSSM (135) — plus Participant_Demographics.xlsx and the README at top level. 32 participant folders, 8 files each: Cam03-09 (6), N02-N15 (10), Pat02-Pat15 (9), Pos01-Pos08 (7) = 32, matching the paper's 15 patients / 7 positive controls / 10 negative controls. Imaging: 64 .nii.gz = 32 hip + 32 knee. Hip = 16 *_Hip_CT.nii.gz and 16 *_Hip_sCT.nii.gz; knee = 16 CT, 6 sCT, 10 VIBE MRI. 32 *_static_DFS_viconspace.txt (Cam03's has 100 rows x 32 columns = two row-major 4x4 transforms per time point). 128 .k surfaces, 52 .stl, 12 .ply, 32 .vtk groomed meshes, 32 cutting-plane .json, 36 .xlsx. ZERO files of any X-ray/fluoroscopy type: no .tif/.tiff/.png/.jpg/.dcm/.avi/.cine/.raw anywhere in the archive, and no calibration/DLT/camera-geometry file of any kind.
verdicts.licence: Record metadata: cc-by-3.0 ("Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported", SPDX, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). README says only "CC BY - Allows others to use and share your data with attribution." No further restriction, no DUA, no registration. (The companion paper is separately CC BY 4.0 per Crossref.) Candidate's licence line is correct.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, but half of it is not CT. Each of the 32 subjects has one hip volume and one knee volume, and the hip volume is real CT for only 16 subjects (the previously-recruited Cam and N groups); the other 16 (Pat, Pos) have BoneMRI v1.6 synthetic CT derived from a 3T T1 multi-echo GRE MR acquisition (0.5x0.5x0.8 mm). The paper states the real hip CTs were acquired UNDER TRACTION (to open the joint for a cartilage study), which is why those CTs were not used for the sacral measurements — relevant if anyone plans DRRs or intensity-based registration from them. Pairing to the standing pose is by 32 per-subject rigid transform files mapping native imaging space to the lab frame.
verdicts.real_xray: No X-ray imagery is released. Dual-fluoroscopy frames were certainly acquired (paper: two validated biplane videoradiography systems, 100 kVp / 457 mA / 7.0 ms continuous for the earlier cohort, 100 kVp / 125 mA / 1.2 ms pulsed for the new cohort; model-based tracking of at least twelve frames of one static standing trial per subject), but the release contains zero image frames and zero calibration. The README's "Additional related data collected that was not included in the current data package: Yes" is the only hint, and it does not say what was withheld — that the withheld material is the BVR frames and calibration is an inference from the file list, not a statement in the record. What you do get is the tracked result: a per-frame 4x4 pose of the femur and of the hemipelvis in the lab/treadmill (Vicon) frame. Without the biplane source/detector geometry that pose cannot be turned back into a projection, so it is a solved pose in a motion-capture frame, not a known imaging pose. (The sibling record cftes-sc590 describes the same lab frame as "the dual fluoroscopy coordinate system in the lab", but likewise releases no frames and no calibration.)
corrections: Candidate field real_xray:true is wrong for the release. I enumerated every entry of the 5 GB archive: 0 X-ray/fluoroscopy images, 0 calibration files. The candidate's prose says this correctly ('0 X-ray images released'), but the boolean contradicts it and would mislead any downstream filter. Its n_images:'0 X-ray images released' and serves:'A' are also in tension — as released this package serves NEED A not at all.

'CT or synthetic CT for 32 living adults' understates the split: exactly 16 subjects have real hip CT (*_Hip_CT.nii.gz: the 6 Cam + 10 N folders, the previously-recruited cohort) and 16 have BoneMRI-derived synthetic CT (*_Hip_sCT.nii.gz: 9 Pat + 7 Pos). Knee volumes are 16 CT, 6 sCT, 10 VIBE MRI. For DRR or intensity-based work only the 16 real CTs are usable as CT, and the paper states those were acquired under hip traction.

'unreleased no route' is half right: there is no repository route (Hive access requests are disabled on this record's parent: allow_user_requests=false, allow_guest_requests=false) and no statement anywhere that the frames can be obtained. The only route is unsolicited email to the PI, [e-mail withheld] (record custom field hive:contact_email; README lists the same plus co-investigator addresses including [e-mail withheld]). Nothing in the record or paper promises the frames, so this is not even an 'available on request' case.

'pelvis and femur meshes' should be 'ipsilateral hemipelvis, proximal femur, distal femur'. There is no whole-pelvis mesh, no sacrum mesh and no spine mesh. The hip VOLUMES do cover the whole pelvis, sacrum and about L3-L5 (verified by rendering coronal/sagittal MIPs of Cam03_Hip_CT: 512x512x313 at 0.658x0.658x1.0 mm), but any spine content would have to be segmented from scratch.

'known pose' overstates what the transforms give. The .txt files map native imaging space to the lab/Vicon/treadmill frame (Cam03: 100 rows x 32 columns = femur then pelvis 4x4, row-major). Without the biplane source and detector geometry, which is not released, this pose cannot be composed into a projection matrix. Even if the frames were later obtained, the calibration would also be needed.

Dates in the candidate need care: metadata publication_date is 2026-02-24 and the README is dated 20260223, but the Hive record object was created 2026-06-18 and last updated 2026-07-20 (it carries hive:old_id xw42n7977, i.e. migrated from the old repository). 'published 2026-02/03' is defensible for the citation date only.

The companion paper has been corrected: Crossref shows 'Corrigendum to Standing anterior pelvic tilt is correlated with the proximal femur shape of individuals with cam morphology' (10.1016/j.clinbiomech.2026.106807, online 2026-03-13, issue 2026-06). I could not retrieve the corrigendum text, so what was corrected is unknown.

I could not find a data availability statement pointing at this record. The PMC author manuscript (PMC13094539) contains no 'data availability' section and never mentions Hive, the DOI 10.7278/... or a repository; the link runs only one way, README -> paper. I could not read the Elsevier version of record, so I cannot rule out a DAS there. Report this as unverified rather than as a promise.

The record is a link-out, not a browsable dataset: everything is inside one 5 GB zip with no per-file access, no preview, and no Range support, so partial or selective download is impossible and an interrupted download restarts from zero.

Participant_Demographics.xlsx sits at byte offset ~4.99 GB of the zip, so I did not open it; its documented columns (sex, side, age, height, mass, BMI, femoral version, pelvic incidence, sacral slope, modality, diagnosis) are taken from the README, not verified.

verdicts.real_xray: Real, but not released. The associated paper (Clin Biomech 133:106767, PMC13094539, Methods 2.5) states the hip of interest was imaged with one of two validated biplane videoradiography (dual fluoroscopy) systems: previously recruited subjects under continuous fluoroscopy at max 100 kVp / 457 mA / 7.0 ms; newly recruited subjects on a pulsed system (Imaging Systems & Services Inc.) at max 100 kVp / 125 mA / 1.2 ms. The sibling record's README describes the same lab's system as two X-ray emitter + image-intensifier pairs, 100 Hz, 78-100 kVp, 1.9-3.2 mAs. That is genuine kV-range fluoroscopy, not DRR, not simulation, not MV portal. However ZERO frames are in the release: the zip listing (549 entries) contains only .particles, .k, .nii.gz, .stl, .ply, .vtk, .xlsx, .json, .txt - no image or video file of any kind. The BVR calibration is also absent, so no projection geometry is recoverable from what is public.
verdicts.paired_ct: Partly. 32 subjects each have one hip volume and one knee volume (.nii.gz), but only 16 are real CT. From the zip listing: Cam03-Cam09 (6) and N02-N15 (10) carry `*_Hip_CT.nii.gz`; Pat02-Pat15 (9) and Pos01-Pos08 (7) carry `*_Hip_sCT.nii.gz`. The paper confirms newly recruited participants (7 positive controls + 9 patients = 16) received NO CT to limit radiation dose and were instead scanned with a 3T Siemens Prisma 3D T1 SPGR multi-echo GRE (0.5x0.5x0.8 mm) converted to synthetic CT by BoneMRI v1.6 (MRIGuidance). Knee volumes are CT (16), sCT (6) or VIBE MRI (10). Two further cautions: the real hip CTs were acquired under hip traction (for a separate cartilage study), which is why the authors did not measure sacral alignment on them; and PI/SS in the demographics sheet come from a separate supine MRI that is not in the release.
verdicts.anatomy: Hip-centred, not spine. Released surfaces per subject are 4 .k meshes: ipsilateral proximal femur, ipsilateral HEMIpelvis, combined femur+pelvis, and distal femur (128 .k for 32 subjects). No sacrum mesh, no lumbar vertebra mesh, no spine of any kind. The paper's imaging FOV is "the full pelvis, proximal femur, and knee" (CT) or "the full pelvis and proximal femurs" (MR), so the sacrum is plausibly inside the hip volume, but nothing in the record or the paper states the craniocaudal extent of the released .nii.gz files and I could not open them (see access). Treat "sacrum present in the volume" as unverified and "lumbar spine present" as refuted - nothing in any primary source claims lumbar coverage. Critically for a fluoroscopy project, the BVR field of view was "the hip of the side of interest", so even the unreleased frames would show the hip joint and part of the ilium, not the lumbar spine and probably not the whole sacrum.
verdicts.counts: 32 participants (15 cam FAIS patients, 7 asymptomatic positive controls with cam, 10 negative controls; IRB #51053) = 32 folders in the zip (6 Cam + 10 N + 9 Pat + 7 Pos). 0 X-ray images released. 64 volumes (32 hip + 32 knee); 16 real CT hips, 16 sCT hips. 128 surface meshes, 32 landmark .xlsx, 32 static transform .txt, 549 total file entries, 5,048,151,035 bytes in one zip. Pose was tracked on "at least twelve frames" of one static standing trial per subject and averaged by quaternion averaging; the released .txt has one row per time point and 32 columns (two row-major 4x4 transforms, femur then pelvis). Row counts per file are unverified (zip not downloaded). Note 16 of the 32 subjects (Cam + N) are the same people re-released from the earlier Hive record cftes-sc590 / DOI 10.7278/S5d-btv7-ztpw, which likewise contains 266 entries and zero X-ray frames.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: Confirmed as described, with one important qualification. Each subject has SubjID_static_DFS_viconspace.txt: rigid 4x4 transforms taking the femur and hemipelvis surfaces from native imaging space into the lab frame during static standing, plus SubjID_Landmarks.xlsx with FJC, AJC, knee midpoint/axis/medial/lateral, L/R ASIS, L/R PSIS (GT, LT, L/R iliac crest only for the Cam and N groups). The earlier sibling record's README says explicitly that this lab frame IS "the dual fluoroscopy coordinate system in the lab". But the source/detector calibration, intrinsics and distortion correction are not released, so this is a bone-to-lab pose, NOT a projection pose; you cannot render or re-project from it. There are no per-pixel or per-vertebra labels of any kind, and no level labels (no spine). A published corrigendum (10.1016/j.clinbiomech.2026.106807) corrected the sign convention used for pelvic axial rotation and a mislabelled multiplicity correction in Fig. 3 - so sign conventions in this group's derived angles have been wrong in print once; verify any angle you recompute.
verdicts.access_now: Files are open: record access is public/open, no embargo, CC BY 3.0, both files downloadable without login (README 16.4 kB; zip 5.05 GB). But the zip is the only container - there is no per-file API for members inside it, and the Hive file endpoint IGNORES HTTP Range (a byte-range request returns 200 and streams the whole 5 GB), so a partial extraction of one .nii.gz is not possible; you must pull all 5 GB. The Invenio zip PREVIEW endpoint does give the complete file tree without downloading (https://hive.utah.edu/records/makj2-87f78/preview/20260223_PelTiltCamMorphology_Anderson.zip), which is how the counts above were verified. For the X-ray frames there is no route in the repository: the record's parent access settings are allow_user_requests=false and allow_guest_requests=false, so the "request access" mechanism is disabled. The only route is email to Andrew Anderson ([e-mail withheld], listed as the record contact) or Penny Atkins. README section "Additional related data collected that was not included in the current data package: Yes" - with no statement of what that additional data is, so even the claim that the frames are archived and shareable is inference, not a stated fact.
verdicts.licence: CC BY 3.0 Unported, confirmed in the record metadata (rights id "cc-by-3.0", SPDX, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/); README says "CC BY - Allows others to use and share your data with attribution". Record is public, files public, embargo inactive, status open. DOI 10.7278/S5d-6yyb-3qjg confirmed in metadata identifiers. Requested citation asks that the Clin Biomech paper be cited alongside. Note the licence covers what is released; it says nothing about the unreleased frames.
corrections: REFUTED as worded: 'CT or synthetic CT for 32 living adults' understates the split. Only 16 of 32 subjects have a real CT (Cam03-09 n=6, N02-N15 n=10). The other 16 (Pat n=9, Pos n=7) have NO CT at all - their hip volume is a BoneMRI v1.6 synthetic CT derived from a 3T T1 SPGR MR, per the paper's Methods 2.2 and Table 1 and per the filenames *_Hip_sCT.nii.gz in the zip listing. For a 2D/3D X-ray project, half the cohort has no true attenuation volume to render or register against.

REFUTED: 'pelvis and femur meshes' implies a whole pelvis. The released mesh is the IPSILATERAL HEMIpelvis only (README variable list B; the paper reflects and aligns single-side pelvis surfaces for the SSM). No sacrum mesh, no spine mesh. The SSM 'sacroiliac region' finding in the abstract refers to the iliac side of the SI joint, not to a sacrum.

UNVERIFIED, treat as refuted: nothing in the record or the paper states that the released hip .nii.gz volumes include the sacrum or any lumbar vertebra. The paper says the CT captured 'the full pelvis, proximal femur, and knee' and the MR 'the full pelvis and proximal femurs', but the craniocaudal extent of the shipped files is unstated and could not be checked - the 5 GB zip is the only container and the server ignores Range requests. Lumbar spine coverage is claimed nowhere.

CORRECTION to the relevance argument: the released transforms are bone-to-LAB-frame, and the BVR calibration is not released. So this is not a 'known pose' in the sense NEED A requires (source/detector geometry). Even with the frames, you would still need the calibration files. The sibling record's README confirms the lab frame is the dual-fluoroscopy coordinate system, which helps, but geometry without intrinsics is not a projection.

ADD: the real hip CTs were acquired UNDER TRACTION (for a separate cartilage study), which is why the authors refused to measure sacral alignment on them and used a separate supine MRI for PI/SS. The hip joint space in those 16 CTs is distracted relative to any standing frame.

ADD: the BVR field of view was 'the hip of the side of interest'. Any frames obtained by request would therefore contain the hip and part of the ilium - not the lumbar spine, and likely not a full sacrum. This is a hip-morphology dataset, not a spinopelvic radiograph dataset.

ADD: 16 of the 32 subjects (Cam and N groups) are re-released from the earlier Hive record cftes-sc590 (DOI 10.7278/S5d-btv7-ztpw, published 2025-09-30), whose own zip (266 entries) also contains zero X-ray frames. Two records from this lab, two dual-fluoroscopy studies, no frames either time - which is evidence about the lab's release habit, not about their willingness on request.

ADD: a corrigendum was published (10.1016/j.clinbiomech.2026.106807, PMID 41826117, 2026-03-13): the sign convention for pelvic axial rotation in Fig. 3 was wrong, and the caption named Holm-Sidak when Benjamini-Hochberg was used. Conclusions unchanged, but sign conventions from this group have been wrong in print once.
MINOR: 'published 2026-02/03' is the metadata publication_date (2026-02-24; README dated 2026-02-23). The Hive record itself was created 2026-06-18 and last updated 2026-07-20.

UNVERIFIED: 'living adults'. The study is in vivo (standing BVR), so living is certain; ages live in Participant_Demographics.xlsx inside the 5 GB zip and were not read. Adult status is inferred from clinic-recruited FAIS patients and the prior publications, not read from a primary source.

NOT CONFIRMED: 'the README says additional data were collected but not included' is literally true but content-free - the README answers 'Yes' and names nothing. There is no primary-source statement anywhere that the biplane frames are retained, shareable, or that the calibration survives.

candidate.name: Bern canine cadaver thoracolumbar end-on fluoroscopy of Steinmann pins (Goffart et al., Front Vet Sci 2022)
candidate.why_relevant: Real surgical mini C-arm fluoroscopy of implants in a spine, with ground truth for each pin (in or out of the canal, partial or complete) confirmed by anatomic sectioning, at named levels T10-L7. The CT comes from a different study and is not of the same specimens. Raw data are available from the authors. It is weak for NEED B because the subjects are animal cadavers.
candidate.institution: Vetsuisse Faculty, University of Bern
candidate.device: OrthoScan FD-OR Mini C-arm (flat detector)
candidate.anatomy: Canine thoracolumbar spine T10-L7 with bicortical pins
candidate.n_images: One end-on image per pin (count not stated)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Pin position relative to the canal, by level, verified by sectioning
candidate.licence: Article CC BY; data on request

verdicts.access_now: None of the image data can be downloaded. The data availability statement, the same in Europe PMC and on the Frontiers page, says: "The raw data supporting the conclusions of this article will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation." That is a promise to share on request, and nothing has been deposited. DataCite lists only two items from these authors, and both are journal articles. The Bern repository (BORIS) record 10.48350/174591 is the article, not a dataset. Zenodo and figshare searches found no image deposit. The only supplement is Data_Sheet_1.docx (66,046 bytes; figshare 10.3389/fvets.2022.982560.s001; https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/37920393). It contains four statistics tables (Tables 4 to 7, univariate and multivariable odds ratios) and no images. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip (467,569 bytes) contains just that docx plus the four article figures. Only one fluoroscopy frame is public: Figure 3 (g0003.jpg, 63,927 bytes), a standard and a grey-inverted copy of the same image showing several pins, one of them end-on at L3. Figure 1 shows two plain radiographs (laterolateral and dorsoventral), Figure 2 is a photo of the C-arm set-up and Figure 4 shows photos of the specimens. The practical route is to email the corresponding author, Bianca F. Hettlich (Vetsuisse Faculty, Bern).
verdicts.licence: The article is CC BY (Europe PMC licence field "cc by"; the XML permissions say "Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY)"). The figshare supplement is CC BY 4.0. No licence has been stated for the raw data, because it has never been released.
verdicts.counts: 193 pins in 5 canine cadaver columns (collected T9 to L7, pins placed T10 to L7). Per level: T10 14, T11 17, T12 17, T13 18, L1 20, L2 20, L3 19, L4 20, L5 19, L6 19, L7 10. By side: 95 left (57 in, 38 out) and 98 right (52 in, 46 out). The paper says each pin was imaged end-on, so there should be about 193 end-on frames. Each frame was also read as a grey-inverted copy, and four evaluators (surgeon, surgery resident, radiologist, neurologist) read both versions. One frame is public (Figure 3).
verdicts.anatomy: Canine thoracolumbar vertebral columns (T9 to L7) taken out of 5 adult medium-to-large dogs (Dalmatian, Australian Shepherd, German spitz, 2 mongrels; mean 23.7 kg). The paraspinal muscle was removed before imaging, so these are isolated, defleshed spines, not intact cadavers. Smooth 2.5 or 3 mm Steinmann pins were placed bicortically in the vertebral bodies, 1 or 2 per side.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes. Real C-arm fluoroscopy on an OrthoScan FD-OR Mini C-arm. The spine was positioned by hand until each pin appeared as a circle (end-on). Plain laterolateral and dorsoventral radiographs were also taken before and after pinning, but they were not used for evaluation.
verdicts.paired_ct: No CT of these specimens. The CT and radiograph comparison uses historical data from Hettlich et al. 2010: 12 different cadaver columns, compared only at the level of accuracy statistics.
corrections: Ground truth was not established by 'anatomic sectioning'. Soft tissue was removed with an enzymatic solution (BIOZYM SE) and pin position was judged by direct visual inspection of the macerated vertebrae.
The image count is stated indirectly: 193 pins were evaluated and each was imaged end-on, so there are about 193 frames, with a per-level breakdown for T10 to L7. 'Count not stated' is wrong.

'Raw data are available from the authors' overstates it. The statement is a promise ('will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation'), not a release. Nothing has been deposited (DataCite, BORIS, Zenodo and figshare checked). 'Raw data supporting the conclusions' may mean the evaluator scoring sheets rather than the images.
The only supplement (Data_Sheet_1.docx, 66 KB, CC BY 4.0) is four statistics tables with no images and no per-pin labels.
Only one fluoroscopy frame is public: Figure 3, the L3 pin, shown standard and inverted. It is a multi-pin view in which one pin is end-on.
The subjects are excised, defleshed spine columns, not whole cadavers. There is no surrounding soft tissue, which moves the images further from clinical fluoroscopy for NEED B.
Labels are pin-level in or out of the canal, with partial or complete penetration and the level, plus four readers' answers and confidence. There is no pose, landmark or pixel annotation.

The first evidence search URL (query=DOI:10.3389/fvets.2022.982560 without quotes) returns only {"version":"6.9"}, with no record. The quoted, encoded query returns PMID 36337187 / PMC9630941, isOpenAccess Y, hasSuppl Y, licence cc by.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes. These are real acquisitions: end-on fluoroscopy of each pin on an OrthoScan FD-OR Mini C-arm (Scottsdale, AZ), on excised cadaver columns that were positioned by hand under the C-arm laser guide. There are no DRRs or simulation. The 'inverted fluoroscopy' (Fi) set is a digital gray-scale inversion of the same frames, not a second acquisition. The same specimens also have real orthogonal laterolateral and dorsoventral radiographs, taken before and after pin placement (Fig. 1), which were not used for evaluation.
verdicts.paired_ct: None. This study acquired no CT or CBCT. The CT and radiograph accuracy figures are historical data from Hettlich et al. 2010 (Vet Surg 39:680-7), taken on 12 different cadaveric vertebral columns. The authors say plainly that 'radiographic and CT assessment were not repeated in the current population'.
verdicts.anatomy: Canine thoracolumbar vertebral columns were excised from T9 to L7, and the paraspinal musculature was stripped. Pins were placed in T10-L7, so canine L1-L7 is present. There is no sacrum, no pelvis and no lumbosacral junction. The published example (Fig. 3, L3) is a lateral-oblique view of about 2-3 vertebral bodies with several pins. The target pin shows as a circle, so each frame is aligned to one pin rather than being a standard AP or lateral view. The paper's standard display is dense = black.
verdicts.counts: 5 cadavers (Dalmatian, Australian Shepherd, German spitz, 2 mongrels; mean 23.7 kg). 193 pins were evaluated: T10 14, T11 17, T12 17, T13 18, L1 20, L2 20, L3 19, L4 20, L5 19, L6 19, L7 10. That is 109 in the canal and 84 out, with 95 left and 98 right. Each pin was imaged end-on and each image labelled with its pin ID, which implies about 193 real fluoroscopic frames. The paper never states the number of image files. Only one fluoroscopic frame is published (Fig. 3, with its inversion).
verdicts.licence: The article is CC BY 4.0, so the 4 published figures are reusable, but only one of them is a fluoroscopy frame. The data availability statement says only that 'the raw data supporting the conclusions of this article will be made available by the authors, without undue reservation.' No repository and no data licence are given, and it is not stated that 'raw data' includes the images rather than the evaluator scores.
verdicts.access_now: No images are public beyond Fig. 3. The only supplement (Data_Sheet_1.docx) holds Supplementary Tables 4-7 of regression results and no images. Getting the frames means an email request to the corresponding author, B. F. Hettlich (Vetsuisse Faculty, University of Bern), and it is not known whether the images are part of the 'raw data'.
corrections: The image count is not truly 'not stated': 193 pins were evaluated with per-level counts (T10 14 ... L7 10), and each pin was imaged end-on, which implies about 193 fluoroscopic frames. The paper does not state a file count.

Ground truth was not 'confirmed by anatomic sectioning'. The paper describes anatomical preparation: soft tissue was removed with an enzymatic solution (BIOZYM SE) and pin position was judged by direct visual inspection of the cleaned vertebrae. Sectioning is never mentioned.
'Flat detector' is not stated in the paper. It names only the 'OrthoScan FD-OR Mini C-arm'.

The subjects are excised, dissected columns (T9-L7, paraspinal muscle removed), not intact cadavers. There is no sacrum or pelvis, and the lumbosacral junction is absent, so the candidate's anatomy must not be read as covering the pelvis.
The inverted-fluoroscopy set (Fi) is a digital inversion of the same frames, not additional acquisitions.

There is no pose or geometry. The specimen was rotated by hand until the pin appeared as a circle under the laser guide, and no C-arm angles or calibration were recorded. Insertion angles are given only as ranges: about 20-40 degrees thoracic, 40-60 degrees lumbar, 0-15 degrees at L7.
The labels are per-pin in/out, with 'in' split into partial or complete, by level and side, plus four evaluators' reads with confidence ratings. There are no masks and no landmarks.

Data 'on request' overstates it slightly. The statement promises 'raw data supporting the conclusions', which may mean evaluator scores and may not include the images. No repository and no data licence exist.
Omitted from the candidate: the same specimens also have real orthogonal laterolateral and dorsoventral radiographs, taken before and after implantation.
The candidate is correct that the CT is historical and from different specimens: 12 cadaveric columns in Hettlich et al. 2010.

candidate.name: Utrecht ISI 'Standardized Evaluation Methodology for 2D-3D Registration' gold-standard database (van de Kraats et al., IEEE TMI 2005)
candidate.why_relevant: This lead turns out to be lost. The set paired real AP and lateral fluoroscopy of two cadaveric lumbar spine segments (3 and 5 vertebrae) with 3DRX, CT and MR of the same specimens, with source, detector and volume poses in one world frame. That is exactly the NEED A kind. The database page was live from 2006 to about 2012-06; by 2013-08-08 it read 'This database is no longer available'. The download (a 51 MB zip, needing a one-day key and a no-redistribution agreement) was never captured in Wayback under any ISI, UMC Utrecht or Erasmus host. The last documented users were Birkfellner and Spoerk in Vienna (2009-2012). The documented formats are .raw/.sta volumes, .raw/.rad projections with 4x4 detector poses, and source .txt files. The only route is a private copy: van Walsum or Niessen (Erasmus MC), Penney (KCL), Tomazevic (Ljubljana), or the earlier Vienna licensees.
candidate.institution: Image Sciences Institute, University Medical Center Utrecht
candidate.device: Calibrated 3D rotational X-ray (3DRX) C-arm; vendor not named
candidate.xray_kind: C-arm fluoroscopy (AP and lateral) from the 3DRX system
candidate.anatomy: Cadaveric lumbar spinal segments: 3 and 5 vertebral bodies
candidate.n_images: 4 fluoroscopic images plus 3DRX, CT and MR per segment; 2D/3D masks for 8 vertebrae; 200 start positions; about 51 MB
candidate.pose_or_labels: Source, detector and volume poses in a world frame; per-vertebra 2D and 3D masks; rotation centres; 200 start offsets
candidate.is_update_of_known: Utrecht ISI 2D-3D gold standard (the task's known lead): withdrawn between 2012-06 and 2013-08, data files never archived, last documented use 2011-2012

verdicts.access_now: NO DOWNLOAD EXISTS TODAY — dead, not gated. Primary record (http://www.isi.uu.nl/Research/Databases/GS/) reads in full: "Standardized Evaluation Methodology for 2D-3D Registration — This database is no longer available." That notice is first captured 2013-08-08 and is the last content the page ever carried; the last live full page is 2012-06-18. The host is now gone entirely: www.isi.uu.nl resolves (143.121.214.137) but REFUSES TCP on both 80 and 443 as of 2026-09-22; Wayback shows the URL returning 404 over https from 2022-03-05 through 2024-02-17. The paper's own data-availability URL (http://www.isi.uu.nl/Research/Databases/, given in the TMI abstract) is dead by the same failure. The 51 MB zip sat behind a key-gated PHP script (commence_download.php), never at a static path, and no GS zip was ever captured by Wayback — I checked every .zip on the isi.uu.nl domain (only unrelated bij.isi.uu.nl ImageJ plugins) and found nothing on umcutrecht.nl, erasmusmc.nl or bigr.nl. Both maintainer addresses ([e-mail withheld], [e-mail withheld]) are on the dead host. Route today = a private copy from a 2006-2012 licensee only, and see licence: that person cannot legally redistribute it.
verdicts.anatomy: Cadaveric lumbar spine, confirmed by the primary record: the agreement page says "3DRX, CT, MR, and X-ray images of cadaver lumbar spine". Two spinal segments, one of 3 vertebral bodies and one of 5, 8 bodies total. NOTE the candidate overstates the labelling: the archived data page gives per-vertebra binary masks (0 or 255, unsigned char), both 2D (on each fluoro image) and 3D (in each volume), with bodies numbered b1..b5 WITHIN a segment (see upload.php naming: 3DRXv1b1f1AP_result.txt). Anatomical level names (L1..L5) are nowhere stated on the archived pages — so this set gives per-vertebra instance masks and poses, NOT named-level identity.
verdicts.counts: 2 segments, 8 vertebral bodies (3 + 5), 4 real fluoroscopic projections (AP + lateral per segment), 3 volumes per segment (3DRX, CT, MR) of the same specimen, 200 start positions (0-20 mm mTRE), ~51 MB zip.
corrections: access field "unreleased no route" is WRONG on "unreleased". This was a genuine public release, not a promise in a paper: download.php, agreement.php and a key-issuing workflow were live and served, and the site's own results.php tabulates two external methods (Tomazevic; Penney) actually evaluated on the data, with linked result graphs 1fluoro.pdf and 2fluoro.pdf. The correct status is RELEASED 2005/2006, then WITHDRAWN between 2012-06-18 (last live page) and 2013-08-08 (first "no longer available"), no route today.

device "vendor not named" is WRONG. The paper names it: the TMI abstract (PubMed 16156355) states the gold standard uses "the calibrated geometry of a 3-D rotational X-ray (3DRX) imaging system (Philips Medical Systems, Best, The Netherlands)". The website does not name the vendor; the paper does.

Citation page range is wrong in the candidate AND on the ISI site. Both say pp. 1177-1190; Crossref and PubMed both give IEEE Trans Med Imaging 2005;24(9):1177-1189. Use 1177-1189. (Crossref also shows 176 citing works.)

"needing a one-day key and a no-redistribution agreement" understates the barrier materially. download.php required that a PERMANENT FACULTY MEMBER serve as investigator for the requesting site and assume responsibility for the data, and that a brief CV (name, position, title, positions held, valid e-mail) be sent to the maintainer first; only then was a unique code e-mailed. commence_download.php confirms the key expired after 1 day. It was never self-serve even when live.

File-format claim is right but omits the fact that most changes how usable a private copy would be: per data.php, "3D image files and 3D mask files (extension .raw) — one byte data (unsigned char)". The CT, MR and 3DRX volumes are 8-BIT, not 16-bit/HU. Only the 2D projections are two-byte unsigned short, little-endian. Voxel order is row-column-slice. So a recovered copy would give you 8-bit CT with no HU scale.

"4x4 detector poses" is an inference, not what the record says. data.php says the .rad (2D projection) and .sta (3D volume) files carry image dimension, voxel size, and "position and orientation of image in the WCS (represented by a matrix)", with position defined at the centre of voxel/pixel (0,0,0)/(0,0). The 4x4 homogeneous convention is only visible on help.php, which writes the transform chain in explicit 4x4 form (last row 0;0;0;1) and gives the Rz*Ry*Rx composition and the centre-of-rotation conjugation.

"last documented users were Birkfellner and Spoerk in Vienna (2009-2012)" is incomplete. The mandated acknowledgement string also appears in Fallavollita 2010, "Is single-view fluoroscopy sufficient in guiding cardiac ablation procedures?" (10.1155/2010/631264), and a Kitware Source article dated 2012-01-27 reports using "the public dataset provided by the Imaging Sciences Institute of the University of Utrecht" citing the same URL. The earliest external users are Tomazevic and Penney on the site's own results table. I found no use after ~2012 — but that null rests on weak coverage (Europe PMC full text is open-access only; OpenAlex fulltext search returned 3 hits against 176 citations), so treat "last use 2012" as unproven rather than established.

"live from 2006" is a Wayback artefact. The earliest capture of any GS page is data.php on 2006-02-23, but the 2005 TMI paper already advertises the data as available on the internet, so the release almost certainly predates the first capture. Launch date is not established by the archive.

The candidate's "data files never archived" is confirmed, but it misses that the DIRECTORY outlived the withdrawal notice: upload.php was still served with a byte-identical hash on 2014-06-10, and geometry.jpg was still served (200, 156 KB) on 2017-10-04 — years after the index page said the database was gone. The host only began 301-ing in 2018-12 and 404s from 2022. So the zip plausibly sat on that server until ~2018; it was simply never linkable, because the download was key-gated through PHP.

The suggested recovery routes (van Walsum, Niessen, Penney, Tomazevic, Vienna licensees) are unverified speculation — I found no primary evidence that any of them still holds a copy or would share one. Also do not conflate Tomazevic with this set: the Ljubljana "gold standard" (Tomazevic, Likar, Pernus, Comput Aided Surg 2004, cadaveric lumbar phantom with fiducials, 18 X-ray images) is a SEPARATE dataset, and its own download page (http://lit.fe.uni-lj.si/Downloads/downloads.asp) 404s today although the lab site lit.fe.uni-lj.si is still up — which makes Ljubljana the only one of the named routes with a living institutional web presence.

The licence blocks the private-copy route as a data-acquisition strategy: the agreement is explicitly "I will not redistribute the provided password" and "I will not redistribute the database or its parts". A 2006-2012 licensee handing you a copy would be violating it. Any legitimate route needs fresh permission from ISI/UMC Utrecht, whose maintainer addresses are on a dead host.
verdicts.licence: No open licence, and no redistribution permitted. Index page: "The data included in this database can be used, free of charge, for research purposes only. Copying, redistribution, and any unauthorized commercial use is prohibited", plus a mandatory acknowledgement sentence and a mandatory citation of van de Kraats 2005. agreement.php adds four binding clauses: no redistribution of the password; no redistribution of the database or its parts; the acknowledgement in any publication; the citation, plus supplying the data provider with copies of such publications. Access additionally required a named permanent faculty member as responsible investigator with a CV on file. Consequence for this project: even if a private copy surfaces, the holder is barred from passing it on, and nothing here permits re-release or commercial use.
verdicts.paired_ct: CONFIRMED and it is the strongest thing about this lead. Per data.php, each of the two segments carries, of the SAME specimen: one 3DRX volume, one CT volume, one MR volume, and two fluoroscopic projections, with the source position (.txt), the detector pose (.rad) and each volume's pose (.sta) all expressed in one world coordinate system whose origin sits between source and detector; the volume poses ARE the ground truth. Per-body 3D masks in every modality are stated to cover the same anatomy across modalities because the ground truth was used to build them, with the explicit warning that 2D and 3D masks must not be used simultaneously as that biases the method. Also provided: per-body centres of rotation and 200 ground-truth offsets. This is exactly NEED A geometry — but 8-bit volumes, 4 projections, and no way to get it.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes — real projections of real cadaveric tissue, not DRRs. data.php: "two fluoroscopic images (anterior-posterior, lateral, unsigned short)" per segment, acquired on the calibrated Philips 3DRX C-arm system, with source and detector poses in the world frame. Caveat on scale: 4 images total. As a benchmark for pose ground truth this is real; as fluoroscopy data volume it is negligible, and it is cadaveric bench acquisition rather than clinical C-arm imaging.

verdicts.access_now: Dead, no route. Verified myself: Wayback CDX for the GS directory shows the full page set live with identical checksums through 2012-06-18; the 2013-08-08 capture (and every capture through 2017) contains only "This database is no longer available."; 2022/2023/2024 captures of the https URL are the ISI WordPress "Page not found"; today www.isi.uu.nl refuses connections on :443 from two different network paths (WSL curl HTTP 000, WebFetch ECONNREFUSED 143.121.214.137). The 51 MB zip was never archived: a domain-wide CDX query on isi.uu.nl returns zero application/zip captures and zero .raw/.sta/.rad captures; bigr.nl and erasmusmc.nl have no matching captures either; a filename search for the distinctive artefacts ("startpositions_200_ordered", "3DRXv1b1f1") finds nothing. Only surviving web artefacts are the HTML pages, geometry.jpg and two results PDFs. So the only route is a private copy. Europe PMC full-text search for the mandatory acknowledgement string returns exactly two papers — Birkfellner/Vienna 2009 (Med Phys) and Spoerk/Vienna 2012 (Z Med Phys) — which corroborates the candidate's "last documented licensees", though Europe PMC only indexes OA/PMC full text so that is not exhaustive.
verdicts.anatomy: Isolated cadaveric spinal segments fixed in foam with some soft tissue left on. NO sacrum, NO pelvis, NO femur, NO whole lumbar column — nothing below the vertebral bodies of two short segments. The "lumbar" claim is contested between two primary sources and I could not settle it: the ISI agreement page (primary, the database's own text) says "3DRX, CT, MR, and X-ray images of cadaver lumbar spine", while the MICCAI 2004 precursor by the same authors, describing the same 3-body + 5-body pair of segments with the same 200 start positions and 8 vertebral bodies, says "Spinal segment 1 consists of 3 thoracolumbal vertebral bodies and segment 2 consists of 5 thoracic vertebral bodies." The IEEE TMI 2005 paper that would arbitrate is closed access with no OA copy (Unpaywall/S2/OpenAlex all "closed", Erasmus RePub record has no full text), so I did not read it. Also: the release carries no anatomical level identity at all — masks are "vertebral body 1, 2, 3" and "1..5" per segment, never L1..L5, and are binary 0/255.
corrections: Anatomy claim 'Cadaveric lumbar spinal segments' is not supported and is contradicted by the authors' own MICCAI 2004 paper, which describes the same 3+5 vertebral-body pair as '3 thoracolumbal' and '5 thoracic'. The ISI agreement page does say 'cadaver lumbar spine'; the two primaries disagree and the arbitrating TMI 2005 full text is paywalled. For a lumbosacral project treat this as at most ~3 thoracolumbar bodies, and zero sacrum/pelvis.

'device: vendor not named' is wrong. Both the TMI 2005 abstract and MICCAI 2004 name it: 3D rotational X-ray C-arm Integris BV5000, Philips Medical Systems, Best, The Netherlands; CT was a Philips 16-detector-row MSCT.

'C-arm fluoroscopy (AP and lateral) from the 3DRX system' is imprecise about how the 2-D images were produced: they are two frames SELECTED from the 100 distortion-corrected projection images of the 8-second, 180-degree 3DRX rotational run ('From the 100 acquired X-ray images per spinal segment two images were selected, one anterior-posterior and one lateral'). Real detector acquisitions, but not a free-running fluoro sequence, and the geometry is the reconstruction geometry rather than an independently posed C-arm.

'pose_or_labels: per-vertebra 2D and 3D masks' is right but carries no level identity: the masks are numbered per segment (b1..b5), never named L1..L5, and label only vertebral bodies. Nothing in the release names a vertebra, so it cannot serve a level-naming task without an external read.

Subject count is unverified. 'Cadaver spine specimens: 2 segments' is what the pages support; no source I could open states how many donors the two segments came from (MICCAI 2004 says 'two defrosted segments of a vertebral column', singular, which may mean one donor). Do NOT import the '2 fresh post-mortem subjects, females aged 102 and 77, 200 X-ray projections' from the companion MICCAI 2005 MR paper — that acquisition has a different 3DRX resolution (0.43 mm vs 0.87/0.52 mm) and is probably not the released set.

Confusion risk flagged: this is NOT the Ljubljana gold standard. A copy of the Ljubljana LIT dataset (Tomazevic/Likar/Pernus, cadaveric lumbar spine phantom L1-L5, 18 real X-ray images + CT + MR, gold-standard poses, target points) is already unzipped in this machine's scratchpad and sits on the desktop as 2D-3D-GS.zip / 2D-3D-GS_UG.pdf. Its user guide names Ljubljana, not Utrecht. Anything claiming the Utrecht set was obtained should be checked against that, because the two are routinely conflated.

Unverifiable from a primary source I could open: that MR exists for BOTH segments and the exact file inventory. That rests entirely on the archived data.php page (which does state it per segment); the TMI 2005 paper text was not readable, and MICCAI 2004 had only 3DRX+CT.
verdicts.counts: 2 spinal segments, 8 vertebral bodies (3 + 5). Only 4 real 2-D X-ray images in the whole release: one AP and one lateral per segment. Per segment: one 3DRX volume, one CT volume, one MR volume, 3-D binary masks per vertebral body, 2-D binary masks per vertebral body per X-ray image, the WCS pose of every volume (.sta) and of every projection (.rad) plus the source position (.txt), a rotation centre per vertebral body, and 200 shared start positions spanning 0-20 mm mTRE (10 per 1 mm bin). Whole zip about 51 MB, which is consistent with four 512x512 projections rather than any image series. MICCAI 2004 lists the underlying sizes: 3DRX 256^3 at 0.87 mm (seg 1) and 0.52 mm (seg 2); CT 320x260x320 and 280x300x300 at ~0.31x0.49x0.31 mm; X-ray 512^2 at 0.63 and 0.53 mm.
verdicts.licence: Research use only, free of charge, no commercial use, no redistribution of the data or of the download password (agreement.php). Required acknowledgement sentence naming the Image Sciences Institute, UMC Utrecht, plus citation of van de Kraats et al., IEEE TMI 2005;24:1177-1190, and the licensee agrees to send copies of publications. Access was gated twice: a permanent faculty member at the requesting site had to send a brief CV to the maintainer ([e-mail withheld], Everine van de Kraats), and the resulting unique key expired after one day (commence_download.php rejects keys "older than 1 day"). No open licence of any kind, so even a surviving private copy cannot be redistributed to this project.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, and unusually strong. Per segment the release shipped one 3DRX (C-arm CBCT) volume, one CT volume and one MR volume of the same specimen, each with its pose in the same world frame as the projections, so CT-to-X-ray and MR-to-X-ray poses are given directly rather than having to be recovered. The chain is stated in the primaries: the 3DRX volume is reconstructed from the calibrated projections (geometry therefore known by construction), and CT and MR were registered to the 3DRX by mutual information to carry the transform across. CT scanner named in MICCAI 2004 as a clinical Philips 16-detector-row MSCT.
verdicts.real_xray: Real acquisitions on a kV image-intensifier C-arm, not DRRs, not simulated, not MV portal — and this is stated in a primary source, not inferred. MICCAI 2004 (same authors, same 3+5 specimen structure, same 200 start positions): "Data is acquired with a clinical floor-mounted 3D Rotational X-ray (3DRX) C-arm system (Integris BV5000, Philips Medical Systems, Best, The Netherlands). During an 8 second run of 180 degrees around the patient the 3DRX system acquires 100 projection images", and "From the 100 acquired X-ray images per spinal segment two images were selected, one anterior-posterior and one lateral". The images are corrected for image-intensifier distortion by the standard system calibration. DRRs appear in the paper only as what the intensity-based registration method generates to match against these real images. Caveat worth carrying: the released 2-D images are selected frames of a rotational run, so they are real projections but not an independently posed fluoro sequence, and the DB page's word "fluoroscopic" should not be read as free-running fluoroscopy.

candidate.name: Ljubljana 'Gold standard for 2D-3D registration' (2D-3D-GS; Tomazevic, Likar, Pernus): current download route, contents and licence conflict
candidate.why_relevant: This set is already known and evaluated, and 2D-3D-GS.zip and 2D-3D-GS_UG.pdf already sit in the CTSpinoPelvic1K-1 working tree. The facts that are probably new: (1) the licence conflicts. The resource page says CC BY-NC-ND, while the bundled user guide still requires a signed agreement. Either way it is non-commercial, which matters for the product track. (2) The 2017 route (contents/tools/GoldStandard/GSPublic/GSPublic.zip) now returns 404; the direct zip is 79,049,365 bytes, dated 2021-06-16. (3) Contents: 18 float32 X-ray images, each with a .rad file giving the detector pose and source position. CT and MR come only as per-vertebra L1-L5 crops, not whole-specimen volumes, so there is no surrounding soft tissue for DRR calibration. The LIT resource list has no other spine 2D-3D set.

verdicts.access_now: Downloadable NOW, unconditionally. GET https://lit.fe.uni-lj.si/data/research/resources/2D-3D-GS/2D-3D-GS.zip returns HTTP 200, Content-Type application/zip, Content-Length 79,049,365, Last-Modified Wed 16 Jun 2021 11:57:56 GMT, ETag "4b63295-5c4e0cd155900". No login, no click-through, no agreement form, no referer or UA check (a range request with an empty User-Agent returned HTTP 206 with Accept-Ranges: bytes, so it is resumable). I downloaded the full 79,049,365 bytes anonymously over WSL curl; md5 98c3aef06d5b218906301f68fb1600e9, magic PK\x03\x04, which is byte-identical to the copy already in the working tree at CTSpinoPelvic1K:2D-3D-GS.zip. The user guide is served separately at .../2D-3D-GS.pdf, 707,342 bytes, Last-Modified 2003-07-14 (identical in size to the local 2D-3D-GS_UG.pdf). The candidate's claim that the 2017 route is dead is CONFIRMED: http://lit.fe.uni-lj.si/contents/tools/GoldStandard/GSPublic/GSPublic.zip 301-redirects to https and then returns 404, and http://lit.fe.uni-lj.si/tools.php?lang=eng also 404s; the Wayback capture of 2017-05-03 shows that exact href, so the path is right and the file is simply gone. The archive holds no capture of the old zip itself (CDX prefix query on contents/tools/GoldStandard* returns no rows), so the 2017 bundle cannot be diffed against today's; the 2017 page advertised "76.3 MB" against today's 75.39 MiB, so the 2021-06-16 refresh probably changed the contents, and three top-level folder entries inside the zip carry 2021-06-16 timestamps while every file inside carries 2002-2004 ones. Access is NOT "on request" today, despite what both the bundled user guide and the two papers say.
verdicts.licence: Licence conflict CONFIRMED, and it is worse than a two-way conflict. (1) The live resource page (EN and SI alike) states, as free text, "License: Creative Commons (CC): BY-NC-ND" / "Licenca Creative Commons (CC): BY-NC-ND". It is unversioned (no 3.0/4.0), and the only hyperlink is to the Wikipedia article en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Commons_license, not to any creativecommons.org deed or legal code. There is no LICENSE file, licence notice or copyright header anywhere inside the zip (157 entries, checked). (2) The bundled user guide, page 2, still says the opposite: "The all rights to gold standard data posses the Laboratory of Imaging Technologies. The non-authorized distribution of this data is strictly forbidden. This gold standard data can only be obtained and used after signing the agreement form between the user and Imaging Technologies Laboratory." That PDF is dated 2003-07-14 and was never revised. (3) The two clauses are substantively contradictory, not merely stale in tone: CC BY-NC-ND expressly permits verbatim redistribution with attribution, while the guide forbids redistribution outright. (4) The 2017 site backs the guide, not the page: the archived tools page reads "The gold standard can only be accessed after signing the agreement with the Laboratory of Imaging Technologies" with PDF and DOC agreement forms linked; those forms are gone from the current page. (5) MICCAI 2002 (bundled in the zip) says "available on request from the authors" in both the abstract and the conclusion. For the product track the answer is unambiguous whichever clause governs: NC in every reading, plus ND, so no commercial use and no distribution of a derivative or adapted version. Given an unversioned free-text CC claim with no deed link, contradicted by the packaged document, I would not rely on the CC grant without written confirmation from LIT ([e-mail withheld]).
verdicts.counts: 157 zip entries, 210,162,660 bytes uncompressed. X-rays: exactly 18, im000-im017, each a 9,734,400-byte .raw (1560x1560 float32 = 2,433,600 px x 4 B) plus a ~260-byte ASCII .rad header. CT: 5 volumes, L1-L5, uint8 .raw + .sta header, 3,414,450 / 4,393,170 / 4,985,420 / 4,818,060 / 3,984,882 bytes. MR: 5 volumes, L1-L5, uint8, 829,872 / 1,097,790 / 1,246,168 / 1,200,420 / 999,702 bytes. Positions: 10 gold-standard 4x4 matrices (gold_ctL1-L5, gold_mrL1-L5), 10 target-point files (TpointsLX = 8 points each, CpointLX = 1 centre each), 20 initial-displacement files (rad_*, start_*, 118,800 B each = the standard start positions). Results: 20 precomputed registration files plus 16 analysed summaries. Matlab: 8 .m evaluation scripts. Documents: Tomazevic MSc thesis (3.45 MB) and the MICCAI 2002 paper (536 KB). NO segmentation masks or vertebra labels of any kind are in the archive.
verdicts.real_xray: Real, CONFIRMED, with caveats that matter for a fluoroscopy project. Per MICCAI 2002 (bundled), the images were captured on a Trixell PIXIUM 4600 digital flat-panel detector, 429x429 mm active area, 0.143 mm native pixels, 14-bit, then 3x3 median filtered and subsampled by 2 to remove dead-pixel artefacts, which is exactly the 0.286 mm pitch and 1560x1560 size in the .rad headers. These are NOT fluoroscopic frames and NOT C-arm frames: "To simulate C-arm acquisition X-ray source and sensor plane were fixed while the spine phantom was rotated on a turntable", deliberately, so as to avoid C-arm gravitational sag and mechanical distortion. So the set contains none of the distortion, sag, vignetting, circular field or image-intensifier geometry a real C-arm shows, which is the whole difficulty in the fluoro formation work. 18 poses at a 20 deg step about the specimen's long axis, 0 to 340 deg. Pixel values are float, not log-attenuation-normalised: im000 spans 0 to 1255.04, median 48.5, and the guide notes "the best range to observe the vertebra bone is 0-110". The subject is a water-filled tube phantom, not a body: no arms, no bowel gas, no scatter from a torso.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same specimen, yes, but the distributed form is heavily restricted, and the candidate's stated reason for that restriction is wrong. CT is a GE HiSpeed CT/i at 100 kV, 0.273438 mm in-plane, 1 mm slices; MR is a Philips Gyroscan NT Intera 1.5 T T1, 0.390625 mm in-plane, 1.9 mm slices, bias-corrected. Both ship ONLY as five per-vertebra crops. The binding limitation is NOT absence of soft tissue but the intensity type: DataType is uint8 in every .sta header and the guide confirms "unsigned 8 bit format". The volumes are rescaled 8-bit, so there are no Hounsfield units and no attenuation calibration is possible without refitting an unknown window. The crops are also NOT bone-masked: L1 is 325x309x34 (88.9 x 84.5 x 34.0 mm), L3 is 341x340x43 (93.2 x 93.0 x 43.0 mm), exactly 0.0 per cent zero voxels, border median 64 = the water/soft-tissue bulk value, so the surrounding medium IS inside each box. What the boxes cut off is the plastic tube wall, the six fiducial markers and everything past roughly a 97 mm transverse field, all of which do appear in the 18 X-rays, so a DRR of any crop is missing attenuating material that is present in the corresponding radiograph.
