The clinically applied physician-approved 6-DoF alignments were used to define the true-negative class but are not described as a released annotation, and the simulated errors are in-plane 2-D translations of the DRR along the spinal column found by a cross-correlation grid search (manually, for hardware/pathology cases), not 6-DoF pose perturbations. There are no per-vertebra naming labels and no landmarks.
'5,700-9,372 training pairs per fold' mis-labels the quantity: those are training-SET sizes in the leave-one-institution-out folds; the corpus totals 3,184 real x-rays and 9,552 two-channel arrays.

'is_update_of_known' has the chronology backwards. This paper is 2023; Charters et al. is 2024. And Charters 2024 is 527 UCLA patients / 4,213 images total (254 is only its paired-kV subset), so 'larger than the 254-patient Charters 2024 set' is true only against that subset.
No code accompanies this paper (no GitHub/GitLab link anywhere in the record). The public github.com/jcharters-mp/DRR belongs to the sibling Charters work.

Same-lineage precedent argues against a future release: the Charters 2024 sibling (10.1088/2057-1976/ad2baa) states outright, 'The data cannot be made publicly available upon publication because they contain sensitive personal information.' The whole UCLA ExacTrac lineage is on-request, and no member of it has ever been deposited.
Corresponding author Rachel Petragallo defended in 2024; the UCLA address on the paper is likely stale. James M Lamb (senior author, rosaml.net) is the durable contact.

verdicts.real_xray: Real. Confirmed kV acquisitions, not DRRs, not MV portal, not simulated: Brainlab ExacTrac, two floor-mounted kilovoltage tubes projecting obliquely through the patient onto ceiling-mounted flat panels, acquired at the treatment couch on real radiotherapy patients at six institutions. 3,184 real clinical x-ray images (two per fraction). CAVEAT that the candidate hides: only the x-ray half of each pair is real. The paired DRR is rendered from the planning CT, and the entire positive class ("off-by-one shift") is manufactured by translating the DRR along the spinal column while the x-ray stays put. No real misaligned x-ray exists in the set; the authors state they visually verified the clinical images contained no actual treatment errors.
verdicts.paired_ct: Not in the dataset as assembled. Refuted as stated. A planning ("simulation") CT necessarily exists per patient clinically, because ExacTrac renders its DRRs from it, but for this 429-patient multi-institutional cohort only anonymised x-ray/DRR pairs were exported from each site into the central UCLA database. No CT volumes were collected. Simulation CT DICOM files were extracted only for a separate, smaller, UCLA-only study (83 patients, 317 fractions, 634 x-rays; dissertation Ch. 3, the stereoscopic-geometry work), not for this one. So there is no CT or CBCT of the same subject available here, and nothing that would support 2D-3D work on this cohort.
verdicts.anatomy: Thoracic spine only. Refuted for lumbar/sacrum/pelvis. Primary wording: "Each institution searched their own internal database to identify thoracic spine patients imaged using ExacTrac." Two independent reasons the region of interest is absent: (1) cohort selection was by thoracic plan name; (2) geometry. The same group's later open-access paper states the ExacTrac stereoscopic system "records oblique, non-orthogonal image pairs with a narrower field of view of 10 x 10 cm", against 30 x 40 cm for gantry AP/LAT. A 10 cm oblique field centred on a thoracic target cannot contain the sacrum or pelvis, and reaches at most T12/L1 for the lowest targets. The images are also oblique stereoscopic pairs, not AP/lateral projections.
verdicts.counts: 429 patients, 1,592 treatment fractions, 3,184 real x-ray images, 9,552 two-channel arrays. Per-institution: UCLA 87 pts / 330 fx / 660 images; Inst 2: 72 / 246 / 492; Inst 3: 45 / 228 / 456; Inst 4: 38 / 116 / 232; Inst 5: 174 / 642 / 1,284; Inst 6: 13 / 30 / 60. One x-ray/DRR pair per fraction was kept (the last of the fraction); each fraction yields two stereoscopic x-rays, each treated independently. 3,184 x 3 = 9,552 arrays, because each real x-ray is paired with three DRRs (unshifted, shifted up one body, shifted down one body). The candidate's "5,700-9,372" is the per-fold training-array count under leave-one-institution-out, not a count of distinct images.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: Binary only. Refuted as stated. The model input is an x-ray/DRR array with a label of "no-error" or "shift"; the shifted class additionally carries a direction (superior or inferior). There are no 6-DoF pose values, no projection matrices, no landmarks, no vertebra identity labels and no segmentations in this dataset. The physician-approved clinical alignment was used only to define the true-negative class, not released as a pose. ExacTrac 6-DoF shift coordinates were recorded in the separate UCLA-only Ch. 3 study, not here. For a level-naming or registration project this set carries no usable geometric ground truth.
verdicts.licence: None. No open licence and no dataset licence. Crossref records only Wiley's VOR terms-and-conditions URL (http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/termsAndConditions#vor), which is a paywall term, not a reuse grant. OpenAlex oa_status "closed"; EuropePMC isOpenAccess "N", license null, no dataLinksTagsList. The only open artifact in this lineage is the author's UCLA dissertation on eScholarship, which is the text, not the data.
verdicts.access_now: No public access, no deposit found. Paper is paywalled (Wiley 403 to every route tried: plain curl, curl_cffi chrome impersonation, WebFetch, r.jina.ai, and both Crossref text-mining endpoints for PDF and full-XML). Not in PMC or EuropePMC despite AHRQ funding (R01 HS026486); pmcid null. OpenAlex lists no repository copy. No Zenodo/TCIA/figshare/GitHub deposit located. I could NOT read the Wiley data-availability statement at the source; two independent search indexes return the same wording, "Research data will be shared to the extent allowed under Institutional Review Board approval and institutional data-sharing agreements, upon request to the corresponding author" — treat that as second-hand. Practically: 429 patients under a six-site IRB with institutional data-sharing agreements, obtainable only by negotiated request to James Lamb at UCLA, with no expectation of redistribution.
corrections: ANATOMY REFUTED. Candidate says 'Spine (radiotherapy targets)', which reads as open. The cohort is thoracic spine only, by explicit plan-name selection at all six sites. No lumbar, sacral or pelvic cohort exists in this dataset.

FOV REFUTED for the target anatomy. ExacTrac records oblique, non-orthogonal pairs at a 10 x 10 cm field of view (stated by the same group in Charters 2024, open access). Sacrum and pelvis are geometrically impossible on a thoracic target; T12/L1 could edge in at best. The candidate's record gives no FOV.

PAIRED CT REFUTED. 'ct_or_cbct_same_subject: true' is wrong for this cohort. Only x-ray/DRR pairs were collected centrally. Simulation CT DICOMs were extracted only for a separate UCLA-only 83-patient / 317-fraction / 634-x-ray study. A planning CT exists clinically but is not part of the assembled multi-institutional dataset and is not obtainable with it.

LABELS REFUTED. 'Physician-approved clinical 6-DoF alignments' overstates the record. The released label is binary ('no-error' / 'shift') plus a shift direction. No 6-DoF values, projection matrices, landmarks, vertebra identities or masks. The clinical alignment only defined which images counted as correct.

IMAGE COUNT INCOMPLETE. 'n_images: 1,592 fractions' undercounts and mislabels. Real x-ray count is 3,184 (two stereoscopic images per fraction). The 9,552 figure is two-channel arrays, i.e. each real x-ray reused three times against three DRRs. '5,700-9,372' is a per-fold training count, not distinct images.

HALF-SYNTHETIC. The candidate's 'real_xray: true' is true but incomplete: every positive example is a real x-ray paired with a deliberately translated DRR, produced by a cross-correlation grid search and manual selection. No real misaligned acquisition is present.

LINEAGE INVERTED. Candidate frames this as 'new counts' and 'larger than the 254-patient Charters 2024 set'. This paper is from March 2023 and PREDATES Charters (Feb 2024); it is the earlier work in the lineage, not an update of it. Charters 2024 is the one with thoracic AND lumbar anatomy at 30 x 40 cm AP/LAT, and its own data-availability statement says the data cannot be made publicly available because they contain sensitive personal information.

INSTITUTION LIST NOT SUPPORTED. Candidate names seven places (UCLA, UCSF, Beth Israel Lahey, UAMS, UT Health San Antonio, Piedmont, Kaiser) for six data-contributing institutions. Those are author affiliations. The per-site table is anonymised as 'Institution 2' through 'Institution 6'; only UCLA is identified with its counts. The mapping of named sites to contributed data is not stated in any source I could read.
ACCESS: no deposit exists. Closed at Wiley, absent from PMC/EuropePMC despite AHRQ funding, no repository copy in OpenAlex. Candidate's 'access: unknown' should be 'on request only, no deposit'.

DATA STATEMENT NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Wiley returned 403 to every route I tried, including the Crossref text-mining PDF and XML endpoints. The 'shared to the extent allowed under IRB approval... upon request to the corresponding author' wording comes from two search indexes, not from my own read of the article.

CONFIRMED, for the record: real kV (not MV portal, not DRR-only, not phantom); 429 patients; 1,592 fractions; six institutions; Brainlab co-author (Pascal Bertram, Brainlab AG, Munich); stereoscopic ExacTrac; DOI, year and journal all correct.

FITNESS FOR A SPINE FLUOROSCOPY PROJECT: low. Thoracic-only, 10 cm oblique fields, no CT, no pose, no per-vertebra labels, closed access, and it is setup radiography rather than fluoroscopy. If the lumbar/sacral anatomy is what is wanted, Charters 2024 (10.1088/2057-1976/ad2baa) is the paper in this lineage that has it, and it is also not publicly releasable.

candidate.name: NAIST/Osaka EOS–CT total hip arthroplasty cohort (Suehara, Gu, Otake, Uemura, Sato; MICCAI 2025 paper 5182)
candidate.why_relevant: A new device in the known Osaka/NAIST lineage: 77 real EOS biplanar pelvis and hip radiographs, each 2D-3D registered to the same patient's CT, before and after surgery, so the pose can be recovered. It is the only real slot-scanner-to-CT pairing found in this pass. The dataset link reads N/A, so this is a collaboration lead only.
candidate.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology; Osaka University; Kameda Daiichi Hospital; Niigata University
candidate.device: EOS biplanar low-dose slot-scanning radiography, plus clinical CT
candidate.anatomy: Pelvis, hip, proximal femur
candidate.pose_or_labels: 2D-3D registration of each EOS image to CT
candidate.is_update_of_known: osaka/naist hip radiographs + qct (gu, otake et al.); osaka university / naist hip-disease cohort

verdicts.access_now: NOT DOWNLOADABLE, and there is no request route stated either. The primary record (papers.miccai.org/miccai-2025/0308-Paper5182.html) exists and resolves HTTP 200. Its own metadata block reads verbatim: "Supplementary Material: Not Submitted | Link to the Code Repository N/A | Link to the Dataset(s) N/A". The accepted-manuscript PDF (10 pp, 1,849,023 bytes, HTTP 200) contains NO data-availability statement, NO code statement, NO ethics/IRB statement, and no "available upon reasonable request" language — grep over the full extracted text for availab|consent|ethic|review board|approv|request returns only unrelated prose plus Acknowledgments (MEXT/JSPS KAKENHI 19H01176, 20H04550, 21K16655, 23K15714; AMED JP25hma322015) and "Disclosure of Interests". So this is weaker than a promise: the paper makes no release commitment at all. The published chapter (DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-05141-7_17) resolves to a PAYWALLED SpringerLink page (Buy Chapter USD 29.95; eBook USD 69.99/89.99); its landing page shows no Data-availability section. The SharedIt read-only link rdcu.be/eHw52 is live (HTTP 202) but serves the article text only, not data. The only artefact obtainable now is the free accepted PDF. Correctly classified as "unreleased no route" — a collaboration-lead only. Contact route inferable from the PDF corresponding addresses {gu.yi.gu4, otake, yoshi}@is.naist.jp.
verdicts.licence: None for data — no dataset exists to licence, and none is stated anywhere in the record. Paper licensing: the accepted manuscript is freely readable on papers.miccai.org (MICCAI open-access proceedings mirror; no explicit CC licence tag found on the page); the version of record on SpringerLink is paywalled (not open access). No DUA, no registry entry, no repository identifier.
verdicts.counts: The paper's own counts do not reconcile, and the candidate inherited the ambiguity. Abstract: "77 pairs of pre- and postoperative EOS images and CT scans". Table 1, Institution 2 (fine-tuning/testing cohort): CT 3D — 77 patients, 77 images; EOS 2D — 77 patients, 77 images. So the table gives 77 images per modality TOTAL, which cannot simultaneously cover a pre-op and a post-op time point for 77 patients (that would be 154 each). Section 3.3 does report a genuine pre-vs-post comparison (PCC 0.995 between pre- and post-op CT aBMD; RMS-CV 1.01% for CT ground truth, 2.67% fine-tuned EOS), so two time points do exist in their archive. Best reading: 77 patients, each with pre- and post-op EOS and CT, and Table 1 is counting one time point (or counting patients). The paper never states a total image count covering both stages. Cohort demographics: 70 female / 7 male, height 153.8 +/- 8.0 cm, weight 59.2 +/- 9.9 kg, BMI 25.0 +/- 3.7. A SEPARATE, larger cohort exists and is also unreleased: Institution 1 pre-training set, 600 patients (484 F / 116 M), 600 lower-extremity CTs with a B-MAS200 QCT phantom plus 2,461 conventional hip radiographs (4-5 per patient). No file sizes, formats or per-file manifests are given anywhere for either cohort.
verdicts.anatomy: Hip, NOT spine. EOS acquisition is full-body standing (Table 1 field of view: "Whole body"), but the paired CT for the EOS cohort is "Pelvis to knee" (text: "complementary lower-limb CT scans"), and the analysis region is the proximal femur only — CT "from the pelvis to the knee" with "the proximal femoral region" extracted by landmark detection, "replicating the imaging range typically used in DXA examinations". Left and right hips are treated as two separate samples for BMD. This is decisive for a spine project: the whole-body EOS film would depict the spine, but the co-registered 3D reference volume does NOT cover the thoracolumbar spine, so no spine-level 3D ground truth could be derived even if the data were released. The pre-training cohort is narrower still (CT "Lower extremity", radiographs "Hip").
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same-patient CT is real and confirmed, with actual 2D-3D registration performed — not a promise. Pipeline per PDF Sec. 2.3: Bayesian U-Net musculoskeletal segmentation and femoral landmarks from CT (ref [6] Hiasa 2019), then 2D-3D registration (ref [9] Otake 2012) to align CT to the EOS image, then DRR generation aligned to the EOS image. So a recovered pose exists internally for each EOS-CT pair. QCT calibration differs by cohort: Institution 1 phantom-based (B-MAS200, Kyoto Kagaku), Institution 2 phantom-LESS using a fixed scanner-specific curve (same scanner model, 120 kVp, same kernel). Caveat: none of these registrations, poses, DRRs or segmentations are published — the only public output is the paper's numbers.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes — real clinical EOS slot-scanning radiographs of living THA patients, plus a real conventional-radiograph pre-training cohort (2,461 films). Not synthetic. But note the DRRs used for training targets ARE synthetic renders derived from the paired CT; the EOS images themselves are the real input domain.
corrections: ACCESS CLAIM ITSELF IS CONFIRMED EXACTLY: 'unreleased no route' is correct and if anything understates it — the record says 'N/A' for both dataset and code, supplementary material was 'Not Submitted', and the paper carries no data-availability statement at all, not even an 'upon reasonable request' promise.

'77 real EOS BIPLANAR ... radiographs, each 2D-3D registered' is WRONG on the biplanar point. EOS is a biplanar modality, but this study used ONE view: PDF Sec. 2.4 states 'We used only frontal images from EOS in this experiment', and the authors' rebuttal says 'We restricted this first study to the AP view to test feasibility in settings where legacy datasets include only a single projection', listing dual-branch/cross-view fusion as future work. Whether lateral EOS views were even retained in their archive is not stated. Do not count this as a biplanar registered pair.

ANATOMY IS OVERSTATED FOR A SPINE PROJECT. The candidate lists 'Pelvis, hip, proximal femur' without flagging that the paired CT is 'Pelvis to knee' only. The whole-body EOS film shows the spine; the co-registered CT does not. No spine-level 3D reference is obtainable from this cohort as described.

IMAGE COUNT DOES NOT RECONCILE IN THE SOURCE. 'n_images: 77 EOS-CT pairs' plus 'before and after surgery' implies 154 EOS and 154 CT, but Table 1 lists 77 images for each modality. Section 3.3's pre/post comparison confirms two time points exist, so the paper is internally inconsistent. Report as '77 patients; pre- and post-op EOS+CT acquired; total image count not stated'.

INSTITUTION MAPPING IS AN INFERENCE, NOT STATED. The paper anonymises the cohorts as 'Institution 1' (600-patient pre-training) and 'Institution 2' (77-patient EOS). It never says which named affiliation supplied the EOS data. Attributing the EOS cohort to Kameda Daiichi / Niigata (or the 600 to Osaka) is plausible from authorship and from ref [11] Uemura 2022, but is not sourced.

AFFILIATION LIST IS INCOMPLETE. The candidate omits CentraleSupelec / Universite Paris-Saclay, France (Hugues Talbot), and the author list omits Okamoto Masashi and Tokunaga Kunihiko. Full list: Suehara(1), Gu(1), Otake(1), Uemura(2), Okamoto(3,4), Tokunaga(4), Talbot(5), Sato(1) with 1=NAIST, 2=Osaka University, 3=Kameda Daiichi Hospital, 4=Niigata University, 5=CentraleSupelec/Paris-Saclay.

'Only real slot-scanner-to-CT pairing found in this pass' is a claim about the search pass, not about this record — I could not verify or refute it from the primary source and did not attempt an exhaustive counter-search. Treat as unverified.

LINEAGE CLAIM ('is_update_of_known: osaka/naist hip radiographs + qct') is SUPPORTED by the reference list: the method is fine-tuned from BMD-GAN (Gu et al., MedIA 2023, ref [4]) and MSKdeX (Gu et al., MICCAI 2023, ref [5]), and the QCT calibration derives from Uemura et al., Archives of Osteoporosis 2022 (ref [11]). Note that this group's public releases have been SOFTWARE, not imaging data (e.g. ref [11] is an 'open-source measurement system'; NAIST-ICB/HipOA-Grading is a code repo) — there is no precedent of this cohort's images being released, which lowers the odds of a future public drop.

COULD NOT FULLY CHECK the version-of-record front matter: SpringerLink is paywalled (USD 29.95) and its landing page shows no Data-availability section, but I could not read the published chapter's back matter to rule out a statement absent from the accepted manuscript.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real acquisitions. The 77 Institution-2 images are EOS low-dose biplanar slot-scan radiographs of living pre-THA patients (kV diagnostic, not MV portal, not simulated). Rendering Fig. 2(b) confirms genuine full-body standing frontal and lateral EOS films with soft tissue, bowel gas and body contour. Caveat: DRRs are everywhere in this pipeline - CT-derived DRRs are the training targets and the networks OUTPUT predicted DRRs - so any file ever obtained from this group must be checked field by field. The 2461 Institution-1 images are real conventional hip radiographs.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same-subject CT, with two limits the candidate omits. Institution 2: 77 patients, each with one EOS and one lower-limb CT, 2D-3D registered (citing Otake et al. 2011/2012) to build DRR/EOS pairs. But Table 1 gives the CT field of view as "Pelvis to knee", so there is no lumbar-spine CT; and "the pose can be recovered" is overstated - the paper reports no pose parameters, no registration accuracy anywhere, no EOS geometry or calibration model (an EOS vertical slot scan is not a single cone-beam view and the paper never says how that was handled), and no code. Institution 1 separately has 600 patients with 600 phantom-calibrated (B-MAS200) lower-extremity CTs plus 2461 conventional hip radiographs, same-patient and also registered - a larger real X-ray-to-CT pairing, equally unreleased.
verdicts.anatomy: Split answer. In the 2D images: whole body. Table 1 gives EOS field of view "Whole body", and the rendered Fig. 2(b) shows head-to-feet frontal and lateral films in which the entire thoracic and lumbar spine, sacrum and pelvis are plainly visible. In the CT and in every label: hip only. CT is pelvis-to-knee, the registration and DRR generation extract "the proximal femoral region based on landmark detection", and the networks are fed "trimmed" pelvis/proximal-femur crops. The sacrum is only implied by the word "pelvis" and is never stated. Nothing spinal is measured, labelled or registered. The candidate's "Pelvis, hip, proximal femur" understates the 2D content and overstates the 3D/label content.
verdicts.counts: Institution 2 (the EOS cohort): 77 patients, 70 female / 7 male, 77 CT volumes, 77 EOS images - one EOS and one CT per patient per Table 1, not 77 pre-plus-post pairs. 5-fold CV over 77 patients (61-62 train / 15-16 test); BMD samples doubled to ~154 by treating left and right hip separately (the from-scratch arm is described as ~120 training images, consistent with 154 x 4/5). Institution 1 (pre-training only): 600 patients, 484 F / 116 M, 600 CTs, 2461 conventional X-rays at 4-5 per patient in abduction, adduction, standing, supine and resting positions.
verdicts.licence: None. The MICCAI open-access page lists "Link to the Code Repository: N/A" and "Link to the Dataset(s): N/A"; the PDF carries no data-availability statement, no DUA, no repository and no registry id. Only funding (MEXT/JSPS KAKENHI 19H01176, 20H04550, 21K16655, 23K15714; AMED JP25hma322015) and a no-competing-interests note.
verdicts.access_now: No route, as the candidate says. Reviewer 1 on the same page states "The submission does not mention open access to source code or data." Stronger evidence against a near-term route: the same senior authors' public tutorial repo for the directly preceding work states "The authors do not have the rights to release the research data used in the paper limited by IRBs" and "Due to the intellectual property protection we do not public the research-level code." Collaboration/e-mail lead only (gu.yi.gu4, otake, yoshi @is.naist.jp). Even if granted, the deliverable for a spine project would be whole-body EOS films with hip-only CT and hip-only labels.
corrections: "77 EOS-CT pairs ... before and after surgery" is not supported as 77 pre plus 77 post. Table 1 lists 77 patients / 77 CT / 77 EOS for Institution 2, and section 2.1 describes these patients as "scheduled to receive THA and had no other implants in either hip prior to surgery", i.e. preoperative. The abstract's phrase "77 pairs of pre- and postoperative EOS images and CT scans" contradicts its own Table 1. Section 3.3 does compare pre- vs post-operative CT and EOS, so some post-operative exams exist, but their number is never stated anywhere in the paper.

"biplanar ... radiographs" as usable data is refuted for this paper: section 2.4 states "We used only frontal images from EOS in this experiment." The acquisition is biplanar and lateral views appear in Fig. 2, but no lateral data, no biplanar calibration and no stereo geometry are described or evaluated. Reviewer 1 raised this as a weakness.

"pelvis and hip radiographs" is wrong about the images. They are whole-body standing EOS films (Table 1 FOV "Whole body"; Fig. 2(b), rendered, shows head to feet). The pelvis/hip crop is a preprocessing step ("Trimmed anterior EOS images"), not the acquisition.

"so the pose can be recovered" is an inference, not a stated result. The paper says 2D-3D registration was performed and cites a C-arm fiducial-based intensity method (Otake et al., IEEE TMI), but reports zero registration accuracy, zero pose values, no EOS slot-scan projection model, and releases no code. Treat the registration quality as unmeasured.

The lumbar spine and sacrum ARE in the 2D EOS images but have no 3D counterpart here: CT field of view is "Pelvis to knee". There is no lumbar-spine CT for these subjects, the sacrum is never named, and every label and ground truth is hip (proximal-femur aBMD/vBMD; gluteus maximus/medius/minimus, iliacus, obturator externus volumes). For level identification or spine registration this cohort supplies real standing spine radiographs with no paired spine 3D and no spine labels.

"Labels" are automatic, not human: musculoskeletal segmentations and femoral landmarks come from a trained Bayesian U-Net (Hiasa et al. 2019) applied to CT, and BMD ground truth for the EOS cohort is PHANTOM-LESS QCT using a fixed scanner-specific calibration curve averaged from a prior study, not per-scan phantom calibration. Reviewer 1 flagged exactly this chain-of-estimation risk. No human-verified annotation of any kind is documented.

"the only real slot-scanner-to-CT pairing found in this pass" is a claim about the search, not about this paper, and no primary source supports it. Note also that the same paper's Institution-1 cohort (600 patients, 2461 real conventional hip radiographs, 600 same-patient phantom-calibrated CTs) is a larger real X-ray-to-CT pairing, and is equally unreleased.

Institution attribution is an inference. The paper names only "Institution 1" and "Institution 2" and never maps either to the listed affiliations (NAIST; Osaka University; Kameda Daiichi Hospital; Niigata University; CentraleSupelec). Assigning the EOS cohort to a named hospital is not stated in the source.
"MICCAI 2025 Paper 5182" is the submission id, not a citable identifier. The record is doi:10.1007/978-3-032-05141-7_17, LNCS 15970, pp. 168-177 (DOI verified to resolve).

Generalisability is narrow and the authors say so: 77 patients, 70 female / 7 male, Japanese THA cohort, single institution for the EOS arm, no external validation; limitations list small sample size, one-or-two-institution data, and positioning/protocol variation.

candidate.name: Alphatec Spine dual C-arm pedicle-screw pairing set (Suh et al., SPIE Medical Imaging 2026)
candidate.why_relevant: Real AP and lateral C-arm images of pedicle screws and screw towers. Screw correspondence between views was set with reference needles, and screw 6-DoF pose comes from CAD 2D-3D alignment, so the set carries screw and needle labels. It is industry data, collection is still ongoing, and no release is mentioned. The subjects (cadaver or sawbones) were not determined. There is no CT.
candidate.institution: AIX Research, Alphatec Spine; Vanderbilt (Moyer)
candidate.device: C-arm (vendor not stated)
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine instrumentation (pedicle screws)
candidate.pose_or_labels: Screw AP/lateral correspondence from reference needles; screw 6-DoF pose from CAD registration

verdicts.access_now: NOT AT ALL. The paper is real and verified; the dataset does not exist as a retrievable artifact. arXiv:2511.05702v1 (submitted 2025-11-07) returns HTTP 200 for abs/html/pdf; Crossref confirms DOI 10.1117/12.3082927 = Proc. SPIE 13927, "Medical Imaging 2026: Image-Guided Procedures, Robotic Interventions, and Modeling", paper 139271W, p. 66, Vancouver 2026-02-15/20, issued 2026-04-01. Against that, every route to the data is absent: the full text (I read all 8 pages, incl. Acknowledgements and References) contains NO data-availability statement, NO code statement, NO repository, NO URL, NO contact-for-data line, NO IRB/ethics statement. The arXiv abs page lists no ancillary files. The corresponding author's GitHub (github.com/yehyunsuh, 51 repos) contains nothing for this paper although he ships public code for his other papers ("Code" buttons on his own site for other entries; this entry links only the paywalled SPIE .short). Zenodo query "pedicle screw" AND "C-arm" = 0 hits. Hugging Face datasets search "pedicle" = 0, "alphatec" = 0. GitHub repo search "pedicle screw c-arm CAD registration" = 0. The only forward-looking sentence is in Discussion: "Ongoing data collection efforts aim to incorporate a wider variety of screw types, patient anatomies, and imaging conditions. This expanded dataset will support broader validation..." — that is an expansion plan for internal use, not even a promise of release. This is industry data (ATEC AIX System team, screws and CAD models from ATEC); the CAD models are proprietary implant geometry, which is a structural reason release is unlikely. There is not even an "available upon reasonable request" sentence to act on. Route: none. The SPIE record itself is behind Imperva/Incapsula (plain curl and curl_cffi impersonate=chrome both blocked, 1.0-1.1 KB block page), but that is irrelevant since the arXiv preprint is the free full text.
verdicts.anatomy: NOT STATED in the paper, and the candidate's "Lumbar spine instrumentation" is an inference, not a source claim. The words cadaver, sawbones, phantom, specimen, human, bone, lumbar (except in a cited reference title), thoracic, vertebral level, L1-L5 appear ZERO times in the body. The only anatomical words are generic Introduction boilerplate ("pedicle screws are inserted into the vertebrae"). I rendered Figures 3 and 4 rather than argue from text: the images DO contain real spinal anatomy — a circular-FOV LAT view showing four to five vertebral bodies with visible endplates and disc spaces, and an AP view of the column with bilateral pedicle screws and screw towers. The bodies are large and rectangular, consistent with lumbar, so "lumbar" is visually plausible — but the paper never says it, never names a level, and never says whether the specimen is cadaver, patient, or a spine phantom. Report it as unstated.
verdicts.counts: Tiny, and no file-level information exists. Five screw "sets" (Table 1: Set 1-5; text: "100% accuracy in all five test cases"). Two screws per set — inferred from two possible combinations per set and from the Discussion's "12 degrees of freedom (DoF), which assumes the screw and tower are rigidly fixed" (2 screws x 6 DoF). Two views per set (AP + LAT). So on the order of 10 images used for classification/registration, plus a parallel ~10 needle-reference images that were captured then discarded for the experiment ("For the classification and registration, we use the images with the needles removed"). The entire "3.1 Dataset" section is TWO sentences and states only the needle trick. NO file count, NO byte size, NO image resolution, NO pixel spacing, NO bit depth, NO C-arm model, NO kVp/mA, NO acquisition date, NO number of subjects. Sizes are unknowable from the primary source.
verdicts.real_xray: YES — confirmed by rendering, not by the abstract. Figures 3 and 4 are genuine C-arm fluoroscopic frames: circular image-intensifier field of view with vignetted corners, real vertebral bodies, real pedicle screws and screw towers, real 22-gauge-looking reference needles, and in Figure 5 screw/tower pairs that have physically decoupled — an artifact you get from hardware, not from a renderer. The text consistently says "real image", "real screw", "the real fluoroscopic images". Crucially the Discussion proposes using DRRs *instead of* matrix projection for the CAD model, which confirms the target images are measured, not synthesized. Note the reference images have metal appearing DARK on a light background (transmission-like display), not the inverted convention.
verdicts.paired_ct: NONE, and the candidate is right for a stronger reason than it states. No CT or CBCT of the subject is mentioned anywhere. The paper's stated motivation is explicitly that preoperative CT is unavailable: it criticises Uneri et al. because "this method requires patient preoperative CT, which is not widely available in spine surgeries". The 3-D prior is the implant CAD mesh supplied by ATEC, not patient imaging. So there is no paired volumetric data to recover even if the images were released, and no vertebra-level 3-D ground truth of any kind.
verdicts.licence: NONE for data — no data licence exists because no data is distributed. For the paper text only: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence (a distribution licence to arXiv, NOT an open reuse/redistribution licence — it does not permit redistribution or derivative use). The SPIE proceedings version is under SPIE copyright; Crossref returns no `license` element for 10.1117/12.3082927 and the SPIE Digital Library page is bot-blocked, so open-access status could not be confirmed either way. The implant CAD models are proprietary ATEC property (Acknowledgements credit E. Zamarripa and T. Semingson "for providing ATEC screws and CAD models"), which independently blocks redistribution of the 3-D component.
corrections: The candidate's core access claim is CORRECT and I could not refute it: 'unreleased no route' is exactly what the primary source shows. Everything below concerns descriptive fields that overstate what the paper supports.

OVERSTATED: 'screw 6-DoF pose comes from CAD 2D-3D alignment, so the set carries screw and needle labels.' There is NO ground-truth 6-DoF pose anywhere in the paper. Pose is an OUTPUT of the optimiser, never validated against a reference — Table 2 reports only Dice and gradient-correlation loss, with zero mm or degree errors. The only ground truth in the paper is the binary PAIRING label (Table 1, 'Ground Truth is the correct combination in each sets'), established by the needle trick. Treating this as a pose-labelled set would import a label that does not exist.

UNSUPPORTED: anatomy 'Lumbar spine instrumentation'. The paper never names a spinal region or level; 'lumbar' occurs only inside a cited reference title. Rendering the figures shows a lumbar-APPEARING segment, but that is my reading of a picture, not a source claim.

UNSTATED, so do not assume it: what the reference mask for the reported Dice score is. Dice is never defined and the paper never says a real-screw segmentation mask was drawn. Whether pixel-level screw masks exist is unknown.

PARTLY MISLEADING: 'device: C-arm (vendor not stated)' is right, but there is a trap next to it — the Acknowledgements thank 'B. Aubert from EOS Imaging for discussion'. That is discussion only. EOS is NOT the imaging system here, and the images are plainly image-intensifier C-arm frames, not EOS slot-scan radiographs. Also unresolved: whether 'dual C-arm' means two physical C-arms or one C-arm at two angles — the text says both 'dual C-arm imaging is employed to provide two distinct views' and 'the projection matrices extracted from the c-arm' (singular).
CORRECT but note the basis: 'ct_or_cbct_same_subject: false' holds, and is stronger than mere silence — the paper's premise is that preop CT is unavailable.
CORRECT: 'subjects: Unknown'. No cadaver/sawbones/phantom/patient word appears, and there is no IRB, ethics, or specimen-source statement of any kind. Do not fill this field by guessing.
CORRECT: 'collection is still ongoing' — verbatim in Discussion, and it is an internal expansion plan, not a release promise.

Metadata nit: the candidate gives 'published: SPIE Medical Imaging 2026 (arXiv Nov 2025)'. Confirmed via Crossref, but note the arXiv abs page carries NO comments field naming the venue — the venue is verifiable only from Crossref, the SPIE DOI resolution, and the author's own site. Full citation: Proc. SPIE 13927, 139271W, p. 66, issued 2026-04-01.

COULD NOT CHECK: SPIE Digital Library full record. spiedigitallibrary.org is behind Imperva/Incapsula and returned a ~1 KB block page to both plain curl and curl_cffi impersonate=chrome. All SPIE-side facts above come from Crossref and the author's homepage, not from the SPIE page itself.

VERDICT FOR THE PROJECT: serves nothing downloadable. Even if it were released it is ~10 fluoroscopic frames of 10 screws with pairing labels only, no CT, no vertebra-level labels, and no stated anatomy — it cannot support level naming or counting-grade evaluation. Do not carry it as a pending or on-request source; it is absent, not gated.

verdicts.real_xray: Real C-arm fluoroscopy, confirmed by inference, never stated as a protocol. The paper has no acquisition section: no kVp, mA, detector, vendor, model, pixel size or frame count appears anywhere. Support is (a) wording throughout Sec. 2.3-3.3 — "the real image I_real", "the real screw", "the real fluoroscopic images", and critically "The elements p_ij^AP and p_ij^LAT are part of the projection matrices extracted from the c-arm"; (b) the five figures, which I downloaded and looked at: circular image-intensifier FOV with peripheral vignetting, blown-out rim, pincushion distortion and scatter, in inverted polarity (metal black, bone light grey). Not DRRs and not MV portal. DRRs appear exactly once, in the Discussion, as a proposed future speed-up for the forward projection step ("The use of digitally reconstructed radiographs instead of direct matrix-based projections may accelerate optimization") — i.e. for rendering the CAD model, not as the source of the images. The images also show zero soft-tissue attenuation (no psoas shadow, no bowel gas, no abdominal wall), so they are a bench/specimen setup, not a live patient.
verdicts.paired_ct: No. Confirmed and unambiguous. "CBCT" and "cone-beam" appear zero times; "CT" appears once, in the Introduction, and it is an argument against needing one: Uneri et al.'s known-component registration "requires patient preoperative CT, which is not widely available in spine surgeries." The whole method is CT-free by design — the 3-D prior is the screw CAD mesh supplied by the vendor, not a patient volume. There is no reconstructed volume of the imaged object at any point.
verdicts.anatomy: The paper NEVER states the anatomy. "Lumbar" appears once and it is inside reference [1]'s title ("Trends in lumbar spinal fusion"); "pelvi" appears once, inside reference [9]'s title ("2d/3d pelvis registration"); "sacrum"/"sacral" appear ZERO times; no vertebral level (L1-L5, T-anything) is named anywhere. The candidate's "Lumbar spine instrumentation" is an inference from figures, not a sourced claim. My own read of the figures: Fig. 3 and Fig. 1 show three to four lumbar-type vertebral bodies with endplates, disc spaces and posterior elements in both AP and LAT, with screws in pedicles — consistent with lumbar. Fig. 5's left (AP) panel shows a large arcuate bone I read as iliac wing/SI-region with lower lumbar or sacral bone in the middle of the field, but that is my read of a low-contrast figure, and the paper says nothing. So: lumbar spine visible in the frames — yes, by inspection. Sacrum or pelvis reliably present and identifiable — NOT established; refuted as a stated claim. Field of view is narrow (single circular II field centred on the instrumented segment), so there is no whole-spine context and nothing from which a vertebral level could be counted.
verdicts.counts: No image count, no subject count, and no specimen description are stated anywhere. What the paper actually gives: five "screw sets" (Tables 1 and 2, "Set 1" through "Set 5"), each evaluated under two candidate pairings, with "100% accuracy in all five test cases". The Discussion fixes the screws per set at two — "the current modeling of the system with 12 degrees of freedom (DoF), which assumes the screw and tower are rigidly fixed" (12 = 2 screws x 6 DoF), and Sec. 3.2 says the step "paired the left and right screws in the AP view with their corresponding screws in the LAT view". So the inferred scale is 5 AP + 5 LAT = ~10 fluoroscopic frames carrying 10 screw instances, plus a duplicate needle-present AP/LAT pair per set used only to fix the correspondence ground truth (Fig. 3) and then discarded ("For the classification and registration, we use the images with the needles removed"). Whether the 5 sets are 5 specimens, 5 segments of one specimen, or 5 re-rigs of the same construct is NOT stated. Words absent from the paper: cadaver (0), phantom (0), sawbones (0), specimen (0), subject (0), IRB (0), ethics (0). "Patient" occurs 3 times and never describes the data (preoperative CT availability; "wider variety of ... patient anatomies" as future work; patient-to-instrument calibration in the Bendini system).
verdicts.pose_or_labels: Two different things are being conflated in the candidate record. (1) Correspondence ground truth — REAL and confirmed: Sec. 3.1, "we aligned needles along one side of the screw towers ... the screw towers remained aligned with the needle, ensuring consistent matching between the two perspectives", illustrated in Fig. 3. That yields 5 binary labels (which of two AP-LAT pairings is correct). (2) 2-D landmarks — REAL: the screw tip and body centre are "derived by manually annotating corresponding landmarks on the 2D projections obtained from both views", i.e. 2 points x 2 screws x 2 views per set. (3) 6-DoF screw pose — NOT a label. It is the output of their differential-evolution optimiser, and there is no independent reference for it. The paper reports only Dice of the projected silhouette and the gradient-correlation loss per view (Table 2); it reports NO pose error in millimetres or degrees, no tracker or CT reference, and no repeatability. Calling the set one that "carries screw 6-DoF pose" overstates it — the set carries correspondence labels and 2-D keypoints; pose is an unvalidated estimate. There are no anatomical labels of any kind: no vertebra segmentation, no vertebral level, no anatomical landmarks, no C-arm pose relative to anatomy.
verdicts.access_now: Unreleased, no route — confirmed. There is no data availability statement, no repository link, no DOI for data, and no supplementary material in the arXiv version. I checked the corresponding author's GitHub (github.com/yehyunsuh, ~50 public repos, including several for his other registration papers) and there is no repo for this work. The Discussion states collection is still running: "Ongoing data collection efforts aim to incorporate a wider variety of screw types, patient anatomies, and imaging conditions." The data are industry-internal (Acknowledgements: "ATEC AIX System team", screws and CAD models from Alphatec/ATEC staff), which makes release unlikely. Only plausible route is a direct request to [e-mail withheld] (corresponding author, Vanderbilt) or Kongbin Kang (AIX Research, Alphatec Spine) — untested and unlikely to clear a device manufacturer.
verdicts.licence: No data licence exists, because no data is released. The preprint itself is under the arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license (stated on the HTML: "License: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license") — that covers the manuscript, not any images, and it is not an open licence for reuse of figures. The version of record is behind the SPIE paywall (Proc. SPIE 13927, 139271W), copyright SPIE. Nothing here is redistributable.
corrections: ANATOMY IS NOT SOURCED. The candidate asserts 'Lumbar spine instrumentation'. The paper never names the anatomy: 'lumbar' appears once and only inside a reference title, 'sacrum/sacral' appears zero times, 'pelvis' appears once and only inside a reference title, and no vertebral level is named. Lumbar vertebrae ARE visible in the figures by inspection, but the claim has no primary-source statement behind it. Sacrum/pelvis presence is refuted as a stated claim; at most one AP figure panel (Fig. 5) appears to include iliac-wing/SI-region bone, which is my visual read only.

6-DoF POSE IS AN OUTPUT, NOT A LABEL. The candidate says the set 'carries screw and needle labels' and that 'screw 6-DoF pose comes from CAD 2D-3D alignment'. There is no ground-truth pose anywhere: the paper reports only projection Dice and gradient-correlation loss (Table 2) and reports NO pose error in mm or degrees, against no tracker, CT or other reference. The real labels are (a) 5 binary AP/LAT correspondence labels from the needle trick, and (b) manually annotated 2-D tip and centre keypoints per screw per view.

NEEDLES ARE NOT A LABEL CARRIED BY THE DATA. The needles are visible only in the ground-truth-establishment frames and are explicitly removed from the frames used for the experiment: 'For the classification and registration, we use the images with the needles removed.' Any expectation of needle annotations on the working images is refuted.

NO SUBJECT, SPECIMEN OR IMAGE COUNT EXISTS IN THE SOURCE. 'Cadaver', 'phantom', 'sawbones', 'specimen', 'subject', 'IRB' and 'ethics' each appear ZERO times. The candidate's 'Unknown (industry test setup)' is right but should be recorded as an absence in the source, not an open question that a reading would settle. The only quantity given is five screw sets; two screws per set follows from the stated 12 DoF, so the scale is roughly 10 fluoroscopic frames and 10 screw instances. That is a case report's worth of data, not a dataset.

REAL-X-RAY IS TRUE BUT UNSTATED AS PROTOCOL. The paper has no acquisition section at all. I am confirming real acquisition from the figures (image-intensifier circular FOV, vignetting, saturation, pincushion, scatter, inverted polarity) plus 'projection matrices extracted from the c-arm' and repeated 'real image'/'real fluoroscopic images'. Nobody should cite the paper for an acquisition claim it does not make. DRRs are mentioned only as a future speed-up for rendering the CAD model.

THE FRAMES SHOW NO SOFT TISSUE. There is no psoas shadow, no bowel gas and no abdominal wall in any panel. These are not live-patient intraoperative frames whatever the surgical framing of the paper; a specimen or synthetic construct on a bench is the only reading the images support. Neither is stated.

NO C-ARM VENDOR, MODEL OR GEOMETRY IS DISCLOSED. The candidate correctly says 'vendor not stated'. Also undisclosed: SID, source-object distance, pixel spacing, image size, and how the per-view projection matrices were calibrated. 'Dual C-arm' is never resolved into two physical C-arms versus one C-arm at two angles.

PUBLICATION METADATA CONFIRMED AND TIGHTENED. Crossref on 10.1117/12.3082927 gives: Proc. SPIE vol. 13927, 'Medical Imaging 2026: Image-Guided Procedures, Robotic Interventions, and Modeling', paper 139271W (13927-66), event Vancouver, Canada, February 2026, published-print April 2026. Semantic Scholar's 'year: 2025' is the arXiv date and is wrong for the proceedings. Affiliations confirmed verbatim from the paper: 'AIX Research, Alphatec Spine, Carlsbad, CA, USA' and 'Department of Computer Science, Vanderbilt University, Nashville, TN, USA'; corresponding author [e-mail withheld].

UTILITY UNDER A CONTENT LENS IS LOWER THAN 'B' IMPLIES. Even if released, this is about ten frames of one narrow circular field over an instrumented segment, with no CT, no whole-spine context, no vertebral-level or anatomical label, and heavy metal occlusion of exactly the vertebral structures a level-identification model would need. It is a screw-correspondence method demonstration, not a spine imaging dataset.

candidate.name: FlowReg: universal spinal CT/X-ray registration (Shen, Nong, Zhou et al.; MICCAI 2026)
candidate.why_relevant: New fact about the known Hohai/Changzhou lumbar intraoperative X-ray plus CT lineage: a third paper, at MICCAI 2026, co-authored by the Changzhou clinical partner (Luming Nong). A repo was created on 2026-06-17 but holds only a README. The sibling lineReg README still lists 'Dual-view registration on Real X-rays' as not done. Neither repo has data or a data link. That FlowReg uses real X-rays is inferred from the lineage, not seen.
candidate.institution: Hohai University; Changzhou Second People's Hospital; USTC (S. Kevin Zhou)
candidate.xray_kind: Intraoperative X-ray (lineage; unverified for this paper)
candidate.anatomy: Lumbar spine
candidate.is_update_of_known: hohai university single-view lumbar 2d/3d registration set (shen et al., med phys 2026); changzhou/hohai lumbar intraoperative x-ray + ct

verdicts.access_now: No route. Nothing downloadable, and no request channel either. The GitHub repo github.com/shenao1995/FlowReg exists but is a GitHub-generated stub: one commit ("Initial commit", 2026-06-17T08:33:48Z, signed, by Shen Ao), one file (README.md, 9 bytes, literally "# FlowReg"), repo size 0 KB, no description, no homepage, no topics, no branches but main, no tags, no releases, no issues (open or closed), no license, no wiki content, 1 star. Not touched since the day it was created (pushed_at == created_at, still true on 2026-09-22, i.e. 97 days untouched). There is no data link, no download form, no "available on request" contact, no DUA, no email address in the repo at all. Not even code, let alone data. The paper itself is not readable yet: no arXiv preprint exists (arXiv API query all:"FlowReg" returns only the unrelated 2021 brain-MRI optical-flow FlowReg, arXiv:2101.09639, and a 2026 cardiac-MR flow-matching paper), no Crossref DOI, no Springer LNCS record — MICCAI 2026 runs 27 Sep - 1 Oct 2026, so the proceedings are not out as of today (2026-09-22), and papers.miccai.org/miccai-2026/ returns HTTP 401. So there is not even a data-availability statement to read. Strong negative prior from the same author: UBEReg (github.com/shenao1995/UBEReg), the repo for another registration paper, was created 2025-11-22 and 10 months later still holds only a 99-byte README and 0 KB of content. The one sibling repo that did get filled, RadGS_Reg, shipped code only — its data-generation script points at local Windows drives (G:/GS_DATA/vertebra_dataset, F:/BaiduNetdiskDownload/total_preprocess) with no public source.
verdicts.licence: None. The FlowReg repo has "license": null in the GitHub API and no LICENSE file — default all-rights-reserved. Same for lineReg and RadGS_Reg (both "license": null). No data licence is stated anywhere because no data is offered anywhere.
verdicts.counts: FlowReg repo total: 1 file, 9 bytes, repo size 0 KB. Zero imaging files, zero releases, zero release assets. The paper's own subject count is unknown because the paper is unreadable, but the lineage's in-house set is documented twice and is small: the MICCAI 2025 sibling RadGS-Reg states "The in-house dataset includes 10 real-scent [sic] intraoperative cases, each containing preoperative CT volumes (512x512x401 voxels, spacing 0.3x0.3x0.625 mm) and paired AP/LA X-rays (976x976 resolution, 1124 mm focal length). Thirty vertebral-level samples were extracted..." The Med Phys sibling (10.1002/mp.70385) uses the same 10 patients: 710 images (X-rays plus DRRs), 568 train / 142 test on a 4:1 patient-specific split, and "300 simulated samples and 90 real clinical samples" for registration. So the group's entire real-X-ray holding is 10 patients / ~90 real registration samples — and none of it has ever been released.
verdicts.real_xray: Still unverified for FlowReg itself, exactly as the candidate flagged. The title from the official program is "FlowReg: Reconstruction-Guided Flow Matching for Universal Spinal CT/X-ray Registration" — it says X-ray but does not distinguish real from DRR, and no paper text is obtainable. What IS now verified from primary sources is that the group holds real intraoperative X-rays: RadGS-Reg (MICCAI 2025 open-access PDF) says results were "analyzed using five-fold cross-validation on real X-ray data from the in-house dataset" and calls it "our proprietary real dataset"; the Med Phys abstract reports "90 real clinical samples". So real X-rays exist in Changzhou; whether FlowReg used them, and in what proportion versus DRRs, is inference from the lineage, not observed. Counter-evidence worth weighing: the lineReg README's release checklist still reads "Single-view registration on simulated X-rays. [done]" / "Dual-view registration on simulated X-rays. [not done]" / "Dual-view registration on Real X-rays. [not done]" — the group's own public roadmap puts real-X-ray work at the unfinished end.
verdicts.paired_ct: Paired same-subject CT is documented for the lineage but unverified for FlowReg. RadGS-Reg, verbatim: each in-house case contains "preoperative CT volumes (512x512x401 voxels, spacing: 0.3x0.3x0.625 mm) and paired AP/LA X-rays (976x976 resolution, 1124 mm focal length)", with "GT poses (CT-to-C-arm coordinate transformation) ... recorded during C-arm circular acquisitions to ensure geometric consistency". That is genuine paired preop-CT / intraop-X-ray with recorded ground-truth pose — which is exactly the rare asset — but it is 10 patients and it is not released. Public data used alongside it was VerSe'20 (253 lumbar CTs, 1280 vertebrae) with synthesised DRRs, not paired real radiographs.
verdicts.anatomy: Spine. FlowReg's title says "Universal Spinal", which suggests a claim beyond the lumbar-only scope of both siblings, but with no paper text the levels covered cannot be checked. The lineage is lumbar: RadGS-Reg used VerSe'20 lumbar CTs plus in-house lumbar cases; the Med Phys paper is explicitly "single-view lumbar spine 2D/3D registration". Treat "universal" as an unverified title word, not a verified coverage claim.
corrections: DEAD EVIDENCE URL: the cited https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shenao1995/lineReg/main/README.md returns 404. lineReg's default_branch is 'master', not 'main'. The working URL is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shenao1995/lineReg/master/README.md. The claim it was cited for does hold there: the News checklist reads 'Single-view registration on simulated X-rays. [checked]', 'Dual-view registration on simulated X-rays. [unchecked]', 'Dual-view registration on Real X-rays. [unchecked]'.

VENUE PRECISION: FlowReg is a POSTER, not an oral. Program entry T-AM-029, Poster Session 2 (Reconstruction, Synthesis and Image Quality), Tuesday 29 September 2026, 10:30-12:30. The conference itself has not happened yet (27 Sep - 1 Oct 2026, Strasbourg); as of 2026-09-22 there is no Springer chapter, no Crossref DOI and no arXiv preprint, so 'published: MICCAI 2026' should read 'accepted, not yet published'.

AUTHOR LIST: the record's 'Shen, Nong, Zhou et al.' is right but incomplete. Program gives: Ao Shen, Junfeng Jiang, Xueming Fu, Qiang Zeng, Ye Tang, Zhengming Chen, Luming Nong, Feng Wang, Shaohua Kevin Zhou. Presenter is Junfeng Jiang (Hohai University), not Shen. Luming Nong's presence is confirmed, so the Changzhou clinical tie is real.

INSTITUTION: the Changzhou clinical partner is printed in RadGS-Reg as 'The Third Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University, Changzhou Jiangsu, 213164' — that is the same hospital as Changzhou Second People's Hospital, but cite it as printed. Also missing from the record: a commercial co-author, Feng Wang of Tuodao Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (Nanjing), which is a navigation-robot vendor. An industry partner on the author list is a further reason a clinical intraoperative set will not be released.

SUBJECT COUNT: record says 'count unknown'. It can be tightened from the lineage's primary sources — 10 intraoperative patients, 30 vertebral-level samples (RadGS-Reg), 710 images / 90 real clinical registration samples across the same 10 patients (Med Phys). If FlowReg reuses this set, it is 10 patients, which is small even if it were ever released.

COULD NOT CHECK: the Medical Physics paper's formal Data Availability Statement. aapm.onlinelibrary.wiley.com returns HTTP 403 and the article is not open access (Europe PMC isOpenAccess=N, PMID 41833531). verdicts.real_xray: Not verified for FlowReg itself — no abstract, preprint, or proceedings text exists yet (arXiv API returns nothing for the title or for "Ao Shen" + this work; papers.miccai.org/miccai-2026 returns HTTP 401). Only the title is confirmed. REAL X-rays ARE confirmed for the same group's two prior papers, so the lineage inference is well founded but is still an inference: (a) Med Phys 2026 (PMID 41833531, Shen A, Jiang J, Tang Y, Chen Z, Nong L, Chen Q, Wang F, Wu X) — "2D/3D registration experiments were conducted separately on 300 simulated samples and 90 real clinical samples"; "On real clinical data, the method achieved a mean in-plane translation error of approximately 1.5 mm". (b) RadGS-Reg (MICCAI 2025, arXiv:2508.21154) §3.1 — "The in-house dataset includes 10 real-scent [sic: real-scene] intraoperative cases... and paired AP/LA X-rays (976x976 resolution, 1,124 mm focal length)", evaluated by "five-fold cross-validation on real X-ray data from the in-house dataset". (c) A third, previously unlisted paper — RadGS-Reg+, Med Image Anal 2026;115:104319 (PMID 42766966) — states "Experiments on a real intraoperative lumbar dataset". Kind = intraoperative C-arm fluoroscopy/radiography, kV, not MV portal, not DRR. Caveat that cuts the other way: in all three papers most of the imaging is DRR. The Med Phys 710-image segmentation set is explicitly "comprising X-rays and Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs" with NO breakdown given, and RadGS-Reg trains on 32,000 synthetic biplanar DRR pairs from VerSe'20 against only 10 real cases. The number of real X-ray frames is nowhere stated in any primary source.
verdicts.paired_ct: CT, not CBCT, and yes for the lineage — same subject, verified. RadGS-Reg §3.1: "10 real-scent intraoperative cases, each containing preoperative CT volumes (512x512x401 voxels, spacing: 0.3x0.3x0.625 mm) and paired AP/LA X-rays". Med Phys abstract: "aligning preoperative CT with intraoperative X-rays". Pose ground truth is also confirmed for the lineage: "Ground Truth poses (CT-to-C-arm coordinate transformation) were recorded during C-arm circular acquisitions to ensure geometric consistency" (RadGS-Reg §3.1). Other labels in the lineage: vertebral segmentation on CT (lineReg README expects `ct_seg.nii.gz`, "21-25 corresponds to L1-L5") and semantic vertebral-body edge masks (ESegMamba, Med Phys). NONE of this is verified for FlowReg; the candidate's `ct_or_cbct_same_subject: true` is a lineage inference, not a stated fact about this paper. No CBCT anywhere in the lineage — the only volumetric modality named is preoperative CT.
verdicts.anatomy: Lumbar vertebrae only, as far as any primary source states — and the sacrum/pelvis claim is unsupported. Med Phys title/purpose: "single-view lumbar spine 2D/3D registration"; RadGS-Reg+ title: "for lumbar CT/X-ray registration"; RadGS-Reg uses "253 lumbar spine Computed Tomography scans" from VerSe'20 and operates on cropped single-vertebra volumes at "vertebral-level"; lineReg's documented target selection is "L1-L5". The word sacrum does not appear in any source I opened, and pelvis appears nowhere as imaged anatomy. The FlowReg title says "Universal Spinal CT/X-ray Registration" — "universal" is undefined and may mean cross-region (cervical/thoracic) or cross-modality/cross-device generalisation; it is NOT evidence that the sacrum or pelvis is in the images. For a lumbosacral-junction use, note the images are vertebral-level crops in the two reconstruction papers, so even if S1 were in the field of view, the released framing is a single vertebra at a time.
verdicts.counts: FlowReg: unknown. No count of subjects, frames, or vertebrae is stated in any source that exists. Lineage counts (all small): 10 patients is the ceiling seen anywhere. Med Phys — 710 images (X-rays AND DRRs combined, no split given) from 10 patients, 568 train / 142 test on a 4:1 patient-specific split; registration on 300 simulated + 90 real clinical samples. RadGS-Reg — 10 real intraoperative cases, 30 vertebral-level samples, against 32,000 synthetic biplanar DRR pairs and 1,280 CT pairs from VerSe'20. RadGS-Reg+ — "a real intraoperative lumbar dataset", five-fold cross-validation, no n given in the abstract. If FlowReg reuses the same in-house cohort (likely, same clinical co-author and same institution), the real-X-ray subject count is on the order of 10 patients and the real-frame count is in the tens-to-low-hundreds.
verdicts.licence: None. No data licence exists because no data exists publicly. The FlowReg, lineReg and RadGS_Reg repositories all have `license: null` in the GitHub API (only shenao1995.github.io and the DiffDRR fork carry MIT). No DUA, no data-use terms, no registry entry, no ethics/data-availability statement reachable from any open source I could fetch (Wiley returns HTTP 403; the MedIA article is Elsevier and its Crossref record has no abstract or data statement).

verdicts.real_xray: NOT ESTABLISHED — treat as unknown, not true. Adversarial evidence pointing the other way: "Virtual-Supervision" is this lab's own house term. Xiongbiao Luo's group published "Virtually Supervised Depth-Aware Registration for Monocular Endoscopic Navigation" (Fang, G. Luo, Wu, Fan, Chen, X. Luo; IEEE T-ASE, 2026), where "virtually supervised" means supervision derived from virtual/rendered views of a CT volume — i.e. rendering-derived labels, the endoscopic analogue of DRR supervision. The candidate's own suspicion is therefore consistent with the group's naming convention, but it is a hypothesis, not a finding. It is equally possible the method is DRR-trained and evaluated on some real frames. I could not read a single sentence of the paper.
verdicts.paired_ct: UNVERIFIED. A method paper can also register to a phantom volume or to public CTs with synthesised projections, which would give "pairing" with no real paired patient at all.

The only skeletal items in 200 titles are two cervical-vertebra CT papers (Zhang et al., ICIP 2023 / IJCNN 2024) and two orthopaedic clinical meta-analyses. Whichever holds, it covers only the spreadsheet; no licence of any kind is asserted over the radiographs or CBCT, which are not in the record. The article itself is closed, VOR under Wiley terms, no CC licence in Crossref.
verdicts.paired_ct: Confirmed as a study design, unavailable as data. The PubMed abstract states horses imaged 2021-2023 with lateral radiographs AND standing CBCT of C6-C7 and C7-T1, 94 met inclusion, CBCT treated as the gold standard - so the same living horses were imaged both ways. But the released record contains no CBCT volume and no radiograph, only derived height measurements from each modality side by side. Nothing paired is downloadable.
verdicts.real_xray: Real diagnostic lateral radiographs of client-owned horses exist behind the study (retrospective clinical images, 2021-2023, New Bolton Center), and the standing CBCT implies live standing sedated animals rather than cadavers. None of those images is released. What is public is a table of centimetre measurements read off them. So real_xray=true for the study, false for anything you can obtain.

verdicts.access_now: Nothing usable now. The DSpace API shows the deposit's ORIGINAL bundle contains exactly ONE bitstream: "C7-T1 CT compared to radiographic measurement.xlsx" (2,711,323 bytes, MD5 aa8a331435e262d89eaadc66d3d2cddf). The other two bundles are a TEXT derivative (.xlsx.txt) and license.txt (a generic ScholarlyCommons submission agreement, no data terms). Zero image files; no DICOM/NIfTI/zip/tif anywhere on the item page or in the API. The spreadsheet downloads without login. The candidate's "images exist at Penn Vet and would have to be requested" has NO primary source: the item record carries no contact, no request procedure, and no dc.relation to the paper. I could not open the Wiley full text (Cloudflare 403 to curl, curl_cffi chrome impersonation, and a reader proxy), so I could not read the data availability statement myself; a search-engine index of it reads "The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Scholarly Commons at https://doi.org/10.48659/9e79-2q14" — i.e. it points at the spreadsheet only and says nothing about images. Treat "access: unreleased no route" as correct and "route on request" as unevidenced.
verdicts.anatomy: Equine caudal cervical / cranial thoracic spine only. PubMed abstract (primary): "Horses imaged between 2021 and 2023 with lateral radiographs and standing CBCT of C6-C7 and C7-T1 were included." The spreadsheet columns confirm the same scope and nothing else: "C7 body height CT (cm)", "7/1 Facet height L/R (cm)", "C6 body height CT (cm)", "6/7 Facet height L/R (cm)", plus the radiographic counterparts. NO lumbar spine, NO sacrum, NO pelvis, NO lumbosacral junction — in the released data or in the underlying study. For a lumbar/sacrum/pelvis fluoroscopy project this is out of anatomy entirely, and it is a quadruped cervical spine at that.
verdicts.counts: 94 is the STUDY cohort, not the released data. PubMed: "Ninety-four horses met inclusion criteria." But the deposited spreadsheet does not contain 94 horses. Sheet 1 ("Measurement data - Justine") has 30 populated data rows (rows 2-31; 617 total <v> cells over a 20-column header, one stray value at A34). Sheets 2 ("Bills Measurements") and 3 ("Brown Measurements") each hold the 15-case observer subset (rows 3-17). So the public release covers 30 horses of single-observer measurements plus a 15-horse two-observer subset — roughly a third of the cohort. Images: 0 released, for 0 subjects. The 2.7 MB file size is bloat (sheet1.xml declares dimension A1:AJ1048512, 36 MB of empty styled rows), not hidden content — the zip has no xl/media directory.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, in the study, and stated in a primary source. The inclusion criterion itself is same-subject pairing: horses had BOTH lateral radiographs AND standing CBCT of C6-C7 and C7-T1 (PubMed abstract, DataCite abstract). It is cone-beam CT, standing, in live clinical patients — not helical CT, and not a cadaver rig. The spreadsheet carries paired per-horse radiograph and CT measurements in the same row (e.g. "C7 body height CT (cm)" alongside "C7 body height rad (cm)"), which is consistent with same-subject pairing. But no paired IMAGES are released, so the pairing is unusable as data — it exists only as two numbers per horse.
verdicts.real_xray: Real acquisitions, but nothing you can see. The study is explicitly a retrospective clinical review of horses imaged 2021-2023 at New Bolton Center: real diagnostic lateral radiographs of live standing horses, and real standing CBCT. Not DRRs, not simulated, not MV portal — and the paper's stated motivation is physical radiographic geometry (scapular superimposition, divergent beam, object-to-detector distance) causing magnification, which only arises with a real source-detector setup. The paper also lists "variability in image quality" as a limitation, consistent with heterogeneous clinical acquisitions. Caveat: I verified "real" from the study description only; I have seen no pixel data, because none is published. "real_xray: true" is a property of an inaccessible archive, not of this deposit.
verdicts.licence: The candidate's "CC BY-NC 4.0" is contradicted by the repository itself. DataCite (api.datacite.org/dois/10.48659/9e79-2q14) gives rightsIdentifier "cc-by-nc-4.0". The DSpace item record for the same object gives dc.rights.uri = https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ (CC BY 4.0), and that is the only CC URI rendered on the item page. The two primary records disagree; neither is obviously authoritative. license.txt in the LICENSE bundle is only the ScholarlyCommons submission agreement and resolves nothing. Whichever holds, it covers the spreadsheet alone — no image licence exists because no images are published.
corrections: REFUTED as stated: the deposit does not release 94 horses. Sheet 1 holds 30 data rows (rows 2-31); sheets 2 and 3 hold the 15-case observer subset (rows 3-17 each). 94 is the paper's inclusion count only. Verified by parsing the downloaded xlsx: 617 populated cells in sheet1 over a 20-column header.

UNSOURCED: 'The images exist at Penn Vet and would have to be requested.' No primary source states any request route. The repository item carries no contact, no access procedure, no embargo note, and no dc.relation linking it to the article. The paper's data availability statement (which I could not open directly — Wiley Cloudflare-blocked curl, curl_cffi chrome impersonation and a reader proxy; text known only from a search index) points at this DOI, i.e. the spreadsheet, and mentions no images. Treat image availability as unknown, not as request-able.
CONTRADICTED: licence. DataCite says CC BY-NC 4.0; the Penn DSpace record for the same item says dc.rights.uri = CC BY 4.0. The candidate reports only the NC form.

IMPRECISE: 'n_images: No images released' is right but understates it — the ORIGINAL bundle contains exactly one bitstream and the xlsx zip has no xl/media entry, so there is not even an embedded figure. The 2.7 MB size is empty-row bloat (dimension A1:AJ1048512).

OUT OF SCOPE for the stated lens: anatomy is equine C6-C7 and C7-T1. There is no lumbar spine, no sacrum and no pelvis in the images or the measurements. This cannot serve a lumbosacral/pelvic fluoroscopy question even if the images were obtained.

NO POSE, and also no landmarks: the released columns are age, sex, breed, weight, linear heights in cm (articular process and vertebral body, left/right, CT and radiograph), derived AP:VB ratios, OA grade 0-3 and a Y/N osteoarthropathy flag. There are no landmark coordinates, no C-arm or source-detector geometry, no pixel spacing, no registration between the radiograph and the CBCT. The candidate's 'No pose was recorded' is confirmed.

DATE: 'published 2026-05-07' is the repository accession (dc.date.accessioned 2026-05-07T19:30:17Z); the journal article first published 2026-05-13 (Equine Vet J, doi 10.1002/evj.70184, PMID 42128607). DataCite publicationYear is 2026 with collection dates 2021-01 to 2023-10.

TITLE/AUTHOR fields check out: creators Cianci, Bills, Skelton, Stewart, Johnson, Colmer, Stefanovski, Brown; affiliation Department of Clinical Studies, New Bolton Center, University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine. The article is not open access (Europe PMC isOpenAccess = N) and registers no data links.
The handle 20.500.14332/62573 redirects to entities/dataset/896f4d7b-ed44-44d5-bb26-9d1e5fe51fed; both resolve, so the record is live and not withdrawn.

candidate.name: MrOS (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men, US): baseline lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs plus spine and hip QCT slabs in the same men — access and protocol facts
candidate.why_relevant: New facts about a known item. (1) Images are not on MrOS Online, which serves derived data only. Publication Guidelines v5.9 (2025-07-25) route image requests through a Publications Committee analysis plan and a DUA, possibly with an ancillary-study proposal. (2) The route works: a UW group received 10,351 annotated lateral spine radiographs (67,215 vertebral bodies) from the Coordinating Center under a DUA. (3) The NIA AgingResearchBiobank holds no MrOS images. (4) As of 2026-09-21 all MrOS Online accounts are disabled pending NIH identity-verified re-registration with an institutional email. (5) Protocol: films and QCT were taken at the same baseline visit, about 3,600-3,786 men have both, and film SID is fixed at 1016 mm. The CT is three limited slabs: T12/L1-L2 at 1 mm, mid-L3 to mid-L5 at 5 mm, and a hip slab at 3 mm. The sacrum, SI joints and L5-S1 junction are in no CT series. The CT is supine, so each vertebra must be registered separately against the films. The NIA terms say 'not available for commercial use', which matters for the product track.
candidate.institution: San Francisco Coordinating Center (UCSF / CPMC Research Institute); CT Reading Center UCSF (T. Lang); 6 US sites
candidate.device: Bucky screen-film at 40 in (1016 mm) FFD, 12:1 grid, later digitised; CT on GE ProSpeed, HiSpeed Advantage, Philips MX-8000, Siemens Somatom Plus 4, Philips CT-Twin/Toshiba Aquilion, Picker PQ-5000, with a hydroxyapatite phantom
candidate.xray_kind: Diagnostic radiographs (lateral thoracic and lumbar spine; Visit 2 standing AP pelvis); QCT scouts may exist
candidate.anatomy: Films: T4-T12 and T12-S1 lateral; AP pelvis at Visit 2. CT: T12/L1-L2, L3-L5 and hip slabs
candidate.subjects: Living men aged 65 and over; 5,994 enrolled; about 3,600-3,786 with baseline films plus QCT
candidate.n_images: 10,351 annotated lateral spine films released to one outside group; about 3,600-3,800 baseline QCT exams of 3 series each
candidate.pose_or_labels: No pose recorded; fixed SID 1016 mm and a fixed central ray (L3 lumbar, T7 thoracic); 6-point vertebral outlines, Genant SQ grades, Cobb T4-T12
candidate.published: Protocols 2000; Publication Guidelines v5.9 2025-07-25; account shutdown notice 2026-09-21
candidate.licence: DUA; not available for commercial use
candidate.is_update_of_known: mros (osteoporotic fractures in men): spine radiographs + hip/spine qct image archive

verdicts.access_now:
NOT DOWNLOADABLE — not now, and images were never downloadable. Two separate barriers, both verified today (2026-09-22).

(1) The site is closed. mrosonline.ucsf.edu/DataRelease 302s to /Account/Login and renders a page titled "RestrictedMode - MrOS Online". /Account/Login and /Account/Register render the same page. Verbatim: "System Maintenance in Progress — Updated guidance from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) requires the MrOS Online website to implement a registration system with enhanced security and identity verification features. While we complete these updates, all user accounts have been temporarily disabled. Once the new registration system is available, users will need to register using an institutional email address rather than a personal email address. NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong; Cuba; Iran; Iraq; North Korea; Russia; and Venezuela. As a result, we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries. Please check back soon to re-register." Only /PublicFiles/*.pdf still serve (Guidelines 321 KB, Measurements 292 KB, Publications listing 789 KB). So even the derived tabular data is unobtainable right now; registration itself is shut.

(2) Even when open, MrOS Online serves derived data only. Publication Guidelines v5.9 (07/25/2025), section H.3, verbatim: "Those interested in collaborating with the MrOS study or are interested in requesting MrOS data or resources that are not available on 'MrOS Online' (e.g. images, polysomnography (PSG) files, actigraphy files) will need to operate within the framework of the MrOS Publications Guidelines. This includes submitting analysis plan proposals and publication materials for review and signing a DUA as needed. Depending on the type of additional data requested, an ancillary study proposal may be required." Section G: the DUA is signed between California Pacific Medical Center (releasing) and the receiving institution.

(3) NIA AgingResearchBiobank holds no MrOS images. Its MrOS record lists "Resources Available: Biospecimens and Study Datasets" and "Materials Available: 24 Hour Urine DNA Plasma Serum Urine Whole Blood". No imaging line anywhere on the record.

Net: this is a mediated, by-request archive gated on a Publications Committee analysis plan plus an institutional DUA plus possibly an ancillary-study proposal, with the intake channel currently offline. Turnaround unknown. No file list, no file names, no formats (DICOM vs scanned TIFF), and no sizes are published for either the film archive or the QCT archive — I could find none on any reachable source.
verdicts.anatomy:
CORRECTED. The candidate's "Films: T4-T12 and T12-S1 lateral" conflates film field with reading range.

Radiology Operations Manual v3.0 (2000-04-07), Special Considerations, verbatim:
- Thoracic lateral: "Include T2 (if possible) to T12 (required). In large participants T2, and T3 in extreme cases, may need to be excluded."
- Lumbar lateral: "Include T12 to S1." and "T12 must be included on both the thoracic and the lumbar images."
So the lumbar lateral does reach S1 — the lumbosacral junction IS on film, which is the interesting part for level-identity work. T4 is not a film boundary; T4–L4 is the SpineAnalyzer reading range and T4–T12 is the Cobb kyphosis range.

CT, from the CT Operations Manual (T. Lang, 2000-04-20):
- Lateral scout: 120 kVp, 70 mA fast mode; "The length of the scoutview should be 40 cm or the scan length necessary to include the sacrum." Scouts are protocol-mandated, not "may exist", and the spine scout is specified to reach the sacrum.
- Series 1: "The superior limit is 5-mm above the L1 superior endplate and the inferior limit is 5-mm below the L2 inferior endplate" — L1/L2, 1 mm, 120 kVp/150 mA, 48 cm FOV, 512². T12 appears only as a fallback: "If L1 or L2 are fractured, scan T12 as an alternate. If both L1 and L2 are fractured, scan T12 and L3 as alternates." So "T12/L1-L2" overstates; T12 is exceptional.
- Series 2: "The superior limit is the mid-L3 vertebra. The inferior limit is the mid L5 vertebra" — 5 mm, 80 kVp/140 mA. Independently confirmed by PMC4029749: "scanning from the mid-L3 to the mid-L5 vertebra at 5-mm slice thickness with participants in the supine position."
- Hip: AP scout, then "The superior limit should be 1 cm superior to the superior aspect of the left femoral head. The inferior scan limit should be 35 mm inferior to the inferior aspect of the lesser trochanter of the left hip" — 3 mm, 80 kVp/280 mA.

The claim "The sacrum, SI joints and L5-S1 junction are in no CT series" is OVERSTATED. Only the L5-S1 junction is genuinely absent (spine series stops at mid-L5; hip slab starts below S1). A slab beginning 1 cm above the femoral head at 48 cm FOV routinely contains the lower sacrum and the inferior SI joints. I found no primary statement that the hip slab excludes them, and the anatomy says otherwise.

Positioning: "The patient is positioned supine, feet first in the scanner", hands behind head, two hydroxyapatite reference phantoms under the lumbar spine and the non-dominant hip. Films are lateral decubitus (left lateral preferred, right accepted). So the candidate is right that CT and film differ in posture — but note CT is supine and the films are LATERAL RECUMBENT, not standing; only the Visit 2 pelvis film is standing.
verdicts.counts:
Films (PMC4152008, MrOS VF methods paper), verbatim: "At baseline all 5994 men had thoracic and lumbar radiographs of which 5958 were technically adequate. At Visit 2, 4,423 men provided both a lumbar and thoracic radiograph of which 4,399 were technically adequate."

That reconciles the 10,351 exactly: 5,958 + 4,399 = 10,357 ≈ 10,351. So the UW release was baseline PLUS Visit 2, not baseline only — the candidate's n_images line reads as if 10,351 were a single-timepoint set.

AJNR 2024 (PMC11448993), verbatim: "A pre-existing multicenter deidentified annotated radiograph data set was obtained from the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study (MrOS) Coordinating Center under a data use agreement." and "Models were trained, validated, and tested on 6695, 1310, and 2346 images, respectively, which were split randomly by patient" (= 10,351). Total vertebral bodies annotated: 67,215.
