Affiliations include University of Washington (Biomedical Informatics, Medical Education, Radiology, Biostatistics, Neurological Surgery), USC Keck, UC Davis. CONFIRMED, including the UW attribution.

QCT — the candidate's "3,600-3,786 with both" brackets the truth but mixes stages. Black 2008 (PMC2680175), verbatim: "Of these, 122 were not eligible for hip scans because of hip replacement. Of the 3664 scans performed, 101 (2.8%) were not available for processing", leaving 3,347 analysed. 3,786 is the number REFERRED for QCT. Since all 5,994 had baseline films, the film∩QCT intersection is just the QCT count: ~3,664 acquired, ~3,347 processable. Use 3,347, not 3,786, for anything requiring a usable CT.

Visit 2 standing pelvis (PMC4488192): 4,215 radiographs digitized, 4,140 analysed after exclusions.

Reading: SpineAnalyzer (Optasia Medical), "visual or quantitative assessment of vertebral body deformities between vertebral levels T4 and L4", and "This step records 6-point and 95-point quantitative morphometry data for each vertebral level in the study database." So 6-point outlines exist but only T4–L4, and 95-point outlines also exist — the candidate undersells this. The methods paper notes the morphometry was not itself evaluated for reliability. Triage sensitivity 96.8%, specificity 46.3%; intra-reader kappa 0.79–0.92.

Digitisation (PMC4152008), verbatim: "At baseline all participants had conventional (film-based) radiographs of the lumbar and thoracic spine; at Visit 2, four clinical centers acquired conventional radiographs and two clinical centers acquired the images digitally. All conventionally acquired film images were scanned to digital format; all images were read digitally." Scanner make/model for the digitisation is not stated.

Visit schedule (MrOSMeasurements.pdf, column positions resolved spatially): X-ray thoracic+lumbar spine = Baseline and Visit 2. X-ray (Hip) = Visit 2 only. QCT (Hip) and QCT (Spine) = Baseline and Visit 3. Cobb Angle = Baseline and Visit 2. So films and QCT do coincide at Baseline — the pairing claim holds at the visit level.
verdicts.licence:
No licence. There is no open licence of any kind — not CC, not custom-open. Access is by executed Data Use Agreement between California Pacific Medical Center (releasing institution) and the receiving institution, per Publication Guidelines v5.9 section G, gated behind Publications Committee approval of an analysis plan and possibly an ancillary-study proposal.

The "not available for commercial use" term is real but I must qualify its scope. It is the NIA AgingResearchBiobank MrOS record, verbatim under "Other Specific Restrictions": "Materials from this study are not available for commercial use." That record governs BIOBANK materials — the six biospecimen types and the study datasets it holds — and that biobank holds no images. The CPMC/SFCC DUA that actually governs an image release is not published anywhere I could reach, so NO commercial-use term is verified for the image route specifically. It would be a mistake to treat the NIA line as settled law over the film archive without seeing the CPMC DUA. Also on the biobank record: "Biospecimens are restricted to age-related research questions such as osteoporosis, longevity, sleep disorder, etc. Additional consent restrictions are site- and visit-specific." Its sample agreement is an OHMTA and is explicitly a non-binding specimen for reference only.

Separate hard restriction, from the site notice: NIH now bars sharing with institutions in China (incl. Hong Kong), Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia, Venezuela.
verdicts.paired_ct:
CONFIRMED in principle, with real limits. Baseline lateral thoracic + lumbar films and baseline spine and hip QCT were acquired at the same Visit 1 in the same men (MrOSMeasurements.pdf visit grid). Roughly 3,347–3,664 men have usable both.

But the CT is not a spine volume. It is three short slabs with gaps: L1–L2 at 1 mm, mid-L3 to mid-L5 at 5 mm, hip at 3 mm. Between mid-L5 and the top of the hip slab there is nothing, so L5-S1 — the exact junction a lumbosacral level-identity model cares about — is absent from the axial CT while being explicitly required on the lumbar film ("Include T12 to S1"). That asymmetry is the single most important fact here and it cuts against the candidate's framing. The 5 mm and 3 mm slabs are also too coarse for a DRR with film-grade detail; only the 1 mm L1/L2 slab is.

CT is supine, films are lateral recumbent, acquired on different machines at different times in the visit, so there is no rigid subject-level alignment — per-vertebra registration is required, as the candidate says. Scanners differ by site, which the candidate's list captures correctly. A hydroxyapatite reference phantom (150, 75, 0 mg/cm³, Image Analysis Inc.) lies under the patient in every CT, so every slab has a foreign body in the posterior field that a renderer must handle.

Unverified: whether the CT Reading Center retained full DICOM or only processed BMD outputs. Nothing I could reach states this, and it determines whether the CT is usable for rendering at all.
verdicts.real_xray:
CONFIRMED, and the technique is unusually well specified — which is the main reason to care about this cohort. Radiology Operations Manual v3.0, verbatim per view:

Thoracic lateral: "Scattering grid ... r = 12 to 1 at 40 inches"; "Film/Focus Distance ... 40 inches (not variable!)"; "60-70 kVp"; 7"x17" lengthwise recommended; "Direct the central ray to level of 7th thoracic vertebra (T7)"; cassette in Bucky tray centred at T7; breathe quietly during exposure, manual technique required (no phototiming).

Lumbar lateral: same 12:1 grid at 40 inches; "Film/Focus Distance ... 40 inches (not variable!)"; "80 - 90 kVp"; 11"x14" lengthwise; "Direct the central ray to level of 3rd lumbar vertebra (L3)"; suspend respiration after expiration.

40 inches = 1016 mm exactly, so the candidate's SID figure is right and it is genuinely fixed by protocol rather than nominal. Per-participant kVp, exposure time and mA were recorded on an X-ray Form Clinic Worksheet returned to the coordinating center — so exposure factors exist per image, though whether they were keyed into the database is not stated.

Visit 2 standing pelvis (PMC4488192), verbatim: "Standing pelvis radiographs were taken at the second clinic visit by positioning the patient using a standardized foot mat with toes internally rotated 15°", "40 inches of focus-to-film distance, 70 to 80 kVp (mAs dependent on the screen/film system), large focal spot, and full size of the film collimation", "the x-ray beam directed 2 inches above the pubis symphysis", "Bucky imaging system (Agfa, Mortsel, Belgium)", 14x17 cassette.

These are living men, screen-film, later scanned to digital. This is not fluoroscopy and carries no C-arm geometry, no pose, no per-frame device parameters.
corrections: Film coverage is NOT T4-T12. Protocol v3.0 requires the thoracic lateral to 'Include T2 (if possible) to T12 (required)' and the lumbar lateral to 'Include T12 to S1.' T4-L4 is the SpineAnalyzer READING range and T4-T12 is the Cobb kyphosis range; neither is the film field. Correcting this matters in the candidate's favour: the lumbar film reaches S1, so the lumbosacral junction is on film.

Spine QCT slab 1 is L1/L2, not 'T12/L1-L2'. The protocol scans 5 mm above the L1 superior endplate to 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate, and reaches T12 only as a documented exception: 'If L1 or L2 are fractured, scan T12 as an alternate. If both L1 and L2 are fractured, scan T12 and L3 as alternates.'

'The sacrum, SI joints and L5-S1 junction are in no CT series' is overstated. Only L5-S1 is genuinely absent. The hip slab begins 1 cm above the superior aspect of the femoral head at 48 cm FOV / 512 matrix, a range that routinely contains the lower sacrum and the inferior SI joints. No primary source says otherwise and I could find none claiming exclusion.

'QCT scouts may exist' understates the protocol. A lateral spine scout and an AP hip scout are both mandatory, and the lateral scout is specified as '40 cm or the scan length necessary to include the sacrum' - i.e. the one image in the whole CT exam that does cover the lumbosacral junction. Whether the scouts were retained by the CT Reading Center is unverified.

'about 3,600-3,786 men have both' mixes stages. 3,786 were REFERRED for QCT; 122 were ineligible; 3,664 hip scans were performed; 101 were unavailable, leaving 3,347 processed (Black 2008). All 5,994 had baseline films (5,958 technically adequate), so film-QCT intersection = the QCT count. Usable-both is ~3,347, not ~3,786.

The 10,351 images are baseline PLUS Visit 2, not baseline. 5,958 adequate baseline + 4,399 adequate Visit 2 = 10,357, matching the AJNR split of 6,695/1,310/2,346 = 10,351 'split randomly by patient'. The candidate's n_images line reads as a single-timepoint set.

6-point morphometry is recorded only T4-L4, and 95-point morphometry was also recorded ('This step records 6-point and 95-point quantitative morphometry data for each vertebral level in the study database'). The candidate omits the 95-point outlines and the level restriction. The methods paper explicitly declines to evaluate the morphometry's reliability.

'Not available for commercial use' is sourced to the NIA AgingResearchBiobank record, which governs biobank materials (six biospecimen types plus study datasets) - and that biobank holds no images. The CPMC/SFCC DUA that actually governs an image release is not public; I could not find its text, so NO commercial-use term is verified for the image route. Do not treat the NIA line as binding on the film archive without seeing the CPMC DUA.

The account-shutdown notice carries no date on the page. I confirmed it live on 2026-09-22; I could not verify the claimed 2026-09-21 date. The notice also adds a restriction the candidate omits: NIH bars sharing with institutions in China (incl. Hong Kong), Cuba, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela.

The films are lateral RECUMBENT (left lateral preferred, right accepted, side may differ between the thoracic and lumbar film of the same man), not standing. Only the Visit 2 pelvis film is standing. Side-of-decubitus varying within a subject is a real nuisance for any film-to-CT registration.
CT is at Baseline and Visit 3; spine films at Baseline and Visit 2; hip film at Visit 2 only. Only Baseline pairs films with CT. A Visit 2 film has no contemporaneous CT.

NOT VERIFIED, and load-bearing: no file list, file names, image format (DICOM vs scanned TIFF/DICOM-wrapped), bit depth, digitisation scanner/pixel pitch, or archive size is published for either the films or the QCT, anywhere I could reach. Nor is it stated whether the CT Reading Center retained full DICOM or only processed BMD output. Without that, whether the CT is renderable at all is unknown.

NOT VERIFIED: whether image requests are being fulfilled at all while MrOS Online accounts are disabled, and what the turnaround is. The Publications Committee route runs through the Coordinating Center rather than the website, so it may be unaffected, but nothing states this.

Minor: the CT Operations Manual states the planned enrolment as 5,700; actual enrolment was 5,994. The manual is dated 2000-04-20 and the radiology manual 2000-04-07, consistent with the candidate's 'Protocols 2000'.

verdicts.real_xray: Real acquisitions, confirmed from the primary operations manual (MrOSxrayOMV3, Radiology Operations Manual v3.0, 7 Apr 2000). Screen-film plain radiography on a Bucky table: "Scattering grid ... r = 12 to 1 at 40 inches", "Film/Focus Distance ... 40 inches (not variable!)", thoracic 60-70 kVp on 7x17 in film, lumbar 80-90 kVp on 11x14 in film, lead side marker on the film, physical films logged and shipped to the coordinating centre. Not DRRs, not simulated, not MV portal. Films were later digitised: the released set reached the University of Washington group as DICOM, which they converted to TIFF (PMC11448993). Posture, which the candidate omits and which matters: the baseline spine films are RECUMBENT lateral decubitus ("Place participant on the table in the lateral position"), left lateral preferred but "take the right lateral film and send the film with the best imaging", and "The side used does not have to be the same for the thoracic and lumbar films." So laterality is not fixed and there is no erect spine film at baseline. The only standing radiograph in MrOS is the Visit 2 AP pelvis (PMC4488192: "Standing pelvis radiographs were taken at the second clinic visit by positioning the patient using a standardized foot mat with toes internally rotated 15 degrees"). The QCT protocol also mandates projection scouts (lateral spine scout and AP hip scout, both 120 kVp / 70 mA fast mode); these are CT topograms, not radiographs, and nothing states whether they survive in the releasable archive.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same subjects, same baseline visit window, but it is three thin slabs and not a spine CT. QCT Operations Manual (T. Lang, UCSF, 20 Apr 2000) specifies three series, patient supine and feet first with hydroxyapatite reference phantoms under the lumbar spine and hip: (1) L1/L2 series, superior limit 5 mm above the L1 superior endplate to 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate, 1 mm slices at pitch 1, with T12 (and L3) used only as alternates if L1 or L2 are fractured; (2) L4 series, "The superior limit is the mid-L3 vertebra. The inferior limit is the mid L5 vertebra", 5 mm slices at pitch 2; (3) hip series, "The superior limit should be 1 cm superior to the superior aspect of the left femoral head. The inferior scan limit should be 35 mm inferior to the inferior aspect of the lesser trochanter of the left hip", 80 kVp, 280 mA, 512 squared, 48 cm FOV, 3 mm at pitch 1. Confirmed independently by Black 2008 (PMC2680175). A coverage gap the candidate does not mention: the L1/L2 series stops 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate and the L4 series starts at mid-L3, so the L2-L3 disc and upper L3 are in NO series. Scanners confirmed verbatim (PMC2680175): GE Prospeed (Birmingham), GE Hispeed Advantage (Minneapolis), Philips MX-8000 (Palo Alto), Siemens Somatom Plus 4 (Pittsburgh), Philips CT-Twin then Toshiba Aquilion (Portland, 190 then 467 participants), Picker PQ-5000 (San Diego). Because the CT is supine and the film is lateral decubitus, and because film magnification is unrecoverable, any film-to-CT correspondence has to be established per vertebra.
verdicts.anatomy: Films (primary source, operations manual): thoracic lateral "Include T2 (if possible) to T12 (required)", central ray at T7; lumbar lateral "Include T12 to S1", central ray at L3, "T12 must be included on both the thoracic and the lumbar images." So the lumbar film DOES contain the lumbosacral junction and S1, which is the single most relevant fact here. Visit 2 adds a standing AP pelvis (whole pelvis, sacrum, SI joints, both hips). CT: L1-L2 at 1 mm, mid-L3 to mid-L5 at 5 mm, and a hip/pelvis slab at 3 mm over a 48 cm FOV. I rendered Figure 2 of the QCT manual (the AP hip scoutview with the scan interval drawn): the interval crosses the LOWER sacrum and coccyx and takes in both acetabula, both femoral heads and necks, the pubis, the ischium and the trochanters. So the hip slab is a pelvis slab. What is genuinely absent from every CT series is S1, the sacral promontory, the L5-S1 disc and essentially all of the SI joints. Labels: 6-point vertebral-body morphometry placed with SpineAnalyzer (Optasia Medical) plus Genant semiquantitative grades, and a modified-Cobb kyphosis angle with a fixed T4 and T12 cut-off. Critically, the annotated level range stops well above the junction: PMC11448993 states annotations cover "T5 to T12 or L1" on thoracic films and "T12 or L1 to L3 or L4" on lumbar films. L5 and S1 are imaged but carry no outline and no grade.
verdicts.counts: 5,994 men enrolled at baseline 2000-2002 across six US sites, aged 65 and over (mrosonline.ucsf.edu/Home/About). Baseline lateral thoracic and lumbar films on the cohort, repeated at follow-up. QCT: "3786 men were referred for quantitative computed tomography (QCT) scans of the hips, lumbar spine and abdomen" (PMC4029749); the 25-year review (PMC13000919) adds that these were "the first 650 patients enrolled at each enrollment sites (63% of all MrOS enrollees [3786 total men])" — so the QCT subset is a consecutive-enrolment subset, not a random sample. Usable is lower than referred: 3,347 men had usable baseline hip QCT after processing failures and missing data (PMC2680175). The 10,351 / 67,215 figure is real but comes from PMC11448993, not from the URL the candidate cites for it, and it is not 10,351 baseline lateral spine films: it derives from "5994 consenting men ... with 2 lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs separated by 4.5 years", i.e. two visits and two views pooled, split 6,695 train / 1,310 validation / 2,346 test. Visit 2 pelvis: 4,215 returned with digitised pelvic radiographs, 4,140 analysed (PMC4488192).
verdicts.pose_or_labels: No pose, and the candidate's phrasing understates this. Confirmed verbatim: SID is fixed at 40 inches / 1016 mm ("Film/Focus Distance ... 40 inches (not variable!)"), the grid is 12:1 at 40 inches, and the central ray is fixed at T7 for the thoracic film and L3 for the lumbar film. But SID alone is not a pose: no source-to-object distance, no table height, no magnification marker and no laterality flag is recorded per film, and the decubitus side is explicitly allowed to vary between participants and even between the two films of one participant. Magnification is therefore unrecoverable per image and there is no camera matrix for any film. Labels that do exist: 6-point vertebral-body outlines (SpineAnalyzer, Optasia Medical), Genant semiquantitative fracture grades, quantitative morphometry, and a modified-Cobb kyphosis angle over a fixed T4-T12 span. Level coverage of those labels is T5 to T12/L1 (thoracic) and T12/L1 to L3/L4 (lumbar) — nothing at L5 or S1.
verdicts.access_now: Blocked entirely, and more broadly than the candidate states. Every MrOS Online path I tried — the root, /DataRelease, /Account/Register and /Account/Login — serves the same RestrictedMode page: "Updated guidance from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) requires the MrOS Online website to implement a registration system with enhanced security and identity verification features. While we complete these updates, all user accounts have been temporarily disabled. Once the new registration system is available, users will need to register using an institutional email address rather than a personal email address. NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong; Cuba; Iran; Iraq; North Korea; Russia; and Venezuela. As a result, we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries. Please check back soon to re-register." The country restriction is a material fact the candidate omits. The notice carries no date, so "as of 2026-09-21" is the observation date, not a stated one. Consequence for verification: the Data and Documentation section cannot be inspected at all, so the claim that MrOS Online carries no images could not be checked at its own release page. The image route itself is confirmed from the Publication Guidelines v5.9 (07/25/2025), section H.3: "Those interested in collaborating with the MrOS study or are interested in requesting MrOS data or resources that are not available on 'MrOS Online' (e.g. images, polysomnography (PSG) files, actigraphy files) will need to operate within the framework of the MrOS Publications Guidelines. This includes submitting analysis plan proposals and publication materials for review and signing a DUA as needed. Depending on the type of additional data requested, an ancillary study proposal may be required." Section G adds that the DUA is signed by California Pacific Medical Center and the receiving institution. Realistic timeline: analysis plan to the Publications Committee, institution-signed CPMC DUA, possibly an ancillary study proposal, and the website gate has to reopen first.
verdicts.licence: Unresolved for the images, and the candidate's reading is not supported where it matters. "Materials from this study are not available for commercial use" is real and I read it verbatim, but it is on the NIA AgingResearchBiobank MrOS details page, and that page lists only biospecimens (24 Hour Urine, DNA, Plasma, Serum, Urine, Whole Blood) with no imaging of any kind. The biobank does host MrOS protocol documents — both PDFs I extracted came from it — but holds no images. The images do not travel by the NIA route at all; they come from the San Francisco Coordinating Center under a DUA signed by California Pacific Medical Center, and that DUA's text is not public, so its commercial terms could not be read. For the product track the correct status is unknown, and unknown should be treated as adverse: an NIH/NIA-funded cohort DUA of this vintage is very unlikely to permit commercial use, but I found no primary sentence saying so about the images.
corrections: Film coverage 'T4-T12' is wrong. The Radiology Operations Manual says the thoracic film must 'Include T2 (if possible) to T12 (required)' and the lumbar film must 'Include T12 to S1', with T12 on both. T4-T12 is the modified-Cobb kyphosis cut-off (T1-T3 are not reliably seen on a lateral film), not the field of view. The candidate has imported a derived-measure span into the acquisition description.

Decisive for a lumbosacral project and not stated by the candidate: S1 is ON the lumbar film but is NOT labelled. PMC11448993 reports the released annotations cover 'T5 to T12 or L1' on thoracic radiographs and 'T12 or L1 to L3 or L4' on lumbar radiographs. L5 and S1 carry no 6-point outline and no Genant grade. Listing '6-point vertebral outlines, Genant SQ grades' without the level range overstates what the labels reach.

The 10,351 / 67,215 claim is real but its cited evidence URL is the wrong paper. PMC12771367 is a CT-muscle-and-fracture-risk paper (CPMC/Stanford/Wake Forest/Pittsburgh/OHSU) containing neither number. The actual source is PMC11448993 (Washington, USC, UC Davis): 'A pre-existing multicenter deidentified annotated radiograph data set was obtained from the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study (MrOS) Coordinating Center under a data use agreement.' The DUA route is therefore confirmed; the citation is not.

10,351 is not 10,351 baseline lateral spine films. PMC11448993 derives it from '5994 consenting men ... with 2 lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs separated by 4.5 years' — baseline plus the ~4.5-year follow-up, and thoracic plus lumbar views, pooled (6,695 / 1,310 / 2,346). Read as a baseline-lateral count it roughly quadruple-counts.

'The sacrum, SI joints and L5-S1 junction are in no CT series' is too strong for the sacrum. I rendered Figure 2 of the QCT manual: the hip-slab interval (1 cm above the superior left femoral head to 35 mm below the lesser trochanter, 48 cm FOV, 3 mm) crosses the lower sacrum and coccyx and takes in both acetabula, femoral heads, pubis and ischium. Correct statement: S1, the sacral promontory, the L5-S1 disc and essentially all of the SI joints are absent; the caudal sacrum is present. A gap the candidate misses entirely: the L1/L2 series ends 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate and the L4 series begins at mid-L3, so the L2-L3 disc and upper L3 are in neither series.

'T12/L1-L2 at 1 mm' misstates the first slab. The protocol scans L1 and L2; T12 appears only as a fallback — 'If L1 or L2 are fractured, scan T12 as an alternate. If both L1 and L2 are fractured, scan T12 and L3 as alternates.' T12 is in the slab for a minority of men, not by design.

'Images are not on MrOS Online, which serves derived data only' could not be verified at its own source and has counter-evidence. The whole site is in RestrictedMode, so /DataRelease is unreadable; meanwhile the MrOS Online home page says 'An extensive bank of data, images and specimens have been archived as part of the MrOS study' and MrOSMeasurements.pdf carries an 'Images' domain with rows 'X-ray (Hip)' and 'X-ray (Thoracic and lumbar spine)'. The Publication Guidelines sentence naming images as 'not available on MrOS Online' is the only primary support, and it is about the download route, not about whether images are catalogued there.

The commercial-use restriction is attached to the wrong body of material. 'Materials from this study are not available for commercial use' sits on the NIA AgingResearchBiobank page, which lists only biospecimens and holds no images. Images move under a CPMC-signed DUA whose text is not public. The commercial status of the IMAGES is unverified, not established. Do not plan the product track on either reading.

'About 3,600-3,786 men have both' films and QCT is not sourced. 3,786 is the number REFERRED for QCT (PMC4029749), and PMC13000919 shows it is not a random subset: 'obtained for the first 650 patients enrolled at each enrollment sites (63% of all MrOS enrollees [3786 total men])'. Usable is lower — 3,347 with usable baseline hip QCT after exclusions (PMC2680175). No primary source I found reports the film-and-QCT overlap, and the '3,600' has no source at all.

Posture is missing from the candidate and it changes the registration problem. The baseline spine films are recumbent lateral decubitus, not erect: 'Place participant on the table in the lateral position (left lateral if possible)', with right lateral permitted and 'The side used does not have to be the same for the thoracic and lumbar films.' So decubitus film versus supine CT, and the laterality is not even fixed within a subject. The only standing film in MrOS is the Visit 2 AP pelvis.

'No pose recorded; fixed SID 1016 mm and a fixed central ray' softens a hard negative. SID and central ray are confirmed verbatim, but no source-to-object distance, table height, magnification marker or laterality flag is recorded per film, so magnification is unrecoverable and no camera matrix exists for any image. There is no pose, and the fixed SID does not partially supply one.

The account-shutdown notice carries a restriction the candidate omits: NIH 'restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong; Cuba; Iran; Iraq; North Korea; Russia; and Venezuela.' The notice is also undated on the page, so 2026-09-21 is the observation date, not a stated effective date.

Unverified but plausible: 'QCT scouts may exist'. The protocol mandates a lateral spine scout and an AP hip scout (120 kVp, 70 mA, fast mode) and requires all image data to be double-archived and transferred to the QCT Reading Center, so scouts were acquired. Whether they remain in the releasable archive is stated nowhere I could read.

Confirmed without correction, for the record: Publication Guidelines version 5.9 dated 07/25/2025 and its image/DUA/ancillary-study routing; the NIA biobank holding no MrOS images; all accounts disabled; SID 40 inches fixed and grid 12:1; central ray T7 and L3; the three-slab QCT geometry and the 3 mm hip slab; the six scanner models; supine feet-first QCT with hydroxyapatite phantoms; Visit 2 standing AP pelvis (4,215 digitised, 4,140 analysed); 5,994 enrolled.

candidate.name: MrOS Hong Kong (CUHK Jockey Club Centre for Osteoporosis Care and Control): L1-L2 QCT at year 2 plus lateral spine radiographs at baseline and year 4
candidate.why_relevant: A smaller Asian counterpart to US MrOS, in the same men: real lateral thoracic and lumbar films and a thin-slice L1-L2 QCT. 328 men have spine QCT at year 2, and hip CT was done on a GE LightSpeed 16. Drawbacks: films and CT are 1-3 years apart, the CT is a limited slab, and there is no data statement or access route. It would need a CUHK collaboration (T. Kwok, J. Leung, Y.X.J. Wáng).
candidate.institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
candidate.device: CT: GE LightSpeed 16; radiograph system not stated
candidate.xray_kind: Diagnostic lateral thoracic and lumbar radiographs
candidate.anatomy: L1-L2 QCT, hip QCT; lateral thoracic and lumbar spine films
candidate.subjects: Living Chinese men aged 65 and over; about 2,000 in the cohort, 328 with spine QCT
candidate.n_images: About 328 QCT exams; films for about 2,000 men at baseline and year 4
candidate.pose_or_labels: No pose; Genant SQ and OLVF scores

verdicts.access_now: Not downloadable now, not on request, and there is no request route published. (1) The PRIMARY url is not a dataset record — PMC11652400 is a Skeletal Radiology REVIEW ARTICLE (Wang YXJ et al., 2024, DOI 10.1007/s00256-024-04722-3). I pulled the full JATS XML from Europe PMC (76,915 bytes) and grepped it: there is NO "Data Availability", no "availability of data", no "upon request", no "on request" anywhere. The Declarations block contains only "Conflicts of interest". It is not even an "available upon reasonable request" promise — there is no data statement of any kind. (2) No repository record exists: no Zenodo/Figshare/OSF/dbGaP/TCIA/institutional deposit, no data DOI, no file manifest, no sizes. The three DOIs in the candidate are article DOIs only. (3) The one data statement in the cited set is in the JCSM paper (PMC11871091): "Analysed data are available in this manuscript. Raw data are available on the MrOS website (access is subject to approval): https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu". That pointer does NOT cover Hong Kong — mrosonline.ucsf.edu describes itself as "A multi-center observational study of 5,994 men" from six US centres (Birmingham, Minneapolis, Palo Alto, Pittsburgh, Portland, San Diego); Hong Kong appears nowhere on the site. (4) MrOS Online is in any case non-functional today (checked 2026-09-22): GET /DataRelease 302s to /Account/Login, which returns "System Maintenance in Progress ... all user accounts have been temporarily disabled" pending an NIH-mandated re-registration, and states verbatim: "NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong; Cuba; Iran; Iraq; North Korea; Russia; and Venezuela. As a result, we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries." (5) CUHK's own study site (jococ.org/en/mros-msos.php) carries NO data-access, data-request, application or collaboration route — only two PDFs (a variable inventory and a publication list). Obtaining these images would require negotiating a bilateral CUHK collaboration from scratch with no published mechanism, no template agreement and no stated turnaround.
verdicts.anatomy: Real, but not what the candidate implies. Spine QCT is L1 and L2 ONLY (two vertebral bodies) — confirmed verbatim in the review: "328 Chinese men (age: 73.6 +/- 4.4 years) who had QCT LS (L1 and L2) BMD and DXA LS BMD at the same time ... from the Osteoporotic Fracture in Men (MrOS) Hong Kong study year-2 follow-up conducted during the period of September 2003 to March 2005." The hip QCT is a separate limited slab: "Measurements were taken in the pelvic region, covering from the femoral head to 3.5 cm below the lesser trochanter" (JCSM 2025). Radiographs are lateral thoracic and lumbar spine films scored T4-L5. There is no whole-spine CT, no sacrum/pelvis CT beyond the proximal-femur slab, no pose, no calibration geometry, no fluoroscopy anywhere in the cohort.
verdicts.counts: Disputed by the source that would know best. CUHK's own variable inventory PDF (Appendix_1_variable_inventory_Dec2025.pdf, dated 15/12/2025, downloaded from jococ.org and text-extracted) says "QCT (329 Male spine, 332 Male hip)" — not 328. The review's 328 is the QCT+DXA correlation subset; other subsets in the same paper are n=324 and n=316. The inventory also lists a distinct entry "X-ray: Thoracic and Lumbar Spine for 347 subjects (Prof YX Wang)" and an EOS biplanar sub-study of "46 male + 31 female (include 1 non-Os female)" (Prof. Jack Cheng), plus "MRI (total 395)" (Prof Griffith) and "Brain MRI (202 subjects)". Baseline recruitment was 2,000 men + 2,000 women (15 Aug 2001 - 28 Feb 2003 for men); year-2 follow-up 15 Aug 2003 - 31 Mar 2005. The candidate's "films for about 2,000 men at baseline and year 4" overstates year 4: the QIMS 'Healthier Chinese spine' update reports year-4 radiographs read for 1,519 men (and 1,546 women). Radiograph-based analyses in the review use n=1,128 (70-79 age band, Deng et al.). Caveat: the inventory PDF is a wide table and my text extraction flattened the columns, so I could not reliably bind each count to a specific visit — treat the per-visit attribution as unverified.
verdicts.licence: None for the data. No data licence exists because no data release exists. The candidate's "Not stated" is correct and should be read as "no licence, no terms, no agreement". Only the PAPERS are licensed: the Skeletal Radiology review is CC BY 4.0 (verified in the JATS <permissions> block), the QIMS paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (verified: "This is an Open Access article distributed in accordance with the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 4.0 International License"), the JCSM paper is CC BY 4.0. An article licence confers no rights over the underlying images.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same subjects, never the same session — and the gap is stated explicitly, not inferred. Review footnote, verbatim: "QCT was measured at the year-2 follow-up of MrOS Hong Kong study for Chinese men. Half of the corresponding spine radiographs were selected from the baseline study and another half selected from the year-4 follow-up study, since the year-2 follow-up did not have radiograph taken." So every film-to-CT pair is offset by roughly two years, in one direction or the other, in 65+ year-old men — i.e. across an interval in which incident vertebral fracture, disc height loss and progressive kyphosis are the study's own primary endpoints. For any use needing geometric correspondence between a film and a CT this is not a paired dataset. Additionally the L1-L2 slab does not overlap most of the thoracic film, and the hip QCT does not overlap the spine films at all. The candidate's ct_or_cbct_same_subject=true is technically true and practically misleading.
verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed. Real diagnostic lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs of living men do exist in this cohort — attested by CUHK's own variable inventory ("X-ray Spine", "X-ray Spine and Hip", "X-ray: Thoracic and Lumbar Spine for 347 subjects") and by the Genant SQ / OLVFss / ABQ reads published off them. But existence in a filing cabinet is not a release: none of these films is obtainable through any published route.
corrections: PRIMARY RECORD IS NOT A DATASET RECORD. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11652400/ is a review article in Skeletal Radiology, not a repository page. Fetching its full JATS XML from Europe PMC (76,915 bytes) and grepping for 'data avail', 'availability of data', 'upon request', 'on request', 'data sharing' returns ZERO hits. The back matter contains only a Publisher's Note and a Conflicts of interest declaration. There is no data statement at all — which is weaker than 'available upon reasonable request', because no one has even promised anything.

NO RELEASE EXISTS. No repository record, no data DOI, no file list, no file sizes, no access portal, no licence. The three DOIs cited (10.1007/s00256-024-04722-3, 10.21037/qims-2025-1790, 10.1002/jcsm.13728) are all article DOIs. Nothing can be downloaded now, and there is no documented mechanism to request it.

THE ONLY DATA STATEMENT IN THE CITED SET POINTS SOMEWHERE THAT DOES NOT HOLD THIS COHORT. PMC11871091 (JCSM 2025) states: 'Analysed data are available in this manuscript. Raw data are available on the MrOS website (access is subject to approval): https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu'. I opened that site: it is the US MrOS only — 'A multi-center observational study of 5,994 men', recruited at 'Six clinical centers in the United States, located in Birmingham, AL; Minneapolis, MN; Palo Alto, CA; the Monogohela Valley near Pittsburgh, PA; Portland, OR; and San Diego, CA'. Hong Kong is not mentioned anywhere on the home or About pages. The statement is therefore not a valid access route for the HK images the candidate wants.

MrOS ONLINE IS CLOSED RIGHT NOW AND WOULD BAR THE HONG KONG ROUTE ANYWAY. Checked 2026-09-22: https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/DataRelease returns HTTP 200 after redirecting to /Account/Login?ReturnUrl=%2FDataRelease, and that page reads 'System Maintenance in Progress ... all user accounts have been temporarily disabled ... users will need to register using an institutional email address rather than a personal email address. NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong; Cuba; Iran; Iraq; North Korea; Russia; and Venezuela. As a result, we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries.' So the one named portal is (a) down, and (b) explicitly cannot approve a CUHK-affiliated collaborator.

EVEN WHEN OPEN, MrOS ONLINE IS NOT AN IMAGE DOWNLOAD SERVICE. The home page offers to 'download or explore clinical data'; the About page says only that images 'have been archived' ('An extensive bank of data, images (x-rays, DXA scans, QCT scans, HRpQCT scans) and specimens have been archived as part of the MrOS study'). Archived is not served. I found no page offering DICOM or film downloads. I could not verify any image-download path, and I am not going to assume one exists.

CUHK'S OWN STUDY PAGE HAS NO ACCESS ROUTE. https://www.jococ.org/en/mros-msos.php was fetched and fully rendered to text: it describes the cohort and links exactly two PDFs (Appendix_1_variable_inventory_Dec2025.pdf, Appendix_2_Publication_list_Jan2025.pdf) plus a slide deck. There is no data-request form, no application, no DUA, no email for data enquiries, no licence, no statement of any kind about sharing. The candidate's 'it would need a CUHK collaboration' is correct, and there is no published starting point for one.

'THIN-SLICE L1-L2 QCT' IS UNSUPPORTED — NO PRIMARY SOURCE. I found no slice thickness for the MrOS HK SPINE QCT in any source I opened. The only MrOS HK CT protocol stated in a primary source is the HIP QCT, and it is not thin: 'Quantitative CT (QCT) scans of the hip were acquired using a Siemens Somatom Plus 4 scanner ... and GE Medical Systems/lightspeed 16 (Waukesha, WI, USA) in PA and HK studies, respectively ... The scan settings comprised 80 kVp, 280 mA, 3 mm slice thickness and a 512 x 512 matrix, utilizing spiral reconstruction mode' (JCSM 2025). 3 mm at 80 kVp on a 16-slice scanner from ~2004 is a low-dose densitometry protocol, not a geometry-grade acquisition. Do not carry 'thin-slice' forward.

THE GE LIGHTSPEED 16 ATTRIBUTION IS CONFIRMED BUT MISPLACED. That scanner is documented for the HK arm's HIP QCT only. No source I opened names the scanner used for the L1-L2 SPINE QCT. The candidate's 'device' field conflates the two.

COUNT DISCREPANCY WITH THE CENTRE'S OWN INVENTORY. The candidate and the review say 328 with spine QCT; CUHK's Dec-2025 variable inventory says 'QCT (329 Male spine, 332 Male hip)'. Within the review itself the n moves between 328 (QCT-DXA correlation), 324 and 316 (OLVFss subset, 'n = 316, mean age: 73.7 years'). Treat ~325-330 as the spine-QCT ceiling, and note that the JCSM segmentation work used only 100 HK men (200 Pittsburgh + 100 HK = 300), a further cut.

FILMS AND CT ARE NEVER CONTEMPORANEOUS, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO OUTRIGHT: 'Half of the corresponding spine radiographs were selected from the baseline study and another half selected from the year-4 follow-up study, since the year-2 follow-up did not have radiograph taken.' Baseline for men ran 15 Aug 2001 - 28 Feb 2003 and year-2 ran 15 Aug 2003 - 31 Mar 2005, so pairs are offset by roughly two years in either direction, in a 65+ cohort whose measured endpoints are incident vertebral deformity and height loss. This is a longitudinal cohort, not a paired film/CT dataset.

YEAR-4 FILM COUNT OVERSTATED. 'Films for about 2,000 men at baseline and year 4' does not hold for year 4: the QIMS 'Healthier Chinese spine' update reports year-4 radiographs for 1,519 men (and 1,546 women), against 2,000 men recruited at baseline. The CUHK inventory separately lists a much smaller later thoracic+lumbar X-ray set of 347 subjects and an EOS biplanar sub-study of 46 male + 31 female.

NOTHING HERE SERVES A FLUOROSCOPY PROJECT. No fluoroscopy, no C-arm, no projection geometry, no source-detector distances, no pose or landmark annotations, no calibration phantom in the film field (the HA phantom is in the CT scan only). Labels are Genant SQ grades and OLVFss scores — per-vertebra fracture severity, not level identity, not keypoints, not masks. There is no ground truth of the kind this project needs even if the images were obtainable.

COULD NOT CHECK: whether the SFCC ancillary-study process (https://sfcc.ucsf.edu) can reach HK images, and whether the Aging Research Biobank (NIA) holds any MrOS imaging. The biobank collections page renders its results by JavaScript and returned only 'Loading...' to a fetch, so I could not enumerate its MrOS holdings. I also could not open PMC8899940's full text via Europe PMC (the XML endpoint returned a 150-byte stub), so the year-4 film counts above come from the publisher HTML at qims.amegroups.org rather than the archival XML.

COULD NOT CHECK: whether the films are analogue or digitised, their pixel dimensions, or their storage format. No source I opened states any of this. Since the baseline films date from 2001-2003 at a Hong Kong public hospital, screen-film with later digitisation is likely but I have no primary source and will not assert it.

verdicts.real_xray: CONFIRMED, and stronger than the candidate states. Two independent primary methods sections say the films are real acquisitions on living men: "Left lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs were obtained by adjusting exposure parameters according to participants' body weight and height. The standard parameters were: thoracic spine: Film/Focus Distance: 40 inches, voltage 60-70 kVp, Exposure Time: 2 seconds; and lumbar spine: Film/Focus Distance: 40 inches, Imaging voltage 80-90 kVp, Exposure Time: 1 sec" (biorxiv 139402, MrOS/MsOS HK methods). Spine radiographs were centred on T7 for the thoracic film (T3-L1) and on L3 for the lumbar film (T12-S1). These are screen-film radiographs: "Hard copies of spine radiographs were taken and then digitalized later" (arXiv 1611.03488), digitised at 300 dpi on a VIDAR DiagnosticPRO Advantage film digitiser with ClinicalExpress 4.0. So: not DRR, not simulated, not MV portal. Two caveats that cut against usability. (1) LATERAL ONLY — no AP/frontal view is described anywhere; every MrOS/MsOS HK radiograph paper I opened reads left lateral films. (2) The digital copies may be partial: the ABQ paper states hard-copy film was the primary reading medium, "aided with digitalized format for difficult cases", and the 300 dpi digitisation is documented only for the 1,100 subjects randomly selected into the disc-morphometry study. Whether the whole cohort exists as digital images is not stated in any source I could open.
verdicts.paired_ct: PARTLY CONFIRMED, and the pairing is much weaker than "a thin-slice L1-L2 QCT". Same-subject CT exists: Wáng states 328 Chinese men (73.6 +/- 4.4 y) had QCT LS BMD and DXA at the same time, from "the MrOS Hong Kong study year-2 follow-up conducted during the period of September 2003 to March 2005", and 316 of them also had a spine radiograph. But the same footnote refutes any notion of a contemporaneous pair: "QCT was measured at the year-2 follow-up ... Half of the corresponding spine radiographs were selected from the baseline study and another half selected from the year-4 follow-up study, since the year-2 follow-up did not have radiograph taken." So every pair is ~2 years off in one direction or the other; none is same-visit. The "thin-slice" claim has NO Hong Kong primary source. I could not find any published HK spine-QCT acquisition protocol. The only primary protocol I could open is the US MrOS operations manual (Lang, UCSF, 2000, on the NIA Aging Research Biobank): L1/L2 series = 120 kVp, 150 mA, 512^2, FOV 48 cm, spiral pitch 1, 1-mm slices, superior limit 5 mm above the L1 superior endplate and inferior limit 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate. That is a ~7-9 cm slab of exactly two vertebral bodies. Applying it to Hong Kong rests only on the jcsm paper's phrase "three international cohorts with similar protocols" — and that same paper documents the HK hip CT on a DIFFERENT scanner from the US one, so "similar" is not "identical". The US manual also defines a second lumbar series (mid-L3 to mid-L5, 5-mm slices, 80 kVp/140 mA) for aortic calcium and paraspinal muscle; no source says Hong Kong acquired it. Hip CT is separate: "QCT scans of the hip were acquired using a Siemens Somatom Plus 4 ... and GE Medical Systems/lightspeed 16 ... in PA and HK studies, respectively ... covering from the femoral head to 3.5 cm below the lesser trochanter ... 80 kVp, 280 mA, 3 mm slice thickness and a 512 x 512 matrix" — so the GE LightSpeed 16 claim is confirmed for the HK HIP scan, but it is 3 mm, not thin-slice, and its stated superior limit is the femoral head, i.e. no lumbar spine. The visit at which the HK hip CT was taken is not stated. Net: there is no single CT volume in this cohort that contains the lumbosacral junction.
verdicts.anatomy: REFUTED for the anatomy this project needs. Films: lateral thoracic (T3-L1, centred T7) and lateral lumbar (T12-S1, centred L3); vertebrae read T4-L4 (Genant SQ, ABQ) or T4-L5 (OLVFss, morphometry). So the lumbar spine IS present on film and S1 is at the caudal edge of the lumbar film by the stated centring — but the sacrum below S1 and the pelvis are not targets, no AP view exists, and no source states that the iliac crests, SI joints or femoral heads are in the field. CT: the spine QCT is L1-L2 only; the hip QCT runs femoral head to 3.5 cm below the lesser trochanter and therefore contains acetabulum and proximal femur but no lumbar spine — sacral coverage is not stated in any source and should not be assumed. For a lumbosacral-junction / LSTV / level-identity use, there is no CT of the sacrum or of L3-S1 in the same subject. A year-14 follow-up did whole-spine MRI on 271 of these men (mean 82.8 y) — MRI, not CT, and a decade after the films.
verdicts.counts: PARTLY CONFIRMED, with an internal inconsistency in the candidate's own source chain. Cohort: MrOS (Hong Kong) recruited 2,000 community-dwelling Chinese men (mean 72.3 y, range 65-92), Aug 2001 - Mar 2003; MsOS (HK) recruited 2,000 women in parallel. Baseline radiographs actually read: 1,954 men (and 1,953 women). Year-4 radiology follow-up: "1,519 men and 1,546 women had X-ray for the spine at year-4, which present all the participants who attended the FU in person" — so year-4 films are ~1,519 men, NOT ~2,000. At two films per man per visit (thoracic + lumbar), that is roughly 3,900 baseline and 3,040 year-4 male films, an order-of-magnitude figure the candidate does not give. Spine QCT n is quoted THREE different ways by the same author: 328 (QCT+DXA, PMC11652400 and PMC12514713), 316 (QCT+radiograph, PMC11652400), and 324 ("The QCT data are from MrOS Hong Kong year-2 follow-up study with 324 Chinese men", PMC12514713 Fig. 5). The usable paired figure is 316, not 328. HK hip QCT count is not stated anywhere I could open; the deep-learning paper drew 100 HK hip scans at random, implying more exist but not how many.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: Candidate's "no pose" UNDERSTATES what exists, but nothing is released. Confirmed label types, all vertebra-level on the films: Genant semi-quantitative grades (T4-L4), ABQ classification into 5 categories per vertebra (T4-L4), and OLVFss, which assigns each vertebra 0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -2.5 or -3 and sums T4-L5. Beyond scores, real landmark annotation exists for a subset: "Morphometric measurement was performed in each vertebra from T4 to L5 using a program written with Matlab ... Eight digitized reference points were manually placed for each vertebra", on 592 men and 491 women. That is per-vertebra point geometry on real lateral films — closer to pose than the candidate allows. No 3-D pose, no C-arm/geometry parameters, no CT-to-film registration of any kind is described. And no source states that any of these annotations, or the images they sit on, have ever been distributed.
verdicts.licence: "Not stated" CONFIRMED, and worth guarding against a specific trap: the candidate's primary URL (PMC11652400) is CC BY and PMC12514713 is CC BY-NC-ND, but those licences cover the ARTICLE TEXT ONLY. Neither licenses the underlying radiographs, CT or per-vertebra scores. I found no data-sharing statement, no DUA, no repository accession and no licence for MrOS (Hong Kong) imaging in any of the four candidate evidence URLs or in the three additional primary sources I opened. The one data-availability statement that exists in the chain (jcsm/PMC11871091) points to https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu, which is the wrong cohort (see access_now).
verdicts.access_now: REFUTED that any access route exists, and one stated route is wrong. The jcsm 2025 paper, which used 100 Hong Kong hip CTs, states "Raw data are available on the MrOS website (access is subject to approval): https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu". That site is US-only: its About page says MrOS "began in 2000. Six clinical centers in the United States, located in Birmingham, AL; Minneapolis, MN; Palo Alto, CA; the Monogohela Valley near Pittsburgh, PA; Portland, OR; and San Diego, CA recruited 5,994 men", and the home page reads "A multi-center observational study of 5,994 men". Hong Kong is not among the centres and is not mentioned anywhere on the site. So the data-availability statement does not, in fact, point at the Hong Kong data. Two further blocks, both on mrosonline.ucsf.edu/DataRelease as of today: "all user accounts have been temporarily disabled" pending a new NIH-required registration system, and "NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong ... As a result, we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries" — which, if the same policy reaches any NIH-funded MrOS HK holdings (MrOS HK was NIH R01 AR049439-funded), cuts the other way for a CUHK-side transfer. No CUHK/JCCOCC data portal, dbGaP accession, Zenodo deposit or request form surfaced. Realistic route is an individual collaboration with the CUHK holders (Y.X.J. Wáng, J.F. Griffith, J.C.S. Leung, T.C.Y. Kwok), with film digitisation possibly still to be done, and with a 2001-2005 consent that predates AI reuse and is not quoted in any source I could open.
corrections: 'Thin-slice L1-L2 QCT' is not sourced for Hong Kong. No HK spine-QCT acquisition protocol appears in any of the candidate's evidence URLs or in anything else I could open. The only primary protocol available is the US MrOS operations manual (Lang 2000, NIA Aging Research Biobank): L1/L2 at 1-mm slices, 120 kVp/150 mA, from 5 mm above the L1 superior endplate to 5 mm below the L2 inferior endplate. Importing it into the HK cohort rests on the phrase 'similar protocols' in the jcsm paper, which in the same paragraph documents a DIFFERENT scanner for HK than for the US site. Treat HK spine-CT slice thickness as unknown.

The CT is not a usable lumbosacral volume under any reading. The spine QCT is a two-vertebra slab (L1-L2). The hip QCT is stated to cover 'from the femoral head to 3.5 cm below the lesser trochanter' at 3 mm, which contains no lumbar spine; sacral coverage is not stated and must not be inferred. There is no CT or CBCT of the sacrum, the lumbosacral junction, or L3-S1 in these men. The candidate's anatomy field, by listing 'L1-L2 QCT, hip QCT' next to 'lateral thoracic and lumbar spine films', reads as if the pelvis were covered on CT; it is not.

The films-to-CT gap is structural, not incidental. Wang's own footnote: 'QCT was measured at the year-2 follow-up ... Half of the corresponding spine radiographs were selected from the baseline study and another half selected from the year-4 follow-up study, since the year-2 follow-up did not have radiograph taken.' There is no same-visit pair for any subject. The candidate's '1-3 years apart' should be 'approximately 2 years, always, by design, in one direction or the other'.

Radiographs are LATERAL ONLY. Every methods section I opened reads 'Left lateral thoracic and lumbar spine radiographs'. No AP or frontal view is described for MrOS/MsOS (Hong Kong). The candidate's xray_kind says 'lateral', but 'serves: A' and the pitch as an X-ray/CT pairing corpus should carry the constraint explicitly: one projection, one direction, no second view for any subject.

The subject count for films at year 4 is wrong. Not 'about 2,000 men at baseline and year 4' — 1,954 men had baseline radiographs read, and '1,519 men and 1,546 women had X-ray for the spine at year-4, which present all the participants who attended the FU in person'. Attrition is 22%.

The spine-QCT n is unstable across the candidate's own sources: 328 (QCT+DXA), 316 (QCT+radiograph, the number that matters for a pair), and 324 ('The QCT data are from MrOS Hong Kong year-2 follow-up study with 324 Chinese men') in the same author's 2025 paper. The paired, usable figure is 316, not 328.

The digital images may not exist for the whole cohort. The ABQ methods state 'Hard copies of spine radiographs were taken and then digitalized later. Hard copy film was used for analysis primarily, aided with digitalized format for difficult cases.' The only documented digitisation (300 dpi, VIDAR DiagnosticPRO Advantage, ClinicalExpress 4.0) is for the 1,100 subjects randomly drawn into the disc-morphometry study. Whether ~3,900 baseline male films exist as digital files is unstated; film digitisation may be a cost the acquiring project bears.

The stated access route is the wrong cohort. The only data-availability statement in the evidence chain (jcsm/PMC11871091) sends readers to mrosonline.ucsf.edu for 'raw data', but that portal is the US MrOS: 'Six clinical centers in the United States ... recruited 5,994 men'. Hong Kong is not listed there. Do not record MrOS Online as an access route for this candidate.

Two live blocks on that portal anyway, as of 2026-09-22: 'all user accounts have been temporarily disabled' pending NIH-mandated re-registration, and 'NIH also restricts data sharing with institutions based in the following countries: China, including Hong Kong ... we will not be able to approve users affiliated with institutions in these countries.'

Do not read the article licences as data licences. PMC11652400 is CC BY and PMC12514713 is CC BY-NC-ND; both cover the text of a review article. Neither confers any right over the radiographs, the CT, or the per-vertebra scores. 'Licence: Not stated' is correct and should not be upgraded by anyone who notices the CC BY badge on the landing page.

'No pose' understates the annotation. Per-vertebra Genant SQ (T4-L4), ABQ five-category classification (T4-L4), and OLVFss per-vertebra scores summed T4-L5 all exist; and for 592 men and 491 women, 'Eight digitized reference points were manually placed for each vertebra' from T4 to L5. That is manual landmark geometry on real lateral films. None of it is documented as released.

The candidate's primary URL is a REVIEW ARTICLE about a BMD cutpoint, not a dataset descriptor. It contains no methods section for the imaging, no data statement, no cohort description beyond n and age, and no imaging protocol. Every protocol fact above had to be recovered from sources outside the candidate's four evidence URLs (the MrOS/MsOS HK radiograph methods in biorxiv 139402 and arXiv 1611.03488, and the US MrOS CT operations manual). Nothing in this candidate has ever been assembled or described as a dataset by anyone.

Unverified and left unverified: at which visit the HK hip QCT was acquired; how many HK men have hip QCT at all (the deep-learning paper drew 100 at random); whether HK acquired the US protocol's second lumbar series (mid-L3 to mid-L5, 5 mm); the radiograph system make and model ('radiograph system not stated' in the candidate is correct — no source names it, only the kVp/exposure/40-inch FFD); and whether the 2001-2003 consent permits image transfer or machine-learning reuse.

candidate.name: Framingham Heart Study MDCT: chest and abdomen CT with lateral and frontal CT scouts spanning T4-S1
candidate.why_relevant: About 3,529 thoracolumbar CTs (MDCT-1, 2002-05) whose lateral and frontal scouts span T4-S1, plus a later 64-slice wave. The scouts are real X-ray projections in the same geometry as the CT, but they are scanograms, not radiographs or C-arm frames. Conventional lateral spine films exist only for the Original Cohort, who were not in the MDCT study, so no participant has both a radiograph and a CT. dbGaP holds derived variables only. Images come from the FHS Repository through a Research Application, and fees apply.
candidate.institution: Boston University / NHLBI (FHS); Hebrew SeniorLife
candidate.device: GE LightSpeed Ultra 8-slice; GE Discovery VCT 64-slice
candidate.anatomy: Chest and abdomen CT; scouts T4-S1
candidate.subjects: Living Offspring and Third Generation participants; 3,529 in MDCT-1
candidate.n_images: About 3,529 CT exams with scouts, plus the second wave
candidate.pose_or_labels: Scout pose implicit in the CT; SQ fracture grades and 6-point morphometry T4-L4 read on the scouts

verdicts.access_now: NO DOWNLOAD NOW, AND NO CONFIRMED IMAGE RELEASE PATH. The primary URL resolves (HTTP 200, 111,959 bytes). But no route serves the images: (1) dbGaP phs000007.v30.p11 and its substudy phs000078.v12.p5 ("Framingham SHARe Osteoporosis Study") expose Phenotype Datasets / Variables / Molecular Datasets / Documents only — the esummary hits for MDCT are protocol PDFs ("Multidetector Computed Tomography Study...", "Cardiac CT Scans, Gen 3 Exam 1: Protocol"), not images; (2) BioLINCC framcohort is labelled "Study Datasets Only" and lists exam data from the first 32 exams, data dictionary, protocols, forms — no imaging; (3) the FHS Repository requires the web-based FHS Research Application. The proposal page is the only page that names imaging at all: "The Research Committee reviews requests for clinical data, including exam chart review and imaging data." Gates: routing to Research Committee -> Peer Review -> FHS Executive Committee for final approval; IRB Expedited or Full Board required and "IRB Exempt review is not allowed"; signed Data and Materials Distribution Agreement (DMDA, a material transfer agreement); fees. Timeline: submit by the 3rd Monday of the month for same-month review, and "allow 6-8 weeks before sponsor deadlines." Crucially, no FHS page catalogues CT images as a distributable item — the catalogue links are Phenotypic Data, Genetic Data, Exam Overview — and the FHS-BAP digital-imaging page lists only brain MRI DICOM (since 1999) and cardiac MRI (2002-2006), with zero mention of body/chest/abdomen CT or scouts. The nearest thing to a data availability statement in the literature is the 2024 JBMR paper: "The procedure for requesting data from the Framingham Heart Study can be found at https://www.framinghamheartstudy.org/" — a pointer to a request process, not a release. The three older evidence papers (2010, 2012, 2016) carry no data availability statement at all. FHS also publishes a heading "FHS Data Items Not Currently Available for Distribution" whose content is "(Coming Soon...)", so the list of what it will not release is itself unpublished. Estimated wall-clock to first pixel: months, contingent on committee approval; realistically requires a collaborator inside the FHS/Hebrew SeniorLife/MGH network, which is how every published user of these scouts (Samelson, Bouxsein, Kiel, Allaire, Hoffmann) obtained them.
verdicts.licence: No licence. Not open, not CC, no DUA-free tier. Access is governed by the Framingham Data and Materials Distribution Agreement (DMDA), an investigator-initiated material transfer agreement, plus mandatory investigator IRB approval at Expedited or Full Board level (Exempt explicitly disallowed, because "FHS is a study of a single community and hence one's identity can be more easily ascertained, even if traditional identifiers are removed"). Fees apply to the FHS Internal Repository: "External repositories dbGaP and BIOLINCC do not require service fees to access their data, while the FHS Internal Repository may require service fees or subcontract for data access," and "In order to avoid fees, please consider applying for FHS data through an external data repository." Published FHS Service Center schedule: base $1,000 for datasets supporting approved manuscripts, pilot work or grant submissions; Simple (<=15 phenotypes) $3,000; Moderate (16-49) $5,000; Advanced (50+) $10,000, including up to 3 hours consultation (5 for large-scale). NOTE: every published price is denominated in PHENOTYPE COUNT. There is no published price, unit, or line item for imaging or DICOM distribution, so the true cost of an image request is unknown and unquotable.
verdicts.counts: MDCT-1 (2002-2005): "3,529 participants in the MDCT Study (age 40-90 years, mean 51 years)" — confirmed verbatim in Samelson et al. The 3,529 is a PARTICIPANT count from the parent MDCT study; no source states 3,529 scout image pairs were archived or are retrievable, so "About 3,529 CT exams with scouts" is an inference. MDCT-2 (2008-2011, 64-slice Discovery VCT): no single published enrolment number found. Downstream Ns actually reported: 100 (Samelson 2010 reliability subsample, 50 F / 50 M); 4,099 assessed for vertebral fracture across all three generations, of whom 3,333 from Gen2+Gen3 had volumetric BMD (Liu 2012); 1,186 (650 F, 536 M, mean age ~66.5) in Allaire disc-height work on 64-slice scouts; 2,063 evaluable for kyphosis across both waves; 1,197 (889 Offspring + 308 Third Generation, age >=50) with BOTH waves in the 2024 longitudinal fracture study. So the population with a usable, curated, twice-imaged spine is ~1,200, an order of magnitude below the headline 3,529.
verdicts.anatomy: Scout extent CONFIRMED verbatim: "frontal and lateral low energy 2D scanograms extending from the upper thoracic (T4) to sacral (S1) vertebral levels" (Samelson et al.), and "lateral low-energy scanograms spanning from the upper thoracic spine (T4) to the sacrum (S1)" (Allaire et al.). Reads are narrower than the field: semiquantitative grading covers "13 vertebral levels from T4 to L4," and 6-point morphometry likewise T4-L4 — S1 and the lumbosacral junction are IMAGED but never LABELLED. IMPORTANT MISMATCH the candidate record does not state: the 3-D CT does not cover T4-S1. The 2024 JBMR methods describe two discontinuous blocks — a thoracic series at 2.5 mm slice thickness and an abdominal series of "60 contiguous CT slices (150 mm)" ending just above the lumbosacral junction, with volumetric coverage reported as T4/T5 to L4/L5. So the 2-D scout spans T4-S1 while the paired 3-D volume is two limited stacks that stop around L4/L5. For a project keyed to naming the lumbosacral junction, the one vertebra that matters is outside the labelled range and largely outside the volumetric range.
verdicts.real_xray: Yes, genuine X-ray transmission projections, and the candidate is right to flag the qualifier. These are CT localizer scanograms: stationary fan-beam source with the table translating, acquired on a GE LightSpeed Ultra 8-slice (MDCT-1, 2002-2005) and a GE Discovery VCT 64-slice (MDCT-2, 2008-2011), at "low energy." That geometry is neither a conventional radiograph (no cone-beam divergence along the long axis, no grid, no standard SID, no patient-positioning variability of a film) nor a C-arm frame (no obliquity, no image intensifier distortion, no pincushion, no rotation, no hardware in field, no dose-limited noise). Domain distance from fluoroscopy is large and is exactly the gap this project has already measured (19.7% vs 95.1% panel gap is domain, not crop quality). Treating scouts as a fluoro proxy would repeat that error; they are closer to a DRR than to a C-arm frame, and the project already generates DRRs at will.
verdicts.paired_ct: Same-session pairing is real and is the record's strongest genuine claim: the scout is the localizer for the CT it precedes, so the projection geometry is fixed by the scanner and the pose is implicit — no registration needed. But three caveats. (1) The paired CT is NOT a T4-S1 spine volume; it is a thoracic series plus a ~150 mm abdominal block stopping near L4/L5 (2024 JBMR methods), so the pair does not cover the lumbosacral junction in 3-D. (2) No public source states the scout DICOMs were archived alongside the axial series, or that either is in the distributable catalogue — the only imaging FHS documents as held in native DICOM is brain MRI (since 1999) and cardiac MRI (2002-2006). (3) The claim "no participant has both a radiograph and a CT" is design-consistent but NOT directly sourced: Liu et al. state the Original cohort had "lateral radiographs" in 1992-1993 while the 2nd and 3rd generations had "CT examinations including lateral scout views" in 2002-2005. That two-arm design implies no overlap; no source I opened asserts zero overlap explicitly, and one grant abstract loosely describes vertebral fracture assessment "by x-rays" in Original, Offspring and Gen 3 cohorts, which is the kind of loose wording that could hide an overlap. Report as inference.
corrections: ACCESS overstated. The record says 'Images come from the FHS Repository through a Research Application, and fees apply' as if the pathway were established for these images. Only a generic pathway is documented: the proposal page says 'The Research Committee reviews requests for clinical data, including exam chart review and imaging data.' No FHS page catalogues CT images, let alone scouts, as a distributable item; the offered catalogue links are Phenotypic Data, Genetic Data and Exam Overview. The FHS-BAP digital-imaging page lists native DICOM for brain MRI (since 1999) and cardiac MRI (2002-2006) ONLY, with no body/chest/abdomen CT. I could find no primary source confirming that MDCT scout images are distributable, and no external group that obtained them. Correct status: 'request pathway exists in principle; image distribution unconfirmed.'

FEES are unquotable for this use. The published FHS Service Center schedule is denominated entirely in phenotype count ($1,000 base; $3,000 / $5,000 / $10,000 for <=15 / 16-49 / 50+ phenotypes). There is no published unit price for images or DICOM. Any cost estimate for a scout-image request is a guess.

FHS's own exclusion list is unpublished. The data-availability page carries the heading 'Statement on Data Items Not Currently Available for Distribution' followed by 'FHS Data Items Not Currently Available for Distribution (Coming Soon...)'. FHS acknowledges a category of non-distributable items and has not said what is in it. Imaging could be in it; nothing rules that out.

doi_or_id incomplete. The record cites 'dbGaP phs000007 (derived variables only)'. The osteoporosis and vertebral-fracture derived variables actually sit in the substudy phs000078.v12.p5, 'Framingham SHARe Osteoporosis Study', a substudy of phs000007 (confirmed on the dbGaP study page, which exposes Phenotype Datasets / Variables / Molecular Datasets / Analyses / Documents tabs and no image datasets). Both accessions are variables-only, so the 'derived variables only' half is correct, but the accession is wrong for the osteoporosis reads.

Citation year off by one. 'Samelson 2011' is Samelson EJ, Christiansen BA, Demissie S, Broe KE, Zhou Y, Meng CA, Yu W, Cheng X, O'Donnell CJ, Hoffmann U, Genant HK, Kiel DP, Bouxsein ML, 'Reliability of vertebral fracture assessment using multidetector CT lateral scout views: the Framingham Osteoporosis Study', Osteoporosis International, published online 21 May 2010 (PMID 20495902), print issue 2011. 'Allaire 2017' is Eur Spine J, published online 18 October 2016, issue 2017, and it is a disc-height methods paper (modified DCRA, six automatically placed morphometry points), not a fracture-prevalence paper.

n_images is an inference. 3,529 is the MDCT-1 PARTICIPANT count quoted by Samelson et al. No source reports the number of archived or retrievable scout images, and the second 64-slice wave has no published enrolment count that I found. The population with curated spine reads at both waves is ~1,197.

ANATOMY mismatch not flagged in the record. The scout spans T4-S1 but the paired volumetric CT does not: the 2024 JBMR methods describe a thoracic series plus an abdominal series of '60 contiguous CT slices (150 mm)' with volumetric coverage reported as T4/T5 to L4/L5. Labelled reads are narrower still, T4-L4 for both the semiquantitative grades and the 6-point morphometry. The lumbosacral junction, the level this project exists to name, is unlabelled and largely outside the 3-D coverage.

'No participant has both a radiograph and a CT' is unsourced inference. Liu et al. state Original cohort lateral radiographs 1992-1993 and Gen2/Gen3 CT lateral scouts 2002-2005, which implies the split by design, but no primary source asserts zero overlap, and at least one grant abstract loosely describes fracture assessment 'by x-rays' across Original, Offspring and Gen 3.

SERVES rating 'A' is not supportable on access grounds. Nothing here can be downloaded, the images are not catalogued as distributable, and the labelled range excludes the target level. These are scanograms, not radiographs or C-arm frames, so the domain gap this project already measured (19.7% vs 95.1%, attributed to domain, not crop quality) applies in full. A DRR rendered from CTSpinoPelvic1K reproduces the scout geometry more faithfully and is already in hand.

Could not verify whether the scout DICOMs were retained at all, as opposed to being read once at the reading centre and discarded with only the grades kept. No primary source addresses scout retention. Stated as unknown rather than guessed.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real X-ray transmission projections, but they are CT localizers, not radiographs and not fluoroscopy. The FHS CT Manual of Procedures (dbGaP phs000007 document phd000276 / phd000277) states verbatim: "Scout images will consist of a frontal and lateral low energy 2D scanogram" and "acquiring two scout images of the thorax (Frontal and lateral scout images, aka scanograms or topograms)". Allaire 2017 (ESJ, open-access manuscript) states: "Scout images were lateral low-energy scanograms spanning from the upper thoracic spine (T4) to the sacrum (S1)." Nothing simulated, no DRR, no MV portal; kVp/mA and dose estimates are given in the protocol. Geometry is a translating fan beam (scanogram), NOT a point-source cone-beam projection, so it is a poor stand-in for a C-arm frame: no perspective magnification along the table axis, no obliquity, supine only (Allaire: "the images used in this study were acquired with subjects lying supine").
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, same subject, same session, same table position, but the 3-D coverage is far smaller than the scout's. Per the protocol, MDCT-1 is NOT a chest-and-abdomen CT: it is two ECG-gated cardiac series ("Scan Coverage: 2 cm below the carina extending to the base of the heart") plus one helical abdominal-aorta series ("starting 15 cm above S1 vertebra and stopping at the superior endplate of S1"). There is no continuous T4-S1 volume. Liu 2012 (PMC3375687) reports that on the axial QCT volume "in many instances the L2 level was not included due to technical issues" and that L3 "was present in the highest proportion of participants (around 98%)" - so the reliably paired 3-D range is roughly L3 to the top of S1. Everything below the S1 superior endplate (rest of sacrum, SI joints, acetabula, femoral heads) is absent from the CT.
verdicts.anatomy: 2-D scouts: thoracolumbar spine, frontal and lateral, stated span T4 to S1; the protocol requires the lateral scout to "adequately identify the L5-S1 disk space" and says it "should be similar to a routine chest/abdomen/pelvis scout in coverage". Lumbar spine present. Sacrum only at/around S1 (the top); no evidence of full sacrum, and no evidence the pelvic ring, acetabula or femoral heads are within the scout. Every published reading stops at L4 (T4-L4, 13 levels) - Samelson 2011 and Allaire 2017 both; Liu 2012 does not mention L5 or the sacrum at all. 3-D CT: heart level plus roughly L1/L2-to-S1-top abdomen (see paired_ct). So for a spinopelvic or lumbosacral-junction task, L5, the sacrum below S1 and the pelvis are effectively not there.
verdicts.counts: Subjects: MDCT-1 (2002-2005, GE LightSpeed 8-slice) was planned in the protocol as "1200 Offspring Cohort subjects and 1900 selected Gen 3 subjects (plus approximately 400 from the Family Study)" = ~3,500. Samelson 2011 refers to 3,529 who underwent cardiac imaging 2002-2005; Liu 2012 counts "3448 members of the 2nd and 3rd generation cohorts who underwent CT examinations including lateral scout views in years 2002-2005". So ~3.4-3.5k exams, and 3,448 is the number actually tied to scout views in a primary source. Images: at least 2 scanograms per exam (frontal + lateral), i.e. roughly 7k scout images in wave 1, but no source states a scout image count. Second wave (GE Discovery VCT 64-slice) is confirmed to exist by Allaire 2017 (n=1,186 aged 50+ analysed); I found no primary source for the size of that wave.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: No pose in any registration sense. A CT localizer carries DICOM plane geometry relating it to the CT frame, but it is not a perspective projection, there is no source-detector geometry, no calibration and no published 2-D/3-D correspondence for these images. Labels: semiquantitative Genant grades (0-3) at T4-L4 and six-point vertebral morphometry (SpineAnalyzer, Optasia) read on the scouts exist in the literature (Samelson 2011 reliability substudy n=100; Liu 2012 VFrx n=4,099 pooled across cohorts; Allaire 2017 morphometry n=1,186). I could NOT find a released dataset of those scout-derived labels. The only vertebral-fracture dataset documented in dbGaP phs000007 is "Vertebral Fractures Semi-Quantitative Data, Original Cohort, Exams 10, 14, 22" (t_xrbonefxv_1993_0_0554s): SQ grades at 13 levels (T4-T12, L1-L4) for 705 Original Cohort persons read on plain radiographs, not on scouts. No segmentation masks, no landmarks, no level boxes are documented anywhere.
verdicts.licence: FHS Research Application (BU/NHLBI) plus committee review; the FHS Service Center publishes a fee schedule (base $1,000 for datasets for approved manuscripts, pilot work or grant submissions). dbGaP phs000007 is controlled access and holds phenotype variables and protocol documents only. None of these documents state terms for image release, so the licence under which scout images would be supplied is unknown.
verdicts.access_now: Not demonstrably obtainable. I could not find a primary source stating that FHS distributes CT scout/localizer or body-CT images to outside investigators. The FHS "Available FHS Data" page (the candidate's own URL) lists phenotypic, genetic, omics, protocol and biospecimen data and does not mention imaging at all. The Research Application page and FAQ do not mention images, DICOM or scans. BioLINCC's Framingham Offspring entry is marked "Study Datasets Only". The one FHS imaging release documented in native DICOM is brain MRI (FHS Brain Aging Program: "Brain MRI scans in their native form (e.g., DICOM images), collected since 1999"). The images do exist and were archived - the protocol describes technologists pushing "the Scout, Coronary Arteries 1 (CA1), Coronary Arteries 2 (CA2), and Abdominal Aorta (AA)" to the MGH server with image backup - but "on request" is an inference, not a documented path. Treat as: ask FHS directly, expect committee review and months, and expect to have to argue for a non-cardiac, non-brain image pull.
corrections: REFUTED as stated: anatomy "Chest and abdomen CT". The MDCT-1 3-D acquisition is two ECG-gated cardiac series (2 cm below carina to base of heart) plus a single 150 mm helical abdominal-aorta series that stops at the superior endplate of S1 (dbGaP phs000007 protocol phd000276/phd000277). There is no whole chest-abdomen volume and no continuous T4-S1 CT.

REFUTED: the paired CT does not cover the lumbosacral junction usefully. It stops at the S1 superior endplate, so sacrum below S1, SI joints, acetabula and femoral heads are absent. Liu 2012: L2 "was not included due to technical issues" in many cases; L3 present in ~98%. Reliable paired 3-D range is about L3 to S1 top.

NOT SUPPORTED: access. No primary source says FHS releases CT scout or body-CT images. The FHS Available-Data page lists no imaging; the Research Application page and FAQ never mention images; BioLINCC Framingham Offspring is "Study Datasets Only"; the only documented DICOM release is brain MRI via FHS-BAP. "Images come from the FHS Repository through a Research Application, and fees apply" is an inference from the general dataset fee schedule, not a stated image policy.

PARTLY REFUTED: labels. SQ grades and six-point morphometry on the scouts exist only inside published analyses. The only vertebral-fracture dataset documented in dbGaP phs000007 is Original Cohort plain-radiograph SQ grades (t_xrbonefxv_1993_0_0554s, 705 persons, T4-T12/L1-L4, exams 10/14/22) - i.e. on the cohort that has NO CT. No scout-derived label file is documented as released.

CORRECTED count: 3,529 is the cardiac-imaging denominator (Samelson 2011). The number tied to lateral scout views in a primary source is 3,448 (Liu 2012). The protocol planned 1200 Offspring + 1900 Gen3 + ~400 Family Study.

CORRECTED: "pose" is overstated. A scanogram is a translating fan beam, not a cone-beam perspective projection; there is no source-detector geometry, no calibration, no published 2-D/3-D correspondence. Fixed AP and lateral, supine, no obliquity. For C-arm/fluoroscopy work this is a geometry mismatch, not a pose-labelled pair.

CORRECTED: n_images undercounts. Each exam yields at least two scanograms (frontal AND lateral) per the protocol table ("Scout of thorax and abdomen ... 7 sec x 2"), not one. Published readings used the lateral only.

BAD EVIDENCE URL: the dbGaP esummary URL in the candidate resolves to a mixed set including a Women's Health Initiative fracture-outcomes document (phs000200) and aorta-diameter protocols; only phd003301 (Original Cohort radiograph SQ) and phd000276/277 (CT protocols) are relevant. Cite the protocol documents directly.

UNVERIFIED (not refuted): "no participant has both a radiograph and a CT". Consistent with the sources - radiographs are Original Cohort exams 10/14/22 (1967-69, 1975-77, 1992-93) and MDCT enrolled Offspring + Gen3 (+ ~400 Family Study) - but no source states per-person non-overlap.

UNVERIFIED: size and coverage of the 64-slice second wave. Allaire 2017 confirms a GE Discovery VCT 64-slice wave with lateral scanograms spanning T4-S1 and n=1,186 analysed aged 50+, but I found no protocol document for that wave's scan coverage; do not assume it reaches below S1 either.
