FIT NOTE: for a spine-fluoroscopy project this serves at best as a large supine AP/lateral thoracolumbar projection corpus with same-session partial CT. It is not a radiograph set, not a fluoroscopy set, has no pelvis, no L5/sacrum reading, and no released labels or pose.

candidate.name: AGES-Reykjavik: L1-L2 and hip QCT with lateral CT scouts T6-L4 (no radiographs)
candidate.why_relevant: A CT-localizer source only. Lateral scouts from T6 to L4 sit in the same geometry as a 1 mm L1-L2 QCT and a hip CT, for thousands of older Icelanders at baseline and follow-up. There are no conventional spine or pelvis radiographs: hip OA was graded on DRRs made from the CT. The IHA provides protocols by request, and published analyses were collaborations.
candidate.institution: Icelandic Heart Association (Hjartavernd) with NIA
candidate.device: Siemens Somatom Sensation 4
candidate.anatomy: L1-L2 QCT, hip/pelvic CT; lateral scout T6-L4
candidate.subjects: Living older adults: 5,764 at baseline, 3,411 at AGES-II
candidate.pose_or_labels: Scout pose implicit in the CT; Genant SQ fracture grades from the scouts

verdicts.access_now:
NO DOWNLOAD, AND NO DATA RECORD OF ANY KIND. The "url" given is not a repository record — https://hjarta.is/en/research/ages-phase-1/ returns HTTP 200 but is a prose study-description page (last modified 2021-03-17). It has no file list, no sizes, no licence, no download link, no application form. I enumerated the whole site from https://hjarta.is/page-sitemap.xml: there is no data-access, data-request or data-portal page in either the English or the Icelandic tree. The single sentence on access is "Access to protocols and the data dictionary is available by request." — that is protocols and a data dictionary, NOT images and not the phenotype data.

The three cited papers' data availability statements, read from the JATS XML, are three different flavours of restricted, and none of them mentions images:
- Front Endocrinol 2025 (PMC11978659, 10.3389/fendo.2025.1566424): "The datasets presented in this article are not readily available because they were used under license. Restrictions also apply to the availability of data generated or analyzed during this study to preserve patient confidentiality. Data from the AGES-Reykjavik study are available through collaboration under a data usage agreement with the Icelandic Heart Association. Requests to access the datasets should be directed to [e-mail withheld]."
- BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2026 (PMC13321617, 10.1186/s12891-026-09893-9): "Data are principally available through the Icelandic Heart Association (hjarta.is). Please check for terms and conditions with the IHA." — a pointer to a page that offers only protocols and a data dictionary.
- JBMR 2025/26 (PMC13525202, 10.1093/jbmr/zjaf202): "The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author." — the canonical non-release; it must be reported as such.

The images themselves sit in Hjartavernd's own PACS. The IHA imaging page (https://hjarta.is/rannsoknir/oldrunarrannsokn-1-afangi/myndgreining/) states all image data are stored in PACS on two mirrored 6.4 TB archives in fire-protected rooms in two separate buildings, pseudonymised with a 10-digit code, ~600 MB of imaging per participant across all modalities (MRI, CT, ultrasound, retinal), with ~12,000 variables per participant in an ORACLE database. Nothing is exposed outside the institution.

Practical read: this is collaboration-only, and specifically it is a negotiated, IRB-plus-DUA collaboration with a named investigator, not a request form. Image access has demonstrably happened (the Erlangen/Kiel group of Engelke, Bartenschlager, Chaudry analysed L1/L2 CT images with Sigurdsson and Gudnason as co-authors), so it is not impossible — but no primary source anywhere states that raw CT or scout images are obtainable, and I found no repository, no dbGaP/EGA/Zenodo record, and no stated turnaround. Treat as months-scale negotiation with a real chance of no.
verdicts.licence: Not stated — confirmed, and the candidate is right to say so. No licence appears on the IHA page, in any data availability statement, or anywhere on hjarta.is. The governing instrument is a bilateral data usage agreement with the Icelandic Heart Association plus IRB approval consistent with the participants' informed consent; a sister AGES paper (PLOS One 10.1371/journal.pone.0221474) spells out that "the participants did not consent for their data to be shared publicly". Note the CC-BY licences on the three articles (Frontiers CC-BY 4.0, JBMR CC-BY 4.0, BMC CC-BY 4.0) cover the text and figures only and say nothing about the data.
verdicts.real_xray: TRUE, with a caveat about what kind. The CT scout/localizer is a genuine X-ray projection (stationary tube, translating table), not a synthetic render, so real_xray: true is defensible. But it is a low-dose CT localizer, not a conventional radiograph and not fluoroscopy: fixed geometry, no C-arm pose variation, scanner-specific formation. The one part of this cohort that IS synthetic is the hip work: the JBMR paper graded Kellgren-Lawrence, minimum joint space width and 3D disease features on digitally reconstructed radiographs made from the pelvic CT, and explicitly conceded "these joint space measurements are only correct for supine radiographs (DRRs) digitally reconstructed from CT and might be different for plain radiographs; we lacked images from both techniques to allow comparisons." That last clause is the strongest primary support for the candidate's "no radiographs" claim — this cohort has no paired plain films to validate DRRs against.
verdicts.paired_ct: TRUE and unusually clean. Every scout is by construction the localizer of a CT acquired on the same table, same session, same scanner: a single Siemens Somatom Sensation 4 for the whole cohort, 120 kV, tube-current modulation at 150 effective mAs, 50 cm FOV, 1 mm slice thickness and 1 mm reconstruction increment, B30s kernel for the L1/L2 spine QCT (confirmed verbatim in both PMC11978659 and PMC13321617). The hip CT is the same scanner, 120 kVp, 140 mAs, pitch 1, 1 mm slices, 512x512 in a 50 cm FOV, 0.977 mm in-plane, standard soft-tissue kernel, supine, covering 1 cm above the acetabular margin to >3 mm below the lesser trochanter (PMC13525202). Kopperdahl et al. (PMC3925753) confirms "All CT scans of the lumbar spine and proximal femur were acquired at IHA on a single scanner (Siemens Sensation 4)". Baseline and 5-year follow-up scouts both exist, so scout-CT pairs exist at two timepoints. Caveat on the candidate's phrasing "same geometry as a 1 mm L1-L2 QCT and a hip CT": the T6-L4 lateral scout is the spine study's localizer; whether the hip/pelvic CT shares that scout or has its own is not stated in any source I opened.
verdicts.anatomy: Confirmed as stated. Scouts cover T6-L4 (verbatim "The scout scans covered T6-L4", PMC13321617; "CT scout scans covering T6-L4", PMC11978659). QCT is of the L1 and L2 vertebrae specifically — only two levels are reconstructed/analysed, not a lumbar block. Hip CT is bilateral proximal femur/acetabulum. The Icelandic imaging page confirms the intent: "Með TS eru teknar myndir af lendhrygg og mjöðmum til að meta ástand beins" (CT images of the lumbar spine and hips to assess bone). Important for a level-naming use: a T6-L4 scout does NOT show the sacrum or the lumbosacral junction, and the QCT volume is L1-L2 only, so the 3-D label source cannot name L3-L5 or S1.
verdicts.counts: Candidate's cohort numbers are right but are NOT the imaging counts. Confirmed from the IHA page: 5,764 recruited to AGES-Reykjavik (recruitment closed January 2006, 72% response, ~300 by home visit); 3,411 recruited to AGES-II (pilot from April 2007, main study from 1 October 2007, last participant 1 September 2011). But the only primary CT count I could open is n=3133 with baseline pelvic CT — the JBMR paper says "Baseline assessment of all 3133 volunteers included pelvic CT" and later calls n=3133 "the entire AGES-Reykjavik cohort", drawn from the 5,764 survivors. So "several thousand CTs with scouts" is directionally right at roughly 3k, not 5.8k. Published spine analyses are far smaller subsets selected by nested case-control: 843 subjects (497 women, 346 men; 167 incident VF, 676 controls) in PMC11978659, 826 (486 women, 340 men; 96 and 78 prevalent VF) in PMC13321617, and 1,110 in Kopperdahl's FEA paper; the JBMR hip study used 258 (74 THR cases, 184 controls). Storage figure from the IHA imaging page: ~600 MB of imaging per participant across ALL modalities (MRI, CT, ultrasound, retinal photography) — the spine/hip CT share of that is unstated, and no per-file or per-series size is published anywhere.
corrections: The 'url' is not a primary data record. https://hjarta.is/en/research/ages-phase-1/ is a study-description page last modified 2021-03-17 with no file list, no sizes, no licence and no download. A full sitemap enumeration of hjarta.is (page-sitemap.xml) turns up no data-access, data-request or portal page in either the English or Icelandic tree.

The IHA page promises PROTOCOLS AND A DATA DICTIONARY on request, not data and not images. Verbatim: 'Access to protocols and the data dictionary is available by request.' The candidate's why_relevant states this correctly, but it should not be read as an imaging-access route.

NO PRIMARY SOURCE ANYWHERE STATES THAT RAW CT OR SCOUT IMAGES CAN BE OBTAINED. All three data availability statements refer to 'data'/'datasets', which in AGES practice means the tabular phenotype database. That images have moved (the Erlangen group analysed L1/L2 CT with IHA co-authors) is inference from co-authorship, not a stated policy. This is the single biggest gap between the candidate's framing and what is documented.

One of the three cited papers is an explicit non-release: JBMR 10.1093/jbmr/zjaf202 says 'The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author.' That is the 'available upon reasonable request' pattern and must be reported as such, not as access.

The three data availability statements are mutually inconsistent — collaboration+DUA+named email (Frontiers), 'principally available through the IHA, check terms and conditions' (BMC), and corresponding-author request (JBMR). No single governing access policy is published.

'lateral' scout is NOT stated in any of the three cited papers — they say only 'CT scout scans covering T6-L4'. I confirmed 'lateral' from a different AGES paper, Kopperdahl et al., PMC3925753: 'Incident vertebral fractures were adjudicated by analyzing the lateral scout of the baseline and five-year follow-up CT exams.' Cite that one for the lateral claim.

'subjects: 5,764 at baseline' conflates cohort size with imaging count. 5,764 is the AGES-Reykjavik recruitment; the only published pelvic-CT count I found is n=3133 (JBMR). Published spine QCT analyses are nested case-control subsets of 843 / 826 / 1110, not the full cohort.

'n_images: Several thousand CTs with scouts' is plausible but unverified as a released quantity — no file inventory, no series counts and no sizes exist in any public source. The only size datum is ~600 MB per participant across ALL modalities, from the Icelandic imaging page, and two mirrored 6.4 TB PACS archives for the whole study.

'pose_or_labels: Scout pose implicit in the CT' is an assumption. No source states that the scout's geometry (SID/SOD, table position, collimation) is retained or recoverable, and no per-vertebra localisation labels exist — the only published scout annotation is a Genant SQ grade per vertebral body from T6 to L4, which is a fracture severity grade, not a level label or a landmark.

'licence: Not stated' is confirmed and is not a formality: PLOS One 10.1371/journal.pone.0221474 (same cohort) records that 'the participants did not consent for their data to be shared publicly', so a public re-release under any licence is unlikely to be grantable regardless of collaboration.

Supporting evidence for the 'no radiographs' claim, which the candidate does not cite: AGES hand osteoarthritis was scored from high-quality digital PHOTOGRAPHS, not hand films (PLOS One 10.1371/journal.pone.0221474). Combined with the JBMR admission that 'we lacked images from both techniques', the cohort appears to contain no plain radiography at all.

Device name is spelled two ways in the sources — 'Sensation 4, Siemens, Erlangen, Germany' (the two QCT papers) and 'Somaton Sensation 4, Siemens Medical Systems' (JBMR, a typo for Somatom). Same scanner; a single scanner for the whole cohort, which is a strength but also means zero scanner diversity.

Publication dates: Frontiers 2025-03-26, JBMR 2025-12-27 (issue 41(9):963), BMC Musculoskelet Disord 2026-06-27. All three DOIs resolve (302 to publisher). The candidate's '2025-2026 papers' is right.

Scope caution for a level-naming use: a T6-L4 scout never shows the sacrum or the lumbosacral junction, and the 3-D CT is L1-L2 plus hip only — there is no contiguous L1-S1 CT to derive level labels from, so scout-to-CT label transfer would be limited to L1 and L2.

verdicts.real_xray: Yes, real transmitted-X-ray projections — but they are CT localizers, not radiographs, and not every claim about them holds. Kopperdahl 2014 (AGES methods paper) states verbatim: "Incident vertebral fractures were adjudicated by analyzing the lateral scout of the baseline and five-year follow-up CT exams," and that the scout covered "any vertebra from T6-L4." The 2026 BMC paper: "Prevalent vertebral fractures ... were identified using CT scout images acquired during the initial CT scan ... The scout scans covered T6-L4." The 2025 Frontiers paper: "Spine fractures were confirmed on CT scout scans covering T6-L4, which were obtained at 5 years after baseline, using the Genant SQ scoring system." So: real acquisitions, kV-range, on a Siemens Somatom Sensation 4, not DRR, not MV portal, not simulated. TWO CAVEATS THE CANDIDATE DOES NOT STATE. (1) The BMC paper lists as an explicit limitation "the use of CT scout views instead of X-rays to identify and grade the vertebral fractures" — the authors themselves treat the scout as a substitute for, not an instance of, a radiograph. (2) A CT scout is a translating fan-beam sweep with a stationary tube, i.e. parallel along the craniocaudal axis and fan in-plane. That is NOT the point-source cone-beam geometry of a C-arm or of a plain film, so this source is a poor geometric surrogate for fluoroscopy even though the photons are real. The only truly cone-beam-like 2-D images in AGES are the hip DRRs, which are synthetic by construction.
verdicts.paired_ct: Yes, and this is the strongest part of the candidate. The scout IS the localizer of the same session's CT, so registration is by construction. Kopperdahl 2014: "All CT scans of the lumbar spine and proximal femur were acquired at IHA on a single scanner (Siemens Sensation 4) using 120 kVp, a pitch of 1.0, and a modulated tube current with a reference exposure of 150 mAs. Images were reconstructed using a 1.0 mm slice thickness, a B30s soft tissue kernel, and a 50 cm field of view." Spine and proximal femur are one visit. Frontiers/BMC confirm the spine reconstruction covers L1 and L2 in most subjects (T12-L1 or L2-L3 substituted when a level was fractured or excluded), with an Image Analysis type-4 calibration phantom in field. It is CT, not CBCT. BUT the pairing the candidate implies does not exist for the pelvis: the JBMR hip paper specifies the pelvic CT ran "from 1 cm above acetabular margin to >3 mm below the lesser trochanter," which lies entirely BELOW the T6-L4 scout range. No primary source I could find describes a scout for the hip/pelvic acquisition at all. So there is a lateral scout paired with a lumbar CT, and a pelvic CT with no documented paired projection.
verdicts.anatomy: Lower thoracic through L4 in the projection images; pelvis and hips only in the axial CT. The scout range T6-L4 is stated identically in three papers. That means the lumbar spine is PARTLY present (L1-L4) and L5, the sacrum, the sacroiliac joints and the pelvis are ABSENT from every documented scout. The BMC paper adds the complementary limitation, "the scout scans did not include the upper thoracic vertebrae." For a lumbosacral-junction or spinopelvic task this is the wrong window: the candidate's own why_relevant leans on the hip CT sitting "in the same geometry," but the pelvis appears only in the reconstructed volume and in the DRRs made from it. The JBMR hip paper confirms the pelvis was read from synthetic projections: "K&L grade assessment, mJSW measurement, and 3D OA disease feature grading were performed on digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs)," produced by "MPR of mean intensity projection slab at each hip ... DRR simulated standard pelvic radiograph," and the authors concede "we lacked images from both techniques to allow comparisons" — i.e. no real pelvic radiographs exist in the cohort.
verdicts.counts: Subject counts partly wrong as given. 5,764 is the AGES-I recruitment total (confirmed on hjarta.is) but is NOT the number imaged. A 2025 primary source (PMC12208951) states: "The full AGES-Reykjavik Study cohort comprises 5764 community-dwelling elderly Icelandic males and females. For this analysis, participants were included only if they had CT scan data available from study entry (n = 4831)." So 4,831 baseline CT exams. 3,411 is the AGES-II recruitment total from hjarta.is, not a follow-up CT count. The JBMR hip paper gives a third figure: "Baseline assessment of all 3133 volunteers included pelvic CT," and calls n=3133 "the entire AGES-Reykjavik cohort" for its purposes — so the hip/pelvic CT subcohort is smaller than the 4,831 with any CT. No primary source states a count of SCOUT IMAGES; "several thousand CTs with scouts" is an inference from the CT count, and Kopperdahl notes attrition against it: "The remaining 93 subjects were excluded from further analysis in the spine arm due to lack of a readable CT scout view (at baseline or follow-up)." Published substudy sizes are far smaller than the cohort: 843 subjects (167 incident VF, 676 controls) in the Frontiers/BMC QCT arm; 258 participants in the JBMR hip arm.
verdicts.access_now: Not obtainable as a dataset; the candidate's "on request" overstates what any source says. The hjarta.is AGES page says only: "Access to protocols and the data dictionary is available by request" — protocols and a data dictionary, not images. The three papers' data statements are collaboration-gated and say nothing about imaging: Frontiers — "The datasets presented in this article are not readily available because they were used under license. Restrictions also apply ... Data from the AGES-Reykjavik study are available through collaboration under a data usage agreement with the Icelandic Heart Association." BMC — "Data are principally available through the Icelandic Heart Association (hjarta.is). Please check for terms and conditions with the IHA." JBMR — "The data underlying this article will be shared on reasonable request to the corresponding author." None of these states that DICOM scouts or CT volumes can be released. Realistically this is a collaboration under a DUA with an Icelandic National Bioethics Committee approval (VSN 00-063) behind it, not a download. Treat serving level "A" as unsupported.
verdicts.licence: Correctly recorded as not stated. I found no licence on hjarta.is or in any of the three papers. The Frontiers statement that data "were used under license" implies a bilateral DUA with terms not published anywhere I could reach. Assume no redistribution right.
corrections: REFUTED (framing): these are not radiographs and the authors say so. BMC 2026 lists as a limitation 'the use of CT scout views instead of X-rays to identify and grade the vertebral fractures.' The candidate's real_xray:true is defensible only in the narrow sense that photons were transmitted through a patient. A CT scout is a translating fan-beam sweep (parallel in z, fan in-plane), not the point-source cone-beam geometry of a C-arm; for a fluoroscopy project this is a different projection model, not a domain-shifted version of the same one.

NOT SUPPORTED: 'lateral scout T6-L4' and every other imaging detail is ABSENT from the candidate's own primary URL. I pulled the full text of https://hjarta.is/en/research/ages-phase-1/ — it mentions only 'calcium scoring of the coronary arteries by computerized tomography (CT) and hippocampal volume by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).' No QCT, no spine, no hip, no scout, no Sensation 4. The imaging claims rest entirely on the journal papers, not on the institutional page cited first.

CORRECTED: the sacrum, pelvis and L5 are NOT in any documented projection image. Scout coverage is T6-L4 in all three papers; the pelvic CT runs '1 cm above acetabular margin to >3 mm below the lesser trochanter,' which does not overlap the scout range. No primary source describes a scout for the hip/pelvic acquisition. The claim that the scouts 'sit in the same geometry as ... a hip CT' is unsupported — they are anatomically disjoint acquisitions.

CORRECTED counts: 5,764 is AGES-I recruitment, not the imaged population. PMC12208951 states 4,831 had baseline CT. 3,411 is AGES-II recruitment, not a follow-up CT count. The JBMR hip paper states 3,133 had baseline pelvic CT. No source gives a count of scout images, and Kopperdahl 2014 excluded 93 subjects 'due to lack of a readable CT scout view'.

OVERSTATED: access. hjarta.is offers 'protocols and the data dictionary ... by request' — not images. Frontiers says data are 'not readily available because they were used under license' and available only 'through collaboration under a data usage agreement.' No primary source states that CT or scout images can be obtained by anyone. Serving level 'A' is not established.

NOT SUPPORTED: 'Scout pose implicit in the CT.' No source I read describes scout geometry, source-detector distance, magnification, or any released calibration, and none releases a pose file. The scout's implicit registration to its own CT is a reasonable engineering assumption, but it is an inference and it does not yield a C-arm-style extrinsic pose. State it as unknown.

QUALIFIED: 'Genant SQ fracture grades from the scouts' are real but are study-derived research variables held by the IHA and its collaborators, graded per level T6-L4. There is no published per-vertebra annotation file, no keypoints, no segmentation, and no level-identity labels released in any form I could find. Do not count this as a labelled dataset.

UNRESOLVED discrepancy across primary sources: tube voltage is given as 120 kVp by Kopperdahl 2014, the 2025 Frontiers paper, the 2026 BMC paper and the 2025 JBMR hip paper, but as 140 kV by PMC12208951 (2025), which also gives voxel size 0.977 x 0.977 x 1 mm. mAs also differs between the spine protocol (150 effective mAs) and the pelvic protocol (140 mAs). I could not determine from the sources which applies to which acquisition, or whether one paper is simply wrong.

CONFIRMED with a caveat worth keeping: the 'no conventional radiographs' claim holds as far as the described protocol goes — the JBMR hip paper grades K&L and mJSW on DRRs and concedes 'we lacked images from both techniques to allow comparisons.' But it is a negative I cannot prove across all AGES substudies, and that same paper notes 'Ascertainment bias may have occurred, if primary care physicians requested their own radiographs of their patients' hips' — clinical films outside the study, not part of any dataset.

NET JUDGEMENT for a spine-fluoroscopy use: the paired CT is genuine and the scouts are genuine acquisitions, which is more than most candidates offer. But the projection geometry is wrong for fluoroscopy, the anatomy stops at L4 so the lumbosacral junction and pelvis are absent from the 2-D images, no pose or public labels exist, no licence exists, and access is a bilateral DUA rather than a release. The pelvic 2-D images that DO exist are DRRs, which is precisely what the task asks to exclude.

candidate.name: TCIA/IDC TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC CT-urography AP abdomen/pelvis radiographs with same-session abdominopelvic CT; one CMB-LCA lateral thoracic-spine film with CT
candidate.why_relevant: New specifics for the known small TCIA overlap, from an IDC v24 sweep (idc-index 0.12.5). Only 15 collections have patients with both CT and RF/XA/DX/CR, and RTIMAGE is absent. The only non-chest pairs not already known are these. TCGA-CW-6088 (2 CT-urogram exams, 4 CR) and TCGA-D1-A2G5 (3 CR) have genuine Fuji CR AP pelvis films taken in the same session as a 1 mm abdominopelvic CT, covering L3-L5, the sacrum and the pelvis. CMB-LCA MSB-09794 has an upright lateral thoracic-spine film with a CT 29 days later. That totals 8 films across 3 patients.

verdicts.access_now: Downloadable NOW, anonymously, no login, no account, no Data Retriever, no request form. I pulled both idc-open-data S3 objects by plain HTTPS GET (200 OK, application/dicom, 7,543,740 and 7,543,712 bytes) and separately pulled three whole series through the NBIA REST endpoint (services.cancerimagingarchive.net/nbia-api/services/v1/getImage?SeriesInstanceUID=...), each returning a zip with the DICOM plus a LICENSE file. Cross-check: the NBIA zip for the TCGA-CW-6088 CR contains a DICOM of exactly 7,543,740 bytes, identical in size to the S3 object, so the IDC and TCIA routes serve the same file. The collection web pages advertise "Download requires TCIA Data Retriever" for the full collection, but the per-series REST route needs nothing. Caveat: CMB-LCA additionally carries a SEPARATE restricted subset (head images, 38.67 GB) gated behind the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy; that gate does not touch the DX or CT discussed here, which are in the public CC BY 4.0 part.
verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed by rendering the pixel data, not by trusting tags. The TCGA films are genuine Fuji computed radiography: Manufacturer FUJIFILM, 2140 x 1760 px at ImagerPixelSpacing 0.20 mm (a 428 x 352 mm CR cassette), MONOCHROME1, 12 bits stored, with a physical lead "R" side marker, technologist initials, and burned-in annotations "CTU / 20MIN" and "CTU / POST VOID" — i.e. delayed-phase and post-void projection urogram films. Not DRRs, not CT topograms (the topograms in the same patients are separate Modality=CT Siemens series). One trap worth naming: ImageType reads DERIVED\PRIMARY\POST_PROCESSED, which looks synthetic but is Fuji's standard FCR processing flag; the manufacturer is the CR vendor, not the CT vendor, and AcquisitionDeviceProcessingDescription is a plate preset ("CTU ABD", "GU ABDOMEN"). The CMB-LCA films are Modality=DX, ImageType ORIGINAL\PRIMARY, FUJIFILM, 0.15 mm pixels, one of them annotated "UPRIGHT". No projection geometry is present on any of them: DistanceSourceToDetector, DistanceSourceToPatient, ViewPosition and (on the CR) PatientOrientation are all absent or empty, so there is no SID/SOD to fit against.
verdicts.anatomy: Verified by looking at the rendered films. TCGA-CW-6088 (1999-10-11, "CTU 20MIN") and TCGA-D1-A2G5 (1992-04-22, "CTU POST VOID") are both coned AP pelvis/lower-abdomen radiographs showing roughly L2/L3 downward: lower lumbar vertebral bodies with visible pedicles and transverse processes, the lumbosacral junction, the whole sacrum and both SI joints, both innominates, both acetabula, femoral heads and proximal femora. The candidate's "L3-L5, sacrum, pelvis, hips" is correct and slightly conservative. Collimation cuts off above about L2, so no thoracolumbar junction and no rib-count anchor on these films. CMB-LCA MSB-09794: the study is XR_ThoracicSpine and contains two films — one upright lateral (2816 x 2373) in which the thoracic vertebral bodies and posterior elements are visible along the posterior margin but heavily overlapped by shoulder girdle and lung, and one smaller coned lower-thoracic/thoracolumbar film (1693 x 1353) whose image content sits rotated ~10-15 degrees within the pixel frame. Note the BodyPartExamined tags on these two are wrong — they read PELVIS and CHEST while the study is a thoracic spine exam — so any filter keyed on BodyPartExamined will miss or mis-route them.
verdicts.paired_ct: Confirmed, same calendar day, via the TCIA getSeries API. TCGA-CW-6088: three CR on 1995-02-26 alongside a same-day Siemens Sensation 64 CT urogram that includes "70 sec AP 1.0 B30f" (559 images, 1.0 mm); one CR on 1999-10-11 alongside a same-day SOMATOM Definition Flash CT including "Thin Combined Abd 1.0 B30f" (344) and "Thin Combined Pelv 1.0 B30f" (300). TCGA-D1-A2G5: three CR on 1992-04-22 alongside a same-day Sensation 64 CT including "70 sec Abd 1.0 B30f" (420) and "70 sec Pelvis 1.0 B30f" (292). So the "1 mm abdominopelvic CT" and the named scanner models both check out. One qualification: the CR sits in its OWN StudyInstanceUID, distinct from the CT study, so it is same-day and same clinical encounter but not one DICOM study. CMB-LCA MSB-09794 is different and weaker: the DX films are 1959-04-01, the nearest CT is 1959-03-03 (GE Revolution EVO chest-abdomen-pelvis) 29 days BEFORE, and the next CT is 1960-02-05, 310 days after. There is also a lumbar-spine MR 12 days after. All dates are TCIA-shifted, but intervals within a patient are preserved.
verdicts.counts: Nine radiographs, not eight, across three named patients; and the collections hold no others of this type. Enumerated exhaustively by API modality query: TCGA-KIRC contains exactly 4 CR series / 4 images, every one in TCGA-CW-6088, and zero DX, RF or XA. TCGA-UCEC contains exactly 3 CR series / 3 images, every one in TCGA-D1-A2G5, and zero DX, RF or XA. CMB-LCA contains 4 DX series / 4 images across TWO patients: MSB-09794 (2 films, study XR_ThoracicSpine, 1959-04-01) and MSB-01459 (2 films, study XR Chest, 1959-12-22, with CT 1959-11-13 and 1959-12-16), and zero CR, RF or XA. So the spine-relevant yield is 7 AP pelvis CR films over 2 patients plus 2 thoracic-spine DX films over 1 patient. File sizes: each CR is ~7.54 MB; the DX pair is 4.58 MB and 13.37 MB. The radiographs total roughly 48 MB. Collection sizes for the paired CT: TCGA-KIRC 267 subjects / 439 studies / 2,654 series / 192,581 images / 91.56 GB; TCGA-UCEC 65 / 226 / 912 / 77,214 / 37.85 GB; CMB-LCA public part 129 / 494 / 2,724 / 348,167 / 191.92 GB.
verdicts.licence: Mixed, and the candidate's single "CC BY 3.0" is wrong for one of the three. TCGA-KIRC: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported, confirmed both in the API LicenseName/LicenseURI fields and on the collection page. TCGA-UCEC: CC BY 3.0, same confirmation. CMB-LCA: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International, confirmed in the API LicenseName and on the collection page; a LICENSE file ships inside every downloaded series zip. CMB-LCA also has a separate restricted-license subset (head images) under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy, which does not cover the thoracic-spine DX or the paired CT. All three require data citation. DOIs all resolve as claimed: 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.V6PBVTDR (KIRC), 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.GKJ0ZWAC (UCEC), 10.7937/3CX3-S132 (CMB-LCA).
corrections: Film count is 9, not 8. CMB-LCA MSB-09794's XR_ThoracicSpine study contains TWO DX films (an upright lateral, 2816x2373, and a coned lower-thoracic film, 1693x1353), not one. 4 (CW-6088 CR) + 3 (D1-A2G5 CR) + 2 (MSB-09794 DX) = 9.

Licence is not uniformly CC BY 3.0. CC BY 3.0 is correct for TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC only; CMB-LCA is CC BY 4.0 (confirmed in the API LicenseName field and on the collection page). CMB-LCA also carries a separate restricted head-image subset under the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy, which does not affect these films.

The CMB-LCA temporal direction is backwards. The candidate says the CT is 29 days AFTER the thoracic-spine film. The DX is 1959-04-01 and the nearest CT is 1959-03-03 — 29 days BEFORE. The next CT after the film is 1960-02-05, i.e. 310 days later. The 29-day magnitude is right; the direction is not.

The 'published: TCGA collections last updated 2020-05-29' line is right for TCGA (KIRC v3, UCEC v4, both 2020/05/29) but wrong for CMB-LCA, which is at Version 12, updated 2026/07/02, and is marked status Ongoing — its DX inventory can grow or change, so the 4-film count there is not stable.

CMB-LCA has a second DX patient the candidate missed: MSB-01459, 2 chest films on 1959-12-22 with CT on 1959-11-13 and 1959-12-16. Chest-only, so it adds no spine value, but the enumeration as stated is incomplete.

BodyPartExamined is wrong on the CMB-LCA thoracic-spine films: the two series are tagged PELVIS and CHEST while StudyDescription is XR_ThoracicSpine. Any pipeline that filters on BodyPartExamined will silently drop or mis-file them. Likewise the TCGA CR films inherit BodyPartExamined 'Kidney' and 'UTERUS' despite being AP pelvis radiographs.

ImageType on the TCGA CR films reads DERIVED\\PRIMARY\\POST_PROCESSED, which will look synthetic to an automated filter. It is Fuji's FCR processing flag, not evidence of a rendered or derived projection — but a sweep that screens out DERIVED images would discard all seven of the useful films.

'pose_or_labels: None' is right and understated: there is no DistanceSourceToDetector, no DistanceSourceToPatient, no ViewPosition, and on the CR no PatientOrientation either. There is nothing to recover projection geometry from, so these cannot support 2-D/3-D registration without estimating SID and pose from scratch.

The CR and the CT sit in DIFFERENT StudyInstanceUIDs on the same date. 'Same-session' is a fair clinical reading (the burned-in 'CTU 20MIN' and 'CTU POST VOID' labels place the films inside the CT-urogram protocol) but they are not one DICOM study, so a study-level join will find no pairs.
Device string is slightly off for one film: TCGA-CW-6088's three 1995-02-26 CR carry Manufacturer 'FUJI PHOTO FILM Co., ltd.'; only the 1999-10-11 film is 'FUJIFILM Corporation'.

COULD NOT VERIFY the sweep claims: 'IDC v24', 'idc-index 0.12.5', 'only 15 collections have patients with both CT and RF/XA/DX/CR', and 'RTIMAGE is absent'. IDC hosting is confirmed (both idc-open-data S3 objects are live), but the IDC v1 and v2 API version endpoints return HTTP 410 deprecated and v3/versions returns 404, so I could not pin the release number, and I did not re-run the cross-collection join. Treat the 15-collection figure as unconfirmed.

All dates are TCIA date-shifted (the collection pages state this; CMB-LCA uses a 1/1/1960 base). Intervals within a patient are preserved, so the same-day pairing holds, but the absolute dates and any age inference are not real.

verdicts.real_xray: Confirmed real acquisitions; I downloaded and decoded all nine files. TCGA-KIRC/TCGA-UCEC: seven Fuji computed radiographs, SOPClass 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.1 (CR Image Storage), Modality=CR, Manufacturer "FUJIFILM Corporation"/"FUJI PHOTO FILM Co., ltd.", PlateID present (a45516764c, a41822708c), Sensitivity (Fuji S-value) 68/80, ImagerPixelSpacing 0.20 mm, 2140x1760 or 1760x1760, MONOCHROME1, 12 bits. Physical lead markers and technologist initials are burned in ("R", "ZWD", "JEP", "HKD", "CTU 20MIN", "CTU POST VOID"), which no DRR carries. CMB-LCA MSB-09794: two Fuji DR images, SOPClass 1.2.840.10008.5.1.4.1.1.1.1.1 (Digital X-Ray, For Processing), Modality=DX, ImageType ORIGINAL/PRIMARY, ImagerPixelSpacing 0.15 mm, KVP 85, XRayTubeCurrent 226/190 mA, ExposureTime 17/69 ms, SoftwareVersions "DR-ID 300CL APL Software V8.0", "UPRIGHT" burned in on one. Nothing is a DRR, simulation or MV portal image (all diagnostic-energy kV, no RTIMAGE class anywhere in TCIA). Caveat the candidate omits: the seven TCGA CR files are ImageType DERIVED/PRIMARY/POST_PROCESSED (Fuji processed presentation image, DerivationDescription "G1.1D#1.60+0.50,R3Q0.1,C*1.0*1.0") with no kVp/mAs recorded; the two CMB-LCA DX are FOR PROCESSING raw DR and need a LUT before they look like a clinical film.
verdicts.paired_ct: Confirmed for all three patients, and for the two TCGA patients it is genuinely same-session. TCGA-CW-6088: CR films sit in their own StudyInstanceUID but on the same StudyDate as a CT urogram, twice - 1995-02-26 (3 CR; CT study "Abdomen^08_3_Type_I_CTU_Dose_Saving", SIEMENS Sensation 64, includes "70 sec AP 1.0 B30f" 559 images and "Topo - KUB") and 1999-10-11 (1 CR; CT study "CT Urogram w 3D", SIEMENS SOMATOM Definition Flash, includes "Thin Combined Abd 1.0 B30f" 344 images and "Thin Combined Pelv 1.0 B30f" 300 images). TCGA-D1-A2G5: 3 CR on 1992-04-22, same date as a Sensation 64 CT urogram with "70 sec Abd 1.0 B30f" (420), "70 sec Pelvis 1.0 B30f" (292) and "20min Pelvis 1.0 B30f" (304). So 1 mm abdominopelvic CT is real. The films' own burned-in text ("CTU 20MIN", "CTU POST VOID") ties them to the same urogram, which is stronger evidence of same session than the date alone, since TCGA dates are shifted. CMB-LCA MSB-09794: nearest CT is study CT_CAP on 1959-03-03 (GE Revolution EVO, CAP WO / BONE / COR CAP / SAG CAP), 29 days BEFORE the 1959-04-01 films, not after; the patient also has CT_AbdPel studies (1958-06-21, 1958-08-18) and an MRI T Spine 12 days after the films. No CT is same-session for this patient.
verdicts.anatomy: Verified by rendering every file, not by tags. Five of the seven TCGA films are AP abdomen/pelvis (KUB-type) urogram films showing roughly T12/L1 through the proximal femora: lower lumbar vertebrae, sacrum, both SI joints, iliac wings, pubic rami, acetabula, femoral heads and necks, with contrast in the bladder. Two of the seven (TCGA-CW-6088 1995-02-26, 1760x1760; TCGA-D1-A2G5 1992-04-22, 1760x1760) are coned higher - mid/lower thoracic through about L4-L5 with ribs visible - and cut the pelvis at the iliac crests, so they do NOT contain the sacrum or hips. The two CMB-LCA DX are both LATERAL thoracic spine (PatientOrientation P/F on the large one, confirmed by eye: thoracic bodies, ribs, no lumbosacral junction); one is a full upright lateral, the other a coned lateral. Neither CMB-LCA film contains lumbar spine, sacrum or pelvis, despite one of them carrying BodyPartExamined = PELVIS. The DICOM tags are unreliable throughout: the TCGA CR carry BodyPartExamined "Kidney"/"UTERUS" and SeriesDescription "projection urogram" or "= NONE =".
verdicts.counts: 3 subjects, 9 radiographs - not 8. TCIA getSeries confirms TCGA-CW-6088 = 4 CR series (3 dated 1995-02-26 in one study, 1 dated 1999-10-11) plus 64 CT series; TCGA-D1-A2G5 = 3 CR series (all one study, 1992-04-22) plus 17 CT series; CMB-LCA MSB-09794 = 2 DX series, both inside study XR_ThoracicSpine (SeriesNumber 1002 and 1003), plus 48 CT series, 22 MR, 8 NM. Every radiograph series has ImageCount = 1. Usable-for-lumbosacral count is smaller: 5 films across 2 patients show sacrum + pelvis; 2 more show thoracolumbar only; the 2 CMB-LCA films are thoracic-only.
verdicts.pose_or_labels: "None" is confirmed and is in fact worse than stated. All nine files lack DistanceSourceToDetector, DistanceSourceToPatient, EstimatedRadiographicMagnificationFactor, GridFocalDistance, PositionerPrimaryAngle/SecondaryAngle and DetectorPrimaryAngle. ViewPosition is an empty string on the seven TCGA CR and absent on the two DX. So there is no SID/SOD, no C-arm or tube angle, and no 2D/3D registration geometry of any kind - pose would have to be estimated from scratch. No segmentations, landmarks, vertebra labels or annotations on any of these series; TCIA reports ThirdPartyAnalysis = NO for the CMB-LCA DX series. The only positional metadata is PatientOrientation (L/F frontal, P/F lateral) on the two CMB-LCA DX.
verdicts.access_now: Open and anonymous, verified today. Both idc-open-data S3 objects in the candidate resolved and downloaded with plain curl, no credentials, and decoded to the exact CR files claimed (7,543,740 and 7,543,712 bytes). The remaining seven radiographs downloaded anonymously from the TCIA NBIA REST API (services.cancerimagingarchive.net/nbia-api/services/v1/getImage?SeriesInstanceUID=...), each returning a zip with the DICOM plus a LICENSE file. No login, no DUA, no restricted-access gate on these series (note CMB-LCA does restrict some head scans under an NIH controlled-access policy, but not these).
verdicts.licence: Not uniform; the candidate's single "CC BY 3.0" is wrong for one third of the data. TCGA-KIRC and TCGA-UCEC series return LicenseName "Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License" from the TCIA API, matching the collection pages. CMB-LCA series return "Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" with LicenseURI https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, and the CMB-LCA collection page states CC BY 4.0. All three DOIs check out: 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.V6PBVTDR (KIRC), 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2016.GKJ0ZWAC (UCEC), 10.7937/3CX3-S132 (CMB-LCA, returned as CollectionURI by the API).
corrections: n_images is wrong: 9 radiographs, not 8. CMB-LCA study XR_ThoracicSpine (MSB-09794, 1959-04-01) contains TWO DX series, SeriesNumber 1002 and 1003, not one. Both are lateral thoracic-spine views: a full upright lateral (2816x2373) and a coned lateral (1693x1353).

The second CMB-LCA DX carries BodyPartExamined = PELVIS but contains no pelvis - it is a coned lateral thoracic spine. Anyone filtering that collection on BodyPartExamined will pull it as a pelvis film and be wrong.

Direction of the CMB-LCA interval is inverted. The nearest CT (CT_CAP, GE Revolution EVO, 1959-03-03) is 29 days BEFORE the films (1959-04-01), not 29 days later. The next CT after the films is 1960-02-05, about 310 days later.
licence 'CC BY 3.0' is wrong for CMB-LCA, which is CC BY 4.0 (confirmed by both the TCIA API LicenseName/LicenseURI and the collection page). Only the two TCGA collections are CC BY 3.0 Unported.

anatomy 'Lower lumbar spine, sacrum, pelvis, hips' does not hold for all seven TCGA films. Two of them (TCGA-CW-6088 1995-02-26 1760x1760, TCGA-D1-A2G5 1992-04-22 1760x1760) are coned to the thoracolumbar spine and exclude the sacrum and most of the pelvis. Only 5 of 9 films in this candidate actually contain the lumbosacral junction and pelvis.

xray_kind is incomplete for the TCGA films: they are ImageType DERIVED/PRIMARY/POST_PROCESSED, i.e. Fuji processed presentation images, not ORIGINAL, and they record no kVp/mAs. They are still real acquisitions (PlateID, Fuji S-value, physical lead markers) but a pipeline expecting raw or ORIGINAL data should know this. Conversely the two CMB-LCA DX are PresentationIntentType = FOR PROCESSING raw DR and will look wrong without a LUT.

device omits the CMB-LCA scanners. Those CTs are TOSHIBA Aquilion ONE / Aquilion PRIME / Aquilion and GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS Revolution EVO, not Siemens. The Siemens Sensation 64 / SOMATOM Definition Flash attribution is correct only for the two TCGA patients.

pose_or_labels 'None' understates the gap: there is no imaging geometry at all. DistanceSourceToDetector, DistanceSourceToPatient, magnification factor, grid focal distance and all positioner/detector angles are ABSENT in all nine files, and ViewPosition is empty or absent. Nothing supports 2D/3D registration without estimating pose de novo.

UNVERIFIED (no primary source found): 'Only 15 collections have patients with both CT and RF/XA/DX/CR' in IDC v24. I could not reproduce that sweep - idc-index is not installed here and I found no published IDC document stating the number. Treat the 15 as unconfirmed. The companion claim 'RTIMAGE is absent' IS supported: TCIA getModalityValues returns CR, CT, DX, FUSION, KO, MG, MR, NM, OT, PR, PT, REG, RF, RTDOSE, RTPLAN, RTSTRUCT, RWV, SEG, SR, US, XA - no RTIMAGE.
UNVERIFIED: 'in IDC v24' specifically. The two idc-open-data S3 objects resolve, so presence in IDC is confirmed, but I found no primary source pinning them to version 24.
published field is stale for CMB-LCA. Its collection page now reports Version 12, most recently updated 2026-07-02; the DX series were DateReleased 2024-08-28. The TCGA 2020-05-29 dates are correct.

Dates are de-identified and shifted. TCGA-CW-6088's studies run 1991-1999 while the patient is listed 060Y-069Y; CMB-LCA states its dates are normalised to a 1960 baseline. Same-day pairing is preserved (and corroborated by the burned-in 'CTU 20MIN'/'POST VOID' text), but no absolute date here is real, so 'same session' rests on the relative date plus the annotation, not on the timestamp alone.

For the intended use this is a static diagnostic-radiograph overlap, not fluoroscopy: modality CR/DX only, no RF or XA in these three patients, one frame per series. It can serve as a handful of real films with same-patient CT, but 9 images across 3 patients with no geometry and no labels is a sanity-check set, not a test set.
